atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file's runtime imports go only to its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must not know the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - import edge, importer kind vs imported kind, both read from the suffix; type-only edges are outside it (matrix is runtime, 875).
atoms.landing: The direction of every edge is readable from two filenames.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service, assembly and boot import no concrete platform/IO code (node:fs, HTTP clients, DB drivers) and no package not declared pure.
atoms.why: Code that imports the machine cannot run without it and bypasses its ports.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - import specifier classified concrete / pure-declared; runtime only.
atoms.landing: From the import block alone, a reader knows the file touches no machine.

atoms.name: pure-lib-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as model only if the project declares it pure; an undeclared package is concrete.
atoms.why: Purity of a package cannot be inferred from its name or its look.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - membership in a config list.
atoms.landing: The set of packages the inside may use is one visible list.

atoms.name: ambient-free
atoms.statement: A file neither reads nor calls ambient globals (environment, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis), at root or in a function.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine through a global depends on it, and no import reveals it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - identifier resolution to ambient globals, anywhere in the file (flavor/reader names the list).
atoms.landing: Everything the file needs from the world arrives in its arguments, so it is visible in the signature.

atoms.name: no-barrel-file
atoms.statement: An import path names the file that declares its layer; no index re-export stands between.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the matrix cannot be enforced.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - resolved target is an index/barrel or a re-export-only file.
atoms.landing: Every import line shows which layer is entered, with no file to open.

atoms.name: composition-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file is imported at runtime only by assembly (private/ files and type-only imports excepted).
atoms.why: The concrete graph is known in one place, so nothing else can pick its own dependencies.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - runtime edge to a public service/adapter file from a non-assembly importer.
atoms.landing: A service or adapter import outside assembly is a red flag visible at the import line.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import from blob, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: Code with no layer guarantees must not contaminate a layer that has them.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - edge to a suffixless file from a non-assembly, non-test, non-blob importer.
atoms.landing: Debt is quarantined: the files that touch it are a short, known list.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from that service's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private may change without notice.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - path contains private/ and importer is outside the owning service directory (layer directories count as inside).
atoms.landing: A private import is an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: service-dag
atoms.statement: Imports between service packages, every import kind included, form no cycle.
atoms.why: A service in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - edges collapsed to service directories; needs the service boundary from config/layout.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a reader can follow in one direction.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between files form no cycle, within a service or across.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently in production bundles.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - runtime import graph cycle detection.
atoms.landing: Load order is a plain order, never a puzzle.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and assemblies (and by tests as caller), type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract; its shape is the services it returns, so nothing may type against it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - importer kind of each edge into an assembly file.
atoms.landing: Who triggers construction is a short list of drivers and sibling assemblies.

atoms.name: driver-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: The driver holds the tech; nothing inside may be reachable from it or reach it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - importer kind of each edge into a driver file.
atoms.landing: The entry chain boot -> driver -> sub-drivers is the only way in.

atoms.name: boot-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file, type imports included.
atoms.why: A boot executes at load; importing it would run the program from inside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - any edge into a boot file.
atoms.landing: A boot is a leaf: one file per entry point, nothing leans on it.

atoms.name: test-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a test file (.spec, .test, .e2e).
atoms.why: A test file registers into the runner at load; importing it would register twice or leak fixtures.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - any edge into a test-kind file.
atoms.landing: Shared test code cannot hide in a spec; it must be placed by what it is.

atoms.name: driver-tech-imports
atoms.statement: Beyond assemblies and drivers, a driver imports only the tech a bound reader claims; never composition units, model, pure libraries, blob or boot (type imports free).
atoms.why: The driver is coupled to the runtime and to nothing of the inside, so nothing there can hold logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - import specifier vs reader's claim list.
atoms.landing: The driver's import block names exactly its tech and its assembly.

atoms.name: driver-claimed-names
atoms.statement: A global name used in a driver must be claimed by a bound reader (process, document where a host reader is bound); an unclaimed name is red.
atoms.why: A name no reading claims cannot be judged as tech or as anything else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - identifier resolution against reader claims.
atoms.landing: What counts as 'tech' is an explicit list, never a guess.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start its one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - import list of a boot-kind file.
atoms.landing: Each entry point shows its driver in one line.

atoms.name: port-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file contains type declarations only, and no runtime import touches a port file in either direction.
atoms.why: A port is a contract of shape; runtime code in it means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - AST of port files has no value declaration or statement; runtime edges to/from port files.
atoms.landing: The contract can be read with nothing executable to wonder about.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter's factory returns something assignable to a port interface it imports.
atoms.why: Adapters are replaceable only behind the one interface the inside holds.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial - needs the type checker (assignability to an imported port type).
atoms.landing: Which port an adapter serves is stated in its own file.

atoms.name: deps-explicit
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory takes every dependency through its arguments, with no default value that builds or imports one.
atoms.why: Defaults create static imports to adapters and scatter assembly across services.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial - default-value expressions of factory parameters in .service/.adapter files (imports already caught by composition-assembly-only).
atoms.landing: What a service needs is exactly its parameter list.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory call: a composition unit's, another assembly's, a blob file's, a model create* factory's, or a declared load; no use case, model function or tech call.
atoms.why: Assembly builds the graph and does nothing else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - callee file kind plus the flavor's factory name for model callees; await counts as the call.
atoms.landing: An assembly reads as a list of constructions, so the map can draw it.

atoms.name: built-untouched
atoms.statement: What assembly builds is passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed.
atoms.why: The assembly never looks into what it built; looking is deciding.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - result flow of each call (binding uses); declared load result is the one that may be read.
atoms.landing: No decision about instances can sit in the wiring.

atoms.name: declared-load
atoms.statement: The use cases an assembly may await are named in project config; an undeclared call is a violation and its resolution is the declaration; a load's result counts as tech value.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - callee against a declared list.
atoms.landing: The program's startup dependencies on data are a visible short list.

atoms.name: plain-arguments
atoms.statement: Arguments in assembly calls and driver wiring calls are literals, tech values received as parameters (reads of fields allowed), or instances; nothing derived.
atoms.why: A derived argument is a computation, and computing belongs to the unit that needs the value.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - argument expression shapes.
atoms.landing: The call sites show who gets what, with no hidden arithmetic.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-shape
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value, against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A decision on an instance's output is invisible on the map and belongs to the unit that owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - condition expression operands and arm statements.
atoms.landing: Conditional wiring is drawn as conditional edges, never as hidden logic.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances only; adapters only when its caller is a test.
atoms.why: Consumers type against service APIs; adapters stay outside the hexagon they serve.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - kind of the callee behind each returned binding, plus the importer kinds when adapters are returned.
atoms.landing: What an assembly hands out is the hexagon's front, nothing of its back.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind names: assembly functions (assembly), hooks and at most one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot); any other definition is residue.
atoms.why: A definition in the outside is logic with no contract, port or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - count and classify run-time declarations (function, class, variable) against the kind's list.
atoms.landing: The outside files are visibly boring: names of hooks and wiring, nothing else.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-closed
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver calls only assembly factories, tech setup and sub-driver wiring functions; never a use case, an adapter or a model.
atoms.why: Wiring is done once and nowhere else; a hook does not wire and wiring does not run use cases.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - callee kind and reader claim for each call outside hook bodies.
atoms.landing: The driver's top level reads as setup, with no behavior.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: Each hook makes exactly one use-case call: zero and two or more are both red; the callee is a service, never an adapter, model or tech.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence no one owns; zero hides logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - count of calls in a hook body (await is the call), callee kind; hook boundaries from the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow, so the outside is reasoned about without opening it.

atoms.name: hook-unconditional
atoms.statement: A hook body holds no branch, loop, ternary or short-circuit around its call.
atoms.why: A condition is a decision, and decisions belong to a facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - control-flow ancestors in the hook body.
atoms.landing: Reading a hook never requires asking when it runs.

atoms.name: hook-args-asis
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals; nothing read off them and no default on the way in.
atoms.why: Translating the event is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - argument expressions are identifiers or literals, no member access or call.
atoms.landing: What the tech hands in is exactly what the service gets.

atoms.name: hook-result-inert
atoms.statement: A hook returns the call's value or drops it; the value is never read, written, handed on or logged.
atoms.why: Using the result (exit code, rendering, branch) is translation, owned by the facade.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - dataflow of the call result: only return or discard.
atoms.landing: Output handling is found in a service behind a port, never in a hook.

atoms.name: hook-bare-body
atoms.statement: A hook body contains no statement besides its call (no assignment, declaration, log).
atoms.why: Anything else in the hook is logic with no contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - statement list of the hook body.
atoms.landing: The hook is one line whose meaning is the use case's name.

atoms.name: wiring-fn-signature
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes no parameters and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: The boot calls with nothing, so the root reads the host; a sub-driver gets what the parent holds.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for the root half (parameter count of what a boot calls); sub half needs reader claims on parameter types.
atoms.landing: Who owns the tech reading is visible at the signature.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot calls its driver's wiring function exactly once, at module root, with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start; arguments would be the boot touching the tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - root call count, callee, argument count.
atoms.landing: The entry of every program is one import and one call.

atoms.name: sub-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver uses an imported driver only to call its wiring function during its own wiring, passing tech and instances; never inside a hook, never with a use-case result.
atoms.why: A call from a hook into a sub-driver would chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - every use of the imported binding is a call in wiring position.
atoms.landing: One entry point can split its hooks across files with no new behavior.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: If a hook is exported, another file can call it and the one-call guarantee leaks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - export list of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: driver-reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a reader bound to its tech (or bound to one that counts it as blob on purpose).
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading that cuts hooks and claims tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - config glob bindings per file.
atoms.landing: A driver's reading is a named, visible choice.

atoms.name: kind-by-name
atoms.statement: A file's kind comes from the flavor's name; a reader binding gives a kind only to a file the flavor leaves blob, or agrees with it.
atoms.why: One source of truth per kind keeps labels from drifting.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - config validation of bindings against the flavor.
atoms.landing: The kind is read from the filename, never negotiated.

atoms.name: tech-listening-driver
atoms.statement: Callbacks handed to the claimed tech to receive its events exist only in a driver (or test) file.
atoms.why: If anything else listens, hooks hide outside the layer ruled for them.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial - function passed to a call on a claimed import in a non-driver file; the line between inbound listening and an outbound call with a callback is not drawn in canon.
atoms.landing: The event surface of the program is the driver list.

atoms.name: exemption-states-reason
atoms.statement: A relaxation of a rule is written down with its reason and drawn from a closed list; there is no open escape.
atoms.why: An open set of escapes is a hole.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial - config schema requires a reason and refuses unknown shapes; judging the reason is not mechanical.
atoms.landing: Each exception in force is visible with its why, so kinds can be audited.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: Every binding at module root is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly array/record/map/set, frozen literal) to its depth.
atoms.why: A test that imports the module must find the state every other test found.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - declaration and initializer syntax/type; opt-out by config (mutableModuleState: true).
atoms.landing: State lives in factory closures, so who holds state is visible at a glance.

atoms.name: root-no-capture
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the tech, the clock or randomness; the module's own location is not such a value.
atoms.why: The file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - initializer dataflow from ambient/tech reads.
atoms.landing: No load-time machine snapshot hides in a constant.

atoms.name: root-calls-inert
atoms.statement: No root call reaches the tech or an unclaimed name, runs a use case, or goes into a local function of an effect-allowed file (adapter, blob); property reads are free, a call is not unless a reader declares it effect-free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - root call callee classification.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing; reading it is enough.

atoms.name: root-statements-inert
atoms.statement: No root statement besides bindings and calls does something at evaluation (assignment, delete and the like); a throw is not one.
atoms.why: A statement that only makes sense at run time is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - root statement kinds.
atoms.landing: A root is declarations and imports only.

atoms.name: registration-root-calls
atoms.statement: In a test file the only root calls are registrations into the runner by the test tech's reading; they alone are exempt from root-calls-inert.
atoms.why: The runner must be handed the hooks at load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - root call callee is a reader-declared registration role.
atoms.landing: Test files show their registrations and nothing else at root.

atoms.name: test-public-api
atoms.statement: A test calls a unit through its public surface (returned API, public layer files), not through private/ internals.
atoms.why: Tests prove the contract; touching internals pins what the architecture freed to move.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial - imports of private/ and of non-exported internals; collides with 'imports anything' and private-sealed.
atoms.landing: A test names the contract it exercises.

atoms.name: scenario-linear
atoms.statement: A test hook body is a straight line: no branch, loop or data-driven indirection around the scenario.
atoms.why: The reviewer reads each test as given X, when Y, expect Z, in the test itself.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes - control-flow nodes in the test hook body; same check as hook-unconditional with a different why.
atoms.landing: A test is legible as a behavior statement without reconstructing it from helpers.

rules.remainder: Lateral OK and the matrix leave open whether a type-only import counts (matrix is runtime, 875; model 'depends on nothing outside model', 291).
none
No atom of its own: transitive closure of per-file import atoms; 'partial extraction produces false guarantees' is its why.
'becomes untestable' is the why only.
Scope (model, service) and exemption (adapters, drivers) are by kind; also double-covers a root read with root-no-capture.
'Build it and inject it behind a port' (489-490) is only partly checkable (param type is a port); driver and model refusals are restatements of other rows.
none
none
Scope flag on composition-assembly-only (type imports exempt), not an atom; SomeService['method'] shorthand is a type-level form of the same flag.
Scope flag on composition-assembly-only (private/ units exempt). The private composition unit is composed by its owner's factory (159-167), an unruled assembly inside a service/adapter: a hole.
none

Hole: 'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no structure to check beyond adapter-implements-port (implied) and composition-assembly-only, which stop a service from naming an adapter.
none
Needs service boundary from layout; the direction law (817-826) is derived from it, plus composition-assembly-only.
none

Holes: 'assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details', 'internal unit tests justified only when closed input set or absurd fixture' (1172-1175); production config absent from tests (1200-1201) is checkable only if the config adapter is designated.

'Imports anything, defines anything' is the absence of import atoms and closed-definitions (laundering venue); 'hook count and services-only do not apply' exempts hook-single-call and wiring-calls-closed only, silent on the other hook atoms; shared-test-code placement by what it is is only partly checkable (test-not-imported covers 'not test kind', 'not blob' is a hole); .e2e is listed as test kind (263) then called 'neither' (1022-1023); use-case-level annotation is a map convention.

'Decides nothing but which factory to call' is the judgment word; 'config wired as dependency by default' is a convention; 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' (498-500) has no stated structure; 'nothing at root but imports' is closed-definitions plus root atoms; ambient-free and no-concrete-import for assembly are implied (488-489).
none
none
Branches or loops in driver wiring are unspecified; 'a hook does not wire' is hook-single-call.
Examples (default, branch on result, print, exitCode) each hit two atoms; 'a facade is missing' and 'logic with no home' are whys; the cut of hooks is the reader's.

Restates callee kinds already in wiring-calls-closed and hook-single-call; 'its own tech' is allowed here but not in a hook per hook-one-call; 'a pure library is model and red' is driver-tech-imports.
none
'Never hexagon data' follows from hook-result-inert and hook-single-call; markup-child mounting is declared out of scope.
none
'Touches no tech' implies ambient-free and no-concrete-import for boot (implied); 'one boot per entry point' needs a definition of entry point (config).

'A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' (1088-1090) is an open judgment; property reads 'presumed free of side effects' is a presumption; exemptions are two by kind (boot call, test registration) - stated as exceptions, they are other atoms replacing root-calls-inert.

kinds.note: Model takes no port or service: its inward-imports set is model only.
Root atoms are vacuous: nothing runs.
Same atoms as model, plus deps-explicit and composition-assembly-only (carried as imported); wider inward-imports set (ports).
Not ambient-free and not no-concrete-import: that is the tech's business. 'Holds nothing of the hexagon's' is a hole.
ambient-free is implied for assembly (488-489); a declared container library is a declared exception to no-concrete-import; blob is importable here because blob-import-gate lives on blob.
Not ambient-free and not no-concrete-import: the driver holds the tech.
Carries boot-calls-once in place of root-calls-inert (the exception becomes a different atom); ambient-free implied by 'touches no tech'.

Carries none of: inward-imports, no-concrete-import, pure-lib-declared, composition-assembly-only (imports anything, acting as assembly), hook-single-call, hook-args-asis, hook-result-inert, hook-bare-body (a test reads the result and asserts), closed-definitions (see testKind).
Carried as imported (gate on its importers) and as importer of composition units (refused). Whether stable-root judges blob files themselves is unclear in canon.

sharedParts.problem: One atom stated in two slugs split by file kind, plus two scope slugs that are modifiers, not constraints; the private/ exemption leaves an unruled assembly (owner's factory, 159-167).
One per-kind allowlist stated four times; test 'defines anything' is the same atom switched off, which makes local test helpers the laundering venue.

'Tech values, instances, literals' reused with different reading rights: assembly may read fields of a tech value (442), a hook may read nothing (601-604), driver wiring says nothing; hook-args-asis is the strict variant.
Allowed callee kinds for a driver stated in two slugs; driver-calls-services also allows 'its own tech' where hook-one-call forbids any other call in a hook.
'Never an adapter, never a model' is a restatement of the hook's callee rule; zero-call and 'a hook does not wire' also appear in the other slugs.

The hook-one-call examples (branch on result, default, print) each hit two of hook-single-call, hook-unconditional, hook-result-inert; the test exemption names only count and services-only, so the other hook atoms still bind a test by the text, which contradicts asserting on a result.
'No blob in a driver or inner layer' is stated in the matrix, in chain-purity, in blob-quarantine and in 'assembly and driver are not blob' (643-652).
Stated in model (295-298), service (341), assembly (481), test isolation (1196-1198) and stable-root: one atom, five wordings.
A model or service file reading the clock at root is caught by ambient-free and by root-no-capture; stable-root defers 'what decides it' to the layer (1122-1123), so scopes overlap.
Exempted for the boot's call and a spec's registrations by kind: these are two other atoms (boot-calls-once, registration-root-calls) swapped in; canon writes them as exceptions.

'Call the imported driver's wiring function only' recurs for boot and for sub-drivers; position and arguments differ (root and none vs wiring and instances), the shared part is that the imported driver is used only through its wiring function.
'Test imports anything' contradicts 'nothing outside a service imports its private/' and 'no implementation details'; canon does not say which wins.
.e2e is named as a test kind (263, 'assembly and driver in one') and as 'neither, outside the graph' (1022-1023): a molecule of two kinds.

Type-import scope is stated per slug: runtime only (inward-imports, no-concrete-import, composition-assembly-only, module-acyclic) vs included (blob-import-gate, private-sealed, service-dag, assembly-importers, driver-importers, boot-not-imported); whether a model may type-import a port is unresolved (291 vs 875).

Six declared-exception mechanisms (declared load, declared container library, declared pure library, reader exemption, effect-free call declared by a reader, mutableModuleState opt-out) are each worded in their own slug.
'No defaults, no exceptions' (381) vs defaults 'right here' for tests (1221-1223): consistent only because a test factory is an assembly function, not a composition unit; not written as a scope.
The clause 'adapters when called by a test' makes an atom depend on its importer's kind, so a test-factory assembly needs its own selection.
A runtime file cycle across two services is caught by both slugs (different whys: extraction vs ESM load); partial overlap, not a clash.

testKind: Test files carry: driver-reader-bound and kind-by-name (read by a test reader), registration-root-calls (instead of root-calls-inert), root-bindings-immutable, root-no-capture, root-statements-inert (the isolation between tests), test-not-imported, hook-unconditional and scenario-linear on every hook body, test-public-api (once the private/ conflict is ruled), no-barrel-file, module-acyclic. They do not carry: inward-imports, no-concrete-import, pure-lib-declared, composition-assembly-only (a test builds units and fires them, so it imports anything, blob included), hook-single-call (a test registers many hooks and calls many units), hook-args-asis, hook-result-inert, hook-bare-body (a test builds inputs and reads results to assert), closed-definitions (nothing imports a test, so no importer needs to be protected, but the venue must not be open, see helpers). Nothing imports a test file, so every importer-side atom (private-sealed, blob-import-gate) applies to the imports it makes, never to what it exports; e2e is a different kind (outside the graph), not a test file.
helpers:
OPEN QUESTION (local helpers such as run()). The loop/branch constraint should reach the helpers, by role and not by place: the atom is hook-unconditional/scenario-linear, applied to every function reachable from a hook body through local calls. Do not ban helpers; replace test 'defines anything' (1019) with 'defines only hooks, assembly functions, model functions', each carrying its own kind's atoms, extending canon's own 'shared test code is placed by what it is' (1017-1019) to local code: a helper that builds units is an assembly function (assembly-calls-factories, built-untouched, wiring-branch-shape: it may branch on a parameter with factory arms, it may not call a use case); a pure data builder is a model function (ambient-free, no tech, no unit calls: it can loop, it cannot assert or fire a unit); a function that fires a unit and returns its value is a hook-shaped function (hook-single-call, hook-unconditional, hook-result-inert apply by reading). A loop that fires units or asserts then has no legal home: it is neither assembly, model nor hook, so it is residue and red. A shared matcher registered on the runner is already a driver per canon (1017-1019) with hook atoms. This closes the venue without a 'no': the no-loop rule never reaches a place a loop could legally live. Note that a helper like a run() that starts the shipped CLI is an e2e concern (outside the graph).

CANON FINDINGS beyond atoms. (1) Prose-only atoms with no slug: tech-listening-driver (535-543), driver-exports-wiring (633-635), kind-by-name (567-572), adapter-implements-port, deps-explicit, scenario-linear; they are written but nothing enforces them. (2) Contradictions: .e2e as test kind (263) vs 'neither' (1022-1023); test 'imports anything' vs private-sealed and test-through-contract; driver-calls-services 'its own tech' vs hook-one-call 'nothing else'; hook exemptions for tests name only count and services-only while hook-result-inert contradicts assertion; 'adapter holds nothing of the hexagon's' (277-278) vs 'adapter has its own model functions' (153-155, 808-811). (3) Kind selections that read as exceptions are really different atoms swapped in: boot gets boot-calls-once instead of root-calls-inert; test gets registration-root-calls; test gets 'assembly-returns-services' only with adapters. (4) Mechanisms that are not atoms: declared exceptions (load, container library, pure library, effect-free call, mutableModuleState, reader exemption); reader claim (tech is only what a reader claims; unclaimed is red); flavor kind (name gives kind; create* tells model factory from function); type-import scope per atom. (5) Holes (judgment words): 'decides nothing but which factory', 'orchestrates, does not compute', 'meaningful port', unified-port branching, 'documented behavior', 'implementation details', 'taste' (685), 'shared instances flow down never sideways', 'a shape nobody has written down yet' in stable-root, sharing progression and distillation signals (1263-1329, 828-844), kernel litmus (1306-1312). (6) The Test kind selection above is the symptom resolved: test exempts about ten rules only because it is an assembly-and-driver in one; with atoms it carries its own selection with no 'except'.

atoms.name: no-outward-import
atoms.statement: A file imports no kind outer than its own in the order model < ports < service,adapter < assembly < driver < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be reasoned about and tested without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: Importer and target kinds from the flavor's suffix, compared to the order. LAUNCH: yes. Type-edge scope is unstated (see inward-deps).
atoms.landing: The direction of every dependency reads off the import path.

atoms.name: no-barrel-import
atoms.statement: Every import path resolves to a layer-named file, never through an index or re-export file.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or layer rules cannot be enforced by shape.
atoms.check: Resolved basename is index, or the target's kind is not derivable from its own name. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A reviewer reads the layer from the import line without opening a file.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service, assembly and boot import no node: builtin, platform/IO package, or external package not declared pure.
atoms.why: Code depending on a concrete bypasses its ports and cannot be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: Specifier is a node: builtin or an external package whose declared class is not pure (container for assembly). LAUNCH: yes, once classes are declared.
atoms.landing: Every package at an import line is declared knowledge or visibly absent; I/O lives in adapters.

atoms.name: lib-purity-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party library counts as model-safe only if config declares it pure.
atoms.why: Structure cannot prove a library side-effect-free and deterministic, so the claim must be stated.
atoms.check: Package name membership in the declared pure list. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Each dependency's purity is a visible declaration, not a guess.

atoms.name: container-declared
atoms.statement: A runtime container library may be imported by an assembly only if config declares it.
atoms.why: A container is tech and nothing in the code shape licenses it; the declaration is the licence.
atoms.check: Package name membership in the declared container list. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The one tech allowed in an assembly is named in config.

atoms.name: no-unit-import
atoms.statement: No runtime import of a public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file, except by an assembly or a test; the importer's own private/ units are not public.
atoms.why: Only the assembly knows the concrete graph; any other importer couples a unit to an implementation and defeats IoC and splitting.
atoms.check: Importer kind not assembly/test, target flavor kind service or adapter, target outside importer's private/, edge not type-only. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Wherever a factory is imported, the importer is an assembly: the graph lives in one kind of file.

atoms.name: no-blob-import
atoms.statement: No import, type-only included, of a suffixless file except by an assembly, a test or another blob.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so importing it voids the importer's guarantees.
atoms.check: Target kind blob (suffixless private files included), importer kind outside assembly/test/blob. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Debt shows on the map as blob edges, only into assembly and tests.

atoms.name: no-private-import
atoms.statement: No import, type-only included, from another service's private/ directory.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: private code belongs to the owning service alone.
atoms.check: Specifier has a private/ segment whose owning service differs from the importer's (layer directories belong to their service). LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import outside its service is an instant red flag.

atoms.name: no-assembly-import
atoms.statement: No import, type-only included, of an assembly file except by a driver, another assembly or a test.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract to depend on, so only who fires the program may reach it.
atoms.check: Target kind assembly, importer kind outside driver/assembly/test, any edge kind. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Consumers type against service APIs only; the build graph has one kind of caller.

atoms.name: no-driver-import
atoms.statement: No import, type-only included, of a driver file except by a boot or another driver.
atoms.why: Any other importer could reach a hook and chain use-case calls outside the one-call rule.
atoms.check: Target kind driver, importer kind outside boot/driver/test, any edge kind. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Drivers are leaves under the boot; the map shows one arrow in.

atoms.name: no-boot-import
atoms.statement: No file imports a boot file, type-only included.
atoms.why: Evaluating a boot starts the program, so only the runtime may evaluate it.
atoms.check: Target kind boot, any importer. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A boot is the visible top of the graph.

atoms.name: no-test-import
atoms.statement: No file imports a .spec/.test/.e2e file.
atoms.why: Inferred: a test file's registration calls run on evaluation, and only the test tech loads it.
atoms.check: Target kind test, any importer. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Tests are leaves, so test edges never carry production meaning.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-level import graph, every edge kind included, is acyclic.
atoms.why: In a cycle neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: Collapse files to owning service, find strongly connected components. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The map is a DAG; extraction order is readable.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: The runtime import graph between modules is acyclic; type-only edges are not counted.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently in minified production.
atoms.check: Module graph on runtime edges, cycle detection. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Load order is a plain tree walk.

atoms.name: port-import-type
atoms.statement: Every import of a port file is an `import type`.
atoms.why: A runtime edge to a port can only be a runtime re-export, a side-effect import or a forgotten `type`.
atoms.check: Import declaration kind where target kind is port. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A port is visibly a contract at every use site.

atoms.name: types-only-file
atoms.statement: A port file holds only type declarations, type imports and type exports.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it is an adapter not yet extracted.
atoms.check: No top-level runtime statement, value binding, value export or non-type import. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Opening a .port.ts file shows shape and nothing else.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file references at least one port type and its factory's result is assignable to it.
atoms.why: An adapter's one job is to implement a port; one implementing none is an unplaced unit.
atoms.check: Type import of a port in the file plus tsc assignability of the factory return. LAUNCH: yes with the TS engine, partial without.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the contract it fulfils.

atoms.name: no-adapter-branch
atoms.statement: Service code does not branch on which adapter it received.
atoms.why: If the inside knows the adapter, the port has not finished abstracting the outside.
atoms.check: Only a shadow is mechanical: instanceof or tag comparisons on a port-typed value (instanceof needs an import no-unit-import already bans). LAUNCH: partial.
atoms.landing: A service reads the same whichever adapter is behind it.

atoms.name: no-model-import
atoms.statement: A driver does not import model, or a pure library, at runtime; type-only is free.
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases; logic in a driver sits with no contract and no test.
atoms.check: Runtime edge to a model file or a declared pure library from a driver. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's imports are assemblies, drivers and tech: nothing to compute with.

atoms.name: no-dependency-default
atoms.statement: A service or adapter factory's dependency parameters carry no default value.
atoms.why: Defaults scatter assembly logic across service modules and create static imports to adapters.
atoms.check: Parameter with an initializer in an exported factory of a service/adapter file. LAUNCH: yes; 'dependency' vs plain argument needs the type, so partial.
atoms.landing: Every dependency is visibly required and only assembly resolves it.

atoms.name: no-ambient-global
atoms.statement: Code reads no ambient environment (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) from a global, at module root or inside functions.
atoms.why: Code reaching the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: Identifier or member resolves to a global in the flavor's ambient list, in any position. LAUNCH: yes; list completeness is config.
atoms.landing: What a unit depends on is its signature.

atoms.name: no-root-mutable-binding
atoms.statement: A module-root binding, exported or not, must be provably immutable by syntax or type.
atoms.why: A module tests import must be the same module every time; mutable root state leaks between tests.
atoms.check: Binding kind and type/initializer matched against the proof list (primitive, as const, readonly, frozen literal) to each proof's depth. LAUNCH: yes; config mutableModuleState lifts only this atom.
atoms.landing: State is only ever found inside a factory closure.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-capture
atoms.statement: A module-root binding stores no value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness).
atoms.why: Stored at load, the value freezes one machine state, so the file cannot be tested under another without reloading.
atoms.check: Initializer data flow reaches a machine read; import.meta.url and __dirname presumed fixed. LAUNCH: yes, sharing the machine-read classifier with no-ambient-global.
atoms.landing: Root constants are constants.

atoms.name: no-root-effect-call
atoms.statement: A call at module root must not reach tech or anything no reading claims, run a use case, or enter a local function of an adapter or blob, unless the reading declares the call effect-free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: Callee resolution at root against reader declarations; await is the call. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing observable.

atoms.name: no-root-effect-statement
atoms.statement: A module-root statement other than import, export or declaration that does something when evaluated (assignment, delete and the like) is red; throw is not.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import.
atoms.check: Root statement kinds against a list. LAUNCH: yes for the listed kinds; 'and their like' is judgment.
atoms.landing: Root is declarations only.

atoms.name: no-stray-definition
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind names (driver: its hooks and at most one wiring function; assembly: assembly functions; boot: nothing), at any depth, variables and classes included; types do not count.
atoms.why: A closed definition list leaves logic no place to hide in the outside kinds.
atoms.check: Function, class, variable declarations at any depth outside the kind's allowed set; the reading cuts hooks. LAUNCH: yes. Parametrised by kind.
atoms.landing: A driver or assembly file is a short list of named entry points.

atoms.name: args-whitelist
atoms.statement: Every call argument in an assembly or driver is a literal, a tech value, or an instance built or received; a tech value may be read by field in assembly and wiring.
atoms.why: An argument computed in the outside is the outside deciding or translating.
atoms.check: Argument expression form: literal, parameter or event reference, binding of a factory result; no call, operator or template. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Arguments at the outside's calls are plain handed-on values.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a composition-unit factory, another assembly's, a blob factory, a model factory, or an awaited use case the project declares as a load.
atoms.why: An assembly's one thing is to build; any other call is a decision or a pipeline hiding in the wiring.
atoms.check: Callee resolved to file kind; model callee must match the flavor's factory name; awaited use cases must be in the declared list; a call on an instance or tech value is not a factory. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The map draws an assembly as construction arrows only.

atoms.name: result-not-read
atoms.statement: A call result is only passed on, returned or dropped, never read, member-accessed, computed with, branched on, written or logged: in assembly for every call (a declared load's result is a tech value instead), in a hook for its use-case call.
atoms.why: Touching what was built, or what a use case returned, is decision or translation owned by a service.
atoms.check: Data flow of the result and its aliases to sinks. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Nothing in the outside inspects what flows through it.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on anything else is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: Condition operands and arm statements. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Conditionals in an assembly read as feature switches.

atoms.name: no-adapter-return
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, no adapter instance, unless every caller is a test.
atoms.why: Adapter instances reaching a driver are effects no contract covers.
atoms.check: Callee kinds of returned values; importers of such an assembly must all be tests. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Production drivers only ever receive services.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-only
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, every call in a driver is an assembly call, a sub-driver wiring call or a call on claimed tech.
atoms.why: The driver's one thing is to connect; any other call is logic outside every contract.
atoms.check: Callee resolution through the bound reader's claims. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's body outside hooks reads as setup.

atoms.name: one-call-per-hook
atoms.statement: Each hook contains exactly one call, a use-case call on an instance the assembly returned; zero or two is red.
atoms.why: Two calls make a sequence nobody owns; zero is logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count calls in the hook body (await is the call), resolve callee to a service instance; hooks cut by the reading. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow.

atoms.name: straight-line-body
atoms.statement: A hook body, and a test body, contains no conditional, loop or try/catch.
atoms.why: The behavior must read top to bottom with no decision hidden between event and call, or between steps of a scenario.
atoms.check: Control-flow nodes in the function body. LAUNCH: yes for statements; iteration by callbacks only for a listed method set. Stated for hooks, implied for tests.
atoms.landing: A body is a sequence the reader follows without simulating.

atoms.name: hook-reads-nothing
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event on as received (host values whole), with instances and literals; nothing is read off, defaulted or transformed.
atoms.why: Translating the event is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: Call arguments are bare hook parameters, host identifiers, instances, literals: no member access, destructuring, ??, call. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The hook shows no knowledge of the event's shape.

atoms.name: claimed-tech-only
atoms.statement: In a driver, every external import and ambient name is claimed by a reader bound to it; the rest is unclaimed and red.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged against a tech the reading does not name.
atoms.check: Package and global names against bound readers' claims; a pure library is model and never claimable. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's tech is an explicit, finite list.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and every test file is read by a reader bound to it by glob.
atoms.why: Every driver rule is judged through the reading: what is tech, what is a hook.
atoms.check: File glob matched against bound readers; reader kind agrees with the flavor. LAUNCH: yes (config).
atoms.landing: No driver is silently unjudged; a blob-counting reader is a visible declaration.

atoms.name: export-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver exports its wiring function and nothing else; no hook is exported.
atoms.why: Importers of a driver can then only attach callbacks, never call a hook or chain a call.
atoms.check: Export list of driver files. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot's only import is exactly one driver.
atoms.why: The boot starts the program: one thing, one driver.
atoms.check: Import list length and target kind. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A boot is one import.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot's module root holds exactly one call, to the imported driver's wiring function, with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot starts and does nothing else; arguments would make the boot hold tech.
atoms.check: Root statements equal one zero-argument call to the imported binding. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A boot is one call.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is contradicted by service-assembly-only and adapter-assembly-only (service to service, adapter to adapter banned). Type-edge scope is unstated: the matrix says runtime imports, yet a model factory taking a port belongs in service (299-302), which needs type edges counted. Every cell of the order except model to ports is also covered by a target-side atom.
'Visible' is a reader's perception; only the absence of index indirection is mechanical.

A theorem of the per-edge atoms, not an atom: if every file honours its edges, chains are pure. 'Least-pure import' needs a purity order of kinds that canon never defines. 'False guarantees' is rationale.
'Concrete' is defined by examples (node:fs, HTTP, DB); 'deterministic' and 'side-effect-free' are judgments made mechanical only by the declaration.

The ambient list is given by example (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis), completeness is config. 'Adapters and drivers reach the environment' is a non-carriage; a driver's reach is governed by claimed-tech-only. Assembly and boot carriage is implied (253-255, 487-491, 713-714).
Rationales for letting assembly (bounded verbs) and test (characterization) in are not checks. 'A driver may not: a blob call there is already a violation' restates driver rules.
'Composition unit - must be composed by assembly' (247, 252) read as existence (a unit some assembly imports) is a rule nowhere.
Twin of service-assembly-only: the same atom with the other target kind.
Not a constraint: a scope modifier (type-only edges exempt) on no-unit-import. Its second sentence needs the checker to treat SomeService["method"] in type position as type-only.
Not a constraint: a scope modifier (private/ units are not public units) on no-unit-import. Internal composition inside a factory (159-167) has no rule at all.
'No logic' adds nothing beyond no runtime statement.
'Which adapter it got' is semantic; only tag and instanceof shadows are mechanical. 'Same result shape' is a type-assignability check, covered by adapter-implements-port.
The direction law (817-826) is derived from this atom plus no-unit-import.
'Input via public API' is only the no-private-import shadow; 'documented behavior' and 'no implementation details' are judgments. It collides with the matrix row 'Test imports anything'.

'Assembly and driver in one' carries none of those kinds' closed lists (it defines anything, imports anything, hook count and services-only off): a union of two bundles with every part exempted. Placement of shared test code by what it is is judgment. 'Fixtures follow same isolation rules' has no check for fakes defined in a spec file. '.e2e' is listed in the kind yet declared 'neither assembly nor driver'.

Model factory vs function is told by the flavor's name (create*), a naming convention. 'Shared instances flow down, never sideways' (497-500) is unchecked. 'Pipeline hiding in the wiring' is rationale. Loads are a config declaration. 'Nothing at root but imports' is derived from no-stray-definition and the root atoms.

Reader content (claims, cut, exemptions) is config, not code structure. A reader that counts a driver as blob on purpose is a declared escape hatch from every driver atom. Binding versus flavor mismatch is a config error.
'Tech setup' is whatever the reader claims; nothing bounds what a setup call does. 'A hook does not wire' is the one-call-per-hook count.

'A facade service is missing', 'logic with no home' are rationale. Hook cut belongs to the reader; techs without callback hooks have no cut (559-565). 'The test tech exempts the count' is an exception inside the rule.
The list of allowed callees is stated three times (here, wiring-outside-hooks, hook-one-call). 'Never an adapter' repeats no-unit-import.
Wiring function signature (root takes nothing and reads its tech, sub takes tech and instances) is stated but unchecked beyond count.

Never inside a hook and never a use-case result handed on are derived from one-call-per-hook and args-whitelist. 'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a tech exemption with no mechanism (web drivers open).
'One per entry point' is existence. 'Imports nothing else, tech included' restates the import bans as a positive allowlist.

'A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' and 'and their like' are open judgment. Presumptions (import.meta.url fixed, property read free, unresolvable named types prove nothing) are readings. Exemptions are a closed list (boot call, spec registration), while 1114-1115 lets a reading declare calls effect-free: two mechanisms for one exemption. Whether blob carries it is unstated.
No slug; 'No exceptions' yet tests are exempt (1221-1223).
'.service.ts declares a composition boundary' has no check besides no-unit-import; '.model.ts declares purity' means model's atoms.
For adapters, 'calls into tech' vs 'listens' (handing a callback) is not mechanical; adapters carry no atom here.
'Abstractness' and 'factories with closure state are model when they depend on nothing' are judgment beyond import edges.
'Orchestrates, does not compute', 'use cases nameable', 'returned API is the contract' have no check. 'Adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' (277-279) is judgment.
'Visible in the test, not reconstructed from helpers' and 'data-driven indirection' are judgment; carriage of straight-line-body is implied here.
'Production config has no place in tests' has no way to name production config. 'Deterministic' implies no-ambient-global for specs, unstated.

kinds.note: Universal atoms, judged on every file (blob and test included). no-private-import lets a file reach its own service's private/.
Plus all-kinds. No exception needed.
Plus all-kinds. Root atoms are vacuous under types-only-file.
Plus all-kinds. no-adapter-branch is only partly mechanical.
Plus all-kinds. Carries neither no-concrete-import nor no-ambient-global: reaching the tech is its job. no-dependency-default is implied (164-167).
Plus all-kinds. Does not carry no-blob-import, no-unit-import, no-assembly-import. no-ambient-global carriage is implied.
Plus all-kinds. Does not carry no-ambient-global: claimed-tech-only governs its names and imports.
Plus all-kinds. Does not carry no-root-effect-call: boot-calls-once is the positive form of the one call that rule would forbid. The import bans are implied by the one-driver allowlist.
Plus all-kinds. Stated at 965-967 although blob claims no guarantee; whether stable-root reaches blob is unstated.

Plus all-kinds. no-root-effect-call needs the test reader to declare registration calls effect-free. straight-line-body is implied. no-root-machine-capture and no-ambient-global are implied by determinism (1193-1194), flagged for a ruling, .spec/.test only.
Proposed split: canon lists .e2e as test yet calls it 'neither assembly nor driver, outside the graph' (1022-1023). It carries all-kinds and nothing else until ruled.

sharedParts.problem: Twin rules state one atom per target kind, two scope modifiers state its exemptions, and driver-calls-services ('never an adapter') and the IoC prose (defaults create static imports) restate the same ban at call level. Fix: one atom, the modifiers as its parameters.

Stated as a quarantine, as a chain property and as 'a blob call in a driver is a violation'; its type-edge scope (included) differs from no-unit-import (excluded) with no reason given beyond per-rule rationale.
Whether type-only edges count is restated per rule with a different reason each time and never for inward-deps. Fix: every edge atom declares its own edge scope once.

The matrix is the intersection of the order and the target-side atoms, so almost every cell is covered twice. Fix: the order keeps only cells no target-side atom covers (model to ports, type edges) and target-side atoms keep only lateral cells.
The allowed callee list of a driver is stated in three rules and a fourth restates its sub-driver part.
Arguments are literals, tech values or instances in four places; hooks add 'nothing read off', which is the separate hook-reads-nothing.
The same data-flow check on a call result appears in two rules with different allowed sinks, plus an assembly branch-on-instance clause that overlaps wiring-branch-only.
One atom with a per-kind allowed set, stated three times, and negated for test ('defines anything'), which is the laundering venue for helpers.

Root stability is restated for model, service, assembly ('nothing but imports'), boot (one call) and test (registration), and exempted by a closed kind list although 1114-1115 already lets a reading declare calls effect-free: two exemption mechanisms.

'Reads from the machine' is judged in ambient-access (anywhere, inside kinds), stable-root (at root, all kinds), boot ('touches no tech'), assembly ('holds no tech') and drivers (claimed tech), so one root read in a model is red twice.
Stated as 'unconditional' for hooks, implied for tests, and assembly allows branches under wiring-branch-only; the test side is never stated.
test-through-contract wants public API only and private-sealed says nothing outside may import private/, while test-is-outside and the matrix say a test imports anything.
Only drivers and assemblies may import assembly, yet shared test factories are assembly functions imported by spec files; the test is implicitly both kinds.
Stated for drivers and tests together, and the test reader's exemption of the hook count is an in-rule exception.
Assembly returns no adapter, a driver calls no adapter, and a test factory returns them anyway; one caller-side condition stated three ways.

testKind: Carry (besides all-kinds): reader-bound, no-root-mutable-binding, no-root-effect-call (registration declared effect-free by the test reader, one mechanism instead of an exemption list), no-root-effect-statement, straight-line-body (implied), no-private-import (a spec may reach its own service's private/). Candidates needing a ruling: no-root-machine-capture and no-ambient-global for .spec/.test, since 1193-1194 says isolation and determinism matter (not .e2e, which touches the machine by design). Not carried: every import ban except no-private-import/no-test-import/no-boot-import, no-outward-import, no-concrete-import, no-stray-definition, args-whitelist, assembly-calls-build, result-not-read, wiring-branch-only, no-adapter-return, wiring-calls-only, one-call-per-hook, hook-reads-nothing, claimed-tech-only, no-model-import, export-wiring-only, no-dependency-default, no-adapter-branch, boot atoms. Why: a test builds with fakes, blob and concrete, calls anything and asserts by reading results, so those atoms would forbid its job. Atoms whose why protects importers (no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle, export-wiring-only, stable-root's same-module-for-every-test argument) are vacuous because nothing imports a test; only isolation between bodies survives (no-root-mutable-binding). 'Assembly and driver in one' decomposes to zero closed-list atoms; a test's own duties are registration at root, no shared root state, and straight bodies. Shared test code already leaves by what it is (fake to adapter, factory to assembly, builder to model, matcher to driver). Also split .e2e out: canon calls it outside the graph.
helpers: Inferred, not verified. The constraint must reach local helpers, otherwise 'defines anything' is the laundering venue. Structure: (1) the atom's subject is every function body defined in the spec file (helpers, lambdas, local fakes), not only registered test bodies, so straight-line-body applies by file kind and not by being called from a body, and a run() helper is judged like a test body. (2) A helper needing a branch or loop is a unit, not test code: it leaves the file for the kind it is (model data builder, adapter fake, assembly test factory, driver wiring) and carries that kind's atoms there, where a loop is placed, named, importable and tested instead of hidden. Branching in a test factory stays limited by wiring-branch-only. (3) Replace 'defines anything' in test-is-outside with 'defines test bodies and straight-line helpers', so the closed list lives in one place. Confessed residue: iteration by callback (.map, .forEach, reduce) and recursion are mechanical only for a listed method set; test.each-style rows need a ruling on whether registration with data is a call (green) or a root loop (red); and a model data builder may loop, which is placed rather than hidden but still unread by a spec reviewer, so the reviewer-legibility judgment (1155-1159) stays unchecked.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file's runtime imports go only to files of its own layer or an inner one in the order model < ports < service, adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: An inner layer keeps its guarantees only if it cannot know anything outer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — importer kind vs target kind from the import graph, kinds from suffix flavor or reader binding.
atoms.landing: The layer is readable from the import path alone, and the map arrows all point one way.

atoms.name: layer-visible-path
atoms.statement: Every import path names the file that declares the layer, with no index or barrel in between.
atoms.why: The layer rules can only be enforced, by tool or reviewer, if the layer shows at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — no file named index.*, no re-export-from statement that hides the source file's layer.
atoms.landing: A reviewer sees a violation in the import line with no file to open.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file of the inside, assembly or boot imports no platform or IO code (node:fs, HTTP client, database driver).
atoms.why: Concrete code bypasses the ports and makes the file untestable without the world.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — import specifier vs a concrete list; pure packages must be declared (pure-lib-declared), the rest counts concrete.
atoms.landing: What can run in isolation is legible by its imports.

atoms.name: pure-lib-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as model only when the config declares it pure and deterministic; anything else counts as concrete.
atoms.why: Purity cannot be inferred from a package name, and an assumed one gives false guarantees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for the declaration lookup, no for the package's transitive truth (node_modules chain is not read).
atoms.landing: A pure dependency is a visible, reviewed decision in config.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: The code reads or calls no ambient global (environment, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis), at module root or in a function, in a condition, value or call.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — free identifiers and member chains resolving to a global-name list; the list is open-ended (a gap).
atoms.landing: Everything the code depends on shows in its arguments.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import a blob file, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: Blob has no guarantees, so any other importer is contaminated by it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — target kind blob (no layer suffix) vs importer kind.
atoms.landing: Unplaced code is visible and its only entrances are the assembly and the characterization tests.

atoms.name: composition-unit-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service or .adapter file is imported at runtime only by assembly; type-only imports and files under private/ are outside the subject.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place where dependencies are resolved, so no layer may reach a concrete unit by itself.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — target kind in {service, adapter}, public path, non-type import, importer kind assembly.
atoms.landing: The chunk graph is the assembly graph; a service's collaborators are always injected.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so nothing can depend on its shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — importer kind vs target kind assembly, every import form.
atoms.landing: Consumers type against service APIs and the wiring stays a one-way pipe.

atoms.name: driver-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: A driver is started by the runtime; letting others import it lets hooks chain through it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — importer kind vs target kind driver.
atoms.landing: The entry graph reads boot → drivers and nothing else touches a driver.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: No file imports a boot or a test file.
atoms.why: Their evaluation acts (starts the program, registers tests), so importing one would run it where nobody expects.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — import edges whose target kind is boot or test.
atoms.landing: Entries are leaves; a test never leaks into the program.

atoms.name: private-owner-only
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports a file under that service's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, not implementation coupling.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — import path contains private/ and the importer sits outside the owning service directory.
atoms.landing: A private import reads as an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: service-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of imports between service packages, every import kind counted, has no cycle.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — contract the file graph onto service directories, find cycles; needs the service-boundary definition.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG, so each service has an extraction order.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of runtime imports between files, even within one service, has no cycle.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports fail silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — runtime-edge file graph, cycle detection.
atoms.landing: Load order is well defined.

atoms.name: port-file-types-only
atoms.statement: A .port file contains only type declarations and type imports, no runtime statement or export.
atoms.why: A port is a contract, and runtime code there means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — statement kinds in the file.
atoms.landing: A port is readable as pure shape.

atoms.name: port-import-type-keyword
atoms.statement: Every import of a port file, from any file, is an import type.
atoms.why: A port has no runtime presence, so a runtime edge to it is a side-effect import, a re-export or a missing keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — import declaration form for targets of kind port.
atoms.landing: The type keyword at the import marks the contract edge.

atoms.name: driver-imports-closed
atoms.statement: A driver's runtime imports of repo files go only to assemblies and other drivers; never composition units, model, blob or boot.
atoms.why: A driver connects events to use cases and holds nothing of the hexagon.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — import graph; the matrix row says imports, line 883 says the ban is on calls, so the form is ambiguous.
atoms.landing: The outside is reasoned about without opening its code.

atoms.name: driver-tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every external package and global name a driver uses is claimed by a reader bound to it; an unclaimed name or a pure library is red.
atoms.why: The driver rules are judged through the reading, and what no reading claims cannot be judged.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — package and name lookup in the bound reader's claims.
atoms.landing: The tech a driver holds is declared, in one place per technology.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one file, a driver, and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: A boot's one thing is to start its one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — import list of a boot-kind file.
atoms.landing: The entry is a single arrow to a single driver.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind allows: assembly only assembly functions, driver only hooks and at most one wiring function, boot nothing.
atoms.why: A definition is where logic hides, so the outside kinds keep a closed verb list.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — top-level and nested declarations of function, class or variable vs the kind's allowed set; a type is not a definition.
atoms.landing: Anything a reader finds in these files is the layer's one thing.

atoms.name: driver-one-entry
atoms.statement: A driver exposes one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Importers of a driver can then only attach its callbacks, never call a hook or chain calls.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — exported symbols of a driver vs the reader's hook cut.
atoms.landing: The driver tree is a registration tree.

atoms.name: build-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory call: a service, adapter or assembly factory, a blob file's, or a model factory; no model function, no use case.
atoms.why: An assembly has one right, build; any other call is logic hidden in the wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — callee file kind plus the flavor's create* name for model; blob callee taken as a build by construction.
atoms.landing: The map draws the assembly as pure construction.

atoms.name: loads-declared
atoms.statement: The only use case an assembly may call or await is one the project declares as a load; its result counts as a tech value.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, so the graph depends on one only by declaration.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — callee against the declared list in config.
atoms.landing: The few places where a graph depends on data are named in config.

atoms.name: build-result-untouched
atoms.statement: What an assembly built is only passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed (await changes nothing).
atoms.why: Touching a built instance is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — value flow from factory calls; the loaded result is the declared aside.
atoms.landing: Assembly output is plumbing, not behavior.

atoms.name: args-closed
atoms.statement: A call's arguments in an assembly or a wiring position are literals, tech values received as parameters, or instances built or received there; nothing computed.
atoms.why: Deriving an argument is the assembly or driver opening the door itself; the unit that needs the value derives it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — argument expression shape and value origin.
atoms.landing: Arguments carry no hidden logic.

atoms.name: wiring-condition-shape
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are only factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or a computed value is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — condition operand origin, comparison form, arm contents.
atoms.landing: Conditional graphs are visible variants, never behavior.

atoms.name: returns-no-adapter
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and an adapter only to a test caller.
atoms.why: An adapter handed to a consumer is a call no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — returned value kinds; the test-caller clause needs importer kinds.
atoms.landing: From outside, assembly shows only services.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-closed
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver calls only assembly factories, its claimed tech's setup, and sub-driver wiring functions.
atoms.why: The wiring region of a driver is where it builds its tech; calls to anything else are logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — callee classification per region, hooks cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: A driver's top level reads as setup.

atoms.name: hook-calls-use-case
atoms.statement: The call a hook makes is a use case on an instance assembly handed over; never an adapter, a model, or the tech.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers, and parsing or rendering belong to a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — callee resolved to a service's API through the assembly's returned value.
atoms.landing: One arrow from each event to a use case.

atoms.name: hook-one-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one call; zero or two is red.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence nobody owns, and zero leaves logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — call count in the hook body, reader-cut hooks; await counts as the call.
atoms.landing: The hook is one edge on the map.

atoms.name: hook-straight-line
atoms.statement: A hook body contains no branch, loop or try; whatever it does is unconditional.
atoms.why: A decision inside a hook is invisible to the map and to the reviewer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — control-flow statements in the hook body (iteration methods taking callbacks need a decision).
atoms.landing: A hook shows its whole behavior by its shape; for tests it is the given-when-expect order.

atoms.name: event-handed-whole
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals, with nothing read off them.
atoms.why: Reading or defaulting at the hook is translation, and translation is a service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — argument expressions, no member access or call on tech values.
atoms.landing: The hook's input contract is the tech's event, untouched.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: A hook returns its call's value or drops it; never read, written, handed on or logged.
atoms.why: Using the result at the hook is translation the facade should own.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — use of the call's value in the hook.
atoms.landing: Rendering and exit codes live in a service behind a port.

atoms.name: driver-import-wiring-use
atoms.statement: A driver import by a boot or another driver is used only to call its wiring function, at the right place, with no hook or hexagon data.
atoms.why: The importer may only let the sub-driver attach its callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — every reference to the import binding.
atoms.landing: Drivers compose by registration only.

atoms.name: boot-root-call
atoms.statement: A boot's module root is exactly one call, to its driver's wiring function, with no arguments.
atoms.why: The one module whose evaluation acts must do one thing, start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — root statements of a boot-kind file.
atoms.landing: The entry is one line.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver-kind and test-kind file has a reader bound to it; one that counts it as blob on purpose is the way out.
atoms.why: The hook cut and the tech claims come from the reader, so no driver rule is judgeable without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — config binding by glob against kind.
atoms.landing: A driver is red until its tech has a stated reading.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: A module-root binding is provably immutable by its syntax or type, exported or not; no let, no unfrozen collection, no instance exported.
atoms.why: A test that imports the module must get the module every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — proof by primitive, as const, readonly, Object.freeze to its depth; unresolved named types prove nothing.
atoms.landing: State lives in factory closures, reached by argument.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: A root binding's value is read from no machine source (tech, clock, randomness, environment); a property read is free, a call is not.
atoms.why: The file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes — initializer reaches tech or global names; import.meta.url and __dirname excepted.
atoms.landing: Load-time snapshots of the machine do not exist.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: A module root runs no side effect: no call that reaches tech or unclaimed names, runs a use case, or goes into an effectful-layer local function; no assignment or delete; a throw is free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — root statements and callees classified; calls declared effect-free by a reading are skipped.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing.

atoms.name: no-dependency-defaults
atoms.statement: A service's or adapter's factory gives no default value to a dependency parameter.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import to an adapter or config source and scatters assembly into services.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — initializers on factory parameters; which parameters are dependencies is not marked.
atoms.landing: The assembly is the only place a dependency is resolved.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file's exported factory returns something assignable to a port type it type-imports.
atoms.why: All adapters of a port must be replaceable behind one interface.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial — assignability by tsc, port identity by import.
atoms.landing: Which port an adapter serves is readable.

rules.remainder: Placeholder removed; see inward-deps.
"Lateral (same layer) OK" is not an atom and contradicts composition-unit-gate (service to service, adapter to adapter); "see dependency matrix" defers to other rules.
Whether a re-export inside a layer file counts as a barrel is undefined.
