The repo-file chain is already covered by inward-imports plus no-concrete-import; the transitive third-party chain cannot be seen by a source checker; "partial extraction produces false guarantees" is a wish.
"Concrete" needs a list or a declaration; "deterministic" is judgment, replaced by declaration.
The ambient name list is open; "handed through a port" is a design remark; adapters and drivers are exempt by kind.
Rationale for why assembly and tests may take blob; the driver ban is restated and already forbidden by driver-imports-closed.
None; the "not by blob, drivers…" list is entailed by the gate.
None; the same atom as service-assembly-only with a different target.
Mostly a scope clause (type imports exempt from composition-unit-gate), not a constraint; also covers the Service["method"] shorthand.
A scope clause of composition-unit-gate (public position) and private-owner-only; no constraint of its own.
"Sign the adapter is not extracted" is a diagnosis, not a check.
"The service layer branches on which adapter it got" is judgment (no structure marks an adapter's identity); its structural half, services never importing adapters, is composition-unit-gate.
None.
What a service package boundary is must be defined by config or directory convention.
None.

All judgment: "documented behavior", "implementation details", "public API"; exceptions (a) and (b) are judgment; only the private-owner-only part is mechanical and it is not in the rule's own wording.

"Defines anything", "imports anything", "hook count and services-only do not apply" are exemptions, not atoms; "shared test code is not blob" is not mechanically separable from legacy blob a test characterizes; "test-purpose adapters, same isolation rules" is judgment; e2e is named in the kind list yet declared "neither".

Blob "factory" versus blob function is not distinguishable; "decides nothing but which factory" is the umbrella wish; "nothing at module root but imports" is entailed by closed-definitions and root-no-effect; container library only by declaration mirrors pure-lib-declared.
None.
A binding that names a file differently from the flavor is a config error, not a code constraint; kind assignment (blob for unbound tech) is classification.
"A hook does not wire" restates hook-one-call and hook-calls-use-case; "laziness is the assembly's" is a design remark.

"Nothing else" does not enumerate other statements (a bare unrelated assignment); "when the view model is the tech's" is the reader's judgment; the facade remedies (second call, zero, translation) are landing; the test tech exempts only the count, which leaves event-handed-whole and result-untouched bound to a test body that must read results.
Almost entirely the union of wiring-outside-hooks and hook-one-call per region; "its own tech" is what readers claim.
"Residue" is the label for the failure; a root main taking nothing is implied by boot-root-call.
"Never data from the hexagon" is args-closed; the web parent-renders-child case is stated not to be this rule (open, research in progress).
None.
"One per entry point" needs an entry designation, not checkable from structure; "holds nothing" and "touches no tech" are entailed by the other atoms.

"A shape nobody wrote down is judged by the rule" is an open list (launch-hostile); proof depth of types is a reader limit; exemptions "by kind" (boot call, spec registration) are a closed list stated as an exception; the config opt-out lifts bindings only.
The matrix is an intersection of rules, not a rule; the Test row "Anything" disagrees with private-owner-only, entry-not-imported (boot) and test-through-contract.
"All dependencies explicit" is a wish beyond the two checks; tests exempt it for the test factory.
"An adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's" and "absorbs specificity" are judgment; direction law is entailed by inward-imports, private-owner-only and service-acyclic.
"Orchestrates, does not compute", "utility bag", "nameable use cases", "returned API is the contract", port test "meaningfully" are judgment words.

kinds.note: Graph-level atoms; blob is the open case (stable-root says every module, blob-quarantine says blob claims none).
Nothing to except.
no-concrete-import is entailed by types only.
Gate carried as target of imports; unified-port stays a hole.
Carries neither no-concrete-import nor no-ambient-access, so no except: those atoms are not selected.
Blob import right is the absence of blob-import-gate on this importer.
Hook atoms apply per hook cut by the reader.
root-no-effect is not carried: its one call is the entry, which stable-root currently handles by exemption.
Plus the all-kinds atoms; see testKind. root-no-effect carries only if registration calls are declared by the test reader instead of exempted by kind.
Target of the gate; carries only the all-kinds graph atoms. Unclear in canon whether the root atoms reach it.

inRules: stable-root (1093-1105, any kind, at root only)
sharedParts.problem: One fact stated four ways with four scopes; ambient-access exempts adapters and drivers while stable-root's machine-read half does not, so adapters get an unwritten partial exemption. Split by scope: no-ambient-access for model, service, assembly, boot; root-no-machine-read for every kind.

Same argument list worded four ways; assembly may read a field off a tech value, a hook may not (opts, never opts.files). The hook-only half must be its own atom (event-handed-whole) or the shared list gets an except.
One shape with a different allowed set per kind; the test kind is handled by exempting it from the shape instead of selecting the atom out.
Two rules are one atom with different targets; runtime-import and public-unit are its scope (type imports, private/) stated as separate rules; matrix cells repeat it.
Seven who-may-import-me atoms each restate whether import type counts (runtime-import exempts, others say included): the type-only question is a parameter per gate, scattered as prose.

inRules: Tests are written for the reviewer (1152-1161, implied)
sharedParts.problem: Same check (no control flow in a hook body) with a driver why and a test why; test-is-outside exempts only the count, leaving the bundle's other parts (value never read, nothing read off the event) binding a body that must read to assert.
The allowed-callee set is stated whole in driver-calls-services and again per region in the other two, so the whole is redundant with the parts; "a hook does not wire" appears in two places.
Same "import a driver only to call its wiring function" shape stated in two kinds.
"Pure libraries are model, declared not presumed" stated four times; chain-purity adds only the transitive claim a source checker cannot verify.
Boot call and spec registration are exempted by kind (closed list), while stable-root already has a mechanism, a reading declaring a call effect-free; two ways to say a root call is fine.
"Lateral OK" contradicts rules that forbid service to service and adapter to adapter imports; the layer order has to be strict-or-equal and let the importer gates carve lateral edges.
The test-as-caller exception is stated three times and turns a returns rule into a rule about who imports the assembly.
The slug bundles callee kind, count, straight-line, argument shape and result handling: five checks, five narrow whys; a kind needing only some (test: straight-line) gets an exemption.
Test is said to import anything, yet private-sealed, "nothing imports a boot" and the default posture of the contract say it cannot or should not; e2e is in the kind list and declared "neither".

testKind: The test kind is not "assembly and driver in one". That bundle takes the union of the two kinds' import rights and drops every verb list (closed-definitions, build-*, hook-*), so the real kind is a selection of atoms. A test file should carry: reader-bound (the test reader is the only way to know which calls are registration); entry-not-imported (nothing imports a test, because evaluation registers tests); the all-kinds atoms private-owner-only, service-acyclic and module-acyclic (fixtures must be test-purpose adapters, not the real nested ones, or the service cycle closes); root-bindings-immutable and root-no-machine-read (shared mutable state between tests is the thing stable-root exists to stop; canon says so at 1017-1018); root-no-effect with registration calls declared by the test reader, not exempted by kind; hook-straight-line on each test body (implied by the reviewer text, 1152-1161); driver-import-wiring-use for shared matchers. It should not carry: closed-definitions, driver-one-entry, wiring-calls-closed, hook-one-call, hook-calls-use-case, event-handed-whole, result-untouched (a test body calls units and adapters, reads results to assert), driver-imports-closed and driver-tech-claimed (it imports anything, blob included), build-* and returns-no-adapter (it builds with fakes and holds adapters), no-ambient-access (determinism is wanted but is not mechanically stated). Nothing imports a test, so no importer-gate atom targets it and exports need no rule. Gap: canon exempts only the hook count, which keeps the rest of the hook bundle on a body that must read; selecting atoms instead of exempting fixes this. Gap: e2e files are test-named yet declared outside the graph; and "no shared test code is blob" cannot be told from legacy blob a test characterizes.
helpers: Yes: the straight-line constraint must reach into local helpers, and the right unit is the hook's reach, not its lexical body. Proposed structure: (1) hook-straight-line is evaluated over the hook body plus the body of every function defined in the same file that it calls directly, transitively (static same-file call graph); a loop or branch in run() counts as one in each test calling it, so moving a loop into a helper cannot change the verdict. Iteration methods (map, forEach, reduce) with a callback count as loops, and an inline callback is part of the body it sits in. (2) A local function never called from a hook is judged by nothing (dead); a local fake passed to the unit under test is not on the hook's call path, so it is judged like a shared fake: an adapter, free to hold logic. (3) A helper in another file is not test kind (canon says shared test code is placed by what it is) so it carries its own kind's atoms, which keeps no venue only if the placement is forced. Hole: a shared run() that calls a use case and returns its result fits none of adapter, assembly, model or driver (an assembly cannot call use cases, a driver may not export a hook); if it defaults to adapter, which allows logic and loops, that is the laundering venue. Close it by refusing the placement (shared helpers that act on units are not allowed outside the test file) or by giving them a kind carrying the hook atoms. Not stated in canon: that a test body may not loop at all; it is only implied by 1152-1161 and is the premise to ratify first.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports no file of a layer outward of its own (model < ports < service, adapters < assembly < drivers < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must be buildable, testable and reasonable without knowing the outside.
atoms.check: Import edge: rank(target kind from suffix) > rank(importer kind). LAUNCH yes. Canon is silent on whether type-only edges count.
atoms.landing: Any import line shows its direction; the map's arrows all point one way.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A model, port, service, assembly or boot file imports no platform, I/O or third-party module unless declared pure (assembly: or a declared container library).
atoms.why: Contact with the world belongs to adapters (called) and drivers (listened); reaching it by import elsewhere bypasses the port.
atoms.check: Import specifier is a node builtin or a package absent from the declared-pure list (assembly: declared container list). LAUNCH yes, resting on an act-of-faith declaration; the checker cannot see inside a package.
atoms.landing: A file's import block proves it is world-free; purity is declared, never presumed.

atoms.name: no-ambient-global
atoms.statement: A model or service never reads or calls the environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis from a global.
atoms.why: Code reaching them depends on the machine it runs on and cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: Identifier or member reference to the closed global list, at any position (root, condition, value, call). LAUNCH yes for the listed names; aliasing (`const g = globalThis`) needs binding resolution.
atoms.landing: The inside's inputs are all visible in its parameters.

atoms.name: blob-importers-only
atoms.statement: A blob (suffixless) file is imported only by assembly, test and other blob files, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any layer importing it loses the guarantees it declared.
atoms.check: Edge whose target has no layer suffix and whose importer kind is not assembly, test or blob. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Debt is quarantined: blob enters the graph in one place and its size is countable.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service or .adapter file is runtime-imported only by assembly (and test); files under the owning service's private/ are out of scope.
atoms.why: Dependencies are resolved in exactly one place, so a service never knows the concrete graph.
atoms.check: Runtime edge to a non-private .service/.adapter file from a kind other than assembly or test. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A service import in an adapter or another service is visible from the path alone.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service package imports a file under its private/ directory, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is hidden stays free to change.
atoms.check: Path contains /private/ and importer is outside the owning service directory. LAUNCH yes once 'service package' is defined (see remainder).
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in a foreign import is an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: no-barrel-index
atoms.statement: Imports name the file that declares the layer; no index file re-exports a service's surface.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the per-layer rules cannot be enforced.
atoms.check: No index.* with re-exports; the specifier resolves to a layer-suffixed or bare-layer file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The layer is in the import path, so no file needs opening to know what is imported.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A port file holds only types: no runtime statement or declaration.
atoms.why: A port is a shape; runtime code in it means the adapter is not extracted yet.
atoms.check: Every top-level node of a .port file is a type, interface or type-only import/export. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Port files read as pure contract, nothing to run.

atoms.name: port-edge-type-only
atoms.statement: No runtime import edge starts at or ends in a port file.
atoms.why: A port has no runtime presence, so a runtime edge is a hidden re-export, a side-effect import or a missing `type` keyword.
atoms.check: Import edge touching a .port file without `import type`. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: `import type` on every port import shows contract-versus-code at a glance.

atoms.name: acyclic-services
atoms.statement: The edges between service packages, of every import kind, form a DAG.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: Package graph built from file edges, cycle search. LAUNCH partial: needs a mechanical definition of service package and of nested/layer directories.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a human can order.

atoms.name: acyclic-modules
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between files form no cycle, even within one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as 'undefined' in production bundles.
atoms.check: File graph over runtime edges only, cycle search. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: File order is linear; no undefined-at-load surprises.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers (including reader-bound components) and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own to depend on; its shape is the services it returns.
atoms.check: Edge whose target is an assembly and importer kind not in {driver, assembly, test}. LAUNCH yes; the web recognition rule is the same check with 'component bound by a driver reader' as driver.
atoms.landing: Who builds the hexagon is answered by the importers list.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: A driver is imported only by a boot or another driver, a boot by nothing, a test file by nothing, type imports included.
atoms.why: The runtime enters these files (node runs the boot, the runner runs the spec, the framework mounts the component); program code importing one reaches tech-coupled code.
atoms.check: Edge whose target is a driver, boot or test file, importer kind outside the allowed set. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The entry chain boot -> driver -> assembly is the only way in; the map shows it.

atoms.name: driver-has-reader
atoms.statement: Every driver file and every test file is read by a reader bound to its tech.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading (hook cut, claimed tech, exemptions).
atoms.check: Config binding lookup per file; a binding that counts the file as blob is the declared way out. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Red 'unread driver' states plainly that the file is not judged and how to fix it.

atoms.name: binding-agrees-flavor
atoms.statement: A reader binding names a file's kind only when the flavor leaves the file blob or agrees with the flavor.
atoms.why: One file must have one kind, not two sources of truth.
atoms.check: Config cross-check of reader globs against flavor names. LAUNCH yes (config-level, not code).
atoms.landing: A file's kind is never ambiguous.

atoms.name: claimed-tech-only
atoms.statement: Within a driver, an imported package or reached global counts as tech only if a bound reader claims it; unclaimed or pure-library imports are red.
atoms.why: Tech is by definition what a reading claims; an unclaimed name cannot be judged.
atoms.check: Resolve each non-service/assembly/driver import and global against the readers' claim lists. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The driver's tech surface is an explicit list.

atoms.name: driver-only-listens
atoms.statement: A callback handed to a claimed tech to be invoked on its events appears only in a driver or test file.
atoms.why: The driver is the one place the program receives the tech's events.
atoms.check: Callback passed to a claimed tech call outside driver/test kinds. LAUNCH partial: separating listening from an adapter's outbound call with a callback relies on the reader's hook cut.
atoms.landing: Event entry points can be found by kind alone.

atoms.name: build-calls-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a build: a factory of a composition unit, of another assembly, of a blob file, or of a model factory.
atoms.why: Assembly's one thing is to build; any other call is logic hiding where everything is importable.
atoms.check: Callee resolved to file kind; model factory told from model function by the flavor's name (create*); tech values may be read but not called. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as a list of constructions; the graph is its only content.

atoms.name: result-unread
atoms.statement: The result of a call in an assembly is only passed on or returned, never member-accessed, computed with, branched on or called.
atoms.why: The layer never looks into or touches what it built.
atoms.check: Dataflow from call result to any read position. LAUNCH yes (binding-level flow). A declared load's result is a tech value and exempt.
atoms.landing: Instances move through assembly as opaque boxes.

atoms.name: no-use-case-call
atoms.statement: An assembly calls no use case except a load the project declares by name.
atoms.why: A use case whose result feeds a factory is a pipeline hiding in the wiring.
atoms.check: Member call on a built instance not in the declared-load list. LAUNCH yes, with the declaration as the resolution of a violation.
atoms.landing: The few graph-shaping loads are named in config, so decisions in assembly are countable.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance's output is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: AST of condition and arms. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The only decisions in assembly are visible graph variants.

atoms.name: return-closed
atoms.statement: An assembly returns service instances and shared model instances; an assembly function that returns an adapter is imported only by test files.
atoms.why: The assembly's product is the hexagon; adapters returned to program code expose concrete tech.
atoms.check: Return expression classified by callee file kind; if adapter, check importers. LAUNCH yes. Stated as 'unless a test is the caller': an exception, here recast as a caller gate.
atoms.landing: What an assembly hands out is knowable from its return type.

atoms.name: arg-closed-set
atoms.statement: The arguments of a call in an assembly, in a driver's wiring or in a hook are literals, tech values, or instances.
atoms.why: What flows into wiring must be nothing computed, so that no logic hides in an argument.
atoms.check: Each argument node is a literal, an identifier bound to a parameter or built instance, or a field/destructured part of a tech value (hooks: see hook-no-read). LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Arguments are legible without evaluation.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-closed
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver calls only assembly factories, its own claimed tech's setup, and sub-driver wiring functions; never an adapter or a model.
atoms.why: A driver's one thing is to connect; any other call is an effect or logic no contract covers.
atoms.check: Callee classification outside hook bodies. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The driver's body is a registration table.

atoms.name: one-use-case-call
atoms.statement: Each hook body contains exactly one call, and it is a use-case call on an instance.
atoms.why: A hook only connects an event to one use case; two calls hide a sequence nobody owns, zero hides logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count of calls in the hook subtree (await counts as the call), callee is a member of an assembly-returned instance. LAUNCH yes given the reader's hook cut. The test tech exempts the count.
atoms.landing: Hook-to-use-case is one arrow on the map.

atoms.name: hook-bare-body
atoms.statement: A hook body is the call alone, returned, awaited or dropped; no condition, default, transform, log or write around it.
atoms.why: Translation around the call is the facade service's use case, not the hook's.
atoms.check: Statement shape of the hook body: one expression statement or return of the call; the value flows nowhere else. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A hook is one line; its translation cost is zero.

atoms.name: hook-no-read
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals; nothing read off them.
atoms.why: A hook reads nothing; reading is translation.
atoms.check: Each argument is a bare identifier or literal: no member access, call, operator or default. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: `opts` versus `opts.files` tells the reader whether the hook is honest.

atoms.name: one-wiring-function
atoms.statement: A driver defines at most one wiring function: a root's main() takes nothing, a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: The entry shape of a driver must be fixed so a boot can start it and a parent can register it.
atoms.check: Count and parameter shape of the non-hook function; boot's call passes zero arguments. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's entry is always one named function.

atoms.name: wiring-import-only
atoms.statement: A driver's import of another driver is used only as the callee of that driver's wiring function, during its own wiring.
atoms.why: Calling a sub-driver from a hook or handing it a use-case result would chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: Every reference to the imported binding is a call at wiring position. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Sub-driver trees are readable as plain registration.

atoms.name: wiring-export-only
atoms.statement: A driver exports its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Exporting a hook would let importers call it and chain use cases.
atoms.check: Export list of a driver file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The importable surface of a driver is one name.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind names: assembly functions (assembly), hooks and one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot).
atoms.why: Every definition is a venue where logic can hide, and a layer's closed verb list forbids that.
atoms.check: Top-level declarations and root statements compared with the kind's closed list. LAUNCH yes. Test kind states 'defines anything'.
atoms.landing: A declared file cannot absorb a line of logic without turning red.

atoms.name: boot-single-import
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The boot starts the program: one call to its one driver.
atoms.check: Import list of a boot file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Entry file is three lines.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's root holds exactly one call: the imported driver's wiring function, no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and that call is only a start.
atoms.check: Root statements of a boot file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The program's start is findable and boring.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: A module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax: primitive type, as const, readonly array/record/map/set, or Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth.
atoms.why: Mutable root state is shared by every test and caller that imports the module.
atoms.check: Initializer and declared type of each root binding; no top-level let; unresolvable named types prove nothing. LAUNCH yes (opt-out `mutableModuleState: true`, bindings only).
atoms.landing: Everything importable is a constant or a factory; state is in closures.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-read
atoms.statement: A root binding holds no value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness); import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed fixed identity.
atoms.why: It captures the machine's state at load, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: Initializer reaches env/clock/random identifiers or a claimed tech property. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A root constant is always a literal, never a snapshot.

atoms.name: no-root-effect-call
atoms.statement: A module-root call does not reach the tech or anything no reading claims, run a use case, or enter a local function of an adapter or blob file.
atoms.why: Evaluating a module must not act, or a test that imports it changes what the next test sees.
atoms.check: Root call-expression callee classification; property reads are presumed free, calls are not. LAUNCH yes given readers' effect-free declarations.
atoms.landing: Importing a file never does anything.

atoms.name: no-root-mutation
atoms.statement: A module-root statement does not assign, delete or otherwise act at evaluation; throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a run-time statement there is a side effect at load.
atoms.check: Root statement kinds (assignment, delete, update). LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Root holds declarations only.

atoms.name: root-registration-only
atoms.statement: In a test file the module-root calls are only registrations of the runner's hooks.
atoms.why: The runner needs its registrations at load; nothing else may act at load.
atoms.check: Root call is a claimed-tech call handing a callback (the reader's hook cut). LAUNCH yes given a test reader. Replaces no-root-effect-call for the test kind.
atoms.landing: A spec's root is its table of contents.

atoms.name: no-dependency-default
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives no default value to an injected dependency.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import from service to adapter or config source and scatters assembly logic.
atoms.check: Default initializers on the dependency parameters of a service/adapter factory. LAUNCH yes. Canon says defaults are 'right' in test factories: an exception encoded in prose.
atoms.landing: All dependencies are explicit, assembly is the only resolver.

atoms.name: exemption-reasoned
atoms.statement: A reader's or config's exemption of a rule is named and carries its reason, within a closed list.
atoms.why: An open set of escapes is a hole.
atoms.check: Config schema: each exemption entry has rule, role and reason. LAUNCH yes (config-level).
atoms.landing: Every escape is a visible, justified, countable entry.

atoms.name: adapter-port-implementation
atoms.statement: An adapter file's factory returns something typed as a port it imports.
atoms.why: An adapter exists only to implement a port for a specific technology.
atoms.check: Return type assignable to an imported .port type. LAUNCH partial: needs type information.
atoms.landing: Each adapter points at the contract it serves.

atoms.name: test-straight-line
atoms.statement: A test hook body and the steps it calls contain no branch or loop.
atoms.why: The reviewer must read given/when/expect in the test itself, not reconstruct it from logic or data-driven indirection.
atoms.check: AST of hook bodies: no if, switch, ternary, loop, try, test.each. LAUNCH yes. Canon states a reading preference, not this ban; implied only.
atoms.landing: A failing test is explained by reading it top to bottom.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' contradicts unit-assembly-only (service and adapter lateral imports are red). Whether type-only edges count is not said.
None; the rest is tradeoff prose.

Consequence, not a part: with every edge checked per kind, a chain is pure by induction. 'Partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a rationale. Only the third-party tail is faith (declared-pure list).
'Pure, deterministic' is judgment; mechanically it is the declaration list.
'Ambient environment' is a closed name list only if canon fixes it; aliasing is open. 'Or through a port' is allowance, not constraint.
None; 'assembly may take it because its rule bounds it' is rationale.
None.
None; twin of service-assembly-only.
Scope parameter (runtime edges only) on unit-assembly-only, not a constraint; the indexed-access shorthand needs a rule for what counts as type-only.
Scope of unit-assembly-only plus the allowance side of private-sealed; no constraint of its own.
'Sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is diagnosis.

Whole rule is judgment: 'branches on which adapter it got' has no mechanical form, and a service cannot import adapters anyway. Nearest mechanical neighbour is the implied adapter-port-implementation.
What a service package is (nesting, 'layer directories are not nested services') is not defined mechanically.
Sharing progression, the kernel litmus and 'the child's role picks the direction' are judgment. The direction law is a consequence of this plus unit-assembly-only.
None.
'Public API', 'documented behavior', 'implementation details' are judgment; the production-config ban (test isolation prose, no slug) is judgment too. Nothing here is mechanical.

'Same isolation rules' for fixtures is judgment. '.e2e' is in the kind yet 'end-to-end tests are neither: outside the graph'. The 'imports anything / defines anything / count and services-only do not apply' clauses are exemptions (non-carried atoms), not constraints. Shared test code placement is a placement rule.

'Decides nothing but which factory to call' is a wish; 'shared instances flow down, never sideways', 'a decision the map cannot show' and 'config wired by default, loaded in the use case' are judgment or guidance. Root-imports-only duplicates stable-root and closed-definitions.
None.
Reader contents (hook cut, claims) are outside canon; 'web drivers are open' is research.
'Tech setup' has no mechanical form beyond what a reader claims. 'A hook does not wire' follows from one-use-case-call.
Non-callback techs (route files, markup handlers, decorators) have no cut yet; 'where the line sits when the view model is the tech's' is open. The test exemption of the count is an except.
Mostly derived from the two call atoms; 'parsing and rendering are use cases' is a why, not a check.
'Residue' is a label.
Which markup nesting is 'the tech mounting it' rather than a sub-driver needs a reader.
None.
'Holds nothing, touches no tech' follows from the others; 'one per entry point' needs an entry-point definition.

'A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' is open-ended; presumptions (property reads, import.meta.url) are rulings. The exemption list (boot call, spec registration) is closed but encoded as except; recast as boot-single-call and root-registration-only.
'Assembly is the only place dependencies are resolved' is covered by unit-assembly-only.
What counts as a hook for a given tech is in the readers.
'An adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' and 'absorbs specificity' are judgment.
'Clever helpers', 'DRY-ed setup that hides the scenario' are judgment.

kinds.note: Graph-level atoms; none needs an except. Blob carries only these. Canon is silent on whether blob carries the stable-root atoms ('no layer guarantees' suggests not).
No-ambient-global and no-root-machine-read overlap for a root read; an outer layer hosting model code inherits its host's atoms.
Type-only by construction, so stable-root and ambient atoms are vacuous.
Target-side gate: unit-assembly-only is checked on edges pointing at it.

Does not carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-global: reaching the world is its business, yet it still carries no-root-machine-read, so 'the inside touches no ambient' and 'the root holds no machine read' must stay two atoms. no-dependency-default for adapters is an extension (canon says service).
Target-side: assembly-importers. no-concrete-import is lifted by a declared container library only.
Target-side: entry-not-imported. Matrix row 'cannot import model' is redundant with wiring-calls-closed plus arg-closed-set. Does not carry result-unread: hook-bare-body subsumes it.
Carries boot-single-call instead of no-root-effect-call: the stable-root exemption disappears by selection. Target-side: entry-not-imported (nothing imports it).

Carries no import-limit atom (imports anything, hence no inward-imports, no-concrete-import), no closed-definitions, no one-use-case-call, no result-unread, no arg-closed-set, no no-dependency-default, no no-ambient-global. Target-side: entry-not-imported. '.e2e' conflicts: kind test but 'neither'.

sharedParts.problem: Stated 4 times with different wordings; assembly and wiring may read a field off a tech value, a hook may not. Splitting into arg-closed-set plus hook-no-read removes the scope clash.

Assembly: 'passed on or returned'; hook: 'returned or dropped, never handed on'. Same why (never look into what you handle), different flow whitelist; the hook half is subsumed by hook-bare-body, so carry result-unread in assembly only.

One 'closed verb list' stated four times (and once in the kinds intro at 278-279), parametrized differently; test says 'defines anything'. One atom with a per-kind list; test simply does not carry it.
Twin rules plus two scope rules; 'lateral OK' in inward-deps contradicts it. With scope kept as edge-kind and private/ parameters, one atom serves all.
Every import rule restates whether type imports count, in prose, as an exception to or extension of runtime-import; inward-deps is silent. One edge-kind parameter per atom, declared once, ends it.

Restated in each layer with its own scope and its own exemption; assembly's 'nothing at root but imports' is narrower than stable-root. stable-root itself is four atoms with two exemptions (boot call, spec registration) that need narrower sibling atoms.
A root machine read is red twice for model and service (ambient-access: touches machine; stable-root: captures it at load), once for adapters; two different whys, overlapping checks.

'No concrete' appears as a matrix cell, an assembly sentence ('never concrete tech'), a boot sentence ('touches no tech') and a driver rule ('claimed or red'); the driver's is the inverse atom (claimed-tech-only). Package classification by declaration (pure, container, claimed) is one mechanism with three declaration lists.
Claimed versus unclaimed classification is the shared primitive across driver rules and stable-root's root-call clause; each restates its own red outcome.
Importer gates for driver, boot and test are one atom spread over four rules and the matrix; assembly-importers has a different why and stays separate.
Importer list restated in each rule's 'not by ... blob'; assembly-builds-only adds the blob factory clause; a blob instance returned from an assembly is not covered.
'No adapter unless a test is the caller' is stated 4 times (459, 505, 1033, 1214) as an exception; a caller gate on the returning function removes the except.
Defaults harmful in services, 'right' in test factories: an except; test factory is an assembly function that does not carry the atom.
'Test tech exempts the count' appears in hook-one-call and test-is-outside; test hooks are simply a kind that does not carry it.

sharedParts.atom: callee classification (factory, use case, model function, adapter)
sharedParts.problem: One classifier with opposite polarity: assembly forbids use-case calls, a hook requires exactly one. Primitive (a helper), not an atom, but nothing in canon names it once.

testKind: Test = a file whose kind is the bundle 'assembly + driver', which is the molecule. By atoms, a test file should carry: driver-has-reader and binding-agrees-flavor (a spec needs its reading), driver-only-listens (it registers on the runner), root-registration-only (replaces no-root-effect-call, so stable-root's 'spec exemption' vanishes), root-bindings-immutable, no-root-machine-read and no-root-mutation (canon: stable-root 'exempts the registration, not mutable state'), entry-not-imported as target (nothing imports it), the two acyclic atoms and no-barrel-index, and implied test-straight-line on hook bodies. It should NOT carry: any import-limit atom (inward-imports, no-concrete-import: it must build units and import the world), closed-definitions, arg-closed-set, build-calls-only, return-closed and no-use-case-call (a test calls units and reads fakes), one-use-case-call, hook-bare-body, hook-no-read and result-unread (a test body calls many things and reads results to assert), no-ambient-global, no-dependency-default (defaults are right in test factories). Why: the two halves of the bundle carry opposite import and call atoms (assembly may import units, a driver may not; assembly forbids use-case calls, a hook requires one), so only the non-contradicting atoms survive; the ~10 'exemptions' are atoms the kind never carries. Because nothing imports a test file, the target-side gates (entry-not-imported) are enough and no reuse rule applies. Hole: '.e2e' is listed as test kind and later called 'neither: outside the graph', so '.e2e' must leave the kind or carry a different selection.
helpers: Answer: yes, the constraint must reach the helper, but by role, not by location, and the role comes from atoms already in canon. Hypothesis, not verified. Canon's gap: test-is-outside says 'defines anything', and only SHARED test code is placed by what it is (adapter, assembly, model, driver); local helpers escape both. A bare 'no' makes a local run() the laundering venue, because the test file is the only kind with open definitions. Structure: stop treating the file as one kind for its definitions; each local definition takes the kind of what it does. (1) A function that calls an instance's use case or asserts is a step: it carries test-straight-line and hook-style one-call discipline (run() starting the CLI is a one-call step; two calls means a missing test factory or facade), and a step is callable only from hooks or steps, so a loop cannot hide behind a callee chain. (2) A function that only builds (calls factories, returns instances) is an assembly function: it carries the assembly atoms, including wiring-branch-only (a loop or branch only on parameters, factory arms) and result-unread. (3) A fake is an adapter. (4) A pure data builder is a model function: loops allowed because it can neither call an instance nor assert, so nothing it loops over can hide a behavior; a data function that invokes a function-typed parameter counts as a step (conservative: dataflow is needed to see through). (5) A local definition that fits none of these is red, and the way out is the one canon already gives shared code: move it to a file where it is placed by kind. So 'defines anything' becomes 'defines anything that classifies', and no unclassified venue exists. Same laundering shape at module root: a loop wrapping test registrations is not covered by root-registration-only unless it also bans branches/loops around registrations; canon is silent, so state the choice explicitly.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file's runtime imports point only to its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot).
atoms.why: An inner layer must be understood and tested without knowing any outer layer exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: rank of importer kind vs rank of resolved target kind, runtime edges only (canon line 875 says the matrix governs runtime imports; line 291 'no ports' for model reads as any edge, see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: Import direction on the map; an outward arrow is the violation, visible without opening the file.

atoms.name: unit-importers
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file is runtime-imported only by assembly (and by a test); never by model, ports, other services, adapters, drivers or blob.
atoms.why: Composition units are built in one place, so no unit knows or reaches another and the concrete graph exists only in assembly.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind in {service, adapter}, not under private/, edge is not `import type`, importer kind not in {assembly, test}. `public` and `runtime` are scope inside the atom, not separate rules.
atoms.landing: One list of files can build things; the chunk graph equals the assembly graph.

atoms.name: blob-importers
atoms.statement: A suffixless (blob) file is imported, by any edge type, only by assembly, test, or other blob.
atoms.why: A layer with guarantees must not be contaminated by code that claims none.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target has no layer suffix and no reader binding; importer kind not in {assembly, test, blob}; type imports included.
atoms.landing: Blob is visibly quarantined; debt is a countable boundary of two kinds of importer.

atoms.name: outside-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers, assemblies and tests; a driver only by boots, drivers and tests; a boot and a test by nothing; type imports included.
atoms.why: The outside files have no contract of their own, so nothing may depend on their shape or reach back into the chain boot > driver > assembly.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind in {assembly, driver, boot, test}, any edge type, importer kind vs a fixed allowed-set table.
atoms.landing: The entry chain reads as one arrow per hop; nobody can type-couple to a wiring file.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service package imports a file under that package's private/ directory, type imports included, nested children and parents included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what the service hides can change without a consumer noticing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path contains /private/ and importer is not under the owning package directory (layer directories are not packages).
atoms.landing: A `private/` segment in an import path is an instant red flag.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service, assembly and boot files import no concrete platform/IO module (node:fs, HTTP client, database driver) unless declared pure.
atoms.why: Contact with the world bypasses ports and makes the code untestable without that world.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: import specifier is node builtin or a package absent from the declared-pure list; purity of a package is a declaration, never inferred. Declared container library is a config parameter for assembly.
atoms.landing: Every outside-world touch is in an adapter or a driver, found by a path search.

atoms.name: claimed-tech-only
atoms.statement: Every package or global name a driver touches that is not a layer file is claimed by a reader bound to that driver.
atoms.why: A tech no reading claims cannot be judged by any driver rule.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: driver imports and free identifiers resolved against the bound readers' claim lists; unclaimed = red, way out is a claim.
atoms.landing: The driver's tech is exactly what its reader lists, nothing implicit.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports no model file and no pure library (a pure library is model).
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service, so a driver holding them is logic with no contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import from a driver to model-kind file or declared-pure package.
atoms.landing: The driver's imports are assembly, drivers, tech: nothing that computes.

atoms.name: port-type-edges
atoms.statement: No runtime import goes from or to a .port.ts file; ports are reached by `import type`.
atoms.why: A port has no runtime presence, so a runtime edge is a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing `type` keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge touching a port file without the type-only form.
atoms.landing: A port edge never carries behavior.

atoms.name: ports-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A .port.ts file contains only types: no runtime statement, no value export.
atoms.why: Runtime code in a port means the adapter has not been extracted yet and the contract carries implementation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any non-type statement or non-type export in the file.
atoms.landing: Opening a port shows a contract and nothing else.

atoms.name: no-index-barrel
atoms.statement: No index.ts barrel re-exports a service's public surface; imports name the layer file.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the matrix is unenforceable by tool or reviewer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file named index re-exporting from layer files. Mostly already caught by blob-importers because a barrel is suffixless blob; residue is a barrel imported by assembly or test.
atoms.landing: The import path alone says model, ports or composition unit.

atoms.name: service-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of service packages, edges from any import kind, has no cycle.
atoms.why: A cycle makes neither service extractable, movable or reasonable alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files to packages, any import type, find strongly connected components.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG, drawable top-down.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of files by runtime import has no cycle, even inside one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail with opaque undefined in production bundles.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime-edge SCC over files.
atoms.landing: No load-order surprises, file order is a partial order.

atoms.name: no-ambient-global
atoms.statement: A model, service, assembly or boot file reads or calls no ambient global (environment, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis), anywhere in the file.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: free identifier resolving to a global in a closed list, in any position. For assembly and boot canon states it as 'holds no tech' (implied for the atom, stated in other words).
atoms.landing: A signature lists every input the function has; no hidden ones.

atoms.name: root-binding-immutable
atoms.statement: A binding at module root is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly forms, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth); no top-level let.
atoms.why: Shared mutable module state lets one test or call change what the next one sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root declarations vs proof forms; unresolvable named types prove nothing; opt-out key is the loose-mode boolean (mutableModuleState).
atoms.landing: Imports give the same module to everyone; state exists only in a called factory.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: A value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness, env) is never stored in a root binding; import.meta.url and __dirname are the stated non-machine reads.
atoms.why: The file could not be tested under another environment or moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root initializer containing a claimed-tech or clock/random read; property read vs call distinction as in canon.
atoms.landing: A module's constants are the same on every load.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation performs no call into tech or unclaimed code, no use-case call, no local call into a side-effect layer, and no assignment or delete statement; throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Loading a file must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root statements and root calls classified by callee claim and file kind; the list of shapes is stated as open ('judged by the rule'), so the checker holds a closed catalogue.
atoms.landing: Importing is inert, so a test or a bundler can load any file safely.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and every test file is covered by a bound reader (or one that counts it as blob on purpose).
atoms.why: Every driver and test judgment goes through the tech's reading and cannot be made without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config glob binding vs file kind from the flavor.
atoms.landing: What a tech's hooks are is declared once, in the reader, not guessed per file.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot has exactly one import, a driver.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start, and any other import gives it something else to do.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list length and target kind.
atoms.landing: Entry file reads in a line: import driver, call it.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's only root statement is one call to the driver's wiring function.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, so it must be exactly the start and nothing around it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements == [call of the imported wiring export].
atoms.landing: One call identifies the entry of the program.

atoms.name: root-wiring-nullary
atoms.statement: The wiring function a boot calls takes no parameters and is called with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot touches no tech, so the root driver reads its own tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter list of the export a boot imports; argument list of the boot's call.
atoms.landing: Which side reads the tech is never ambiguous.

atoms.name: defines-nothing
atoms.statement: A boot defines nothing and holds nothing: no function, class or variable.
atoms.why: A definition is where logic hides, and the boot has no thing to hold.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations in the file other than imports and types.
atoms.landing: Boots are identical in shape.

atoms.name: defines-assembly-fns
atoms.statement: An assembly file defines nothing except assembly functions (types allowed), as many as the author wants.
atoms.why: The widest import right must come with nothing else to host, or logic hides there.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every root declaration is a function whose calls are builds; plus no other root statement beyond imports.
atoms.landing: An assembly is a list of factories being wired.

atoms.name: defines-hooks-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver defines nothing but its hooks and at most one wiring function (root: no parameters; sub-driver: tech and instances from the parent).
atoms.why: Any other definition is residue: logic without a contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations vs reader's hook cut; wiring function parameter shape.
atoms.landing: A driver file is hooks hung on a tech.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports exactly its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: A parent can then only let the sub-driver attach its callbacks, never chain a hook.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver file.
atoms.landing: The driver-to-driver surface is one function.

atoms.name: calls-build-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a build: a factory of a composition unit, another assembly's, a blob file's, or a model factory by flavor name; a model function that computes is not called.
atoms.why: The assembly decides nothing but which factory to call, otherwise logic hides in the file that may import everything.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind (service/adapter/assembly/blob are factories by construction) and for model the flavor's create* name; declared loads are the parameter that lifts one call.
atoms.landing: The assembly is the graph and nothing else, drawn as arrows.

atoms.name: result-opaque
atoms.statement: A call result is never read into, branched on, computed with, member-accessed (a use-case call is member access), logged or written to tech state; a declared load's result counts as a tech value and is exempt.
atoms.why: The outside never looks into what the inside gave it, so the map shows everything it does.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of each call result binding; sinks are classified; declared-loads list is a config parameter.
atoms.landing: Reading one assembly or hook tells everything it does with a built value: nothing.

atoms.name: result-not-forwarded
atoms.statement: A hook's call value is returned or dropped, never passed on as an argument.
atoms.why: Handing the result on makes the driver a pipeline between two services.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow sinks of the one call's value inside a hook.
atoms.landing: Event in, call, value out: a one-line arrow.

atoms.name: args-not-computed
atoms.statement: An argument in an assembly call, a wiring call or a hook call is a literal, a tech value (possibly a field read or a destructured part, in assembly and wiring), or an instance; never a call, operator, default or template.
atoms.why: A computed argument is the outside doing the inside's job.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression AST kinds; classification of tech values from parameters and reader claims.
atoms.landing: Arguments are nouns already in scope.

atoms.name: hook-args-raw
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, host values handed whole (process, not process.cwd()), instances and literals, nothing read off them.
atoms.why: A translation of the event belongs to the facade service, where it has a contract and test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no property access or destructuring on hook parameters inside arguments; host name handed whole.
atoms.landing: The link from event to service is a pass-through.

atoms.name: returns-services-only
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances; it returns adapters only when every importer is a test.
atoms.why: Consumers type against service APIs and an adapter is the assembly's inside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: returned values' kinds; for adapter returns, importer set of the file.
atoms.landing: What reaches the driver is a use-case surface.

atoms.name: wiring-condition-simple
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or a loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are builds.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand classification; arm contents via calls-build-only.
atoms.landing: Branches in assembly are drawable as variants of the graph.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call (zero and two are both red).
atoms.why: Anything between an event and a service not owned by a service is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count of calls per hook cut by the reader; the test tech replaces this atom, canon calls it 'exempts the count'.
atoms.landing: One arrow per hook on the map.

atoms.name: hook-calls-use-case
atoms.statement: The call a hook makes is to a use case of a service instance, never an adapter, a model, a tech call or wiring.
atoms.why: An effect or computation from a hook has no contract covering it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee resolved via instance flow from assembly's return type; sub-driver wiring from a hook is red.
atoms.landing: A hook names one use case.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-wiring
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver calls only assembly, claimed tech setup and sub-driver wiring functions; a hook does not wire and the wiring does not call use cases.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place so that hooks stay the only event-to-service links.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee kind by position (outside vs inside hook cut).
atoms.landing: A driver has two readable zones: setup and hooks.

atoms.name: body-linear
atoms.statement: A hook or test body contains no branch, loop, switch, ternary, short-circuit or iteration callback.
atoms.why: A body is read as one behavior statement and a branch makes it two behaviors under one name.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow constructs in function bodies; stated for hooks as 'unconditional', for tests only implied by the reviewer principle; cut the why in two (hook-linear, test-linear) if the authors judge the justifications distinct.
atoms.landing: Reading a body is reading a sequence; table-driven scenarios are visible as such.

atoms.name: hook-body-closed
atoms.statement: A hook body holds only the one call, optionally awaited, and a return of its value: no declaration, try/catch, throw or other statement.
atoms.why: Nothing may stand between the event and the call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds in a hook body.
atoms.landing: Every hook has the same shape.

atoms.name: subdriver-call-only
atoms.statement: An imported driver binding is used only as a callee of its wiring function, outside hooks, with tech and instances as arguments.
atoms.why: So the importer can only let the sub-driver attach its callbacks, not chain two calls through an indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: usage sites of bindings imported from a driver.
atoms.landing: Driver imports are one-hop registrations.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An .adapter.ts file's factory result is assignable to a port interface of the hexagon it serves.
atoms.why: The suffix declares a port implementation, so adapters are interchangeable behind the port.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with the TS engine: assignability of the exported factory's return to a port type; canon states it as a declaration, never as a rule.
atoms.landing: Every adapter says which port it fills.

atoms.name: factory-no-defaults
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory's dependency parameters have no default values.
atoms.why: Defaults create hidden static imports and scatter assembly logic into service modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers in a service/adapter factory's parameter pattern; telling dependencies from plain arguments is not mechanical (see rules remainder).
atoms.landing: All dependencies are named and supplied from assembly; test factories carry defaults by being assembly functions, not by exception.

atoms.name: instance-per-test
atoms.statement: In a test file, a composition-unit factory (or an assembly function) is called only inside a test hook, never at module or describe scope.
atoms.why: A shared instance is shared mutable state between tests.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: factory calls by position vs reader's hook cut.
atoms.landing: Each scenario shows its own setup.

atoms.name: spec-registration-only
atoms.statement: At the root of a test file the only calls are registrations the test reader declares; other root statements are imports and definitions.
atoms.why: Loading a spec must only register tests, so nothing it runs changes what the next test sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root calls vs reader's registration list; replaces root-no-effect for the test kind, as boot-single-call does for boot.
atoms.landing: The root of a spec is a list of registrations.

rules.remainder: Order line 'service, adapters' is lateral, but the matrix and composition rules forbid service-service and adapter-adapter: the lateral allowance is dead letter and left to unit-importers.
Why clause (layer visible at import site) is a landing, not a check; mostly duplicates blob-importers because a barrel is blob.
No atom of its own: it is the induction of the three atoms over every file. 'False guarantees' is a wish. Candidate to be a derived statement, not a rule.
'Side-effect-free and deterministic' of a third-party package is judgment; the checker reads only a declaration ('declared, not presumed').
'The same at module root or in a function' restates a root clause that stable-root states again; scope list (model or service) omits assembly and boot though they hold no tech.
Justifications for why assembly and test may import (assembly 'bounds what it can do with it') are explanation, they point at calls-build-only and result-opaque.
Identical to service-assembly-only except the target kind: one atom, two slugs.
Pure scoping: it adds no constraint, it only edits the edge type of unit-importers (and the 'type imports included' of five others says the opposite). It is the exemption without a constraint.
Pure scoping of unit-importers (private/ of own service exempt). No constraint of its own; private-sealed already bounds who reaches private/.
'Sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is a diagnosis. Two checks (file content, edge form) with one shared why.
'Service layer branches on which adapter it got' is not structurally visible (the service cannot import adapters); the stated condition is a judgment. Only the implied atom is checkable.
Where a package boundary is (layer directories vs nested services, private/ children) is a classification the checker needs; direction law is a corollary with unit-importers.

'Input via public API', 'assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details' are judgments; the only mechanical content is that a test does not import private/ it does not own. Rule is ~all remainder.

'Assembly and driver in one' is a description that explains the exemptions; 'imports anything, defines anything, hook count and services-only do not apply' are absences of atoms, not constraints. '.e2e' is named test kind (263, 567) but 1022-1023 says end-to-end tests are neither and outside the graph: contradiction. 'Test-purpose adapters, same isolation rules' is a judgment about fixtures.

'Decides nothing but which factory' and 'pipeline hiding in the wiring' are the why. 'Shared instances flow down, never sideways' (497-503) has no stated check. Whether a dependency is 'not yet extracted' is a judgment. Biggest molecule of canon (about 9 atoms).
'Tech setup' is only what the reader claims; 'a lazily loaded feature is an assembly importing another' is a statement, not a check.

'Use-case call' identification and the exact hook cut are the reader's; 'where the line sits when the view model is the tech's' is a hole; 'a second call means a facade service is missing' is advice. Second molecule of canon (8 atoms).
No atom of its own: it is the union of hook-calls-use-case and wiring-calls-wiring, plus 'never an adapter' (unit-importers), 'never a model' (driver-no-model) and unclaimed-red (claimed-tech-only).
'Residue' and 'a model without a test' are explanations.
'Never data from the hexagon' reduces to args-not-computed plus result-opaque; 'a parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a reader cut.
'Holds nothing, touches no tech' folds into defines-nothing and no-ambient-global. 'A program has one boot per entry' is a count, not mechanical per file.

'The shapes below are the known ones, not a closed list; a shape nobody has written is judged by the rule' is an open judgment, not LAUNCH-able beyond a catalogue. 'Presumed free of side effects' for property reads and import.meta.url is a classification by fiat.

'The bar is abstractness', 'domain of ideas' and the factory-with-port rule (factory taking a port is a composition unit) are judgments, only the import consequence is checkable; model 'full coverage expected' is not a check.

'Each function on the returned API is a use case', 'if you cannot name them you have a utility bag', 'orchestrates, does not compute' (contradicted by 274-276: model logic in a service is fine) are judgment. Dependency vs plain argument (default values) is not mechanical.
'One thing each', 'boring', 'thin', 'logic hides' are the whys; every one reduces to a closed definitions list per kind (three atoms with one shared why).

'Adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's', 'absorbs specificity', 'normalizing' are not mechanical; the port test 'can I meaningfully define a port' (687-690) is a judgment word.

'Production config has no place in tests', 'determinism', 'shared fixtures follow sharing rules' and 'test factory systematic use' are wishes; default-argument allowance for test factories is a scoping by kind.
'Legible as a behavior statement', 'no clever helpers, no data-driven indirection' are the why of an implied atom; never written as a rule, so tests are today unconstrained.

kinds.note: Atoms about a target or about the whole graph apply wherever an edge exists; the kind of the importer only chooses whether it is in the target's allowed set. root-binding-immutable and root-no-machine-read are canon's 'everywhere' via stable-root (blob is ambiguous: blob 'claims no guarantees' vs 'stable-root holds everywhere else').
Type-only imports of ports/services contradict 'no ports' (lines 291 vs 974): the edge scope of inward-imports must be fixed once.
Trivial for no-concrete-import and no-ambient-global since nothing runs.
unit-importers is carried as target: only assembly (and test) import it. Model code inside a service is not separated by atoms, it just inherits the host's.
Allowed to touch concrete and ambient: carries neither no-concrete-import nor no-ambient-global; root-no-effect applies in its 'local function of a side-effect layer' form.
blob-importers is the right of assembly, not a constraint on it. Declared loads and declared container libraries are parameters of result-opaque and no-concrete-import.
hook-* atoms apply to the hooks a reader cuts; a reader may exempt an atom for a role with a stated reason (the test tech replaces hook-single-call).
boot-single-call replaces root-no-effect for the boot, so boot's 'exemption' is a different atom, not an exception.
Everything else it is exempted from today is simply not carried. .e2e conflicts with 1022-1023 and should leave the kind or get its own reader.
As a target only. Whether the universal root atoms apply to blob is unstated.

sharedParts.problem: The type-import exemption is stated once (runtime-import) and then un-stated in six rules ('type imports included'), while the model prose bans ports with no edge qualifier and line 974 says a type import is legal anywhere. Every import atom needs its own edge-type value, stated in the atom, so no rule needs to carry the exemption.
Same atom stated per target kind in two slugs and re-stated for drivers; scope words (public, runtime) are scoping, not rules.
One 'who may import me' table stated four times in four wordings, and again from the importer side in the dependency matrix.

Each forbidden edge in the matrix is also forbidden by an importee-side rule (assembly importing a driver is red twice). Double statement from both ends of one edge: duplicate violations and two places to keep in sync.
One 'no platform/IO imports' constraint worded as purity, concrete, tech, unclaimed; a kind carries it or not.
ambient-access scopes to model and service; assembly and boot say the same thing in other words, so a reader can think they differ.

inRules: assembly-builds-only (nothing at module root but imports)
sharedParts.problem: Module-root statelessness appears in four places with different scopes, and test-is-outside exempts 'the registration, not mutable state' inside the same rule family.

Ambient reads at root are judged by two rules for model/service; for adapters only stable-root applies, with property read presumed free, which clashes with ambient-access for model/service (`process.env` in a condition is red for one, green for the other).
A closed exemption list ('boot's one call, spec registration') inside stable-root; the two exemptions are in truth different atoms replacing root-no-effect for their kinds.
One 'closed list of definitions per kind' clause with one why (a definition is where logic hides) and three lists; atoms parametrised by a role list or three atoms, never inline exceptions.
Same restriction on arguments in three kinds with slightly different value lists (field reads allowed in assembly and wiring, forbidden in hooks); hook-args-raw is the true difference.
'Never looked into' stated for assembly (passed on or returned) and for hooks (returned only); hook sink set is stricter, so a second atom (result-not-forwarded) carries the difference.
driver-calls-services is the union of the two position-specific callee lists and adds nothing else: a rule that is only a bundle of two others and three import atoms.
The same constraint seen from the call site (no arguments) and the definition site (main takes nothing).
Hooks state it, tests only imply it, assembly relaxes it into wiring-condition-simple; kind selection can carry it for test without an exception, today tests are unconstrained.
chain-purity is the induction of three atoms and adds no check: redundant.
A barrel is suffixless blob so blob-quarantine already refuses it for every importer except assembly and test.
About ten places state 'except tests' because test = assembly + driver while atoms are bundled; once atoms are separate, test carries a selection and none of these exemptions is written.

Declared pure libs, declared container libraries, declared loads, mutableModuleState, reader exemptions are lists inside atoms; they are parameters, to name once (one declaration site per atom) so none reads as an exception.

testKind: Test builds units with fixtures, calls them from hooks, asserts, and nobody imports it. It should carry: reader-bound (judgments go through the test reader), outside-importers (imported by nothing), spec-registration-only (root calls are the runner's registrations), root-binding-immutable and root-no-machine-read (no shared mutable state or clock at root), instance-per-test (factories only inside hooks), body-linear (a test is one scenario, no branch or loop, see helpers), port-type-edges, private-sealed (no import of private/ it does not own), and the graph atoms (service-acyclic, module-acyclic). It should not carry: inward-imports, unit-importers, blob-importers as importer, no-concrete-import, driver-no-model, claimed-tech-only (it imports anything), the three defines-* atoms (it defines anything), calls-build-only, wiring-condition-simple, returns-services-only, hook-single-call, hook-calls-use-case, hook-body-closed, hook-args-raw, args-not-computed, result-opaque, result-not-forwarded (it calls many things, builds inputs and reads results because asserting is reading), no-ambient-global (fixtures may use temp dirs and fake clocks: hole, determinism is a wish in canon), factory-no-defaults (test factories carry defaults by being assembly functions). Why: a test is assembly-side (builds) and driver-side (hook calls) but the atoms that make each of those kinds boring (closed calls, opaque results, closed definitions) would forbid the very act of asserting. Open points: .e2e is named a test kind (263, 567) and then excluded as 'outside the graph' (1022-1023): either its own reader and kind, or leave the test kind; 'Production config has no place in tests' and 'determinism' have no check.
helpers: Answer: the constraint must reach inside the helpers, and it must reach them by file kind, not by reachability from a body. Why the 'no' is wrong: body-linear stated on a position (the test body) leaves 'defines anything' as a bypass, since any loop moves one function away, which is exactly the laundering venue; canon already closes the same hole for drivers (driver-hooks-only: any other definition is residue). Problem statement as I read it: when an atom is scoped to a position P of a kind K, and K lets code be defined outside P and called from P, the atom must follow the call or the definition space must be closed; otherwise the kind's own 'defines anything' is an exception to the atom. Two structures that close it. (1) Atom on every function defined in the spec file: body-linear applies to each function declared there (hooks, local helpers, factories, callbacks), whoever calls it, no call graph needed (mechanical, cheap). A helper that needs a loop or a branch leaves the file and becomes what canon says shared test code is: a data builder is model, a test factory an assembly function, a fake an adapter, a started CLI process an adapter, and there the file's own atoms judge it (model may loop but cannot touch tech or call expect; an adapter may reach tech but implements a port). The loop did not vanish, it moved to a layer with a why and a checker. (2) Reachability: body-linear over the closure of local functions called from test bodies (call graph inside the file); more permissive and heavier, and it misses callbacks and iteration methods (forEach, map, test.each tables) unless those are counted as loops. I recommend (1) with iteration callbacks and test.each counted as loops, so the test kind carries body-linear on all its definitions; the canon sentence 'it defines anything' then narrows to 'it defines functions that are linear'. Run() that starts the CLI: if it only calls a spawn or the driver's wiring function and returns, it is linear and stays local; if it retries or loops until ready, it is an adapter and moves out. Caveat of the framing: whether single-use helpers exiting the file is a cost the authors accept is their ruling; structure (2) is the fallback if they prefer to keep local helpers rich.

atoms.name: inward-only-imports
atoms.statement: A runtime import never points from an inner layer to an outer one in model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: An inner layer stays knowable and testable without anything outside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind and target kind come from the flavor suffix, compared on the layer order; the edge kind (type vs runtime) is a parameter canon leaves unstated here.
atoms.landing: A reader sees from the import path alone that nothing inside depends on the outside.

atoms.name: no-barrel-file
atoms.statement: No file exists only to re-export other modules (index.ts); consumers import from the layer file itself.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the layer rules cannot be read or enforced.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file named index.* or whose body is only re-exports.
atoms.landing: The import path names the layer, so a violation is visible without opening a file.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A model, port, service, assembly or boot file imports no concrete platform/IO module and no third-party package not declared pure; a declared container library is the only assembly exception.
atoms.why: Contact with the world must sit behind a port so the file can be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: import specifier classified against builtin/IO lists and a declared-pure list; purity of a package is a declaration, not a proof.
atoms.landing: Every world-touching import is in an adapter or a claimed driver tech, so the map shows where the world is.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A model, service or assembly never reads or calls an ambient global (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis); the caller hands it in.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: identifier/member references against the machine-name registry, at module root or in any function, in any position.
atoms.landing: Inputs from the machine are visible as parameters.

atoms.name: blob-gate
atoms.statement: A blob file is imported (type imports included) only by blob, assembly and test files.
atoms.why: Blob has no guarantees, so letting a layer consume it contaminates the layer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind blob, importer kind allow-list, all edge kinds.
atoms.landing: The blob frontier is a visible, shrinking set of edges owned as debt.

atoms.name: composition-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (and test files).
atoms.why: The construction graph lives in one place, which is also the chunk graph.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind service/adapter outside private/, importer kind allow-list, type-only edges ignored.
atoms.landing: Only assembly files show how the program is built.

atoms.name: assembly-gate
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported (type imports included) only by drivers, other assemblies and test files.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own; consumers must type against service APIs, not against the root.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind assembly, importer allow-list, all edge kinds.
atoms.landing: Who builds the hexagon for whom is one arrow from driver to assembly.

atoms.name: driver-gate
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported (type imports included) only by a boot, another driver, or a test file.
atoms.why: A driver is a start point; imported by anything else its hooks could chain calls through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind driver, importer allow-list, all edge kinds.
atoms.landing: The outside is a tree from boot down to drivers.

atoms.name: entry-unimported
atoms.statement: No file imports a boot file or a test file.
atoms.why: An entry is started by the runtime, so nothing may depend on it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any import edge whose target kind is boot or test.
atoms.landing: A file named .spec/.boot is surely a leaf; shared test code visibly cannot wear the test name.

atoms.name: private-seal
atoms.statement: No file outside a service imports from that service's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership of the internals, independent of implementation coupling.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path contains private/ and importer is not under the owning service directory.
