atoms.landing: A private/ segment in a foreign import path is an instant violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-package graph, built from every import kind including types, has no cycle.
atoms.why: Services in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: SCC over service-level edges (any file of A importing any file of B).
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a reader can order.

atoms.name: no-module-cycle
atoms.statement: The runtime import graph between files has no cycle.
atoms.why: ESM cycles work in dev and silently yield undefined in minified production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: SCC over runtime-only file edges.
atoms.landing: Load order is unambiguous.

atoms.name: types-only-port
atoms.statement: A port file holds only type declarations, and no runtime import touches a port file in either direction.
atoms.why: A contract carries shape and no behavior; runtime code in a port means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no runtime statements in a port file, and every import to or from one is import type.
atoms.landing: The boundary file is pure shape, readable at a glance.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file is the implementation of a port it type-imports and holds only what that port needs.
atoms.why: The adapter is the translation point between port shape and the world, nothing else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: a type import of a port plus a typecheck of the exported value against it; 'holds only what the port needs' is not structural.
atoms.landing: Each adapter points at the one contract it fulfils.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports no model file and no pure library (type imports free).
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service; model in a driver is logic with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import target kind model, or a package classified pure, in a driver file.
atoms.landing: The driver's box has arrows only to assembly, drivers and its tech.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot file imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start one program.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list equals one driver.
atoms.landing: The entry reads as 'start this driver'.

atoms.name: boot-call-once
atoms.statement: A boot's module root is exactly one call, without arguments, to the wiring function of the driver it imports.
atoms.why: The only thing allowed to evaluate a call at load is the single start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement list shape; touching tech or holding anything is impossible by shape.
atoms.landing: The program's start is one line.

atoms.name: builds-only-calls
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly resolves to a factory: a service, adapter, assembly or blob file's, or a model create* factory; a model function or use case is never called.
atoms.why: The assembly decides nothing but which factory to call, so no pipeline can hide in the wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus the flavor's name (create*) for model files; an await is the call.
atoms.landing: An assembly reads as a list of constructions.

atoms.name: declared-load
atoms.statement: The only use-case calls an assembly may make are those the project declares as loads, and their results count as tech values.
atoms.why: A graph that varies with config needs that data, but nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee matches the declared list; undeclared is red and the fix is the declaration.
atoms.landing: Every data dependency of the graph is a named, declared exception.

atoms.name: args-not-computed
atoms.statement: Every call argument is a literal, a tech value (a field or destructured part allowed) or an instance, never a computed expression.
atoms.why: A derived argument is logic done in a layer with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression shape and provenance (parameter, built instance, literal); no operator or call over them.
atoms.landing: Arguments show what flows in, not how it was made.

atoms.name: result-not-read
atoms.statement: A call's result is never member-accessed, branched on, or computed with (a declared load's tech-value result excepted).
atoms.why: Touching what was built or returned is a decision the layer's one thing does not allow.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of the call-result binding.
atoms.landing: Instances move through the layer opaquely, visible as arrows only.

atoms.name: result-not-forwarded
atoms.statement: A hook's call result is returned or dropped, never assigned, written to the tech's state, logged or passed to another call.
atoms.why: Translating or rendering the result is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: result binding used only in return or not at all.
atoms.landing: A hook shows nothing between call and tech.

atoms.name: no-read-off-tech
atoms.statement: A hook reads nothing off the event or host value it receives and hands it whole (process, never process.cwd(); opts, never opts.files).
atoms.why: Reading off an event is translation, which belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no property access or destructuring on hook parameters or host globals inside a hook.
atoms.landing: The event reaches the use case as received.

atoms.name: one-call-per-hook
atoms.statement: A hook body is exactly one call, to a use case, and nothing else (awaited or returned at most).
atoms.why: Two calls make a sequence no one owns and zero makes logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: hook cut by the reader, then body AST shape and callee kind; the test tech exempts the count by reader.
atoms.landing: Each hook is one arrow from event to use case on the map.

atoms.name: no-branch
atoms.statement: A body contains no conditional and no loop.
atoms.why: Branching in a body is logic whose outcome the reader must reconstruct instead of read.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no if, ternary, ?:, &&-guard, switch, for, while, or iterator callback in the body.
atoms.landing: The body reads linearly as given, when, expect.

atoms.name: branch-on-tech-only
atoms.statement: In an assembly, a branch or loop tests only parameters or loaded values against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand provenance and arm call kinds.
atoms.landing: Variation in the graph traces to configuration, never to behavior.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-closed
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver calls only assembly factories, its claimed tech setup and sub-driver wiring functions, never an adapter, model or use case.
atoms.why: Wiring is done here and nowhere else, and effects must go through contracts.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee class outside hook bodies; hook cut and tech claims come from the reader.
atoms.landing: The driver's top level reads as set-up: assemble, register, mount.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines nothing beyond what its kind names: assembly functions; a driver's hooks and at most one wiring function; nothing in a boot.
atoms.why: Any other definition is residue, logic with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declaration inventory (function, class, variable) against the kind's allowed set.
atoms.landing: The outside kinds contain no stray names to read.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver file exports exactly its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: The importer can then only let it attach callbacks, never chain a hook's call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: subdriver-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver uses an imported driver only to call its wiring function during its own wiring, passing tech and instances, never from a hook and never with a use-case result.
atoms.why: A call from a hook or a handed result would chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: usage of the imported binding is a wiring-position call.
atoms.landing: Driver trees split hooks across files without hiding calls.

atoms.name: driver-tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every import or global a driver or test file uses as tech is claimed by a reader bound to that file; unclaimed is red.
atoms.why: A name no reading claims cannot be classified, so no driver atom can judge it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package and name claim lists in the bound readers.
atoms.landing: The file's tech surface is the reader's explicit claim list.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a reader bound to its tech, or is bound to a reader that counts it as blob on purpose.
atoms.why: Every driver atom is judged through the reading, so none works without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding coverage per file of kind driver or test; binding vs flavor disagreement is a config error.
atoms.landing: Each driver's tech and hook cut are named in config.

atoms.name: no-root-state
atoms.statement: A module root creates no binding whose immutability the syntax does not prove (primitive type, as const, readonly, Object.freeze over a literal), exported or not.
atoms.why: A test that imports the module must get what every other test got, and nothing it runs may change the next.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root binding initializer and annotation against an immutability proof, depth-aware, depends on type resolution; config mutableModuleState lifts exactly this atom.
atoms.landing: State is only in factory closures, reached by argument and never by import.

atoms.name: no-load-time-capture
atoms.statement: A module root stores no value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness), regardless of its type annotation; the module's own location is exempt.
atoms.why: The stored snapshot cannot be varied by a test without reloading the file.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root binding initializer reaches the machine-name registry or a claimed tech; import.meta.url and __dirname exempt.
atoms.landing: Nothing in a file's constants differs from one load to the next.

atoms.name: no-root-effect
atoms.statement: Evaluating a module root performs no side effect: no call that reaches tech, an unclaimed name or a use case, no call into a local function of an effect-allowed file, no assignment or delete (a throw is allowed).
atoms.why: Importing a file must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root statements classified by kind and callee class; a reader may declare a call effect-free; boot's one call and a test runner's registrations are the closed exemptions.
atoms.landing: Loading a module is silent, which is what makes a file testable in its own right.

atoms.name: no-default-dependency
atoms.statement: A production factory takes every dependency as a parameter with no default value.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place where dependencies are resolved.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: default initializer on a dependency parameter of a service, adapter or model-composition factory (test factories excepted by canon).
atoms.landing: All dependencies come from the caller.

atoms.name: returns-services-only
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and an adapter only when every importer of that assembly is a test.
atoms.why: Consumers must type against service APIs, and an adapter returned would hand out an effect no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: return type kinds, plus importer kinds of the assembly for the adapter case.
atoms.landing: The driver receives only use-case surfaces.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral OK' is false for service-service and adapter-adapter (composition-gate); whether import type edges follow the order is unstated; 'see matrix' defers to a derived table.
'Layer is visible' is a landing; the suffix-declares-layer classification is substrate for every atom, not a constraint.

Derived, no atom of its own: inward-only-imports plus no-concrete-import applied to every file make the chain pure; only transitive purity of third-party packages is left, a declaration taken on trust.
'Purity declared, not presumed' needs a declaration list; 'becomes untestable' is the why.
Scope is model and service in canon; assembly is implied by 'holds no tech'; adapters and drivers exempt.
'Owned as debt, shrinking' is a plan; the reasons assembly and test may take blob lean on other atoms (builds-only-calls, port injection).
None; identical to adapter-assembly-only.
None; identical to service-assembly-only.
Not an atom: the type-only exemption is a scope bit of composition-gate (and the SomeService["method"] shorthand a consequence), restated as 'does not cover' in four other rules.
Not an atom: 'private units are ungated' is a scope bit of composition-gate; what a private composition unit may do is constrained by nothing.
'A sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is a diagnosis.

Entire rule is judgment: 'branches on which adapter it got' has no structural signature beyond what composition-gate already forbids (importing the adapter); same-interface-same-shape is adapter-implements-port (implied).
None.
The direction law (nested adapter edges point up) is this atom plus composition-gate; 'service' package boundary needs a definition of a service directory.
None.
Judgment: 'documented behavior', 'no implementation details'; the only structural shadow is private-seal applied to tests, which test-is-outside's 'imports anything' contradicts.

A bundle of waivers: 'defines anything' (closed-definitions waived), 'hook count and services-only do not apply' (one-call-per-hook and wiring-calls-closed waived), 'imports anything' (allow-lists and driver-no-model waived), 'same isolation rules' for fixtures (unchecked); '.e2e' is listed as test kind but 'end-to-end are outside the graph'; 'assembly and driver in one' is a claim, not a constraint.
'Tech value' is defined by a reader that assembly says it has none bound; 'nothing at module root but imports' restates stable-root plus closed-definitions.
None.
The 'count as blob on purpose' reader is a confessed laundering venue: such a driver escapes every hook atom; reader-vs-flavor disagreement is a config error, not a code constraint.
'Tech setup' needs the reader's claims to be recognized.
Which functions are hooks is the reader's cut (stock cut only handles callbacks); 'facade is missing' and 'logic with no home' are diagnoses; non-callback tech has no cut yet.
'Never an adapter' in a hook is carried by one-call-per-hook's callee class; 'pure library is model' rests on a purity declaration.
'Residue' is a label for the violation; root-vs-sub wiring signature (takes nothing vs takes tech and instances) is implied by boot-call-once and by the parent's call, not stated as a check.
A parent component rendering a child in markup is explicitly outside this rule.
None.
'One boot per entry point' needs a definition of entry point; 'touches no tech' is impossible by shape, hence derived.
'A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' is an open-world clause (judgment); immutability proof depends on type resolution; module-identity presumption is a name allow-list.

kinds.note: Imports only model and declared-pure libraries; the abstractness kind.
Root atoms are trivially satisfied by types only.
Target of composition-gate. Orchestrate-not-compute stays a remainder.
Carries neither no-concrete-import nor no-ambient-access; target of composition-gate.
Allowed importer of blob; target of assembly-gate.
Target of driver-gate; no-concrete-import is replaced by driver-tech-claimed.
closed-definitions with an empty allowed set; no-root-effect is replaced by boot-call-once.
Everything else is simply not carried; test-is-outside's waivers disappear (see testKind). private-seal is contested by 'imports anything'.
Target of blob-gate; no layer guarantees. Whether stable-root reaches blob is unstated.

sharedParts.problem: One atom stated as two identical slugs, with its two scope bits (type-only, private) as two more slugs; test-is-outside ('imports anything') and inward-deps ('lateral OK') each contradict it from outside, so test and sibling services get an 'except'.

Whether import type counts is restated per rule with 'covers composition rules only' wording in five places and left unstated for inward-deps and model's 'no ports', so a model type-importing a port is undecided.

Stated in the model bullet (295-298), the service bullet (341) and stable-root; assembly-builds-only re-states 'nothing at module root but imports'; test-is-outside exempts registration but 'not mutable state' (a second statement of the same split).

The same globals (process, Date, Math.random, console, document) are 'ambient' for inside kinds, 'machine reads' in stable-root, 'tech' in driver readers and 'holds no tech' for assembly, three registries of one list.
Three wordings of 'literals, tech values, instances'; the hook version is stricter (reads nothing) and hides a second atom, no-read-off-tech, that the other two do not carry.
'Never computed with or member-accessed' vs 'never read, written, handed on or logged': the common core is the same, but 'handed on' is required in assembly and forbidden in a hook.
Four wordings of one atom with four allowed sets; test-is-outside's 'defines anything' is the except, and it is what opens the helper laundering venue.
Two strengths of one atom (none vs on-tech-only) stated in different rules; a test's body has no stated strength at all.
Four overlapping allow-lists of what a driver may call, split by position (inside or outside a hook) in one rule and not in the others.
Importer allow-list stated in the rule, again in the matrix, again in the driver text (650-651) and in the assembly text (487-491); test is an allowed importer by a separate sentence.
'Nothing imports it' is stated for boot, for test, and as a near-twin for driver with a different allow-list; one atom family with three whys-in-words.
The boot's single root call is stated positively in boot-one-call and again as stable-root's closed-list exemption; the two must stay identical by hand.
IoC 'no defaults' (unslugged) overlaps composition-gate (static imports to adapters) and no-ambient-access (default = console), and is reversed for test factories; canon gives no slug for it.
Both rules require a reading for tests and drivers; the 'counts as blob on purpose' escape inside driver-reader reintroduces ungoverned drivers.
Tests 'import anything' but must test through the public API; the matrix gives test everything while private-sealed says nothing outside may import private.
Concrete-ness and pure-lib-is-model restated in model, matrix, service-purity, chain-purity, assembly and driver text; chain-purity is no atom, only the transitive closure.

testKind: Carry: reader-bound and driver-tech-claimed (a test is read by a test reader that claims the runner), entry-unimported (nothing imports a test; so shared test code cannot keep the test name), no-root-state and no-load-time-capture (isolation between tests is exactly stable-root, and 'each test assembles its own instance' follows from it), no-root-effect with the runner's registration calls declared effect-free by the reader (no kind-level exemption needed), subdriver-wiring-only (spec calling registerMatchers), the graph atoms (no-module-cycle, no-service-cycle, no-barrel-file), and the proposed no-branch on every function reachable from a hook (implied by the 'given, when, expect' legibility paragraph). Do not carry: inward-only-imports (a test sits above all layers), the importer allow-lists as exceptions (test is simply listed as an allowed importer of blob, composition units, assemblies and drivers, so no 'except' text is needed), no-concrete-import and no-ambient-access (units under test and fixtures touch the world; tech is bounded by the reader's claims instead), driver-no-model (tests of model import model), one-call-per-hook and wiring-calls-closed (a hook-body test builds, calls several times, asserts), result-not-read and args-not-computed (asserting means reading results), closed-definitions in its full form (but see helpers), builds-only-calls and returns-services-only (the test factory belongs in an assembly file). Why: a test builds units (assembly half) and calls then asserts (driver half) but is a leaf: nothing imports it, so only atoms about what it imports, how it loads and what its body looks like have anything to judge; atoms about being imported or about what a layer may hold do not apply. Unresolved: e2e (listed as test kind yet 'outside the graph'); private-seal vs 'imports anything'; 'same isolation rules' for fixtures has no atom.
helpers: Open question, answer: the no-branch/loop constraint cannot be 'no' for helpers, and it cannot be lexical (hook body only). Apply it by reachability: no-branch binds the body of every hook AND every function in the file reachable by call from a hook, so a local run() with a loop is red the same as a loop in the body. Second leg: a helper that needs a loop leaves the file and is placed by what it is, as canon already does for shared test code: a fake with iteration is an adapter, a builder an assembly function (builds-only-calls, branch-on-tech-only), a data builder model, a runner-registered matcher a driver; each destination kind closes its own venue. Third leg, to make this airtight: 'defines anything' in test-is-outside should shrink to 'defines hooks and literal data', so closed-definitions applies to tests with their own allowed set; local helpers then do not exist, and the question dissolves into placement. Residual holes: a model-kind data builder may loop (loop hidden in model, legible only by naming); fakes passed as values and called by the unit under test are not reachable from hooks (they must live as adapters); a run() that starts the CLI is a driver-like call and should be a wiring function in a driver file, not a local helper. Checker helpers implied by the atoms: (1) one importer-allow-list table (target kind to importer kinds, edge kinds) serving composition-gate, blob-gate, assembly-gate, driver-gate, entry-unimported, private-seal; (2) one machine-name registry feeding no-ambient-access, no-load-time-capture, driver-tech-claimed; (3) one callee classifier (factory, use case, model function, adapter, tech, unclaimed) and one result-flow tracer (read, forwarded, returned, dropped) shared by assembly and hook atoms; (4) one reader hook cut. Method note: rule-by-rule split yielded 37 atoms; 28 slugs, of which chain-purity, runtime-import and public-unit carry no atom of their own, unified-port and test-through-contract are mostly judgment.

atoms.name: inward-only-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or an inner one in the order model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be developable and testable without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolve each import edge, compare the importer's kind rank to the importee's. Whether type edges count is unsettled (see sharedParts, edge-kind).
atoms.landing: The suffix of a file tells what it may reach, so a wrong-way import is visible at the import line.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file imports no platform/IO package (node builtins, HTTP clients, DB drivers) that is not declared pure.
atoms.why: A layer that must run without the machine cannot reach the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: specifier is a node builtin or a package absent from the project's declared-pure list. A runtime container library enters only through config.
atoms.landing: The reader knows a file with this atom never touches infrastructure, whatever its body says.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A file neither reads nor calls ambient sources (process.env, Date, Math.random, console, timers, globalThis, import.meta.env) anywhere, at root or in a function.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine's state depends on the machine and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: unbound global identifiers and import.meta.env members, matched against the ambient name set.
atoms.landing: Every input of the file is visible in its signature: time, randomness and environment arrive as arguments.

atoms.name: no-root-mutable-binding
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly type, Object.freeze over a literal); no top-level let; a module exports factories, never instances.
atoms.why: State lives in factory closures so that no test can see what another test left behind.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes, with a TS engine for the type proofs: root declarations against the closed proof list; a type the reader cannot resolve proves nothing; opt-out mutableModuleState lifts the bindings only.
atoms.landing: Opening a module shows it holds no state; every instance has a visible call site.

atoms.name: no-machine-at-root
atoms.statement: A root binding stores no value read from the machine (environment, clock, randomness, tech); a property read in a condition is not a store; import.meta.url and __dirname are the module's identity, not the machine.
atoms.why: A value captured at load time cannot be varied by a test without reloading the module.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root initializer contains a read of a name in the ambient/tech set, minus the identity exceptions.
atoms.landing: A constant at root is the same constant everywhere; nothing at root depends on when or where it ran.

atoms.name: no-root-effect
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation makes no call that reaches tech or unclaimed code, runs a use case, or enters a local function of a side-effect layer, and runs no assignment or delete; a throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act, so one test's imports cannot change what the next sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root statements and calls classified by the readers' claims; a call is red until a reading declares it effect-free. The open clause 'a shape nobody wrote down is judged by the rule' is not mechanical.
atoms.landing: Importing a file is silent: reading the imports of a program tells nothing was started.

atoms.name: boot-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one module, a driver, and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The program starts from one place and that place knows one thing: its driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import count and importee kind of the file.
atoms.landing: The entry of the program is one line to read, the start of the map's single arrow.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's module root holds exactly one statement: a call, with no arguments, of its driver's wiring function.
atoms.why: Starting the program is the one call allowed outside any function, and it must be only that.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement count, callee is the imported driver's wiring export, zero arguments, no touch of tech names.
atoms.landing: What the runtime executes on load is fully legible in one glance.

atoms.name: test-root-registration
atoms.statement: A test file's root calls are only registrations on the test runner that a bound test reader names.
atoms.why: The test tech owns registration; nothing else may run at load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a test reader that lists registration names; whether test.each counts as registration or as a loop is for the reader to say.
atoms.landing: The root of a spec reads as a list of scenarios and nothing else.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: Every definition in a file (function, class, variable) belongs to the closed list of its kind: ports types only; assembly the assembly functions; driver its hooks plus at most one wiring function (root: takes nothing; sub-driver: takes tech and instances); boot none.
atoms.why: A file with wide import rights or tech access must not absorb logic, so anything unlisted is residue.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declaration scan against the kind's list; a type is not a definition.
atoms.landing: The reader knows these files contain no function that needs a test or a contract.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: An import specifier names the file that declares the layer; there is no index.ts and no barrel re-export.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the dependency rules cannot be enforced by shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no index file, no re-export across layers, specifier resolves directly to a suffixed file.
atoms.landing: The layer being imported is readable from the path without opening anything.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file (not under private/) is imported at runtime only by assembly (and by tests, and by files of its own service for private units).
atoms.why: Dependencies are resolved in one place, so no unit scatters wiring or binds to another unit.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind and path, importer kind, runtime edges only.
atoms.landing: The chunk graph and the map's wiring are the assembly graph, nothing else.

atoms.name: blob-importers-closed
atoms.statement: A suffixless file is imported, type edges included, only by blob, assembly or test files.
atoms.why: Importing blob carries its absent guarantees into a layer that claims some.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee has no layer suffix; importer kind in {blob, assembly, test}.
atoms.landing: Every blob dependency sits at an assembly, so debt is visible on the map at one kind of file.

atoms.name: assembly-importers-closed
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported, type edges included, only by drivers and assemblies (and tests acting as drivers).
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract, so the type-only exemption cannot apply and consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind assembly, every edge kind.
atoms.landing: Who builds the graph is known by kind: only the driver side reaches it.

atoms.name: driver-importers-closed
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported, type edges included, only by a boot or another driver.
atoms.why: Only wiring may reach a driver, so one hook cannot chain two calls through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind driver, every edge kind.
atoms.landing: The map draws a driver's only incoming arrows from boot and sub-driver wiring.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: A boot or a test file is imported by nothing.
atoms.why: The runtime (Node, the test runner) runs an entry; an import would run it twice or chain it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no edge targets a file of kind boot or test, so shared test code cannot keep a test name.
atoms.landing: Entry points are leaves of the graph; any file imported by others is placed by what it is.

atoms.name: private-owner-only
atoms.statement: A file under private/ is imported, type edges included, only from within its owning service.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, not implementation coupling.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a service-boundary definition (nearest directory holding private/); path scan of importer vs importee.
atoms.landing: An import of a private path is an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: port-import-type-only
atoms.statement: Every import of or from a port file is an import type.
atoms.why: A port is a contract shape; a runtime edge means leaked runtime code or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import syntax at edges whose importee or importer is a port.
atoms.landing: A port edge in the graph is always a shape dependency, never an implementation one.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The graph of service packages, all import kinds counted, type imports included, is acyclic.
atoms.why: Services in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files into service packages, run cycle detection.
atoms.landing: The service DAG on the map reads as a hierarchy.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: The graph of files over runtime imports is acyclic.
atoms.why: Circular ESM works in dev and fails silently in bundled production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-level cycle detection on runtime edges only.
atoms.landing: Module load order is a plain tree walk.

atoms.name: unit-exports-factory
atoms.statement: A composition unit exports factory functions that return its API, never instances.
atoms.why: Assembly builds units by calling factories; where an instance exists is assembly's decision.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: exported value declarations in .service/.adapter files are functions; instances are already caught by no-root-mutable-binding.
atoms.landing: Every instance of a unit has a call site in an assembly.

atoms.name: no-dependency-default
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory's parameters carry no default values for dependencies.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import from the unit to its adapters or config and scatters assembly logic across units.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers on factory parameters in .service/.adapter; which parameters are dependencies versus plain options is a judgment unless every default is refused.
atoms.landing: Every dependency of a unit is visibly supplied by its caller.

atoms.name: no-adapter-branching
atoms.statement: Service code does not branch on which adapter it received.
atoms.why: If the inside must know which adapter it talks to, the port has not abstracted the outside away.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: instanceof or access to a member absent from the port type, needs the TS engine; a name-based test of identity is not seen.
atoms.landing: A service reads as written against one contract only.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file's exported factory returns a value typed against a port it imports.
atoms.why: An adapter exists to implement the inside's contract for one technology.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs TS assignability of the factory's return type to an imported port type.
atoms.landing: Each adapter points at the contract it serves.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly targets a factory (of a service, adapter, other assembly, blob file injected behind a port, or a model factory by flavor name) or a declared load; no model function, no call on a tech value.
atoms.why: Assembly decides nothing but which factory to call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee resolved by import to file kind; model factory vs function told by the flavor's name (create*); a container library's dynamic resolve is not seen.
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as the graph itself, one arrow per call.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: A use-case call in an assembly is allowed only if the project declares it as a load; its result then counts as a tech value.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for its effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee on a service instance, membership in the config's declared list; undeclared is red and the way out is the declaration.
atoms.landing: The list of use cases the graph depends on is explicit in config.

atoms.name: wiring-args-closed
atoms.statement: Arguments of calls in an assembly or in a driver's wiring are literals, tech values (a field or destructured part may be read, never called), or instances built or received.
atoms.why: Whoever needs a derived value derives it under its own rules; wiring computes nothing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: classify each argument expression; no call except factory calls, no model function.
atoms.landing: A wiring call shows exactly what flows where, with no hidden computation.

atoms.name: built-result-untouched
atoms.statement: In an assembly, a call's result is passed on or returned only, never computed with, member-accessed or branched on; a declared load's result is the exception because it is a tech value.
atoms.why: Assembly never looks into or touches what it built.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of the binding bound to the call (await is the call): uses limited to argument position and return.
atoms.landing: Instances in an assembly are opaque tokens, so the map's arrows are the whole story.

atoms.name: assembly-branch-wiring
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or its output is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operands resolved by origin; arm statements are factory calls.
atoms.landing: Variation in the graph is visible as wiring and traceable to a parameter.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services or shared model instances, and an assembly that returns an adapter is imported only by tests.
atoms.why: Only contracts reach the driver; an adapter is an effect no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return expressions traced to the callee kind; if an adapter is returned, every importer is a test file.
atoms.landing: What a driver gets from assembly is always something with a contract.

atoms.name: driver-reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file has a reader bound to its tech.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading (hooks, claims, exemptions).
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding resolves for the file; a binding that disagrees with the flavor's kind is a config error.
atoms.landing: The tech of each driver is named in config; an unread driver is visible as red.

atoms.name: driver-reach-closed
atoms.statement: A driver's runtime imports and global names are assemblies, drivers, or tech a bound reader claims; never a composition unit, model, blob, boot, or an unclaimed name or package (a pure library is model, red).
atoms.why: A driver holds the tech and nothing of the hexagon, and what no reader claims cannot be judged.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind and reader claim lookup; type imports are free.
atoms.landing: A driver is the only place where the tech appears, named by its reader.

atoms.name: wiring-callee-kinds
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver calls only assembly factories, claimed tech setup and sub-driver wiring functions.
atoms.why: A driver connects; it builds or decides nothing, so every call has a named home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee resolved to assembly/driver file or reader claim; call position (hook or outside) comes from the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: The driver body is a list of setup calls, each of a known kind.

atoms.name: hook-body-is-call
atoms.statement: A hook's body is exactly one unconditional use-case call (awaited or returned, or dropped) and nothing else; zero calls, two calls, a branch or any other statement is red.
atoms.why: One hook connects one event to one use case, and any sequence or condition around it is a use case nobody owns.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statements of each hook the reader cuts; callee is a use-case member of an instance the hook received.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow with nothing to read.

atoms.name: hook-args-untouched
atoms.statement: A hook's call arguments are the event as received, host values whole, instances or literals; nothing read off them, no default, no transform.
atoms.why: Translating the event is the facade service's use case, with contract and test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: each argument is an identifier of a hook parameter, a host name, an instance or a literal; no member access.
atoms.landing: The hook shows the event passes through unchanged.

atoms.name: hook-result-untouched
atoms.statement: A hook returns the call's value or drops it; it never reads, writes, hands on or logs it.
atoms.why: Using the result (exit code, rendering) is the facade's job through its ports.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of the call result in the hook: only return or no use.
atoms.landing: What the service did with the outcome is on the service side, not in the driver.

atoms.name: driver-import-called
atoms.statement: A driver import of another driver is used only as the call of its wiring function, outside any hook.
atoms.why: The only thing a root can do with a sub-driver is let it attach its callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every use of the imported binding is a callee at wiring position.
atoms.landing: Hook splitting across files is visible as registration calls only.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver that another driver imports exports its one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: If a hook were exported, a parent could call it and chain two use calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver with a driver importer.
atoms.landing: A sub-driver's public face is one function.

atoms.name: test-body-straight-line
atoms.statement: No branch or loop appears in a test body or in any function defined in the test file.
atoms.why: The reviewer must read the scenario as given X, when Y, expect A, with no reconstruction from helpers or data-driven indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: if/switch/ternary/&&/||/??, for/while, iteration callbacks (map, forEach, reduce, Array.from) and recursion in every function defined in the file; test.each judged as registration or loop by the reader.
atoms.landing: A spec reads top to bottom as a list of scenarios.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is overridden by unit-assembly-only for service and adapter files; the sentence is not an atom.
None.

Adds no atom: a file being only as pure as its least-pure import follows by induction from inward-only-imports, no-concrete-import and blob-importers-closed; 'partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a wish.
'Pure, deterministic' third-party library is a judgment; the mechanical form is the declared-pure list ('declared, not presumed'). 'Becomes untestable' is the why, not a check.
'Adapters and drivers reach the environment' is not an exemption but kind carriage: those kinds do not carry the atom.
'Assembly may take it because its rule bounds what it does with it' is carried by assembly-calls-factories and built-result-untouched, not by this rule.
'Must be composed by assembly' (246, 252) can be read as a requirement (every unit has an assembly caller), which no rule states mechanically.
None; same atom as service-assembly-only with another suffix.

A scope modifier, not a constraint: it says which atoms count type edges (see sharedParts, edge-kind). Its 'legal anywhere' for type imports contradicts inward-deps for model and ports files and 881-883 contradicts assembly-driver-only and driver-not-imported.

A scope modifier on unit-assembly-only ('public' means not under private/). Not covered: an adapter's or service's factory building its own private sub-units (166-167) is wiring inside a unit, and no atom of assembly applies to it.
'Runtime code in a port file is a sign the adapter has not been extracted yet' is a diagnosis.
'All adapters produce the same result shape' and 'the port has finished abstracting' are not seen mechanically beyond type conformance.
What a service boundary is (directory with private/? layer directories are not nested services) is a helper definition.

Direction law ('child's edges point up', 'parent import-blind') adds no atom: it is no-service-cycle plus unit-assembly-only. A service's own assembly filed in its folder importing a nested adapter closes a cycle the canon also allows (230-231, 909-912): unresolved.
None.

'Assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details', 'documented' and the seam-testing exceptions (a)/(b) are judgments; only the import side is mechanical (private-owner-only, already carried).

'Imports anything, defines anything, hook count and services-only do not apply' are non-carriage, not atoms. 'Fixtures are adapters, same isolation rules' is placement of fakes, not checkable from a spec alone. '.e2e' is named as test kind (263) yet 'end-to-end tests are neither, outside the graph' (1022-1023). 'Test edges never count for use-case level' is a map annotation.

Container library by configuration and 'it constructs and never calls a use case' (a container's dynamic resolve is not seen); 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' (497-503); 'one root per entry point' (523-525); whether types or exported consts may sit at root ('nothing but imports').
None.

'Bound to a reader that counts it as blob on purpose' is an escape hatch; reader exemptions 'stated with their reason' (559-562) are exactly the except this study removes; non-callback techs (routes, markup, decorators) have no cut yet (558-566, 572-575).
'Tech setup' is whatever the reader claims; whether wiring may branch is not stated.

'The test tech exempts the count' (an except); 'a reader with a cut of its own says where the line sits' (614-615) opens a relaxation canon forbids elsewhere (558-562); 'a facade is missing' is a diagnosis.
Adds nothing beyond the union of the three: never an adapter, never a model follow from them.
'A local parseFoo is a model without a test, a table of lambdas a service without a contract' is the why.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' needs a web reader; 'never hexagon data' is wiring-args-closed (a use-case result is no tech value or instance).
None.
'A program has one boot per entry point' is not checkable; 'the one module whose evaluation performs a call' is not true as written (test registrations, stable-root's exemption list).

'Shapes below are known ones, not a closed list; a new shape is judged by the rule' (1088-1090) is a judgment hole; config opt-out mutableModuleState; exemptions boot-single-call and test-root-registration (1126-1129) are the except, expressed here as replacement atoms; 'what decides it is judged where it sits' defers to ambient-access.

kinds.note: The only kind that carries both no-ambient-access and no-root atoms and needs no outside concession. Pure libraries need a declared-pure list.
closed-definitions list is types only.
Model logic may live in a service file; it inherits the service's atoms. unit-assembly-only is carried as an importee-side atom.
Does not carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-access: that is what makes it the place for tech, carried by absence not by exemption.

no-ambient-access is implied (a global read is no literal, parameter or instance). Does not carry no-dependency-default: test factories rely on defaults. A declared container library lifts no-concrete-import for that package only.
Does not carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-access (its tech is claimed by the reader). Hooks are cut by the reader.
Carries boot-single-call instead of no-root-effect: a replacement atom, not an exemption.

Carries test-root-registration instead of no-root-effect. Does not carry no-concrete-import, closed-definitions, any hook atom, wiring atoms, assembly atoms, no-dependency-default; imports side must be listed in unit-assembly-only and blob-importers-closed as an allowed importer. See testKind.
No layer guarantees; the one carried atom is on the importee side. It still cannot import a unit (unit-assembly-only is carried by the unit).

sharedParts.problem: One constraint (definitions limited to a closed list) is stated four times with four wordings: 'no runtime code', 'only assembly functions', 'only hooks and one wiring function', 'defines nothing', and a fifth that lifts it ('defines anything'). 'Definition' is defined once (443-447) but the ports and boot rules do not use it.

'Nothing imports a boot' and 'nothing imports a test' are the same atom for the same why, stated in two kinds; the matrix test row says imports anything, and no rule says whether a test may import a boot.

The class of allowed arguments (tech values, instances, literals) is stated in four places; hook-one-call narrows it (no read off the event) while assembly and wiring allow reading a field. Two atoms with one shared vocabulary, never stated once.
'Tech value' is defined in the Terminology (80-89) and again in the Assembly section (438-442) with different content (event, process whole, declared load vs argv, env, state, props, context).
The set of things a driver may call is split across four rules; driver-calls-services is the union plus two negations that already follow, and hook placement (hook vs outside) is repeated in each.

Stable root, 'nothing at module root but imports', 'boot is the one module that performs a call' and the spec registration exemption restate what may run at root; stable-root's exemption list (boot, spec) is the except the atoms remove with boot-single-call and test-root-registration.

The ambient name set (env, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) is reached by ambient-access (any position, inside kinds) and by no-machine-at-root (root binding, all kinds), each listing it differently; stable-root defers 'what decides it' back to ambient-access.

'No tech import' is stated for service (service-purity), model (bullets and 'pure third-party libs'), assembly ('never concrete tech') and boot, each with its own wording, and a container library exception only by config; the driver has the inverse atom (driver-reach-closed).
Who may import blob appears in blob-quarantine, in the unit rules ('or blob'), in the assembly imports and in the driver text and matrix; consistent, but the same set stated five times.

Two rules are one atom with two suffixes, plus two scope modifiers. Test imports units (263-266) though the rule says only assembly, so the allowed importer list needs test mentioned or the rule is false for tests.

Each import atom restates whether type edges count; the general statement (881-883) says drivers and assemblies may type-import any layer, contradicting assembly-driver-only, driver-not-imported ('type imports included') and 'never a driver'; runtime-import's 'legal anywhere' contradicts the model and ports rows. The edge kind belongs inside each atom, once.

'Adapters only when a test is the caller' and its corollary are stated four times (461-463, 505-508, 1033-1035, 1215-1217); a constraint conditional on importers cannot be carried by a kind, it needs the importer-side clause.

IoC says 'no defaults, no exceptions' (380-381) and the test factory pattern says defaults are right (1221-1223): the same constraint with an except; it is solved by kind carriage (service and adapter carry it, assembly does not).
Stated in the prose three times (553-557, 567-571, 584-588) and again in the summary; the 'bound to a reader that counts it as blob' hatch stands outside every atom.
'A hook does not wire', 'no sub-driver call from a hook' and 'no adapter call from a hook' are consequences of one atom, restated in three other rules.

testKind: The test kind should carry: driver-reader-bound (the test reader cuts hooks), entry-not-imported (the runner is the only importer; it makes shared test code leave the kind), test-root-registration (the replacement for no-root-effect), no-root-mutable-binding and no-machine-at-root (isolation between tests; canon says stable-root exempts the registration, not mutable state), the universal import atoms layer-in-path, private-owner-only, port-import-type-only, no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle, and implied test-body-straight-line (reviewer legibility, 1150-1161). It should NOT carry no-concrete-import, closed-definitions, hook-body-is-call/hook-args-untouched/hook-result-untouched (a test body builds, calls and asserts, so several calls are its nature), wiring-callee-kinds, driver-reach-closed, wiring-args-closed or the assembly atoms (setup calls arbitrary fixtures and asserts), no-dependency-default (defaults are right in tests, 1221-1223). Test is not exempted from about ten rules: it simply does not carry those atoms, and it appears in the importer lists of unit-assembly-only and blob-importers-closed, which today omit it for units (270). No rule needs 'except test'. Open: whether tests carry no-ambient-access (determinism is wished at 1193-1194, never stated), and .e2e is named test kind (263) while 1022-1023 says end-to-end tests are neither, outside the graph, so either e2e leaves the test kind or the canon sentence goes.
helpers: Yes, the straight-line constraint must reach inside local helpers, and the way to do it is to attach it to the file's kind, not to a position: test-body-straight-line applies to every function defined in a test file (hooks and local helpers alike), including iteration callbacks and recursion, so no function in the file is a place to hide a branch or loop. A 'no' (hooks only) opens the laundering venue. The cost is paid honestly: a helper that needs a loop or branch (polling, fixture generation, a run() that retries) leaves the file and becomes a file of its own kind under canon's existing placement rule: a data builder is model, a fake or a CLI runner behind a port is an adapter, a test factory is an assembly function; there it is judged by that kind's atoms (and tested), and the spec file imports it. A local run() that merely wraps one call (start the CLI, return its output) stays local because it is straight-line. Helper reach through imports needs no extra rule: imported functions are judged where they sit.

atoms.name: inward-only
atoms.statement: An import never points to a higher rank in model < ports < service,adapter < assembly < driver < boot.
atoms.why: Each layer knows more of the system than the one before, so inner code stays testable without outer code.
atoms.check: Import edge between two declared kinds, compared by rank. Launch: yes. Type-edge scope is unspecified: lines 880-882 let driver and assembly type-import 'from any layer'.
atoms.landing: Reader knows an inner file cannot lean on an outer one.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: An import specifier resolves straight to the file that declares the layer; no barrel or index re-export.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site, or no matrix rule can be checked or reviewed.
atoms.check: Resolved target is not an index/re-export-only file. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The import path names the layer being imported.

atoms.name: kind-from-name
atoms.statement: A file's kind comes only from its name (flavor), or from a reader binding that agrees with it; no suffix means blob.
atoms.why: Every other atom is selected by kind, so the kind must be readable from the name alone.
atoms.check: Filename pattern plus reader glob. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: File name tells which constraints the file carries.

atoms.name: tech-import-scope
atoms.statement: Only adapters, drivers (their own tech) and tests import concrete platform/IO packages; model, ports, service, assembly and boot do not.
atoms.why: Contact with the world stays in the layers whose job it is, so every other layer runs without the world.
atoms.check: Import specifier resolves to a package or node: module that is not declared pure. Launch: yes, given tech-declared.
atoms.landing: Reader knows which files touch the world.

atoms.name: tech-declared
atoms.statement: A package counts as pure model, as a container, or as a driver's tech only if a declaration (config or a bound reader) says so; otherwise it is red or unclaimed.
atoms.why: Purity and tech-ness cannot be judged from the code's shape, and presuming either gives false guarantees.
atoms.check: Lookup of the import or name in config lists and reader claims. Launch: yes. The declaration is trusted, not verified.
atoms.landing: The set of trusted libraries and claimed tech is written down in one place.

atoms.name: blob-import-scope
atoms.statement: Blob is imported only by assembly, test and other blob, type imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any other importer loses its own.
atoms.check: Import edge whose target kind is blob. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Unplaced code is visible and cannot leak into a guaranteed layer.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (and test); type imports and files under private/ are exempt.
atoms.why: Composition units are built where the graph is built, so services never know the concrete graph.
atoms.check: Runtime edge whose target is a public service/adapter file and whose importer kind is not assembly/test. Launch: yes. Carries the 'not by blob', 'not by drivers', 'not by other services' cells.
atoms.landing: Only assembly files show which units are instantiated.

atoms.name: assembly-importers-closed
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers, tests and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract to depend on; consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: Edges whose target kind is assembly. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Reader knows who can reach the graph builder.

atoms.name: driver-importers-closed
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: A driver is started or registered, never depended on, so one hook cannot chain through another.
atoms.check: Edges whose target kind is driver. Launch: yes. Test files also call driver wiring functions (lines 634, 1021), so the allowed set must name test.
atoms.landing: Entry wiring reads as a tree from the boot.

atoms.name: root-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file or a test file.
atoms.why: They are entries the runtime or runner loads, so no edge may point at one.
atoms.check: Edges whose target kind is boot or test. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Entry points are the leaves of the import graph.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver makes no runtime import of model, and a pure library counts as model.
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service with a contract and a test, not logic parked in the driver.
atoms.check: Runtime edge driver to model, or to a package declared pure. Launch: yes; type imports are free (lines 881-883) while the matrix cell says 'cannot import'.
atoms.landing: The driver's imports show it holds no knowledge.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included; a nested service is outside its parent.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, whether or not it is implementation coupling.
atoms.check: Import path contains /private/ and importer is not under the owning service. Launch: yes, once service vs layer directory is defined (lines 808-814).
atoms.landing: A private/ path in a foreign import is an instant violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-package import graph is acyclic; every import kind counts, type-only included.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: Collapse files to service directories, find cycles. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a human can read in order.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Modules have no cycle through runtime imports; type-only edges do not count.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports fail silently in production as undefined.
atoms.check: File-level runtime graph cycle detection. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Load order is well defined.

atoms.name: ports-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file contains types only, no runtime statement or export.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it is an adapter not yet extracted.
atoms.check: Any non-type declaration or statement in a port file. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: A port file reads as pure shape.

atoms.name: port-edge-type-only
atoms.statement: Every import edge to or from a port file is type-only.
atoms.why: A port must stay a compile-time dependency; a runtime edge is a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: Import edges incident to port files lacking the type modifier. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The boundary never shows up in the runtime graph.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file's exported factory yields something assignable to a port interface declared elsewhere; all adapters of one port share that interface.
atoms.why: The inside must not know which adapter it talks to, so every adapter conforms to the one port shape.
atoms.check: Type-checker assignability of the factory result to a port type. Launch: yes with tsc; never stated as a rule, only through 'port implementation' wording.
atoms.landing: Each adapter is paired with the contract it fulfils.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory takes its dependencies through arguments without default values.
atoms.why: A default resolves a dependency outside assembly, scattering assembly logic and defeating code splitting.
atoms.check: Defaulted parameter in a service/adapter factory. Launch: partial; telling a dependency from a plain option is judgment.
atoms.landing: Assembly is the only place dependencies are chosen.

atoms.name: unit-has-assembler
atoms.statement: Every public composition unit is built by some assembly.
atoms.why: A unit declares 'I am built by assembly', and an unbuilt unit is dead or built where it should not be.
atoms.check: Reachability: an assembly or test imports the unit. Launch: partial; stated in prose only, in no slug.
atoms.landing: Every unit appears on the map as a built node.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: Model and service (and by implication assembly and boot) never read or call the environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis; callers hand them in.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: Free identifier resolving to a global in a closed name list, anywhere in the file. Launch: yes; the list is only named, not enumerated.
atoms.landing: Inputs of a model or service are all in its signature.

atoms.name: root-immutable-bindings
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax or type (primitive, as const, readonly, frozen literal); state lives in factory closures.
atoms.why: Tests importing a module must get the module every other test got, so nothing one runs changes what the next sees.
atoms.check: Root declaration plus type proof depth. Launch: yes; config can lift this half only (mutableModuleState).
atoms.landing: Module scope holds only facts, never state.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness); import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed fixed.
atoms.why: The stored value freezes the machine's state at load, so the file cannot be tested under another environment without a reload.
atoms.check: Initializer of a root binding reads an ambient or tech source. Launch: yes. Overlaps no-ambient-access for model and service.
atoms.landing: Config values arrive by argument, not by import-time capture.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation performs no effect: no call into tech, unclaimed names, use cases or local functions of side-effect layers, and no assignment or delete; a reader may declare calls effect-free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act, or testing it acts too.
atoms.check: Root statement kinds and callee resolution. Launch: yes; 'a shape nobody has written down yet' is judgment.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing visible.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory call (service, adapter, assembly or blob factory; a model function only if the flavor names it a factory); no use-case call, no call on a tech value.
atoms.why: The assembly decides nothing but which factory to call.
atoms.check: Callee file kind plus flavor word (create*). Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The wiring file reads as a list of constructions.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: The use cases an assembly may await are named by the project; any other use-case call there is red, and the resolution is the declaration.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, so only a declaration can.
atoms.check: Callee in a config list. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Every graph-shaping load is on a list.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: A call's result is never read, member-accessed, computed on or branched on; an assembly may pass it on or return it, a hook may only return it or drop it.
atoms.why: Touching a result is deciding or translating, which the outside may not do.
atoms.check: Dataflow of the result binding or expression. Launch: yes; a declared load's result is the one that may be read.
atoms.landing: Results flow through the outside unopened.

atoms.name: result-not-handed-on
atoms.statement: A hook's call result is not passed to another call, written, or logged.
atoms.why: Handing a result on chains a second call, so a sequence no service owns.
atoms.check: Result appears as an argument, assignment target or log argument. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: A hook is visibly a straight pipe.

atoms.name: args-underived
atoms.statement: Call arguments are literals, parameters or tech values (a field or destructured part is fine), or built instances; never a computed value.
atoms.why: An argument computed in the outside is logic the outside opened the door to.
atoms.check: Syntax of each argument expression. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: What goes into a factory or hook call is visible at a glance.

atoms.name: args-unread
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are its parameters whole, host values whole, instances or literals: no member read, no default.
atoms.why: Reading a field or defaulting a value is translation, which belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: Argument is a bare identifier or literal. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The event goes to the service as received.

atoms.name: no-result-condition
atoms.statement: No branch or loop tests an instance or a value computed from one; a condition may test a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness, with factory-call arms.
atoms.why: A decision on an instance's output is one the graph map cannot show.
atoms.check: Condition expression operands traced to parameters or load results. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: Conditional wiring depends only on inputs, visible in the signature.

atoms.name: no-control-flow
atoms.statement: A hook body holds no branch, loop or try; the call is unconditional.
atoms.why: A choice around the call is translation, which belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: Control-flow nodes in the function body. Launch: yes. A stronger form of no-result-condition.
atoms.landing: A hook reads as one line.

atoms.name: assembly-return-shape
atoms.statement: An assembly returns only services and shared model instances, and an adapter only when every importer of that assembly is a test.
atoms.why: The hexagon handed to the driver is its services; adapters sit outside it.
atoms.check: Return expression traced to factory kinds, plus importer kinds. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The driver gets the hexagon and nothing else.

atoms.name: definitions-closed
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind's one thing needs: assembly, assembly functions; driver, hooks plus at most one wiring function; boot, nothing. A definition is any function, class or variable.
atoms.why: Anything else is residue, logic with no contract and no test.
atoms.check: Declaration inventory against the kind's allowed set. Launch: yes; 'assembly function' is defined by the other assembly atoms.
atoms.landing: The outside file is a short list of known shapes.

atoms.name: driver-one-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver defines at most one wiring function, which a sub-driver exports with no hook; a root's takes no parameters.
atoms.why: The only thing a parent can do with a sub-driver is attach its callbacks.
atoms.check: Export and parameter inventory. Launch: yes; root arity follows only from the boot's no-argument call.
atoms.landing: One entry per driver file.

atoms.name: driver-callee-kinds
atoms.statement: Every call in a driver resolves to a use case on an assembly-built instance, an assembly function, a sub-driver wiring function, or a member of a claimed tech.
atoms.why: Any other callee is an effect or logic no contract covers.
atoms.check: Callee resolution by kind and reader claim. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The driver's call list is a closed set.

atoms.name: use-case-in-hook
atoms.statement: The one call in a hook is a use case, and use-case calls occur only in hooks; wiring calls occur only outside hooks.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place and hooks only connect events to use cases.
atoms.check: Call position (inside or outside a hook) against callee class. Launch: yes, given the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: Every hook shows the single use case it fires.

atoms.name: hook-at-most-one
atoms.statement: A hook makes at most one use-case call.
atoms.why: A sequence of two calls is a use case nobody owns, so it needs a facade service with a contract.
atoms.check: Count of calls in a hook. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: One arrow per hook on the map.

atoms.name: hook-at-least-one
atoms.statement: A hook makes at least one use-case call.
atoms.why: A hook with no use case is logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count of calls in a hook. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: No hook is a dead end on the map.

atoms.name: hook-nothing-else
atoms.statement: A hook body holds no statement other than the call: no assignment, delete or logging.
atoms.why: Any other statement is behavior the outside must not host.
atoms.check: Statement inventory of the hook body. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The hook body is the call.

atoms.name: driver-import-called
atoms.statement: A driver imported by a driver is used only as the callee of its wiring function, outside hooks.
atoms.why: It lets one entry split its hooks across files without letting one hook chain two calls.
atoms.check: Every reference to the imported binding is in callee position at a wiring site. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The driver tree is a registration tree.

atoms.name: listen-in-driver
atoms.statement: A callback handed to a claimed tech for it to invoke (a hook) exists only in a driver or a test.
atoms.why: Events enter the program in one place, the driver.
atoms.check: Reader cut finds a hook in a file of another kind. Launch: partial; an adapter's outbound call to the same tech is not told from listening by shape alone.
atoms.landing: Only drivers show where events come in.

atoms.name: driver-reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a reader bound by glob to its tech, or by a reader that counts it as blob on purpose; otherwise it is red.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading.
atoms.check: Kind driver or test with no matching reader glob. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The tech and the cut into hooks are named in one reader.

atoms.name: binding-agrees-flavor
atoms.statement: A reader binding gives a kind only to a file the flavor leaves blob, or agrees with the flavor; a contradiction is a config error.
atoms.why: A file has one kind.
atoms.check: Glob against flavor name. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: No file has two possible readings.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The entry only starts one thing.
atoms.check: Import list of the file. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: The boot is one import long.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot calls its driver's wiring function once, at module root, with no arguments.
atoms.why: Starting is the boot's one thing; the driver reads tech itself.
atoms.check: Root call count and argument count. Launch: yes.
atoms.landing: A boot is one line.

atoms.name: test-assert-in-hook
atoms.statement: Every assertion call appears lexically inside a hook body, not in a helper.
atoms.why: The reviewer must read the scenario in the test, not reconstruct it from helpers.
atoms.check: Calls the test reader claims as assertions, by enclosing function. Launch: yes with the reader; not stated as a rule, implied by lines 1152-1161.
atoms.landing: Expected results sit next to inputs.

atoms.name: hook-own-instance
atoms.statement: Each hook builds its own instance; no unit instance is bound outside a hook and used by two hooks.
atoms.why: Nothing one test does may change what the next sees.
atoms.check: Instance binding in the enclosing scope referenced by two or more hooks. Launch: partial; stable-root covers module root only, not describe scope.
atoms.landing: A test's whole scenario is visible inside it.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is overridden by unit-assembly-only (service to service, adapter to adapter) and by the matrix. Line 254 'Imports everything' contradicts the matrix and line 491 (no driver, no concrete). The test is outside the order, unstated here.
'Unenforceable by review' is the why, not a constraint.

Restates inward-only, tech-import-scope, tech-declared and blob-import-scope by induction over the import chain. 'False guarantees from partial extraction' is a theorem, not a constraint. Unclear whether the chain walks into node_modules; elsewhere packages are trusted on declaration.
'Side-effect-free and deterministic' and 'untestable' are judgment; only the declaration is mechanical.
The ambient name list is described, not enumerated. 'Depends on the machine it runs on' is the why. Scope over assembly and boot is implied, not stated.

'Build it and inject it behind a port' (assembly's use) is carried by assembly-calls-factories; 'behind a contract the service already holds' is typing judgment. 'Unplaced code needs characterization tests' is a wish.
Identical to service-assembly-only except for the filename; 'not by blob' is stated only here and in the sibling.

Not a constraint: an edge-class parameter (runtime vs type) that each atom must declare. Canon states it per rule with opposite answers: type imports count in private-sealed, blob-import-scope, assembly-importers-closed, driver-importers-closed, root-not-imported, no-service-cycle; they are exempt in unit-assembly-only; unspecified in inward-only, tech-import-scope, driver-no-model.

Scope parameter of unit-assembly-only: 'public' means not under private/. Leaves a gap: a unit factory building private/ sub-units (fractal assembly, lines 159-167) does assembly work in a service file under no atom.
'A sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is a diagnosis.
'If the service layer branches on which adapter it got' is not mechanically visible: the service imports no adapter, and no structural proxy is named.
Which directory is a service and which a layer directory (lines 808-814) is a naming convention to define.
The 'direction law' paragraph (817-826) restates it; the sharing progression (litmus 'delete a consumer') is judgment.
'Documented behavior', 'no implementation details' and the (a)/(b) unit-test exceptions are judgment. private-sealed on tests conflicts with 'imports anything' in test-is-outside: a ruling is needed.

'Imports anything, defines anything, hook count and services-only do not apply' is an exemption list; with atoms nothing attaches that needs lifting. 'Fixtures are adapters' and 'production config has no place in tests' (1200) depend on judging determinism. 'End-to-end tests are neither, outside the graph' is a scoping decision. Test edges count 'for rights and coverage, never use-case level' is accounting.

'A pipeline hiding in the wiring' is the why. 'Config is wired by default and loaded in the use case' is prescription. 'Shared instances flow down, never sideways' (497-503) has no defined tree to check. 'Behind the port that awaits it' is typing judgment. 'Tech value' is a definition (see helpers).
'Consumers type against service APIs' is guidance.
The reader that counts a driver as blob on purpose is an escape hatch inside the rule. Whether such a file is held to blob rules or driver rules is half stated ('stays imported only as a driver').

'Tech setup' is whatever the reader claims. Whether a branch or loop in wiring is legal is unstated, while assembly states its rule. 'A hook does not wire' is the same atom as hook-one-call's use-case-only. 'Lazy loading is an assembly importing another' is explanation.

Which functions are hooks comes from the reader's cut. 'A facade service is missing' and 'logic with no home' are diagnoses. Telling a use-case call from another call needs dataflow from the assembly's return. 'Ruled for the stock cut' leaves other cuts open.

'Never an adapter' repeats unit-assembly-only. 'An effect no contract covers' is a why. The matrix says drivers cannot import model, line 883 says the prohibition is about calls: runtime import of a model constant is undecided.
'Residue' is the why.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a per-reader exemption stated in prose only. 'Never data from the hexagon' reduces to the other atoms.
Test files call a driver's wiring function (634, 1021) yet the rule lists only boot and driver.
'A program has one per entry point' needs a defined entry point. 'Holds nothing' has no separate check beyond definitions-closed.

'A shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' is an open judgment clause. Exemption list (boot's call, spec registration) vanishes if boot carries boot-calls-once instead of root-no-effect and the test reader declares registrations effect-free. Proof depth of Readonly<T> depends on type resolution. The mutableModuleState opt-out already lifts only the first atom, confirming the split.
'Dependencies are injected through arguments' is a molecule of those five; 'the returned API is the contract' is judgment.
Outbound call versus listening is not told by shape.
'An adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' (277-278) and 'adapters absorb specifics' have no structural check.
'Tests are written for the reviewer', 'clever helpers' and 'data-driven indirection' are judgment; see helpers.

kinds.note: Most atoms of any kind; can import only model and declared-pure packages.
Ambient and root atoms hold trivially because the file is types only.
Model plus no-default-deps; a facade service is an ordinary service and carries nothing extra.
Does not carry tech-import-scope or no-ambient-access, which is the whole difference from service; no exemption needed.
Allowed importer of units and blob by the target atoms' importer sets. no-ambient-access is implied by 'tech values arrive as parameters'. Line 254 'Imports everything' contradicts line 491.
Does not carry tech-import-scope: its own tech is what the reader claims. Wiring-position control flow is unruled.
Carries boot-calls-once instead of root-no-effect, so stable-root's boot exemption disappears.

Never receives inward-only, tech-import-scope, blob-import-scope, unit-assembly-only, definitions-closed, hook-at-most-one, driver-callee-kinds, driver-no-model, args-unread, result-untouched, no-default-deps; test is an allowed importer in those atoms' sets. private-sealed is an open ruling.
No layer guarantees; blob-import-scope constrains its importers, not blob.

sharedParts.problem: One import ban is restated per layer with different words and different whys (testability, holds no tech, starts only); each kind would need its own copy and cannot take the atom a la carte.
