The same 'never read the result' constraint, with assembly allowing pass-on and hook forbidding it; one atom plus result-not-handed-on removes the two variants.
Argument rules are restated with a gradient of strictness (field read ok in assembly and wiring, forbidden in a hook, none in boot) with no common core.
One constraint at two strengths; hook's 'unconditional' contains assembly's weaker one, so a kind needing the weaker has to be handled by exception.
Same line is red twice in model and service (reading env at root) with different whys; diagnostics duplicate.
State at module scope is stated five times with different scopes; the test-isolation version also leaks into describe scope, which stable-root does not cover.
One mechanism with four parameter values, written as four rules; test becomes 'defines anything' only because no value was given.
The adapter-return exception is written three times and couples to assembly-importers-closed (only tests may import such an assembly), which no rule checks.
Two slugs for one constraint, plus restatements in the driver and blob rules; matrix cells for drivers duplicate them.
'A hook does not wire' appears three times in different words.
Stated three times; harmless duplicate, but test-is-outside re-states it without the blob-on-purpose escape.
Same shape (kind K imported only by set S, type included) written per rule; driver-not-imported omits test, which test-is-outside needs.
Stated five times, with the type-import clause worded differently from runtime-import's exemption.
The runtime/type split is rewritten in each rule; atoms must declare which edge class they count, or rules like inward-only stay ambiguous (lines 880-882).

A closed exemption list was needed because root-no-effect was bundled with the immutable-bindings clauses; with atoms, boot carries boot-calls-once and test's reader declares registration calls effect-free.
Restates four atoms transitively; no constraint of its own, so keeping it as a rule double-counts.

testKind: The test builds units, calls them and asserts; nothing imports it. It should carry the atoms that make a test deterministic and reviewable, and none that protect other layers from it. Carries: driver-reader-bound, binding-agrees-flavor, layer-in-path, root-not-imported, root-immutable-bindings, root-no-machine-read, root-no-effect (the test reader declares runner registration calls effect-free), hook-own-instance, test-assert-in-hook (implied), no-control-flow (on every function in the file, see helpers), assembly-return-shape (its setup may hand back adapters), no-runtime-cycle. Open ruling: private-sealed (canon says 'imports anything' and 'through the contract'). Does not carry: inward-only, tech-import-scope, blob-import-scope, unit-assembly-only, assembly-importers-closed, driver-importers-closed (test is an allowed importer in the sets, so no 'except' is written), no-default-deps (a test factory is assembly, so defaults need no exemption), definitions-closed, assembly-calls-factories, driver-callee-kinds, driver-no-model, hook-at-most-one, use-case-in-hook, args-unread, result-untouched, result-not-handed-on, hook-nothing-else (a test calls units, models and anything, and must read results to assert). The roughly ten exemptions in canon (imports anything, defines anything, hook count, services-only, registration at root, defaults in factories) are all atoms the test simply never receives.
helpers: Answer (my inference, not canon): yes, the straight-flow constraint must reach local helpers, and it should attach to the file's kind, not to the syntax of a hook body. A 'no' makes the helper a third thing between hook and assembly with no atoms, which is a laundering venue. Structure: (1) no-control-flow applies to every function defined in a test file, not only to hooks and not only to functions reachable from hooks; reachability fails on helpers passed as values (.map(run), tables of lambdas). (2) A local function has two admissible roles by what its body does: build-role (every call is a factory call: assembly atoms apply, so parameter-conditional branches with factory arms stay legal) or hook-role (no-control-flow, assertions stay in hooks per test-assert-in-hook). A run() that starts the CLI calls a use case, so it is hook-role: straight, no loop. (3) Anything needing flow leaves the file and lands in the kind it is, where its verb list judges it: data builder to model, shared test factory to assembly, matcher or runner registration to driver wiring (canon already says shared test code is placed by what it is). The loop is not banned, it is homed under rules; the closure stops at file boundaries because an imported helper is judged by its own file's kind. (4) The same hole exists one level up: describe-level loops and .each tables generate hooks, and neither root-no-effect nor no-control-flow looks at them (stable-root exempts registration calls); canon's own warning against data-driven indirection (1157-1159) is unchecked, so root-level control flow around registration needs a ruling. Assumption to verify: that a test hook need not be one call, only straight; canon exempts only the count.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file's runtime and type imports target only kinds at or below its own in model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be buildable, testable and reasonable without knowing what lies outside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: rank of importer kind vs target kind on every import edge.
atoms.landing: A file's suffix tells what it can possibly depend on.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service and assembly import no concrete module (platform/IO code, HTTP/DB clients, any package not declared pure).
atoms.why: A concrete import bypasses the ports, so the unit cannot be exercised without the machine behind it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import specifier vs the declared-pure list and the readers' claims (needs declared-not-presumed).
atoms.landing: Inside kinds are visibly world-free: nothing in their imports touches the machine.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: The file reads or calls no ambient environment global (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis, process), at module root or in a function, in a condition, a value or a call.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: references to a listed set of global names anywhere in the file (the list comes from the flavor/readers).
atoms.landing: What the file needs from the world is all in its parameters.

atoms.name: composition-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by files holding the assembly role; type-only imports and private/ files are outside the atom.
atoms.why: Dependencies are resolved in one place, so services never learn their implementations.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime edge to a non-private composition-unit file from an importer not in the assembly role.
atoms.landing: Reading any import in a service or adapter, you know it is never a concrete neighbour.

atoms.name: blob-closed-importers
atoms.statement: A suffixless (blob) file is imported, type imports included, only by assembly, test or other blob files.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any layer importing it loses the guarantees it declared.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge to a suffixless file from an importer kind outside {assembly, test, blob}.
atoms.landing: Debt is visible as a short list of legal importers; contamination cannot spread silently.

atoms.name: assembly-closed-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported, type imports included, only by drivers, assemblies and (as caller of a test factory) test files.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so consumers must type against the services it returns.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge to an assembly file.
atoms.landing: An assembly is only ever reached from the driver side; the map shows it as a pure feeder.

atoms.name: driver-closed-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported, type imports included, only by a boot or another driver.
atoms.why: The tech reaches a driver's hooks and nothing else may, or one hook could chain through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge to a driver file.
atoms.landing: The only way into a hook is the tech; reading the import graph confirms it.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file or a test file, type imports included.
atoms.why: The runtime starts a boot and the test runner starts a spec; an importer would make an entry a library.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: in-degree of boot/test files is zero.
atoms.landing: Entries are leaves: the program's starts and checks are listable.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service package imports a file under that service's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private may move without its neighbours knowing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path segment private/ vs importer's service package; layer directories are not packages.
atoms.landing: Any import path containing private/ from outside is an instant visible violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-package import graph, every import kind counted, has no cycle.
atoms.why: Services in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package graph SCC detection over all edges.
atoms.landing: The map of services is a DAG a reader can lay out left to right.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: The runtime (non-type) import graph between modules has no cycle, even inside one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports fail silently in minified production code.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-level SCC over runtime edges.
atoms.landing: Module load order is unambiguous.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: Every import path names the layer it imports from: no index/barrel file re-exports across layers.
atoms.why: Dependency rules are enforceable by shape only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: re-export-from across layers or an index file standing for several layers; specifier resolves to a file whose name/path declares its layer.
atoms.landing: A wrong import is spotted by reading its path, with no file to open.

atoms.name: port-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file contains no runtime code, and nothing imports or re-exports a port at runtime in either direction.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: emitted statements in a .port file; runtime-import edge to or from one (missing type keyword, side-effect import, runtime re-export).
atoms.landing: Opening a port file shows only shapes.

atoms.name: root-binding-proven
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is proven immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly array/record/map/set, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth).
atoms.why: The module root must be the same on every load so a test importing it gets what every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root bindings vs the proof forms; unresolvable named types prove nothing. Config mutableModuleState lifts this atom only.
atoms.landing: Nothing at root can change under a reader's feet; state is visibly in factories.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the tech, the clock, randomness or the environment (a module's own location excepted).
atoms.why: Storing it freezes load-time machine state, so the file cannot be tested under another environment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: initializer of a root binding reads a non-module-location global/tech name; no type annotation lifts it.
atoms.landing: Configuration enters through parameters, never captured at load.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-call
atoms.statement: No call at module root reaches the tech or an unclaimed name, runs a use case, or enters a local function of an effect-allowed file, unless the reading declares that call effect-free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act, or the file cannot be tested in its own right.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for calls the readers classify; partial for unclaimed ones (red until declared). A property read is presumed free.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing visible; effects only occur by calling a factory.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-statement
atoms.statement: No root statement other than declarations and imports acts when evaluated (assignment, delete and their like); throw is exempt.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a run-time-only statement there is a load-time side effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement kinds.
atoms.landing: The root of a file reads as declarations only.

atoms.name: root-imports-only
atoms.statement: An assembly or driver module root holds only imports and the function definitions its kind allows; any other root statement is red.
atoms.why: Each builds or wires inside its function, so nothing runs or hides at load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: top-level statement kinds.
atoms.landing: A reader scanning the root sees imports and named functions, nothing else.

atoms.name: defines-nothing-else
atoms.statement: Outside kinds define at run time only what their one job needs: assembly its assembly functions, a driver its hooks and at most one wiring function, a boot nothing.
atoms.why: Any other definition is logic hiding in a layer allowed to import anything.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: function/class/variable declarations vs the kind's allowed set; types are free.
atoms.landing: The file's list of names is its entire job.

atoms.name: args-no-compute
atoms.statement: An argument in a call in assembly, driver wiring or a hook is a literal, a tech value, or an instance, never a value computed there.
atoms.why: A derived argument means the layer opens the door itself and decides, where a service or adapter should.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression shape; a call or operator in an argument is red (join(cwd,'notes'), opts.cwd ?? process.cwd()).
atoms.landing: Every argument is traceable to where it came from, with no transformation.

atoms.name: hook-args-as-received
atoms.statement: A hook passes the event it was handed as received: nothing read off it, host values handed whole (process, not process.cwd()).
atoms.why: Reading or translating the event is a use case, and belongs to the facade service with a contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no member access/destructuring/default on the hook parameter or host value used as an argument.
atoms.landing: What the hook receives is what the service gets.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: The result of a call in assembly or a hook is only returned, awaited, or handed on, never read, computed on, member-accessed, branched on, written or logged (a declared load's result excepted).
atoms.why: The layer must not look into what it built or called, or a decision hides where the map cannot show it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow from the call result in the function body.
atoms.landing: Results pass through; nothing is decided on them here.

atoms.name: hook-call-count
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call: two is red, zero is red.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence nobody owns, zero hides logic with no home; both belong to a facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count of use-case calls in a hook body, hook cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: One arrow per hook on the map.

atoms.name: hook-bare-body
atoms.statement: A hook body holds nothing but its one call (returned or dropped): no other statement, call, log, assignment or declaration.
atoms.why: Anything else between event and call is translation, and translation is the facade's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement list of a hook body.
atoms.landing: A hook can be read in one glance.

atoms.name: body-straight-line
atoms.statement: A function body contains no branch or loop (if, switch, ternary, &&, ||, ??, ?., try, loops, iteration calls, recursion).
atoms.why: Control flow in a body is logic; a reader must see the scenario, not reconstruct it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow nodes plus a listed set of iteration calls and a local call-graph cycle check. Stated for hooks (unconditional); extended to test bodies only by 1152-1161.
atoms.landing: Bodies read top to bottom as given/when/then.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory: a composition unit's or assembly's, a blob's built behind a port, or a model factory; a model function that computes a value is never called.
atoms.why: The assembly's one right is build; any other call is its own logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus the flavor's create* name to split model factory from function.
atoms.landing: An assembly's body is a list of constructions.

atoms.name: assembly-wiring-branches
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show; it belongs to the owning service or adapter.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: origin of the condition's operands and the arm statements.
atoms.landing: Conditional graph shapes stay visible as wiring.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns only services and shared model instances, never an adapter.
atoms.why: Outside instances leaking to the caller give it a handle on effects with no contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return expression sources by kind.
atoms.landing: What a driver gets is a service surface.

atoms.name: adapter-returner-tests-only
atoms.statement: An assembly that returns an adapter is imported only by test files.
atoms.why: Only a test asserts on what its fakes recorded; any other caller would hold an adapter.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return kinds of the assembly cross-checked with importer kinds.
atoms.landing: Test factories are recognisable as test-only.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: An awaited use-case call in an assembly must be on the project's declared list of loads.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, so the project declares which ones the graph may depend on.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config lookup; undeclared is red and the fix is the declaration.
atoms.landing: The list of what an assembly may run is one short declaration.

atoms.name: driver-calls-services
atoms.statement: A driver calls only use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring functions and its own claimed tech, never an adapter or a model.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers; parsing and rendering are use cases of a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee kind and reader claim of each call.
atoms.landing: A driver's calls are the only edges leaving the outside, all to services.

atoms.name: driver-wiring-only
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver only wires: assembly calls, tech setup and sub-driver registration.
atoms.why: Wiring is done at one site and a hook does not wire; the driver's one thing is to connect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement and callee classification outside hook bodies.
atoms.landing: Setup is separated from event handling in the file.

atoms.name: wiring-import-only
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported by another file only to call its wiring function, at the right site: a boot at module root with no arguments, a driver during its own wiring, a spec in its setup with tech and instances.
atoms.why: The importer can only let it attach callbacks, so no hook chains a second call through an extra layer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every use of the imported name is the call of its exported wiring function.
atoms.landing: Sub-drivers are visibly registrations, not logic.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Without an exported hook the importer cannot do anything with the import but attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export set of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's surface is one function.

atoms.name: only-driver-listens
atoms.statement: Only a driver file receives the tech's events (a callback handed to a claimed tech as a hook).
atoms.why: Inbound there is nothing to abstract; events must reach the program at one place per entry.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs each reader to separate listening from outbound callback use; unreadable files are not judged.
atoms.landing: Where an event enters the program is findable by file kind.

atoms.name: boot-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The boot only starts the program; anything else imported is a second job.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list of a boot file.
atoms.landing: Every entry point names its one driver.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's module root holds exactly one statement beyond imports: one call to the driver's wiring function with no arguments.
atoms.why: Starting is the boot's one thing; the program has to execute somewhere.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement count and argument list.
atoms.landing: The only evaluated call of a program is on one line.

atoms.name: driver-reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver or test file is read by a reader bound to it, and a reader binding agrees with the flavor's kind.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading; the report must say what it could not read.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reader globs vs files of driver and test kind; mismatch is a config error.
atoms.landing: Which tech each driver listens to is declared.

atoms.name: declared-not-presumed
atoms.statement: A name or package counts as pure, as claimed tech or as an effect-free call only by explicit declaration; an undeclared one is red where a verdict depends on it.
atoms.why: The tool judges only what is declared; guessing would pass or block code on presumption.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: lookup in the pure list, the readers' claims and the declared loads.
atoms.landing: Every green verdict rests on a visible declaration.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A service factory's dependency parameters carry no default values.
atoms.why: Defaults import adapters or config into a service, defeating splitting and scattering assembly logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter initializers on service factories; no slug backs it.
atoms.landing: Every dependency in a service is visibly passed from outside.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file's public surface is typed against the port it implements.
atoms.why: The adapter is the outside's implementation of a boundary contract; without it nothing ties it to a port.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: implements/satisfies or type reference to an imported port; not enforced by any slug.
atoms.landing: Which port an adapter serves is readable in its first lines.

rules.remainder: Matrix cells without a slug: drivers cannot import model (871) while 880-883 says the driver prohibition is about calls (ambiguous). Assembly imports 'everything' (254) vs matrix forbids concrete (871).
none

'Pure, deterministic' third-party is a judgment until declared; 'becomes untestable' is the why.
Scope sentence (adapters and drivers allowed) is kind data, not an atom.
Why assembly may take it ('its rule bounds what it can do') is assembly-calls-factories; why test may is characterization of unplaced code (justification only).

Same atom as service-assembly-only, only the target suffix differs.
Not an atom: a scoping parameter (type edges exempt) of composition-assembly-only; other atoms state their own edge scope (type included or not).
Not an atom: scope clause (private/ exempt) of composition-assembly-only; private files still carry private-sealed.

HOLE: 'service branches on which adapter it got' has no structural mark; judgment. 'Ports shaped to inside's needs' (118-123) is a wish.

Direction law (817-826) is a consequence of this plus adapter-assembly-only, not a new atom.
none

HOLE: 'assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details' is judgment; only the import part (private-sealed for tests) is mechanical and canon never says tests carry it (test 'imports anything').

The bundling claim 'assembly and driver in one' is not an atom. Shared test code placed by what it is (1017-1021) has no check: a shared helper filed as blob passes. 'e2e are neither, outside the graph' (1022-1023) contradicts the .e2e suffix in the Test kind (263). 'Test edges count for rights and coverage, never use-case level' is a map annotation.
Wish: 'config wired by default and loaded inside the use case' (463-466); 'decides nothing but which factory to call' is the doctrine, enforced by the atoms.

'A hook does not wire' is hook-bare-body; 'laziness is the assembly's' is prose.
Test tech exempts the whole rule (1057), losing body-straight-line with it. 'A reader with a cut of its own says where the line sits' (614-615) is an open escape. The hook cut itself is the reader's.

Wiring-function signature (main takes nothing, sub-driver takes tech and instances) restates boot-single-call's 'no arguments'; a local parseFoo is residue only by the closed list.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is scope, belongs to the reader.

'One per entry point' has no structural mark (entry points live outside the code).

HOLE: 'a shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' (1088-1090) is an open judgment clause. Ambiguity: whether mutableModuleState lifts root-no-machine-read too (1107-1110). Exemptions by kind (boot call, spec registration) duplicate the reader's effect-free declaration (1115-1117).
Stated at 374-381 with 'No exceptions' yet no slug exists; tests are allowed defaults (1221-1223).

Judgment: 'legible as behavior statement', 'unit identifiable at a glance'. 'Clever helpers, data-driven indirection' is only a smell. No rule says a test may not branch or loop; the atom is implied here.
387-419 is the shared why of every closed verb list. Remainder: 'convenience does not enter', 'the last mile is taste'.

kinds.note: Universal import/graph atoms; carried by the importer side (private-sealed, cycles, layer-in-path) wherever a file imports.
Constrained by what it may depend on (import atoms) plus a stable root.
Root atoms are vacuous for a types-only file.
composition-assembly-only is carried as target. Orchestration-not-compute is a judgment hole.
No ambient-access or concrete-import atom: the tech is its business. Root atoms still apply, because root effects are not the adapter's job.
no-ambient-access is implied (holds no tech, 254, 435, 490). Verb atoms are the narrowest list; the import right is the widest.
Hook atoms apply to hook bodies; wiring atoms to the rest. May hold tech and ambient: no no-ambient-access.
Carries boot-single-call instead of root-no-effect-call, so the exemption is replaced by an atom of its own.

Plus the importer rights of assembly and of driver (composition-assembly-only, blob-closed-importers, assembly-closed-importers, adapter-returner-tests-only, wiring-import-only). root-no-effect-call holds with the test reader declaring registration calls effect-free.
Declares nothing; only its importers are constrained. Whether root atoms touch blob is ambiguous (1110-1113 names a blob's local functions).

sharedParts.problem: One closed-definition check stated three times with three allowed sets; the test kind gets an 'anything' exception because the bundle that includes it also includes the test's rights.

stable-root bundles four checks. The assembly sentence cites it but is stricter (root-imports-only). The spec registration exemption exists twice: kind exemption (1127-1128) and reader's effect-free declaration (1115-1117). Boot's exemption by kind could be an atom (boot-single-call).
Slug names only model and service; boot and assembly repeat it as 'holds no tech' in other words.
Same ban worded 'passed on or returned' vs 'returned or dropped'; inside assembly-builds-only the branch-on-instance ban is stated twice (result never branched on; condition on instance not wiring).
Argument shape restated per rule; wiring/assembly allow reading a tech value's field (440-442) while hook reads nothing (hook-args-as-received); one atom plus one stricter atom.
One import-use check worded three ways with different arguments and sites; the test case is stated only in a list of shared code.
Assembly said to import 'everything' (254) but matrix forbids concrete (871); the model-pure-library vs concrete line is a declaration, not a rule.
Same classification-by-declaration mechanism in five places, with different consequences (concrete / red unclaimed / presumed free), nowhere stated as one rule.

sharedParts.atom: assembly-closed-importers, driver-closed-importers, entry-not-imported, blob-closed-importers, composition-assembly-only, private-sealed
sharedParts.problem: One 'who may import X' check, a column of the matrix, restated per rule, with 'type imports included or exempt' decided differently by each; the matrix restates all of them as a derived table.
hook-one-call bundles count, no branch, bare body, args and result; the test exemption removes all of them, losing the no-branch part a test also needs.
The test factory is an exception to 'assembly returns no adapter'; it lives in the same atoms because test factories have no kind of their own.
Slug names drivers but its text and the test rule also cover test files.
One fact, a root wiring function taking nothing, stated at call site and at definition; neither has its own atom.

testKind: WHY GROUPS (method record): testable inside without the outside (112-114, 940-952, 1081-1086) -> inward-imports, no-concrete-import, no-ambient-access, root atoms; layer visible by shape (24-25, 759-766) -> layer-in-path; extraction independence/ownership (898-912, 993-997) -> no-service-cycle, private-sealed; ESM silent failure (914) -> no-runtime-cycle; contamination (936-961) -> blob-closed-importers; IoC, resolve in one place (378-381) -> composition-assembly-only, no-default-deps; logic hides where rights are wide (435-437, 643-650, 387-419) -> defines-nothing-else, assembly-calls-factories, hook atoms; translation is a use case with a contract (609-628) -> hook-args-as-received, hook-bare-body, driver-calls-services; decisions invisible on the map (477-479) -> result-untouched, assembly-wiring-branches; judged only through a declared reading (587-588, 942-943) -> driver-reader-bound, declared-not-presumed; entry started by the tech, no hook chaining (542-543, 636-639) -> entry-not-imported, driver-closed-importers, wiring-import-only, driver-exports-wiring; port is contract (136-137) -> port-types-only; reviewer reads suite as spec (1152-1161) -> body-straight-line (implied for tests).\n\nTEST KIND. A test builds units, calls them and asserts; nothing imports it. Carries: driver-reader-bound (a test reader), entry-not-imported, wiring-import-only (shared registrars), only-driver-listens, root-binding-proven, root-no-machine-read, root-no-effect-statement, root-no-effect-call (registration calls declared effect-free by the test reader, which replaces the stable-root kind exemption), private-sealed (implied: tests go through the contract, 1008-1010), body-straight-line on every function defined in the file, the universals, and the importer rights of assembly plus driver (composition units, blob, assemblies, driver wiring). Not carried: inward-imports and no-concrete-import (imports anything, 873), no-ambient-access (it hosts the tech, e.g. starts the CLI; determinism is a judgment, 1193-1194, hole), hook-call-count, hook-bare-body, hook-args-as-received, result-untouched, driver-calls-services (an assertion IS reading a result, so those verb lists contradict the job), defines-nothing-else (defines anything), the assembly verb atoms, no-default-deps (defaults wanted, 1221-1223). Why: test is not assembly plus driver; it takes their import rights (union) and none of their verb lists, since each verb list exists to stop logic hiding in a layer that imports anything, and for a test the equivalent guard is straight-line bodies. Because 'each test assembles its own instance' puts setup inside hooks, setup and assertion are not separable regions, so assembly's verb atoms cannot be applied to the setup half. Open flags: .e2e is listed as test (263) but 'neither' at 1022-1023; a shared helper filed as blob passes every check, so 'no shared test code is blob' has no checker.
helpers: The constraint must reach inside local helpers, but not as a call-graph walk from the hook. Structure: attach body-straight-line to the DEFINITION SITE, not to the hook. Every function defined in a test file (hook callbacks and local helpers such as run() alike) carries it, as a per-function check. That closes the laundering venue: a loop in a local helper is red where the helper sits. Iteration spelled as a call (.forEach/.map/test.each over data) and recursion count as loops: the atom lists iteration calls and checks local call-graph cycles. A helper that truly needs a loop or branch (poll until the server is up, retry) is no longer test code: it moves to a file that is placed by what it is (a test-purpose adapter, an assembly function, a model builder, a driver registrar, per 1017-1021), imported by the spec, where its own kind's atoms, tests and map presence apply. Code imported by a spec is therefore always some other kind (nothing is test kind except spec files, and nothing imports a spec file), so the hole cannot be re-opened by importing. The cost is a few more files, consistent with 'no rule reaches into service territory to be lenient' (418-419). Definition choices to settle: whether ??, ?. and default parameter values count as branches; whether a try/catch in a helper is a branch (it is, by structure).

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must be developable, testable and reasonable without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import edge, layer rank of importer vs imported (kind from flavor name). Type-edge scope for inside kinds is unstated (see helpers).
atoms.landing: Every arrow on the map points one way; the layer of an import is read from the path.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: An import specifier names the layer file itself; no index.ts or barrel re-exports.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the matrix cannot be enforced by tool or by eye.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no index files, no re-export-only modules, specifier resolves to a layer-declared file.
atoms.landing: A reviewer sees the layer crossed from the import line alone.

atoms.name: chain-purity
atoms.statement: A layer guarantee holds only if the whole transitive runtime-import chain honours the same constraints, unlabeled and third-party files included.
atoms.why: Partial extraction otherwise produces false guarantees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: transitive closure of imports, each node judged by the other atoms. It is the other atoms applied transitively, not a second check of its own.
atoms.landing: A green label can be trusted without opening its imports.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file whose kind holds no tech imports no concrete platform/IO module (node:fs, HTTP clients, DB drivers, an undeclared third-party library, a runtime container unless declared in config).
atoms.why: Tech is reachable only through a port (outbound) or a driver (inbound); anywhere else it bypasses the contract and makes the file untestable or a hiding place for logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: specifier classified concrete by builtin list plus declared packages; third-party counts concrete until declared pure.
atoms.landing: The reader knows a file touches no machine without reading it.

atoms.name: no-ambient-global
atoms.statement: A file whose kind holds no tech reads no ambient global (env, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) at any position: root, function, condition, value or call.
atoms.why: Code reaching the machine without an import depends on the machine and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: identifier/member references against the reader-or-flavor global list; distinct from no-concrete-import because no import is involved.
atoms.landing: Time, randomness and the environment are visible as parameters of the unit.

atoms.name: no-blob-import
atoms.statement: An importer imports no blob file, type imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so importing it contaminates a layer that had some.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: imported file's kind is blob (suffixless or reader-bound as blob); carried by every kind but assembly, test and blob.
atoms.landing: Blob is visible as debt and enters the graph only at assembly or a test.

atoms.name: no-unit-import
atoms.statement: An importer imports no public composition unit (.service.ts, .adapter.ts) at runtime; type-only imports and imports of files under its own private/ do not count as edges here.
atoms.why: Composition happens in one place, assembly, so services never bind to their adapters or to each other and chunks follow the assembly graph.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import edge to a public unit file; carried by every kind but assembly and test.
atoms.landing: The concrete graph exists in one file kind only; a service import line is a red flag at a glance.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: private/ is the only boundary.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer path vs target path under a private/ segment, service package membership.
atoms.landing: private/ in an import path is an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: service-dag
atoms.statement: Service-package edges, every import kind counted, form a directed acyclic graph.
atoms.why: A cycle makes neither service extractable, movable or reasonable alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package-level graph built from all imports (types too), cycle detection.
atoms.landing: Services can be reasoned about and moved independently; the map is a DAG.

atoms.name: module-dag
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules form no cycle, even inside one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM works in dev and fails silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-level runtime import graph cycle detection; type-only edges ignored.
atoms.landing: No opaque undefined at load in minified output.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A port file contains no runtime code or logic, only types.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it is an adapter not yet extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any statement that emits JS in a .port file.
atoms.landing: Opening a port shows only the shape the inside needs.

atoms.name: port-type-edges
atoms.statement: No runtime import edge touches a port file, in either direction.
atoms.why: A runtime edge on a type-only file is always a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing `type` keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import edge whose source or target is a port file.
atoms.landing: `import type` on a port path is the only legal sight.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: Every adapter implements the one interface of the port it serves, with the same result shape for all adapters of that port.
atoms.why: The inside must never know or need to know which adapter it talks to.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: adapter's exported value assignable to the port interface (type checker); the shape part is checkable, the 'service never branches on the adapter' part is not.
atoms.landing: Replaceability: the port name tells what any adapter file offers.

atoms.name: root-immutable-binding
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax: primitive type, `as const`, readonly array/record/map/set, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth.
atoms.why: A stable root is what lets a file be tested in its own right: a test gets the module every other test got and nothing one test runs changes what the next sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: type/syntax proof per root binding; unresolvable named types prove nothing; lifted wholesale by config `mutableModuleState: true`.
atoms.landing: State is only in factory closures; a module exports factories, never instances.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness); a module's own location (import.meta.url, __dirname) is not one.
atoms.why: The stored value captures the machine at load time, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: initializer of a root binding contains a reader-claimed or global machine read; needs the reading to tell what is tech.
atoms.landing: No constant secretly frozen from the environment.

atoms.name: root-no-assignment
atoms.statement: No module-root statement is an assignment, a delete or the like; imports, declarations and types only.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a statement meaningful only at run time is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement kinds. Config setting does not lift it.
atoms.landing: Loading a file does nothing.

atoms.name: root-no-call
atoms.statement: No module-root call reaches the tech or something no reading claims, runs a use case, or goes into a local function of a side-effect-allowed file; a property read is presumed free, a call is not, until the reading declares it effect-free.
atoms.why: A call at root acts at load, so the file is not stable and the next test sees its trace.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root call callee classification by reader and layer. Boot and test carry their own root-call atom instead (boot-one-call, root-registration-only).
atoms.landing: A root call is either absent or the one the kind owns.

atoms.name: no-dependency-defaults
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives no default value to a parameter that is a dependency.
atoms.why: Defaults create static imports from the service to its adapters or config and scatter assembly logic across service modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers on factory parameters; telling a dependency from a plain argument needs the parameter's type (port/service API).
atoms.landing: All dependencies appear at the call site in assembly.

atoms.name: outside-chain-only
atoms.statement: An outside-kind file is imported only by the next kind outward on the chain: assembly by drivers and assemblies, a driver by a boot or drivers, a boot and a test by nothing, type imports included.
atoms.why: The outside is one chain boot, driver, assembly drawn as arrows on the map; an assembly has no contract to depend on and a driver's hooks must not be reachable from elsewhere.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kinds of a file of that kind.
atoms.landing: Who can reach the outside is known without opening anything.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A run-time definition (function, class, variable) in an outside-kind file is only one of the kind's named functions: assembly functions for assembly, hooks plus at most one wiring function for a driver, nothing for a boot.
atoms.why: Anything else defined there is logic with no contract, port or test; the widest import rights carry the narrowest verb list.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations by name/position per kind, hooks cut by the reader. Ambiguity: local const bindings of built instances inside assembly functions (see rules).
atoms.landing: The outside holds nothing but named entry points, so it can be read as one arrow.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a build: a factory of a composition unit, of another assembly, of a blob file, a model factory (flavor's create*), or a use case the project declared as a load.
atoms.why: An assembly decides nothing but which factory to call; any other call is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, flavor name for model, config-declared load list.
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as the graph itself; a use-case call there is a pipeline hiding in the wiring.

atoms.name: result-opaque
atoms.statement: The result of a call is only passed on as a bare argument, returned, or (in a hook) dropped; never read, member-accessed, computed with, written, or logged. A declared load's result is a tech value, not subject to this.
atoms.why: The layer's one thing is to carry what it got, never to look into it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every use site of a binding holding a call result; sink set differs by kind (assembly: factory argument or return; hook: return or drop).
atoms.landing: Nothing in the outside inspects what it moves.

atoms.name: no-arg-derivation
atoms.statement: An argument in a wiring call, assembly call or hook call is a literal, an instance, or a tech value; never computed in place (no call, operator, default or transform).
atoms.why: A computed argument is the outside opening a door that belongs to the service or adapter receiving the value.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: expression form of each argument; tech value field reads allowed in assembly/wiring, not in a hook (no-event-read).
atoms.landing: Arguments are things already named.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-closed
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value, against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are builds.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or on a value computed from one is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: provenance of the condition operands, shape of the arms.
atoms.landing: Conditional graph shape follows config or options, visibly.

atoms.name: adapter-return-tests-only
atoms.statement: A function returning an adapter has only tests as callers.
atoms.why: Production consumers type against service APIs; adapters come back only so a spec can assert on what its fakes recorded.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return value kind plus callers' kinds in the graph.
atoms.landing: A returned adapter announces a test factory.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file has a reader bound by glob; a file no reader reads is red, and the way out is binding a reader (possibly one that counts it as blob).
atoms.why: Hooks, tech and exemptions exist only through a reading, so no driver atom can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding lookup. Precondition atom, not a constraint on code itself.
atoms.landing: The tech each driver listens to is declared, not guessed.

atoms.name: tech-listener-driver
atoms.statement: Only a driver or test file receives the tech's events: a callback handed to a claimed tech in any other kind is a violation.
atoms.why: The driver is the one place the program receives events, so on the inbound side nothing else needs abstracting.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callback passed to a reader-claimed tech call in a file of another kind; no slug carries it today.
atoms.landing: The map shows where the program is started by the world.

atoms.name: claimed-tech-only
atoms.statement: A driver's tech is only what its bound readers claim; an import or name no reader claims is unclaimed and red.
atoms.why: Without a claim the checker cannot tell tech from logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: imports and global names in a driver vs the reader's claim list.
atoms.landing: The way out is stated: a reader that claims it.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver imports no model (runtime) and calls none, a pure library included.
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service, so a model in a driver is a model without a test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import/call to a model file or an unclaimed pure library.
atoms.landing: Drivers are about tech, never about the domain.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-closed
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver's calls are assembly calls, tech setup and sub-driver registration only; a hook does not wire.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place and one place only so hooks stay events handed to use cases.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee kind outside hook bodies vs reader-claimed tech; hooks cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: The driver's top level is a boot sequence of the tech.

atoms.name: hook-call-count
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one call, and it is to a service use case, not an adapter, a model or blob; zero or two is red.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence nobody owns that belongs in a facade service with contract and test; zero is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call count in hook bodies, callee kind. Test tech does not carry it.
atoms.landing: A driver link to a service is one arrow and nothing more.

atoms.name: hook-body-bare
atoms.statement: A hook body holds nothing but the call: no branch, loop, declaration, assignment, try/catch or second expression.
atoms.why: A branch, error mapping or printing in a hook is translation, which belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds in hook body (await and return of the call allowed).
atoms.landing: Reading a hook costs one glance.

atoms.name: no-event-read
atoms.statement: A hook reads nothing off what the tech handed it and hands the event or host value whole (`opts`, `process`), never `opts.files` or `process.cwd()`.
atoms.why: Reading the event is the translation a facade service owns, with a contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: member access or call on hook parameters or host globals.
atoms.landing: The hook proves it translates nothing.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports at most its one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: If the only thing importable is the wiring function, another file can only let it attach callbacks, never chain two hooks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: exported declarations of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: subdriver-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, during its own wiring, passing tech and instances, never from a hook and never with hexagon data.
atoms.why: A call from a hook or a handed-on use-case result would let one hook chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: uses of the imported binding are call sites at wiring level with closed-set arguments.
atoms.landing: A large entry point splits across files without any new place for logic.

atoms.name: boot-one-import
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The boot starts the program: one thing, one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list of the boot file; read by flavor kind, no reader.
atoms.landing: Entry point legible in one line.

atoms.name: boot-one-call
atoms.statement: A boot's module root is one call to the imported driver's wiring function, with no arguments, and nothing else.
atoms.why: It is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and that call is the start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement list shape.
atoms.landing: The program's start is a single line.

atoms.name: root-registration-only
atoms.statement: The only calls at a test file's module root are registration calls into the test runner that the test reader claims.
atoms.why: The runner owns those calls and they only register hooks, so load stays free of other effects.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root call callee vs reader's registration list. Exclusive alternative to root-no-call and boot-one-call, never combined with them.
atoms.landing: A spec's root reads as a list of test registrations.

atoms.name: test-body-linear
atoms.statement: A test body is straight-line: no branch or loop, so given, when and expect read in order; the constraint holds for every function a spec file defines.
atoms.why: The reviewer reads tests as the behavioural specification, so the scenario must be visible in the test and not reconstructed from indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for control-flow statements in spec hooks and in functions defined in the spec file; the 'clever helper' judgment is not checkable.
atoms.landing: Each test is a behaviour statement.

atoms.name: binding-agrees-flavor
atoms.statement: A reader binding that names a file's kind differently from the flavor is a config error; a binding may only give a kind to a file the flavor leaves blob.
atoms.why: A file's kind must stay readable from its name.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config consistency pass, not a code check.
atoms.landing: The kind in the path never lies.

none
none, but it is a scope (transitivity) on other atoms, not a constraint of its own.
'pure, deterministic third-party' is not provable by structure; only a declaration can carry it. 'untestable' is the why.

none; the why of the assembly and test exceptions ('bounds what it can do with it') is carried by assembly atoms, not by this slug.
none
none
A scope modifier (type-only edges exempt from no-unit-import), not a constraint; restated per rule elsewhere.
A scope modifier (private/ files are not public units) on no-unit-import.
'a sign the adapter has not been extracted' is a diagnosis.
'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' and 'same result shape' are not mechanical in general; only assignability is.
