Almost all of it: 'documented behavior', 'implementation details', 'contract' are judgment; only the no-private-import slice is structural. Hole.

'assembly and driver in one' is a bundle label, not a constraint; its exemption list (hook count, services-only, stable-root registration, imports anything, defines anything) is the symptom. 'by the shape of the test tech' and 'end-to-end tests are neither' are descriptive.

'decides nothing but which factory to call' is the why; 'a pipeline hiding in the wiring' a diagnosis. Hole: 'definition' counts variables, yet assembly binds built instances to consts, and canon does not say they are exempt. Return-only-services is derived from the rest.
none
none; same statement appears three times in prose.
'tech setup' means whatever the reader claims.
'for a tech that answers by return value' and 'where the view model is the tech's' are reader-cut territory; 'a facade service is missing' is a diagnosis.
'never an adapter' duplicates no-unit-import and hook-call-count; 'a pure library is model' needs declared purity.
'residue' is a diagnosis.
'a parent component rendering a child is not this rule' is reader territory.
none
'holds nothing, touches no tech' follows from shape; 'one per entry point' is not checkable as written.

'the shapes below are the known ones, not a closed list ... judged by the rule' is an open judgment clause; 'a property read is presumed free' is a presumption. Exemptions (boot call, spec registration) are separate atoms by kind. 'throw is not one' is a ruling.
'decisions, not compute', 'orchestrates', 'if you cannot name the use cases you have a utility bag', use-case level labels: all judgment, no slug.
'holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's', 'absorbs specificity', the port test 'can I meaningfully define a port': judgment.

'production config has no place in tests', 'fixtures follow sharing rules', 'agents encouraged to use the pattern': wishes or judgment. Determinism of tests is claimed but no atom checks ambient reads in a test.
Stated in prose only, no slug.
Stated in prose only, no slug.

kinds.note: The most constrained kind. Bundle-selection by atoms is exact; no exemption needed.
Root and ambient atoms are vacuous since no runtime code exists.
Model code inside a service file is judged by service atoms, which are a superset of model's.
Carries no concrete or ambient atom: that is its job. Whether no-dependency-defaults reaches adapters is unstated (implied by 'dependencies genuinely external are injected').
No-ambient-global is implied by 'holds no tech' (canon states it only for model and service). Does not carry no-unit-import or no-blob-import: those are the permissions the kind exists for.
Carries no no-concrete-import and no ambient atom: its claimed tech is its business. Hook-level atoms are scoped to hook bodies by the reader's cut.
Carries boot-one-call instead of root-no-call; most atoms are satisfied by the one-import one-call shape.

Carries root-registration-only in place of root-no-call. Not carried: inward-imports, no-concrete-import, no-ambient-global, no-blob-import, no-unit-import, closed-definitions, hook-call-count, hook-body-bare, no-event-read, no-arg-derivation, result-opaque, no-dependency-defaults, assembly-* atoms.

Canon is silent on whether the root atoms reach blob; 'no layer guarantees' suggests not. Imports blob freely (blob claims none), but no-unit-import (service/adapter files not importable by blob) applies.

sharedParts.problem: Same atom stated twice scoped by target kind (service, adapter), a third time as 'driver never calls an adapter', plus the matrix cells (adapters cannot import adapters); two scope modifiers (runtime-import, public-unit) are stated as rules instead of as the atom's scope.
'Never computed with, member-accessed' for an assembly and 'never read, written, handed on or logged' for a hook are one idea with different sinks, worded twice.

Argument vocabulary (literal, tech value, instance) is repeated in three rules with a different tech-value read right: assembly may read a field, a hook may not (no-event-read). Also overlaps result-opaque when an argument is computed from an instance.

Three rules and the prose ('assembly, driver and boot define nothing at all') each state a kind-specific allow-list for definitions; the 'nothing but assembly functions' clause also contradicts instance-binding consts.
'Who may import me' is restated four times, plus the web recognition rule, with type-import scope restated each time.

Boot's one call and spec registration are exemptions of stable-root. Split by kind instead: root-no-call (most), boot-one-call (boot), root-registration-only (test); exclusive alternatives, none carried with another.

Model bullet ('no module-level mutable state'), service bullet ('module-level code must be stateless'), test isolation ('no shared mutable state') and 'nothing at module root but imports' all restate it; stable-root is itself three or four atoms (binding, machine-read, assignment, call) with one why.
Stated as service-purity, as 'model depends on nothing concrete', as 'assembly never concrete tech' and as 'boot touches no tech'; one specifier check, four wordings, four scopes.
Stated for model and service in ambient-access and again in model bullet and service bullet; assembly's version is only implied.
Stated three times in prose and once as a slug; test-is-outside restates it for tests.
'Unclaimed is red' is stated in the terminology, in driver-reader and in driver-calls-services.

Test exemption is stated two ways: hook-one-call says 'the test tech exempts the count', test-is-outside says 'hook count and services-only do not apply'; whether the rest of hook-one-call reaches a test hook is unsettled, hence the unease.
private/ exemption stated as a matrix cell ('private/ of own service'), in public-unit, and via nesting rules.

Which import kinds count (runtime vs type) is restated per rule: exempt in runtime-import, counted in blob-quarantine, private-sealed, assembly-driver-only, driver-not-imported, no-service-cycle; excluded in no-runtime-cycle. Import-kind scope should be one parameter per atom, not prose per rule.

testKind: Test files carry the atoms that protect isolation and the shared graph, and none that exist to make logic unable to hide in a file nobody reads. Carried: reader-bound (a test reader gives hooks and registration), tech-listener-driver, outside-chain-only (nothing imports a test file), root-immutable-binding / root-no-machine-read / root-no-assignment (a spec's root state would leak between tests, which is stable-root's own why), root-registration-only in place of root-no-call, subdriver-wiring-only (a shared registerMatchers), private-sealed and service-dag (test edges count), layer-in-path, and test-body-linear (implied: the reviewer reads the test as the spec). Not carried: inward-imports, no-unit-import, no-blob-import, no-concrete-import and no-ambient-global (a test builds units, imports blob for characterization tests and uses controlled production adapters or fakes); closed-definitions (it defines anything, but see helpers); hook-call-count, hook-body-bare, no-event-read, no-arg-derivation, result-opaque (a test hook builds, calls several times and asserts on results, which hook-one-call and result-opaque forbid in a driver hook); assembly-calls-build, wiring-branch-closed, adapter-return-tests-only (setup is inside hooks); no-dependency-defaults (defaults are right in test factories). The reason: nothing imports a test, so atoms that guard importers or consumers have nothing to protect; the test is the one kind whose body IS behavior, so atoms that make bodies boring would empty it. Hole: canon claims determinism for tests yet no atom checks ambient reads in a spec.
helpers: Yes, the constraint must reach the helpers; 'no' reopens exactly the laundering venue the closed-definitions atoms were written to close. Structure that avoids it: scope test-body-linear to every function DEFINED in a spec file (hooks and local helpers alike), not to hook bodies and not to the call graph from a hook. Per-definition scoping is cheap and mechanical, whereas call-graph reachability fails on callbacks, aliases and passing a helper as a value. A run() that starts the CLI is straight-line, so it stays legal. A helper that truly needs a branch or loop (polling, a table expansion) is red in the spec, and its exit is canon's own placement rule, which already exists: shared test code is not test kind, so it moves to a file of the kind it is (fake becomes an adapter, test factory an assembly function, data builder a model, shared hook a driver wiring function) where that kind's atoms judge it and where its own tests apply. Residual leak, to be confessed: a loop inside a shared model data builder imported by the spec is legal by its own kind; the guard is that the call sits visibly in the test body and the builder is itself tested. Note this also dissolves the contradiction in the half-bundle: the spec file is no longer 'assembly and driver in one' but a kind carrying a selection (reader-bound, root atoms, registration, linear definitions), with no exemptions.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file's import edges (runtime and type) go to its own rank or lower in model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot, with test at the top.
atoms.why: [G1 inside ignorant of outside] The inside must not know the outside exists, or it cannot be built, tested or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolve each import to a file kind and compare ranks; the narrower matrix cells come from other atoms, not from this one.
atoms.landing: Every arrow on the map points one way, so the layer of a file tells what it may know.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file of a kind that may not touch the world imports no concrete module (node builtins, I/O, HTTP, database packages); a third-party package counts as pure only if declared so.
atoms.why: [G2 world is handed, not discovered] A file that reaches the world itself bypasses its ports and cannot be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with config: classify each import specifier as pure, concrete, container or claimed tech by declaration, then compare with the kind's allowed classes (model, ports, service, assembly, boot).
atoms.landing: Reading the import list shows at once whether the file can reach the machine.

atoms.name: no-ambient-global
atoms.statement: A file of a kind that may not touch the world names no global for environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis, in any position.
atoms.why: [G2] Code that discovers its environment depends on the machine it runs on and cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: free-variable and member-root names against the global list, at root or in a function, in a condition, value or call.
atoms.landing: Every input of the file is visible in its parameters.

atoms.name: composition-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service or .adapter file is imported at runtime only by assembly (and test); type-only imports and files under private/ are outside the atom.
atoms.why: [G3 assembly sole resolver] Assembly is the only place dependencies are resolved, so services never know the concrete graph and bundlers can split along assembly.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import edge whose target is a composition unit outside private/, importer kind not in {assembly, test}.
atoms.landing: A composition unit's importers are all assemblies, so the chunk graph and the wiring graph are the same thing.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory's dependency parameters carry no default values.
atoms.why: [G3] A default dependency puts assembly logic and a static import inside the service module.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter initializers in service and adapter factories (a default that needs an import, a global or a call is already caught by the import and ambient atoms).
atoms.landing: The factory signature lists every dependency, none hidden behind a fallback.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service package imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: [G5 ownership] Visibility is ownership: private/ is the one boundary behind which a service may change freely.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import path contains private/ and the importer sits outside the owning service directory.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import path in review is an instant, visible violation.

atoms.name: blob-gate
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import blob, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: [G9 blob contamination] A layer that imports blob inherits code with no guarantees and loses its own.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target file has no layer suffix and no reader binding; importer kind not in {assembly, test, blob}.
atoms.landing: Blob debt is visible as the set of assembly and test imports that reach it.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: Every import path resolves to a file whose own name declares its layer; no index or barrel file re-exports across layers.
atoms.why: [G4 layer visible by shape] If the layer is not visible at the import site, the dependency matrix cannot be enforced by tooling or by review.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import resolves to a kind-named file and not to an index or re-export file (bare model.ts is the degenerate declaration).
atoms.landing: The path of any import tells the layer it comes from with no file to open.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A .port file holds only types, no runtime statement or value.
atoms.why: [G5 contract] A port is a contract; runtime code in it means an adapter has not been extracted yet.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any non-type statement in a port file.
atoms.landing: Opening a port file shows only the shape of what the inside needs or offers.

atoms.name: port-edge-type-only
atoms.statement: Every import into or out of a port file carries the type keyword.
atoms.why: [G5] A contract has no run-time presence, so a runtime edge on it is a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import declaration lacking import type where the importer or the target is a port file.
atoms.landing: Runtime graphs never contain port nodes.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An .adapter file type-imports a port and exports a value conforming to that port's interface, the same interface and result shape as every other adapter of that port.
atoms.why: [G1] The inside codes against the port and never learns which adapter it talks to, so adapters must absorb source specifics and conform.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with tsc: assignability of the adapter factory's return to the imported port type (the second source of truth is the TS checker).
atoms.landing: An adapter reads as the translation of one named port into one technology.

atoms.name: no-adapter-branching
atoms.statement: Service-layer code does not branch on which adapter it was given.
atoms.why: [G1] A branch on adapter identity means the port did not finish abstracting the outside away.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: instanceof, tag or kind comparisons on a port-typed value are visible; the rest is judgment.
atoms.landing: A service reads the same for every adapter that could be plugged in.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The graph of edges between service packages, every import kind included, has no cycle.
atoms.why: [G6 extractability] Services in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files to their service package, then find cycles in the package graph.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a reader can walk from leaves to roots.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: The graph of runtime imports between modules, within one service or across, has no cycle.
atoms.why: [G6] Circular imports in bundled ESM work in dev and fail silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: cycle detection on runtime import edges only (madge or dpdm style).
atoms.landing: Module evaluation order is a straight line.

atoms.name: importer-gate
atoms.statement: An outside kind is imported only by kinds from its list, type imports included: assembly by drivers, assemblies and tests; a driver by boot, drivers and tests; a boot and a test by nothing.
atoms.why: [G8 outside is boring] The outside kinds have no contract and are started or entered, never depended on.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: for each file of these kinds, every importer's kind against the list, ignoring the type keyword.
atoms.landing: A reader knows nothing depends on an assembly, driver or boot except what starts or fires it.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: No module-root binding holds state the syntax does not prove immutable (primitive type, as const, readonly shapes, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its proven depth); modules export factories, never instances.
atoms.why: [G7 stable load] Nothing a test runs may change what the next test sees, and state lives in factory closures reached by argument.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: type and initializer of each root binding against the proof list; a named type the reader cannot resolve proves nothing; config mutableModuleState lifts this atom only.
atoms.landing: A module's import brings nothing that can change, so state is found only inside factories.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-capture
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the tech, the clock, randomness or the environment; the module's own location (import.meta.url, __dirname) is presumed fine.
atoms.why: [G7] A file holding what differs from one load to the next cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: taint of root initializers by globals and claimed-tech reads; a call result is judged at the call.
atoms.landing: No constant in the file secretly depends on where or when it loaded.

atoms.name: root-calls-inert
atoms.statement: No call at module root unless it is declared effect-free: calls to tech or to anything no reading claims, to a use case, or into a local function of a side-effect-layer file are red; property reads are free.
atoms.why: [G7] Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: classify each root call by callee kind and claimed tech; the reader of the claiming tech may declare a call effect-free.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing observable.

atoms.name: root-no-side-effects
atoms.statement: No root statement acts when evaluated: no assignment, no delete, nothing like them (a throw is not one).
atoms.why: [G7] Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a statement that only makes sense at run time is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds at module root.
atoms.landing: Root statements are declarations only.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly builds: a composition unit's factory, another assembly's, a blob factory injected behind a port, or a model factory (flavor-named); no model function, no use case.
atoms.why: [G8] A file with the widest import right must do almost nothing, or it becomes the place where logic hides.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, and for model callees the flavor's factory name (create*), by config.
atoms.landing: Reading an assembly shows only which factories are called, a graph the map draws as boxes and arrows.

atoms.name: assembly-no-touch
atoms.statement: What a call in an assembly returned is only passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed (a declared load's result excepted by declared-load).
atoms.why: [G8] A decision on an instance is one the map cannot show; assembly never looks into or touches what it built.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: result-flow analysis of each binding built in an assembly.
atoms.landing: Instances are opaque tokens moving between factories.

atoms.name: plain-arguments
atoms.statement: A call's arguments in assembly or driver wiring are literals, tech values (a field or destructured part may be read, never called) or instances; never a value derived by a call or computation.
atoms.why: [G8] A derived argument is the assembly or driver opening the door itself; the unit that needs the value derives it under its own rules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: expression kinds of argument positions, tech-value provenance from parameters.
atoms.landing: Every argument is either typed in place or handed through, so nothing is computed in the outside.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-shape
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: [G8] Such a condition is a choice of graph the map can show, unlike a condition on an instance's output.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand provenance plus arm statement classification.
atoms.landing: Conditional wiring is readable as variants of the graph.

atoms.name: declared-load
atoms.statement: An assembly awaits only use cases the project declares as loads, and a load's result counts as tech values from then on.
atoms.why: [G8] Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for its effect, so the project names them.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with config: callee against the declared list; undeclared call is red, resolution is the declaration.
atoms.landing: The few use cases the graph depends on are listed in one place.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and adapters only when every caller of it is a test.
atoms.why: [G3] Consumers type against service APIs, and an adapter handed out is an effect outside any contract, except fakes a test asserts on.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return expression kinds of assembly functions, plus caller kinds from the import graph.
atoms.landing: An assembly's return type reads as the program's services.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A kind defines only what its one right needs: assembly its assembly functions, a driver its hooks and at most one wiring function, a boot nothing; assembly and boot hold only imports at root.
atoms.why: [G8] Any other definition is logic hiding as blob under a label, residue with no contract and no test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: definition kinds (function, class, variable) in the file against the kind's list; hooks identified by the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: Opening an outside file shows only imports, wiring and hooks.

atoms.name: root-wiring-nullary
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes no parameters and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: [G8] The boot calls it with no arguments and touches no tech, so the driver is where the tech is read.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter list of the exported wiring function, root versus sub-driver by importer kind.
atoms.landing: main() is the one place the program meets process or document.

atoms.name: driver-reader
atoms.statement: Every driver file and every test file has a reader bound to its tech (a reader that counts it as blob counts as a bound reader).
atoms.why: [G11 checkability] Every driver rule is judged through the reading, so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config glob coverage of driver and test files; unread is red; kind-versus-binding mismatch is a config error.
atoms.landing: Each driver's tech and hook cut is declared, not guessed.

atoms.name: wiring-outside-hooks
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver only wires: assembly calls, tech setup (parser, server, mount), sub-driver registration.
atoms.why: [G8] Wiring is done in the driver's wiring function and nowhere else; a hook does not wire.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: classify each call outside hook bodies by callee (assembly, claimed tech, sub-driver wiring).
atoms.landing: A driver reads as setup followed by hooks.

atoms.name: hook-calls-use-case
atoms.statement: Every hook contains at least one use-case call.
atoms.why: [G8] A hook with no use case is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee classification inside each hook body (hooks cut by the reader).
atoms.landing: Every event visibly lands on a use case.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: Every hook contains at most one use-case call.
atoms.why: [G8] Two calls mean the sequence between them is a use case nobody owns, which needs a facade service with a contract and a test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count of use-case calls in the hook body.
atoms.landing: One arrow per hook on the map.

atoms.name: hook-body-bare
atoms.statement: A hook body is only the call, awaited or returned or dropped: unconditional, nothing else, and its result is never read, written, handed on or logged.
atoms.why: [G8] Whatever is done around the call is translation, which is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: AST shape of the hook body and use of the call's value.
atoms.landing: The hook reads as a pure link, so the outside is understood without opening it.

atoms.name: hook-args-as-received
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are what the event handed it as received, host values whole (process, never process.cwd()), instances and literals; nothing read off them.
atoms.why: [G8] Defaults, reads and mapping on the way in are translation, which belongs to the facade.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expressions are parameters or the literal, with no member access or call.
atoms.landing: The facade's contract can be read as exactly what the tech hands over.

atoms.name: driver-imports-closed
atoms.statement: A driver's runtime imports are assemblies, other drivers and tech a bound reader claims; an unclaimed package, a pure library, a model, a composition unit or blob is red (type imports free).
atoms.why: [G8] Anything else a driver imports is logic or tech nobody has read.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import classes against the matrix row and the reader's claims.
atoms.landing: A driver's import list is its whole world.

atoms.name: driver-callee-closed
atoms.statement: A driver calls only use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring functions and its own claimed tech; never an adapter, never a model, never an unclaimed name.
atoms.why: [G8] An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers, and parsing or rendering is a use case of a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee provenance by result flow from assembly and by claimed names.
atoms.landing: Every call in a driver is either a service call or tech plumbing.

atoms.name: sub-driver-wiring
atoms.statement: An imported driver's binding is used only as a call to its wiring function, inside the importer's own wiring, passing tech and instances, never a hook or a use-case result.
atoms.why: [G8] Otherwise one hook could chain two calls through a level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: usage sites of each driver-kind import.
atoms.landing: A driver tree reads as hooks grouped by file.

atoms.name: tech-listened-by-driver
atoms.statement: Only driver files hand callbacks to a claimed tech for it to call back; adapters call the tech outbound.
atoms.why: [G8] The driver is the one place the program receives the tech's events.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callback arguments to claimed-tech calls by file kind, but claims come from driver-bound readers and listening is not distinct from calling without a cut.
atoms.landing: Every entry from the outside world is in a driver.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, type imports included.
atoms.why: [G8] The boot's one right is to start the program through its one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list of the boot file.
atoms.landing: The entry reads as one import.

atoms.name: boot-calls-wiring
atoms.statement: A boot's only statement is one call, at module root, to that driver's wiring function with no arguments.
atoms.why: [G8] The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and it carries nothing else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement list of the boot file and call arity.
atoms.landing: The entry reads as one call.

atoms.name: root-registration-only
atoms.statement: Root calls in a test file are only registrations on the test tech's runner.
atoms.why: [G7] The runner owns registration, so it is the one root call a spec needs; any other root call acts on load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root call callees against the test reader's registration set.
atoms.landing: A spec's root reads as a list of registered tests.

atoms.name: test-body-straight
atoms.statement: No function defined in a test file branches or loops.
atoms.why: [G10 reviewer reads scenarios] A test reads as given-when-then only if the scenario is visible in the body rather than hidden in control flow.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: if, switch, loops, ternary and the reader's iteration calls in every function body of the file.
atoms.landing: Each test reads top to bottom as one scenario.

atoms.name: test-owns-instance
atoms.statement: A test builds its own instance: no instance or mutable binding is declared in a scope shared by several hooks.
atoms.why: [G7 and G10] Isolation is structural: each factory call has its own closure, and no state is shared between tests.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: binding scopes in a test file against the hooks that use them.
atoms.landing: Each test shows the instance it builds.

kinds.note: The edge atoms (layer-in-path, private-sealed, blob-gate, composition-gate, cycles) are carried by every kind as importer; they differ only by allowed-set data. The widest verb list is none, so model needs no exception.
Types only; adds the two port atoms to the model's import atoms.
A composition unit and a target of composition-gate; model logic inside it needs no allowance, because it carries no model-only atom beyond these.
Does not carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-global: reaching the world is its business.
Widest import rights, so the longest verb list; no-concrete-import has a declared container-library allowance in its classification, not an exception. No reader bound.
No stable-root exception needed (each builds inside its function).
Carries boot-calls-wiring instead of root-calls-inert, so stable-root loses its boot exemption. No reader bound.

Union of the rights (rank top, importer sets that name test), not of the verb lists; canon's rule that the widest import rights carry the narrowest verb lists is met only by the three test-specific atoms.
Edge atoms only; stable-root scope for blob is unstated in canon (it names blob as a layer allowed side effects but declares no guarantees).

sharedParts.problem: One constraint is restated per kind (model L295, service L341, test L1013 and L1196, assembly 'nothing at root but imports') and then carved by a closed exemption list in stable-root; the exemptions disappear once boot and test carry their own root-call atoms.
`const T = Date.now()` in a model or service is red by both the stored-value half of stable-root and ambient-access (canon defers: 'judged where it sits'), giving two diagnostics for one fact.

The same check is worded as 'cannot depend on concrete' (service), 'holds no tech, never concrete tech' (assembly), 'touches no tech' (boot) and 'unclaimed is red' (driver), each with its own scope; one import classification (pure, concrete, container, claimed tech) with kinds picking allowed classes covers all.
Stated for model and service, implied for assembly and boot only through their closed verb lists; also applies to chain-purity as a derived rule.

Two slugs for one atom with two scopes; its 'not by model, ports' half repeats inward-imports; the importer set says 'only assembly' in rule text while test imports services by exemption; edge kind (runtime-only) and private/ scope live in two further slugs.
Stated 'lateral OK' while composition-gate forbids service-service and adapter-adapter edges; the matrix intersects several atoms, so its cells appear to be rules of their own when they are not.

Four statements of 'who may import this kind', each repeating 'type imports included' because runtime-import's global type exemption does not apply; the test version is stated as 'imported by nothing' in two places.

Stated in blob-quarantine, the matrix, the 'assembly and driver are not blob' prose, and again with 'not by ... blob' in the composition rules (which is the opposite edge direction, composition-gate).

One argument-shape constraint in three rules; assembly and wiring allow reading a field off a tech value, a hook allows no read at all, so the strict variant is hook-args-as-received on top of the base.
One 'defines only what its one right needs' atom with a per-kind list, written as four rules and one exemption ('test defines anything').

'A hook does not wire', 'translation around the call' and 'never a model, parsing and rendering are use cases' are the same why (translation is the facade's) stated in three rules; hook-one-call alone holds five atoms.
One constraint stated from both ends (boot passes nothing; main takes nothing); it holds on one side and tsc closes the other.
'Returns adapters only to tests' makes the atom depend on callers' kinds (importer-gate), a cross-file check, and the test-factory section restates it a third time.
Stated 'no exceptions' for composition units and reversed as 'right here' for test factories without naming the scope: the scope is the kind (service and adapter factories, not assembly or test).

Test is said to import 'anything' (test-is-outside, matrix) while test-through-contract bans implementation details; the consistent reading is 'any layer, any kind, but private/ only of its own service'.

testKind: Test files (.spec, .test, .e2e) carry the edge atoms with permissive importer sets or top rank (inward-imports at top, blob-gate and composition-gate listing test, layer-in-path, private-sealed for the service the test sits in, no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle), driver-reader, importer-gate with the empty set, and root-bindings-immutable, root-no-machine-capture (moderate confidence, from determinism, L1192-1194) and root-no-side-effects. They also carry three atoms that give them the narrow verb list that canon's own rule 'widest import rights carry the narrowest verb lists' (L234-236) demands: root-registration-only (the runner's registration is the only root call), test-body-straight (implied by 'data-driven indirection ... hides the scenario', L1156-1158), and test-owns-instance (L1196-1198; same why as root-bindings-immutable one scope inward). They do not carry: no-concrete-import and no-ambient-global (fixtures and controlled production adapters reach the world; tests of adapters must), closed-definitions (defines anything, until helpers are decided below), every assembly-* atom, every hook-* atom and driver-callee-closed and driver-imports-closed (a test body builds, calls several units and asserts), plain-arguments, wiring-outside-hooks, root-wiring-nullary, no-default-deps (test factory defaults are right, L1221-1223), the boot atoms, and tech-listened-by-driver (the runner is the tech listening to the spec). Reason: nothing imports a test, so any atom whose why is about importers (composition-gate, importer-gate as target, stable-root's 'a test that imports it gets the module every other test got') is empty or moot, and a test is not assembly and driver by verb lists, only by the union of import rights; it exempts about ten rules in canon because it carries none of the verb atoms of either, which is why the label is a metaphor, not a bundle. Mismatches to settle: .e2e is listed as test kind (L263, L567) yet L1022-1023 says end-to-end tests are 'neither' and 'outside the graph'; and 'imports anything' (L265, L873) versus private-sealed.
helpers: Answer: yes, the no-branch-no-loop constraint must reach inside local helpers, but not by tracing calls from test bodies; it attaches to every function defined in a test file (test-body-straight is a definition-level atom of the test kind, not a hook-level one). A 'no' opens the laundering venue; a 'reaches only helpers called from hooks' answer lets a loop hide behind a callback or an alias, and needs call-graph analysis. Per-file, per-function scope needs none and cannot be indirected. What keeps run() legitimate when it must loop (collect output, poll, retry) is that control flow has a legal home elsewhere: shared test code is already 'placed by what it is' (L263-266, L1217-1219), so a run() that starts the CLI and loops is a test-purpose adapter or assembly function in its own file of that kind, where it carries that kind's atoms and, for an adapter, its own port and tests; a straight-line run() (build, call, return) stays local. Consequence for canon: 'defines anything' (L265, L1016) narrows to 'defines only straight-line functions, literals and registration calls'; closed-definitions then reaches the test kind with that list. Remaining holes to judge: iteration by call (.map, .forEach, test.each) is a loop only if the test reader lists those callees, and data builders are model files, so a loop in an imported builder is allowed but visible as a model with its own tests. Why groups used in the tags: G1 inside ignorant of outside; G2 world is handed, not discovered; G3 assembly the sole resolver; G4 layer visible by shape; G5 contract and ownership; G6 extractable graph; G7 stable load, independent tests; G8 outside is boring, one right per kind; G9 blob contamination; G10 reviewer reads scenarios; G11 checkability precondition.

atoms.name: no-outward-import
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or a layer inside it.
atoms.why: The inside must be developed, tested and reasoned about without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer and importee kinds from the flavor, compared on the order model < ports < service,adapter < assembly < driver < boot; every import edge, type-only included.
atoms.landing: A reader sees from a file's suffix which layers it can possibly lean on.

atoms.name: concrete-import-gate
atoms.statement: Platform/IO code (node:fs, HTTP clients, DB drivers, undeclared packages) is imported only by kinds whose one job is the machine: adapter, driver (its claimed tech), blob, test.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine cannot be exercised through its ports, so any kind above that line loses its testability.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: import specifier classified concrete / pure-declared / claimed-tech from config declarations; purity is declared, never presumed; a declared container library is the one configured entry for assembly.
atoms.landing: Concreteness is visible at import sites: no concrete import means nothing in the file touches the world.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: A suffixless file is imported only by assembly, test and other blob, type imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any layer importing it contaminates a guarantee it had.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee has no layer suffix, importer kind not in {assembly, test, blob}.
atoms.landing: Debt stays visible: blob appears only at graph-building and characterization sites.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (test also), never from its own private/ siblings' restriction.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place dependencies are resolved, so an import of an implementation elsewhere re-couples what IoC decoupled.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind in {service, adapter}, not under private/, edge not type-only, importer kind not in {assembly, test}; scope flags: private/ files exempt, type-only edges exempt.
atoms.landing: Every concrete implementation is reached from the assembly graph only, so the map's wiring is the whole story.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers, other assemblies (and tests), type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so nothing may type or call against it except what fires or builds with it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind assembly, importer kind not in {driver, assembly, test}; type edges count.
atoms.landing: One glance at an assembly's importers shows who builds the hexagon; services type against service APIs, never the wiring.

atoms.name: driver-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver (and a spec calling a shared wiring function), type imports included.
atoms.why: A driver is entered by the runtime through the boot or mounted by a parent driver, never reached from inside the program.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind driver, importer kind not in {boot, driver, test}; type edges count. The WHY is thinly stated in canon: inferred from 'node runs the boot, the runner runs the spec, the framework mounts the component'.
atoms.landing: Tech never leaks inward through a call chain; the entry tree is a plain tree of drivers under a boot.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: No file imports a boot or a test file.
atoms.why: These files act when loaded (start, register), so loading them from anywhere else would carry that act into the stable module root everywhere else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind in {boot, test}: any import edge is red.
atoms.landing: The entry points are leaves of nothing: the reader knows what starts the program and what the runner loads.

atoms.name: private-seal
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from that service's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is hidden must stay movable by its owner alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee path contains private/, importer outside the owning service folder.
atoms.landing: A private/ in an import path is an instant red flag: ownership is readable from the path.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Service packages form a DAG over every import kind, type-only included, test edges included.
atoms.why: A cycle between services means neither can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: service-level graph from file edges and service boundaries; any cycle is red. The nested-adapter direction law is its consequence.
atoms.landing: The service map is a drawable DAG.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Modules do not import each other in a runtime cycle, even inside one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in minified production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: module graph over runtime (non-type) edges.
atoms.landing: Load order is a plain tree; nothing depends on evaluation order luck.

atoms.name: no-barrel-import
atoms.statement: An import path names the layer file it takes from, never an index.ts that re-exports.
atoms.why: The layer rules are enforceable only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee is an index/barrel re-exporting other files.
atoms.landing: The path alone tells a reviewer which layer an import comes from, with no file to open.

atoms.name: root-immutable-bindings
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by its syntax or type (primitive, as const, readonly shapes, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth).
atoms.why: A file stays testable in its own right only if loading it gives every test the same module and nothing a test runs changes what the next one sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root binding's declaration/type proof; unresolved named types prove nothing; the mutableModuleState opt-out lifts this atom alone.
atoms.landing: State lives in factory closures only: an instance exists where it was called and is reached by argument, never import.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the machine (env, clock, randomness, tech); the module's own location is exempt.
atoms.why: Such a binding fixes the machine's state at load time, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: a root binding's initializer reaches a global/tech/clock/random read; import.meta.url and __dirname excluded.
atoms.landing: Every value at root is the same on every run: constants mean constants.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation performs no side effect: no call into the tech or unclaimed code, no use-case call, no call to a local function of an effect-allowed file, no assignment or delete statement.
atoms.why: A file whose loading acts or leaves things behind cannot be imported by a test without the act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements and calls classified by callee (reader-claimed registration calls declared effect-free, boot call exempt by kind); throw is not an effect.
atoms.landing: Importing a file is always safe: loading never does anything.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A model or a service never reads the environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis from a global; they arrive as arguments or through a port.
atoms.why: Code reaching them depends on the machine it runs on and cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: references to a global list in any position (root, function, condition, value, call); adapters and drivers exempt by not carrying it.
atoms.landing: Inputs are visible in signatures: nothing is discovered behind the reader's back.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind allows: assembly functions only (assembly), hooks plus at most one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot).
atoms.why: Outside kinds hold no logic, so a definition there is blob hiding under a label and logic with no contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations in the file (function, class, variable) against a per-kind allow list; hooks and wiring functions excluded by the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: The outside is the most boring part of the program: its contents are only the allowed shapes.

atoms.name: wiring-fn-signature
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes nothing and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: The boot calls with no arguments, so tech is read only inside a driver, and a sub-driver gets everything from its parent.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter list of the wiring function against the driver's role (imported by a boot or by a driver).
atoms.landing: A reader sees where tech enters: once, at the root driver.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is to a composition unit's factory, another assembly, a blob file's factory, or a model factory.
atoms.why: An assembly decides nothing but which factory to call, so the graph it builds can be drawn on the map.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee resolved to file kind; model callee must match the flavor's factory name (create*); a model function that computes is red; await is the call.
atoms.landing: An assembly reads as a list of constructions; it cannot hold a hidden sequence.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: The only use-case call an assembly may make is a load the project has declared in config.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load the graph depends on from a use case run for its effect, so the declaration is the evidence.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: use-case callee in an assembly checked against the project's declared load list; the resolution of a red is the declaration.
atoms.landing: Every use-case run inside the wiring is a named, declared exception, not an accident.

atoms.name: args-no-compute
atoms.statement: Arguments to a call in assembly, wiring or a hook are literals, received tech values, or instances, never derived by calls or operators.
atoms.why: A derived argument is the outside opening the door itself: computation belongs to the unit that needs the value, under that unit's rules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: expression form of each argument (literal, parameter or destructured part, built instance reference).
atoms.landing: What a call is handed is exactly what the reader sees named nearby.

atoms.name: result-passed-on
atoms.statement: The result of a call in assembly or a hook is only passed on, returned or dropped, never branched on, computed with, member-accessed, written, logged or handed on.
atoms.why: The outside never looks at what comes back, so no decision or translation can live there.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of the call's value in the enclosing function; await is the call; a declared load's result is classed as a tech value.
atoms.landing: The map's one arrow per link is the whole truth about the link.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or its output is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition expression operands (parameter/loaded value vs literal), arm statements are build calls.
atoms.landing: Conditional graphs stay drawable: variation is by config, never by behavior.

atoms.name: adapter-return-gate
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and an adapter only if every caller of that assembly is a test.
atoms.why: A driver handed an adapter could call it, an effect no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return expression's value kinds and the importer set of the assembly file.
atoms.landing: The reader knows an adapter in an assembly's return implies a test factory.

atoms.name: driver-read
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file has a reader bound to it by glob (or one that counts it as blob on purpose).
atoms.why: What a hook, a call or tech is depends on the technology, so no driver rule can be judged without the reading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file kind from flavor, reader binding from config; a binding naming the file differently from the flavor is a config error.
atoms.landing: Every driver's tech is explicit and declared: no silent default reading.

atoms.name: tech-must-be-claimed
atoms.statement: Every import or global name a driver uses as tech is claimed by a reader bound to it; an unclaimed one is red.
atoms.why: Without a claim the checker cannot tell tech from residue, so no verdict on that name can be given.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: names and imports in a driver matched against the bound readers' claim lists; a pure library is model, red regardless.
atoms.landing: The driver's tech is a declared list, not whatever happened to be imported.

atoms.name: hook-call-count
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call and no other call, wiring included.
atoms.why: Two calls make a sequence no service owns and zero make logic with no home: both want a facade service with a contract and a test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: hooks cut by the reader (stock cut: every callback handed to claimed tech); count of use-case callee calls and other calls in the body, await counts.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow, so the outside can be reasoned about without opening it.

atoms.name: hook-straight-line
atoms.statement: A hook body has no branch or loop around its calls.
atoms.why: Control flow in a hook is logic nobody tests; a straight line is read as one statement of what happens, whatever the kind.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no if, switch, ternary, loop, iteration method with callback in the body. Canon states the driver why (translation has no home); the test why (reviewer legibility, 1150-1161) is a second one: see sharedParts.
atoms.landing: A hook reads top to bottom with no state to simulate.

atoms.name: args-whole-event
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event, the host value and instances to its call whole, reading nothing off them.
atoms.why: Choosing a part, defaulting or reshaping the event is translation, and translation is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no member access, destructuring, default or operator on the hook's parameters or host values in call arguments (opts, never opts.files; process, never process.cwd()).
atoms.landing: The facade's contract is the event itself: argv in, text out.

atoms.name: driver-callee-kinds
atoms.statement: A driver calls only use cases (inside hooks), assembly factories, sub-driver wiring functions and claimed tech (outside hooks), never an adapter, a model or unclaimed code.
atoms.why: An adapter call is an effect no contract covers and a model call is a use case (parsing, rendering) with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind plus position (inside or outside a hook) per the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: The outside only builds, fires and attaches; every real call lands on something with a contract.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A sub-driver exports exactly one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: If the only thing importable is wiring, the parent can only let it attach callbacks, never chain two calls through it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export surface of a driver file imported by another driver.
atoms.landing: One entry per driver file: the way a CLI splits across files is visible by shape.

atoms.name: only-driver-listens
atoms.statement: Only a driver hands callbacks to claimed tech; elsewhere tech is only called outbound, behind a port.
atoms.why: The inbound side then has one place and nothing to abstract, so a driver technology is never a port.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: a callback handed to a claimed tech outside a driver file; needs a reader's claim list to apply outside drivers.
atoms.landing: Where events enter the program is a short, known list of files.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one
atoms.statement: A boot imports a single driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: A boot starts the program and does nothing more.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: the import list of a boot file is exactly one driver.
atoms.landing: The entry is one arrow to the root driver.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot makes exactly one call at module root, to its driver's wiring function, with no arguments.
atoms.why: One call to its one driver is the whole start; the boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements are that single call, zero arguments; reads no tech name.
atoms.landing: What runs when the program loads fits in one line.

atoms.name: ports-type-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds only types and no runtime edge touches it in either direction.
atoms.why: A port is a contract, and runtime code in it means the adapter has not been extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime statements in a .port file; a runtime import from or of a port file is a runtime re-export, side-effect import or missing type keyword.
atoms.landing: Opening a port shows only the shape the inside needs.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file exposes a factory whose result conforms to a port type it type-imports.
atoms.why: Replaceable adapters absorb the outside's specifics into the port's one shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: the exported factory's return type is assignable to a .port type via the TypeScript engine; 'absorbs specificity' stays judgment.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the port it serves, so the map draws its single edge.

atoms.name: no-adapter-branch
atoms.statement: The service layer never branches on which adapter it was handed.
atoms.why: A branch on the adapter proves the port has not abstracted the outside away.
atoms.check: LAUNCH weak: instanceof or discriminator comparisons on an injected dependency; a service cannot import adapter classes, so only tag/kind-string tests are catchable.
atoms.landing: Replacing an adapter never needs a service edit.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A service factory gives its dependency parameters no default values.
atoms.why: A default pulls an adapter or config source into the service, scattering assembly logic and defeating code splitting.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: default initializers on the factory's dependency parameters in a service file.
atoms.landing: Assembly is the only place a reader looks for what was chosen.

atoms.name: no-blob-test-support
atoms.statement: A blob file imported only by test files is red: it is shared test code placed as blob.
atoms.why: Shared test code is placed by what it is (adapter, assembly, model, driver), or it hides logic under a label no rule reads.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer set of a blob file contained in the test kind.
atoms.landing: Test helpers cannot sit unruled under the blob label.

rules.remainder: Says 'see the matrix for the combined result': the matrix is the intersection of other rules, not a rule.
None. Kind-by-suffix (flavor) is the helper that makes it checkable.

Owns no atom: it is a theorem of the per-edge atoms. Left over: purity of third-party packages' own transitive imports, never checked; 'partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a claim, not a check.
'Pure, deterministic' is judgment, resolved only by declaration.
None beyond overlap with root atoms for a read at module root.

Same atom as adapter-assembly-only; scope differs only by importee kind.
Same atom as service-assembly-only.
Owns no atom: a scope parameter (runtime edges only) of unit-assembly-gate, restated by other rules with the opposite value.
Owns no atom: a scope parameter (public, not under private/) of unit-assembly-gate.
'Sign the adapter is not extracted yet' is a diagnosis.
'The port has not finished abstracting' and 'same result shape' are judgment.
None.
None.
None.
Everything: 'documented behavior', 'no implementation details', 'how it calls and what it asserts' are judgment. The only mechanical shadow is private-seal and no-barrel-import on test imports.

It lists exemptions, not atoms: whitelist membership in four importer gates, absence of closed-definitions, hook-call-count, driver-callee-kinds, tech-must-be-claimed. Judgment left: 'same isolation rules' and fixture determinism; e2e declared 'neither' yet named by flavor.
A seven-atom molecule. Left: 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' (prose, 497-500) has no check.
Whitelist omits test, while canon has tests calling assemblies (505-508, 1213-1217).

'A facade is missing' is diagnosis; hook cut is the reader's judgment per tech; 'the test tech exempts the count' is an except clause.
'A pure library is model and red regardless' needs the declared-pure list.
'Residue' is a diagnosis.

Whitelist omits test (spec calls registerMatchers, 633-634, 1217-1219).
'One per entry point' cannot be counted by structure.

'A shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' is an open judgment; the exemptions (boot, spec registration) are by kind, and the reader's effect-free declaration is a second mechanism for the same thing.
'No exceptions' contradicts 1221-1223 (defaults are right in test factories).
'Domain machines, entities' and 'what the service knows' are judgment.
'It orchestrates; it does not compute', 'if you cannot name the use cases it is a utility bag' are judgment words.
'Holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's', 'absorbs specificity' are judgment.
'Is this line doing its layer's one thing?' is the unifying question; not itself a check.
'The child's role picks the direction' is judgment.
'Slice the port to what the service asks for' is judgment.
'Production config has no place in tests', 'fixtures deterministic', 'controlled side effects' are judgment unless config adapters are declared.
'Legible as given/when/then', 'clever helpers', 'DRY-ed setup that hides the scenario' are judgment; the only mechanical proxy is the straight-line atom, canon never states it for tests.
All judgment: test at the hexagon boundary, (a)/(b) exceptions, kernel litmus, 'never misc', distillation signals.

kinds.note: Graph-wide atoms on edges; blob only as a gated importee or importer.
Boot, test included. Canon silent on blob: assumed no guarantee.

Root atoms trivial on a type-only file.
Gate atom is carried as importee.
Ambient and concrete reach are allowed by simply not carrying their atoms.
Importer whitelist includes tests.
Importer whitelist includes tests (registerMatchers).

Plus the two universal groups. Appears as an allowed importer in unit-assembly-gate, blob-import-gate, assembly-importers, driver-importers. Registration calls pass root-no-effect by the reader's effect-free declaration.
