inRules: assembly-builds-only (480-481, 1036: nothing at root but imports)
sharedParts.problem: One discipline stated seven times with different scope and different exemption (assembly stricter, boot and spec exempt). Exemptions by kind AND by reader declaration (1113-1115) coexist for the same thing. As three atoms by check, each kind selects: boot drops root-no-effect, test gets registration through the reader.
The same 'define nothing but X' check stated per kind with different allow lists. One atom with a per-kind list leaves only test (defines anything) not carrying it.
Same check on arguments; assembly lets a tech value be read (441-443) while hook forbids it. The divergence is a separate atom (args-whole-event), so no except clause remains.
One dataflow check on a call's result, written twice with different words ('built instance never touched' vs 'result never read, written, logged').

Same structural check, two whys: driver (translation has no home) and test (legibility). Either one deeper why ('a hook body reads as one statement') or two atoms with one check. Decision owed to the authors.
Stated in two rules, with the why given only for boot (719-720). Test's why is never stated.

Five statements for one atom; two are scope parameters (runtime-only, public-only) re-asserted per rule, and each other rule restates whether type imports count, with opposite answers (blob, private, assembly, driver, service cycle: yes; composition: no).
Three places say a driver must not reach an adapter, differently scoped (import, call, return).
'A driver has no legal use for a blob import' stated four times.

Platform imports confined to some kinds are stated per kind, with different positive lists (declared-pure, claimed, container declared). The 'concrete' classification differs between inside kinds (platform/IO) and driver (claimed list).
An environment read at module root of a model is two violations. Stable-root says it is 'judged where it sits, by its layer' (1122-1123) but also red by itself.
Whitelists exclude the test kind while canon's own text has tests calling assemblies and shared drivers. Test is not an exception but a member of four importer sets.

inRules: wiring-outside-hooks (593: a hook does not wire)
sharedParts.problem: 'A hook does not wire' stated twice; follows already from count plus callee kinds.
Eleven-odd except clauses: each is an atom the test kind does not select or a whitelist it belongs to. 'Assembly and driver in one' hides that it carries neither's logic-holding atoms.

testKind: TEST carries: entry-not-imported (nothing imports it), driver-read (a test reader), the two universal root atoms plus root-no-effect (registration calls pass by the reader's effect-free declaration; this alone gives per-test isolation, no root-held instances), hook-straight-line (file-wide, see helpers; canon never states it for tests, implied by 1150-1161), no-barrel-import, private-seal, both cycle atoms (test edges count for the DAG, 911-912), no-outward-import (trivially). It also appears as an allowed importer in unit-assembly-gate, blob-import-gate, assembly-importers, driver-importers: those are listings, not exceptions. TEST does not carry: closed-definitions (defines anything: fakes, builders), hook-call-count and driver-callee-kinds (tests call many units and fakes then assert), args-whole-event, args-no-compute, result-passed-on (assertion is reading a result), concrete-import-gate and tech-must-be-claimed (imports anything, e2e real adapters), no-default-deps (defaults are right in test factories), no-ambient-access (ambient reach is the test tech's business; determinism stays judgment), the assembly set (assembly-calls-build, load-declared, wiring-branch-only, adapter-return-gate: a test is not an assembly, it merely calls them). Why: a test builds units, calls them and asserts, and nothing imports it, so it needs the atoms that keep the module stable and its own body legible, and none that bound what logic a layer may hold. Two canon contradictions: e2e is named by the flavor yet 'neither, outside the graph' (1022-1023); test-through-contract has no mechanical atom.
helpers: LOCAL-HELPER QUESTION. Answer: a plain 'no' is unacceptable. Scope hook-straight-line by FILE, not by hook: every function body defined in a test file (hook, local helper such as run(), inline callback) has no if, switch, ternary, loop, or iteration method with a callback (forEach, map, reduce by name list; short-circuit guards are judgment). Then a local helper cannot hide a loop, and one that needs a loop is not test code: it is a model (data builder), adapter (fake), assembly function (test factory) or driver (shared matcher), imported, carrying its own kind's atoms and its own tests (placement rule 1216-1219). run() that starts the CLI is straight-line (await a spawn) and passes. Two venues stay open and need a stated closure: (1) blob, since a test may import blob: no-blob-test-support (blob imported only by tests is red) is the proposed mechanical form, a canon rewrite of 1216-1219; (2) loops inside the runner (test.each and friends): the reader declares each-registration either as a loop (red) or as an accepted shape with its reason; canon is silent. Residue: a helper that must branch and is neither of the four kinds is the signal that a unit is missing. MECHANICAL INPUTS the atoms lean on, not atoms: (a) flavor: file kind from name, create* factory naming in model; (b) reader: hook cut, tech claim list, effect-free calls, registration calls, bound by glob; (c) declarations in config: pure packages, declared loads, container library, mutableModuleState opt-out; (d) edge kind (runtime or type-only), a parameter every importer-side atom restates; (e) tech value, literal, definition, 'await is the call' definitions (437-449). Holes where canon is silent: ambient globals read in assembly or boot (covered only through 'holds no tech' and argument forms), a branch or loop in driver wiring, the e2e kind.

atoms.name: inward-edges
atoms.statement: A file's runtime imports stay within the set its kind allows in the layer order model < ports < service/adapter < assembly < driver < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be developed, tested and reasoned about without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: Resolve each import to its target file's kind (suffix) and test the (importer kind, target kind) pair against the matrix. LAUNCH: yes (kinds from suffix; type-import treatment is per atom, see helpers).
atoms.landing: Reading a file's import list says everything it cannot know; a violation is visible by path shape.

atoms.name: composition-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A runtime import of a public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file comes only from assembly (test files in the assembly role).
atoms.why: Assembly is the single place where dependencies are resolved, so services never scatter wiring or default to concrete adapters.
atoms.check: Edge check on target kind service/adapter, public (outside private/), runtime import only; importer kind in {assembly, test}. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The chunk graph and the dependency graph are the assembly graph; a service never knows its neighbours' implementations.

atoms.name: blob-importers
atoms.statement: A suffixless blob file is imported (type imports included) only by assembly, test or other blob files.
atoms.why: A layer with guarantees that imports blob inherits its lack of guarantees.
atoms.check: Edge check on target kind blob; importer kind in {assembly, test, blob}; type-only imports counted. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Blob is contained at assembly and tests, so the debt is visible as one boundary on the map.

atoms.name: outside-importers
atoms.statement: A driver, assembly, boot or test file is imported (type imports included) only by the kinds listed for it: driver by boot and drivers, assembly by drivers and assemblies, boot by nothing, test by nothing.
atoms.why: These files define no contract to depend on, and each outside kind has one right that importing it from elsewhere would leak.
atoms.check: Edge check on target kinds assembly/driver/boot/test with type imports counted; the importer lists are data. LAUNCH: yes. Why is explicit for assembly only; for the others it is implied.
atoms.landing: A reader knows the outside is reachable only along the boot, driver, assembly chain.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports (type imports included) from that service's private/ directory.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private may move without anyone noticing.
atoms.check: Path check: importer outside the owning service directory and target under that service's private/; layer directories are not nested services. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import path is an instant violation in review.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Import edges between service packages, every import kind counted, form a DAG.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: Collapse file imports to service-package edges and detect cycles (type imports and test edges included). LAUNCH: yes (needs service boundary knowledge).
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG; the direction of every pair is readable.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between files form no cycle.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently in minified production.
atoms.check: Cycle detection over runtime import edges only. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Load order is a tree; no undefined-at-import surprises.

atoms.name: no-barrel-index
atoms.statement: Imports name the file of the layer they need; no index file re-exports a service's surface.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the matrix cannot be enforced by tooling or review.
atoms.check: Flag index/barrel files that only re-export and imports resolving to them; the bare layer filename is not a barrel. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The import path alone tells the reader the layer.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file imports no platform or I/O package (node:fs, HTTP clients, database drivers) and no unclaimed package.
atoms.why: Reaching concrete code bypasses the ports, so the file cannot be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: Classify third-party/node imports as pure (declared) or concrete (everything else); concrete import in a kind that carries this atom is red; a declared container library in assembly is the sole configured exemption. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Concrete code is findable only in adapters (and tech in drivers).

atoms.name: declared-pure-lib
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as model only if the project declares it pure.
atoms.why: Purity is declared, not presumed, or a model's chain silently includes impure code.
atoms.check: Imported package must be in the config's pure list. LAUNCH: yes for the declaration; whether the library is really pure is not checkable (see remainders).
atoms.landing: The list of pure libraries the model trusts is one visible declaration.

atoms.name: no-ambient-name
atoms.statement: A file reads or calls no ambient global (environment, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis, host names like process) anywhere in it.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: Resolve identifiers to unbound globals or host names, anywhere (root, function, condition, value, call). LAUNCH: yes (needs the global list).
atoms.landing: Everything the code depends on arrives as an argument, so it is readable from the signature.

atoms.name: no-root-mutable
atoms.statement: A module root holds no binding whose immutability the syntax does not prove, exported or not.
atoms.why: A test importing the module gets the module every other test got, and state left behind would change what the next test sees.
atoms.check: Root bindings must be primitives, as const, readonly types, or Object.freeze over a literal, to their depth; unresolved named types prove nothing. LAUNCH: yes (type engine); the config can lift it (mutableModuleState).
atoms.landing: State exists only inside factory closures, reached by argument and never by import.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-read
atoms.statement: No value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness) is stored in a root binding.
atoms.why: The file cannot be tested under another environment or at another moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: Root binding initializers reaching host/clock/random names; import.meta.url and __dirname are exempt as module identity. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A module's root is the same on every load.

atoms.name: no-root-effect
atoms.statement: Evaluating a module root performs no effect: no call reaching tech, an unclaimed name, a use case or a local side-effect function, and no assignment or delete statement.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, and loading must neither act nor leave anything behind.
atoms.check: Root statements and calls classified by callee and statement kind; a throw is not an effect. LAUNCH: partial (the open set 'judged by the rule' and reader-declared effect-free calls are judgment).
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing; behavior starts only where something calls a function.

atoms.name: root-registration-only
atoms.statement: The only calls at a test file's module root are registrations into the claimed test runner.
atoms.why: The test tech owns when bodies run, and any other root call would act on load.
atoms.check: Root-level calls in test-kind files must target names the test reader claims. LAUNCH: yes (reader claims).
atoms.landing: A spec's root reads as a list of registered scenarios.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: An outside file defines at run time only what its kind names: assembly functions in an assembly, hooks and at most one wiring function in a driver, nothing in a boot.
atoms.why: Any other definition is residue, logic hiding in a layer with no contract and no test.
atoms.check: Enumerate runtime declarations (function, class, variable) and compare to the kind's allowed set; types are free. LAUNCH: yes (hook identification comes from the reader).
atoms.landing: What the outside defines can be listed from the file's top level: it is boring on sight.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly builds: it targets a factory from a service, adapter, assembly or blob file, or a model factory, never a model function that computes.
atoms.why: An assembly decides nothing but which factory to call; any other call is where logic would hide.
atoms.check: Callee file kind plus the flavor's factory naming for model files (stock create*). LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as the graph itself: factory, factory, factory.

atoms.name: assembly-result-inert
atoms.statement: What an assembly builds is only passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed.
atoms.why: An assembly that touches what it built is opening the door itself and the graph map can no longer show the wiring.
atoms.check: Result-flow analysis of bindings from factory calls (a declared load's result is a tech value, not a build). LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The assembly is a pure plumbing diagram; every decision lives in a service.

atoms.name: args-closed
atoms.statement: Call arguments in assembly, driver wiring and hooks are literals, tech values received as parameters, or instances built or received there, never a derived value.
atoms.why: Deriving a value in the outside is logic with no contract; the service or adapter that needs it derives it under its own rules.
atoms.check: Classify each argument expression: literal, parameter (field read allowed in assembly, never in a hook), or instance binding. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A call's arguments show the data flowing in the outside is only handed, never made.

atoms.name: returns-no-adapters
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances and no adapter, unless its only importers are tests.
atoms.why: An adapter handed out is an effect the contract does not cover; only a spec asserts on what its fakes recorded.
atoms.check: Returned bindings' callee kinds; if adapter, importers of the file must all be test-kind. LAUNCH: yes (importer-derived kind, see helpers).
atoms.landing: What leaves assembly is exactly what drivers may call.

atoms.name: declared-loads-only
atoms.statement: An assembly calls or awaits a use case only if the project declares it a load.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, and a use case feeding a factory is a pipeline hiding in the wiring.
atoms.check: Callee on a service instance must be in the project's declared load list. LAUNCH: yes (a declaration the user makes).
atoms.landing: The loads the graph depends on are named and visible.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness and has only factory calls in its arms.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or on a value computed from one is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: Condition operand classification (parameter/loaded vs instance-derived) plus arm contents. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: Conditional graphs vary only by config the map can name.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a reader bound to its tech, and a binding that names a file differently from the flavor is a config error.
atoms.why: Every other driver rule is judged through the reading, so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: Config glob binding exists for the file (or a reader that counts it blob on purpose). LAUNCH: yes (config check, not code structure).
atoms.landing: The map knows which tech each outside file listens to.

atoms.name: tech-claimed-only
atoms.statement: A driver's tech is only what its bound readers claim; an import or name no reader claims is unclaimed and red.
atoms.why: Tech is what a reading claims and nothing else, and no rule can judge what no reader sees.
atoms.check: Match each import/name in a driver against the readers' claim lists. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The tech a driver touches is exactly the reader's declared list.

atoms.name: listen-driver-only
atoms.statement: Only a driver (a test file in the driver role) receives events from the claimed tech by handing it callbacks.
atoms.why: The driver is the one place where tech events reach the program, so nowhere else needs reasoning about them.
atoms.check: Callbacks passed to claimed tech in files with a reader. LAUNCH: partial (adapters have no reader, so inbound subscription in an adapter looks like outbound).
atoms.landing: All entry points of events are findable in driver files.

atoms.name: hook-one-call
atoms.statement: Each hook makes exactly one call, to a use case.
atoms.why: Two calls mean the sequence between them is a use case nobody owns, and zero means logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count calls in the hook body (await counts as the call) and classify the callee as a use-case method on an assembly-returned instance. LAUNCH: yes (hook cut from the reader).
atoms.landing: The map draws a driver-to-service link as a single arrow.

atoms.name: hook-straight-line
atoms.statement: A hook body is straight-line: no branch, loop or statement besides its call.
atoms.why: A decision or translation around the call has no contract or test in the outside; it is a facade service's use case.
atoms.check: No control-flow statements, conditional or short-circuit expressions, or iteration calls in the hook body. LAUNCH: yes. Applied to a test body this is implied, not stated.
atoms.landing: The hook shows nothing to read beyond the call.

atoms.name: hook-args-verbatim
atoms.statement: A hook's call arguments are the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals, with nothing read off them and no default.
atoms.why: Translating the event is the facade service's use case, so it belongs where a contract and a test exist.
atoms.check: Each argument is a hook parameter or whole host value, an instance or a literal; no member access, no ?? or default. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: What the tech hands in is exactly what the service receives.

atoms.name: hook-result-inert
atoms.statement: A hook returns the call's value or drops it, and never reads, writes, hands on or logs it.
atoms.why: Using the result (exit code, rendering, branching) is translation, which belongs to the facade service through its ports.
atoms.check: Result-flow analysis on the single call's value. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The driver is humble enough that nothing in it needs a test.

atoms.name: wiring-closed-calls
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver calls only assembly, claimed tech setup, and sub-driver wiring functions, with closed arguments.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in the wiring function and nowhere else, so a driver holds no logic between setup and hooks.
atoms.check: Callee classification for calls outside hook bodies, args per args-closed. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: A driver's top level reads as assemble, set up the parser, register.

atoms.name: wiring-sole-export
atoms.statement: A driver exports at most its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Otherwise a hook could chain a second call through one level of indirection, defeating the one-call rule.
atoms.check: Enumerate the exports of a driver file. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The only handle another driver has on a driver is its wiring function.

atoms.name: root-wiring-bare
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes no parameters and reads its tech itself.
atoms.why: The boot passes no arguments so that it touches no tech.
atoms.check: Wiring function signature in the root driver; the sub-driver form takes tech and instances. LAUNCH: partial (which driver is root comes from the importer, the boot).
atoms.landing: The entry reads as main() with no arguments.

atoms.name: boot-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start, and any other import gives it something to do or know.
atoms.check: Import list of a boot file has length one with a driver target. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The entry point is a two-line file.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot makes exactly one call, at module root, to its driver's wiring function with no arguments.
atoms.why: It is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and that call is all the starting there is.
atoms.check: Root statements = imports plus one call expression whose callee is the imported wiring function with zero arguments. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The program's single start is locatable per entry point.

atoms.name: ports-type-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds only types, and no runtime import touches it from or of it.
atoms.why: A port is a boundary contract, and runtime code in it means an adapter has not been extracted yet.
atoms.check: Port file statements are type declarations and import type only; any runtime edge into or out of a port file is red. LAUNCH: yes.
atoms.landing: The contract of the hexagon is pure shape, safe to read and to depend on.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter's factory conforms to a port type it imports, so all adapters of a port have the same interface and result shape.
atoms.why: The inside must never know which adapter it is talking to.
atoms.check: Adapter file type-imports a port and its public factory is assignable to it. LAUNCH: partial (needs the TS engine; 'absorbs source-specific details' is not checkable).
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the port it implements; replaceability is visible.

atoms.name: no-dependency-defaults
atoms.statement: A service or adapter factory's dependency parameters carry no default value.
atoms.why: Defaults create static imports to adapters or config sources and scatter assembly logic across service modules.
atoms.check: Default initializers on factory parameters typed by a port or service API. LAUNCH: partial (what is a dependency comes from parameter types; the import ban already blocks most defaults).
atoms.landing: Every dependency is explicit at the call site in assembly.

rules.remainder: Lateral (same-layer) imports are allowed is a statement of what is not forbidden, not a constraint.
None.

Not an atom: transitive closure of per-file edge atoms when every file in the chain is labelled. Holes: that a declared pure library is really pure, and 'partial extraction produces false guarantees' (a wish).
'Pure, deterministic' is judgment; 'becomes untestable' is the why, not a check.
'Adapters and drivers reach the environment: that is the tech's business' is a kind selection, not a part.
'A driver may not: its hooks call services' re-states driver edges; 'characterization tests' is a justification.
None; the atom is stated again for adapters.
None; same atom as service-assembly-only with the target kind adapter.

Not an atom: a scope parameter (type-only imports exempt) of composition-assembly-only; the 'depending on shape is not depending on implementation' sentence is its why. It must not be read as an exemption of private-sealed, blob-importers, outside-importers or no-service-cycle, which count type imports.

Not an atom: a scope parameter (private/ of the same service exempt) of composition-assembly-only; it also lets a unit's factory compose internal sub-units with no assembly atom applying (see helpers).
None.
'If the service layer branches on which adapter it got' is not mechanically checkable; no atom.
None.
None.
None.

'Assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details' is judgment; only the private/ import edge is mechanical, and test-is-outside says tests import anything, which collides (see sharedParts).

'It defines anything' and 'imports anything' are the absence of atoms, not parts; 'fixtures are adapters with the same isolation rules' and 'placed by what it is' are classification, not checks; hook-straight-line for tests is implied, not stated; end-to-end tests are outside the graph (scope).

'A pipeline hiding in the wiring', 'a model function that computes a value' and 'decision the map cannot show' are judgment words backed only by the atoms above; 'nothing at module root but imports' is stable-root plus closed-definitions restated.
None.
'A driver the project does not want read yet is bound to a blob-counting reader' is config policy, not code structure.
'Tech setup (the parser, the server, the mount)' depends on the reader's claim list; 'a hook does not wire' is carried by hook-one-call.

Molecule of four atoms. Holes: 'a reader with a cut of its own says where the line sits', 'a second call means a facade is missing' (why, not check). The test reader exempts only the count, though the other three forbid assertions.

'Never an adapter, never a model' is the driver row of the matrix plus assembly not returning adapters; 'parsing and rendering are use cases of a service' is judgment; an adapter call from a hook has no extra atom of its own.
'A local parseFoo is a model without a test' is the why.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a scope decision left to the reader.
None; same atom as assembly-driver-only with another target kind.
'One per entry point' is not checkable from code (needs entry-point declaration).

'A shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' is an open set (judgment); reader-declared effect-free calls are configuration; the closed exemption list (boot's one call, a spec's registrations) becomes boot-calls-once and root-registration-only on their kinds.

kinds.note: Model carries no outside atom; the last five atoms in this list are universal and every kind carries them, so they are not repeated below. Canon's Model row is 'model and pure libs only': pure-lib is declared-pure-lib.
inward-edges allows model and ports only. Other atoms are vacuous because a port holds only types.
composition-assembly-only is carried as a target. 'Orchestrates, does not compute' is a remainder; a service has no hook or definition atoms.
Does not carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-name: reaching the tech is its one job. 'Holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' is inward-edges plus the importee atoms.
outside-importers and blob-importers are carried as importer or target data. Test-purpose assembly files are the same kind: returns-no-adapters is conditional on importers being tests.
Does not carry no-ambient-name or no-concrete-import: its tech is what the reader claims (tech-claimed-only stands in). The hook atoms apply to hook bodies only.
No reader is bound. no-root-effect is not carried because boot-calls-once replaces it (the exemption becomes the kind's own atom). No-root-mutable follows from closed-definitions.

The last four atoms apply to non-hook functions only (the assembly half, by position); hook-straight-line applies to hook bodies only. Not carried: inward-edges, composition-assembly-only, blob-importers (a test is the permitted importer), no-concrete-import, no-ambient-name, hook-one-call, hook-args-verbatim, hook-result-inert, closed-definitions, returns-no-adapters, no-root-effect. Canon's 'defines anything' is removed: a spec's definitions are only hooks or assembly functions.

Canon names blob in stable-root's local-function clause, so the root atoms apply; other guarantees are none by definition. It is also the only kind assembly and test may import (blob-importers, target side). Whether blob carries the root atoms is ambiguous in canon.

sharedParts.problem: One atom stated twice under two slugs (once per target kind), plus two scope modifiers stated as separate slugs, plus matrix rows (L864-873) and L270 saying 'only assembly' while test files also import units: the test case needs an exception that should be a data entry in the importer list.

The same allowed-edge set is stated from the importer side (matrix) and from the importee side (four slugs); they disagree: runtime-import says a type import of IconsServiceAPI is legal anywhere while the Adapters row and L276-277 say an adapter holds only what its port needs, and L881 says drivers and assemblies may type-import any layer while the Drivers row says no model.
Worded 'concrete', 'tech' and 'unclaimed' depending on the kind, and only the model section adds the pure-library carve-out; boot says 'tech included' where assembly says 'never concrete tech'.

stable-root's 'nothing read from the machine stored at root' (L1093-1105) is the same check as ambient-access with a position added; for model and service the first is a subset of the second, so the same read is red twice with two slugs.

Stated in model (L295-298), service (L341), assembly ('nothing at module root but imports') and the test isolation text (L1196-1198); only the exemption list, repeated at L719, L1126-1129 and L1011-1014, differs by kind.
The exemption list (the boot's call, a spec's registrations) is an 'except' stated in three places; made atoms of their own kinds (boot-calls-once, root-registration-only) it needs no except.
One atom stated four times with three allowed sets and a fourth 'defines anything' for test, which is the same atom with an empty restriction and is where the test kind leaks.
Assembly allows a field read on a tech value while a hook allows none; the shared part (literal, tech parameter, instance, never derived) is stated three times with different permitted reads.

hook-one-call is a molecule of four atoms (count/callee, straight-line, args verbatim, result inert); the test reader exempts only the count and services-only, so a test body asserting on a result violates the other three and the list of real test exemptions is hidden in the reader.
Control flow in function bodies is ruled three ways (none in a hook, wiring-only in assembly, unstated for test bodies) with the same why: decisions belong to a service.

Stated per kind in four slugs and a matrix; assembly's list ignores test factories (L1213-1219 put them in assembly files imported by tests) while L882 says only drivers and assemblies import assemblies.
The 'except when a test is the caller' clause is a kind-by-importer distinction canon never names; driver-calls-services 'never an adapter' relies on it.
Tests 'import anything' (test-is-outside) while test-through-contract says no implementation details and private-sealed says nothing outside a service imports private/; canon never says which wins.

The direction law (nested adapter edges point up, the parent is import-blind to children) is the same atom restated; the test-fixture clause (L909-912) shows tests carry it, which test-is-outside never says.
What counts as claimed tech is stated in the terminology, in the driver prose and in two slugs, with overlapping 'unclaimed' and 'red regardless' wording.

Fractal assembly (L159-167) and public-unit let a service or adapter factory build internal sub-adapters and wire internal ports, so a composition unit holds assembly work with none of the assembly atoms applying: a laundering venue for wiring logic.
'No shared test code is blob' (L1218-1219) restates blob-importers for tests, but nothing checks a blob file imported only by tests, which can hold shared test logic.

testKind: Carry: reader-bound, outside-importers (nothing imports a test), no-root-mutable and no-root-machine-read (the next test must see the same module), root-registration-only (root calls are runner registrations), private-sealed and no-service-cycle (test edges count for cycles, and the contract is the public surface), plus the hook atom hook-straight-line on test() bodies (no branch or loop: stated for hooks, implied for tests). Because the file is assembly and driver in one, the assembly atoms (assembly-calls-build, assembly-result-inert, args-closed, wiring-branch-only) apply by position to every non-hook function, and the driver hook atoms apply to hook bodies only. Do not carry: inward-edges, composition-assembly-only, blob-importers (the test is their permitted importer), no-concrete-import, no-ambient-name (it holds the test tech), hook-one-call, hook-args-verbatim and hook-result-inert (a test body must pass fixtures and read results to assert), closed-definitions, returns-no-adapters, no-root-effect (replaced by root-registration-only). Why: a test builds units, calls them and asserts, and nothing imports it, so the edge atoms are moot and the importer atoms are vacuous, while the atoms that protect the next test (stable root) and the reviewer (no control flow in the scenario) stay. Open question: yes, the no-branch constraint must reach the helpers, and the structure that avoids the laundering venue is positional. A function in a spec file is either a hook (hook-straight-line) or an assembly function (assembly atoms), and nothing else may be defined there; canon's 'it defines anything' is dropped. A helper like run() that starts the CLI is neither (it spawns, loops, branches), so it moves to its own file and is classified by what it is: an adapter (a test-purpose runner behind a port, built by a test factory), a model (data builder) or a driver (a shared hook registered on the runner), each under its own atoms where its control flow is legal and visible. This closes the in-file venue. Two venues remain open and need decisions: a suffixless helper imported only by tests (blob, forbidden by canon L1218-1219 but not checked; flag a blob file whose importers are all tests unless declared as characterization of legacy code) and the fractal-assembly/public-unit venue.
helpers: Notes for reconciling the runs. 1) Kind is data: every atom is scoped by (kind, position, type-import flag). Position: module root, hook body, outside hooks. Type-import flag per atom: composition-assembly-only exempts type imports; private-sealed, blob-importers, outside-importers and no-service-cycle count them; this is why runtime-import and public-unit are scope modifiers, not atoms. 2) The matrix is derived: each cell is the conjunction of inward-edges, composition-assembly-only, blob-importers, outside-importers and private-sealed; it should be generated, not stated, since canon states each edge from both sides. 3) Why-clusters: machine-dependence (no-concrete-import, no-ambient-name, no-root-machine-read), test-isolation (no-root-mutable, no-root-effect), outside-has-one-thing (closed-definitions, assembly-*, hook-*, wiring-*, boot-*), contract-shape (ports-type-only, adapter-implements-port, no-dependency-defaults), graph-shape (inward-edges, composition-assembly-only, blob-importers, outside-importers, private-sealed, cycles, no-barrel-index). Different atoms share a cluster but each has its own check. 4) Canon inconsistencies found while decomposing: (a) runtime-import says type import of a service API is legal anywhere vs adapter row and direction law allowing only port and model; (b) test imports anything vs private-sealed; (c) test hook exempts only count and services-only yet test bodies must read results and pass fixtures; (d) blob is subject to stable-root though it has no guarantees; (e) assembly files imported by tests (test factories) vs assembly-driver-only; (f) fractal assembly inside a unit's factory carries none of the assembly atoms. 5) Holes (judgment words, never atoms): thin, boring, meaningful port, orchestrates not computes, abstractness, 'branches on which adapter', pure library really pure, documented behavior, implementation details, legible as behavior statement, one boot per entry point, kernel-consumer litmus, tasteless last mile, an open set of root shapes. 6) Not in the 37: layer-declared-by-suffix and use-case-level labels (definition and map annotation, not constraints), config-binding consistency (config check), and rules in Lifecycle/Patterns (guidance, not checks). 7) Launch summary: yes for all graph atoms; partial for no-root-effect, listen-driver-only, root-wiring-bare, adapter-implements-port, no-dependency-defaults; judgment parts are in remainders.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: An import specifier shows the layer of its target in its path; no index/barrel file re-exports across layers.
atoms.why: The dependency matrix is enforceable only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolved target's suffix/folder gives a layer; no index.* re-export file.
atoms.landing: A reader sees the layer of every dependency from the import line, without opening a file.

atoms.name: inward-deps
atoms.statement: A runtime import goes to the same or an inner layer in model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be developable and testable without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge rank from importer and target layers.
atoms.landing: Direction of every edge; the inside never names the outside.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service and assembly import no concrete (platform/IO) package; a declared container library is the one assembly exception.
atoms.why: Contact with the world bypasses the ports and makes the file untestable in isolation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a declared list: import specifiers vs concrete/pure classification.
atoms.landing: The world is touched only in adapters and drivers.

atoms.name: lib-purity-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as model only if the project declares it pure; undeclared means concrete.
atoms.why: Purity presumed rather than declared gives a false guarantee.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config list lookup per package.
atoms.landing: The pure/concrete split is a visible list, not a guess.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A file of a kind that does not hold the tech reads no ambient global (environment, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis, or the tech's own names), at root or in a function.
atoms.why: Reaching the machine is the tech layers' business; elsewhere it makes the file depend on the machine and untestable without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: identifier resolves to a global in a name set (stock list; reader claims for tech names).
atoms.landing: Everything the file uses arrived by argument; no hidden inputs.

atoms.name: blob-import-gated
atoms.statement: A suffixless (blob) file is imported, type imports included, only by assembly, test or other blob.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any other importer would be contaminated.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target suffixless, importer kind in the allowed set.
atoms.landing: Debt is visible: its only consumers are the build and its characterization tests.

atoms.name: unit-import-gated
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (and test); private/ of the own service and type-only imports are out of scope.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place that resolves dependencies and knows the concrete graph.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target suffix, importer kind, type-only flag, private path.
atoms.landing: Who builds what; the chunk graph is the assembly graph.

atoms.name: outside-import-gated
atoms.statement: An assembly is imported only by drivers and assemblies, a driver only by boot or drivers, a boot and a test file by nothing, type imports included.
atoms.why: Outside kinds have no contract to depend on; their only legitimate edge is from what starts them.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reverse-edge importer kinds per target kind.
atoms.landing: The entry chain boot -> driver -> assembly is the only path; nothing depends on the outside.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import path contains private/ and importer is outside the owning service.
atoms.landing: private/ in a path proves internal; outside use is an instant violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-level import graph, every import kind counted, has no cycle.
atoms.why: Services in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package graph from all import edges.
atoms.landing: Services form a DAG on the map.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: The module-level runtime import graph has no cycle.
atoms.why: ESM circular imports work in dev and fail silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime edge graph.
atoms.landing: Module load order is unambiguous.

atoms.name: ports-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds no runtime code and no runtime import touches it in either direction.
atoms.why: A port is a contract shape; runtime code there means an adapter is not extracted yet.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: emitted runtime statements in port files; runtime edges to/from them.
atoms.landing: Ports read as pure shape.

atoms.name: no-adapter-branch
atoms.statement: Service code does not branch on which adapter it was given.
atoms.why: The inside must not know or need to know which adapter it talks to.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: instanceof or discriminant tests on an injected dependency are visible; 'which adapter' in general is not.
atoms.landing: A service reads the same whatever adapter is behind the port.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter's factory result conforms to an interface defined in a ports file.
atoms.why: All adapters of a port must expose the same interface and result shape so the inside is spared source specifics.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with the type checker: assignability of the returned object to a port type.
atoms.landing: Which port each adapter serves.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A service factory's dependency parameters have no default value.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import to the adapter or config source and scatters assembly logic across services.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: parameter initializers on factory params typed by ports or services.
atoms.landing: Every dependency visibly comes from assembly.

atoms.name: root-immutable-bindings
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly types, frozen literal); a module exports factories, never mutable instances.
atoms.why: A file must be the same on every load so a test that imports it gets what every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root binding's type/initializer against the proofs; config mutableModuleState lifts exactly this.
atoms.landing: State lives only in factory closures; instances are reached by argument.

atoms.name: root-no-capture
atoms.statement: No value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness) is stored in a root binding; import.meta.url and __dirname are not machine reads.
atoms.why: Stored at load, it freezes the machine's state and the file cannot be tested under another environment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: dataflow from ambient/tech reads into root bindings, depth bounded.
atoms.landing: No hidden load-time inputs.

atoms.name: root-no-effects
atoms.statement: Module root runs no call reaching tech, an unclaimed name, a use case or a local function of an effectful layer, and no effectful statement (assignment, delete); exempt by kind: the boot's one call, a spec's runner registrations.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act or leave anything behind.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement kinds and callee kind; property reads presumed free; reader may declare a call effect-free.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file of an outside kind defines at runtime only what its kind names: assembly its assembly functions; driver its hooks and at most one wiring function; boot and port nothing; a type is not a definition.
atoms.why: A layer with wide import rights that may define freely becomes where logic hides, with no contract and no test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime declarations vs the kind's allow-set.
atoms.landing: Outside files are visibly boring; any residue is a violation, not a smell.

atoms.name: args-underived
atoms.statement: Every argument of a call is a literal, a tech value received as parameter, or an instance built or received; none is derived by a call or computation.
atoms.why: A derived argument is logic the outside kind has taken for itself instead of the service that needs the value.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression forms.
atoms.landing: Wiring reads as pass-through.

atoms.name: result-not-read
atoms.statement: The result of a call in an assembly or a hook is never branched on, computed with or member-accessed; a declared load's result is the one exception.
atoms.why: An outside file that looks into a result is deciding, and nothing owns the decision.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: uses of the call's binding or awaited value.
atoms.landing: Instances flow through, data does not.

atoms.name: entry-no-args
atoms.statement: The root wiring function takes no parameters and the boot calls it with none.
atoms.why: The root driver reads its tech itself and the boot touches no tech, so there is nothing to pass.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: signature arity and call arity.
atoms.landing: Entry is a bare start.

atoms.name: tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every package or name a driver uses beyond assemblies and drivers is claimed by a bound reader; an unclaimed name is red and a pure library is model, red regardless.
atoms.why: The reading cuts the hooks and sets what counts as tech, so what no reading claims cannot be judged.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: names and imports vs reader claims.
atoms.landing: A driver's tech is an explicit list.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: An assembly awaits only use cases the project declares as loads.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for its effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config list of callee names.
atoms.landing: The few non-build calls of the graph are listed.

atoms.name: build-calls-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory (composition unit, other assembly, flavor-named model factory, or a blob file injected behind a port) or a declared load; no use-case call, no model function.
atoms.why: The file with the widest import right must do almost nothing or logic hides in it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind and flavor name.
atoms.landing: The assembly is the graph the map draws.

atoms.name: wiring-branches-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A decision on an instance or computed value is one the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operands and arm statements.
atoms.landing: Variation in the graph depends on inputs only.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services or shared model instances, no adapter unless a test is the caller.
atoms.why: Consumers type against service APIs; an adapter handed back is reachable past its contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: returned value kinds and caller kinds.
atoms.landing: What the outside receives is a service.

atoms.name: driver-reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a bound reader (or deliberately bound to one that counts it as blob).
atoms.why: No other driver rule can be judged without the reading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-to-reader binding by glob.
atoms.landing: Config shows which technologies the project reads.

atoms.name: listen-driver-only
atoms.statement: Only a driver (and a test) hands callbacks to a claimed tech to receive its events; an adapter calls the tech outbound only.
atoms.why: One place receives events, so the outside is reasoned about from that place.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: reader's hook cut finds hook-shaped callbacks outside drivers; inbound vs outbound relies on the reader.
atoms.landing: All entry points of the program are in driver files.

atoms.name: hook-one-call
atoms.statement: A hook's only call is exactly one use-case call.
atoms.why: Two calls make a sequence nobody owns and zero is logic with no home; both belong in a facade service with a contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a reader cut: calls in hook body by callee kind.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow.

atoms.name: hook-straight-line
atoms.statement: A hook has no branch, loop or catch around or beside its call.
atoms.why: A decision in a hook is translation with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow nodes in the hook body.
atoms.landing: Hooks are readable at a glance as one line.

atoms.name: hook-args-verbatim
atoms.statement: A hook passes the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals; nothing read off them, no default.
atoms.why: Reading or defaulting the event is translation, which is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument forms in the hook call.
atoms.landing: What the tech gives is what the service receives.

atoms.name: hook-result-unforwarded
atoms.statement: A hook returns the call's value or drops it; it never writes, hands on or logs it.
atoms.why: Using the result (exit code, rendering) is translation, done by the service through ports.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: uses of the call value.
atoms.landing: Output and exit are in a service, testable.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-only
atoms.statement: Outside hooks a driver calls only assembly factories, tech setup and sub-driver wiring; a hook does not wire.
atoms.why: Wiring happens once at startup apart from firing, in the one place for it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes with reader: callee kind by site (hook or not).
atoms.landing: Setup and firing are separated in every driver.

atoms.name: sub-driver-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, in its own wiring, passing tech and instances; the sub-driver exports that one function and no hook.
atoms.why: Otherwise one hook could chain two calls through an indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: use sites of the import, exports of the target.
atoms.landing: Hook splitting across files is visible as a tree of registrations.

atoms.name: boot-single-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: The boot only starts the program and touches nothing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list.
atoms.landing: The entry is one line to read.

atoms.name: boot-one-call
atoms.statement: A boot's only statement is one call to its driver's wiring function at module root.
atoms.why: Something must execute at load, and it must be the one thing that does.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements.
atoms.landing: Start is a single call.

atoms.name: test-isolated-state
atoms.statement: No mutable state is shared between tests: no mutable root binding, no binding outside hooks assigned from hooks.
atoms.why: Each test sees only what it built, so nothing one test runs changes what the next sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root bindings and cross-hook assignment of outer bindings.
atoms.landing: Scenario state is all inside the test.

atoms.name: test-via-contract
atoms.statement: A test reaches a unit through its public surface, never private/ or non-exported internals.
atoms.why: Tests prove the contract so internals stay free to move.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: imports in tests (private/ even inside the own service); behavior itself is not checkable.
atoms.landing: The unit under test is the one named in the import.

atoms.name: no-prod-config
atoms.statement: A test file imports no production config source.
atoms.why: Production config couples the test to an environment.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs the config source declared.
atoms.landing: Test inputs are all written in or beside the test.

atoms.name: test-body-straight
atoms.statement: A test hook has no branch or loop, iteration methods and test.each included.
atoms.why: The reviewer must read each test as given/when/expect visible in the test, not reconstructed from indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow nodes in the hook body; iteration calls need a stated list.
atoms.landing: One test, one scenario, readable top to bottom.

atoms.name: local-helper-kinded
atoms.statement: Every function a spec defines is a hook, an assembly function (build-only) or a wiring function; a helper called from a hook inherits the hook constraints; anything else lives in a file of its kind.
atoms.why: Logic must live where its kind's rules judge it, or the free definitions of a test become a laundering venue.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: spec-local call graph from hooks.
atoms.landing: The spec shows what each test does, with no hidden logic.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral OK' and 'outer layer may hold inner-layer code' are scopes, not constraints.

Molecule only in name: a transitive restatement of four edge atoms. 'Partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a wish; its only non-redundant duty is third-party and unlabelled nodes.
'Becomes untestable' is the why, not a check.
none
'Assembly may take it because its rule bounds what it does' belongs to build-calls-only; 'characterization tests' is a wish.
none
none
Not a constraint: the type-only scope of unit-import-gated, while five other atoms count type edges.
Not a constraint: the private/ scope of unit-import-gated.
Port shape 'to the inside's needs' (118) is judgment.
'Port hasn't finished abstracting' is a wish; 'same result shape' only as far as types go.

Direction law (817-826) is derived from it, no atom of its own.
none
'Assertions on documented behavior' and 'no implementation details' are not checkable; exceptions (a)(b) at 1172-1175 are judgment.

The rule is mostly absences (exempt from closed-definitions, hook-one-call and the importer-side limits). 'Assembly and driver in one' is a classification claim, not a check; 'same isolation rules' for fixtures is unspecified; end-to-end 'neither, outside the graph' is a kind with no definition.

'Pipeline hiding in the wiring' and 'opening the door itself' are the why; 'the adapter or service derives the value' is placement advice; 'blob behind the port that awaits it' is checked only as far as types.

none
'Laziness is the assembly's' is a statement of placement. Silent on branches and loops in wiring.
'A second call means a facade is missing' is advice; 'when the view model is the tech's' leaves the line to the reader (open); 'a tech that answers by return value' is reader judgment.
'Never an adapter, never a model' adds no check beyond the call-site atoms and tech-claimed; it restates them.
'Residue' and 'a model without a test' are labels.
A parent component rendering a child in markup is excluded by reader scope.

'One per entry point' needs the entry points declared; not a structural check.
'Shapes below are not a closed list, judged by the rule' is explicit judgment; 'presumed not machine' for import.meta.url is a parameter; 'effect decided where it sits' delegates to the layer rules.
'No exceptions' (381) vs tests exempt (1221-1224).
'Fixtures are adapters', 'production adapters fair game when controlled' are judgment.

Intersection of other rules, no atom of its own; its driver row 'cannot import model' is derived from args-underived and wiring-calls-only; the adapter row 'may import concrete' sits against 165-167 (an adapter's HTTP client injected from outside).

kinds.note: Graph atoms are per edge or per package, not per kind. Test files carry them too (canon says fixtures are test-purpose adapters, not real nested ones, 911-912).
Importer-side limits only; nothing about being imported.
Emits nothing at runtime, so the root and ambient atoms are vacuous.
As importer it may not import blob; as target it is gated by unit-import-gated.
Carries neither no-concrete-import nor no-ambient-access: reaching tech is its reason to exist. Canon 165-167 vs matrix needs a ruling.
Allowed importer of blob and units (an allow-set parameter). Root: nothing but imports, as closed-definitions with an empty variable set plus zero root calls.
No exemption in root-no-effects (each builds inside its function). Its imports are the closed set assemblies, drivers, claimed tech, with types free.
closed-definitions with an empty set; root-no-effects exempts exactly its one call.
See testKind.
Target-side gate only, plus the graph atoms. Canon silent on whether the root atoms apply to blob; 1110-1114 treats a blob's local call as effectful, which implies yes.

sharedParts.problem: One allow-set check is stated five times: assembly 'assembly functions only', driver 'hooks and one wiring function', boot 'nothing', port 'no runtime code', test 'defines anything'. The test version is a grant with no allow-set, which is where the helper venue comes from; 'a type is not a definition' is stated only in Terminology (444-446). Candidate merge: ports-types-only is closed-definitions with an empty set plus its edge facet.

Four kinds restate who may import them, with a table of allowed importers hidden in four rules. Only assembly's states a why ('no contract'); the test spec imports a shared test factory (assembly) while 'assembly and driver in one' is not itself an assembly or driver, and the web recognition rule (572-574) is the same atom for component files in prose without a slug.

Allowed importers (assembly, test) are re-argued per kind: for a driver the prohibition is justified from hook-one-call ('a blob call there is already a violation', 958-960) instead of from blob's why, so the same prohibition has two owners.

Two slugs with one check parameterized by suffix, plus two rules that are only scope clauses (type-only, private/). The test as allowed importer is stated in matrix and test-is-outside, not in the slugs.

Exemptions by kind (boot's one call, spec registrations) are carved in stable-root's closed list while boot-one-call and test-is-outside restate them from their side; assembly's 'nothing at root but imports' is closed-definitions plus this atom, restated.

A machine read stored at root is red by stable-root in every kind, a machine read anywhere is red by ambient-access for model and service. Canon delegates ('judged where it sits, by its layer', 1122-1123) while also stating `const PORT = process.env...` red; two owners for the same line.

One check ('this file reaches no machine name') appears with two name sets: the ambient list (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) and 'tech' (reader claims) for assembly 'holds no tech' and boot 'touches no tech'; whys worded differently, and `if (process.env.X)` is green by stable-root yet touches tech in a boot.

Assembly may read a field or destructure a tech value; a hook may read nothing off the event. Same check, two scopes, and the 'tech value' definition (440-446) serves only assembly and driver; hook-args-verbatim is the stricter sub-atom.
Assembly passes the result on or returns it; a hook may not hand it on, write or log it; a declared load is exempt in assembly only; test hooks must read results to assert.

Same control-flow check, two whys (translation belongs to the facade vs reviewer legibility); canon exempts 'the hook count' for tests and never says which other hook atoms hold, so the straight-line check is implicit for tests.
The two ends of one signature (main takes nothing, boot passes nothing) are stated in two rules.
Allowed callee kinds per site are split over three rules and driver-calls-services restates their union; none of wiring-outside-hooks' text addresses branches or loops outside hooks.
Model, service and assembly each state it differently (model bullet, service-purity, assembly 'holds no tech'); the adapter's injected HTTP client (165-167) contradicts the adapter row of the matrix.
chain-purity states the same why ('false guarantees' through a less-pure import) as inward-deps, no-concrete-import and blob-import-gated and adds only a transitive closure.

The edge-kind scope is a parameter stated in prose per rule: 'type imports included' for five atoms, 'type-only exempt' for unit-import-gated, and 'type imports free' for driver and assembly as importers. Each time with its own why, none in one place.
'No exceptions' (381) and the test factory's default values 'right here' (1221-1224) are an except clause on one atom.

testKind: Canon's 'assembly and driver in one' does not hold atom by atom. A test calls data builders (model functions, forbidden to assembly), calls fakes and adapters (forbidden to a driver), reads results to assert (forbidden to a hook), makes many calls per body, and defines freely. So it carries the union of the importer RIGHTS but none of the VERB lists, which is why about ten rules get exempted. Carry: driver-reader-bound (test reader), outside-import-gated (imported by nothing), root-immutable-bindings plus root-no-effects (only runner registrations exempt, and root-no-effects as its own atom lets that be said once by kind), test-isolated-state (a different why from stable-root: tests in one file share a module), no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle, private-sealed, test-via-contract (partial), no-prod-config (partial), test-body-straight (implied from the reviewer rationale, canon never states it), local-helper-kinded. Do not carry: inward-deps, no-concrete-import and the other importer-side limits (it imports anything), blob-import-gated and unit-import-gated as limits (it is an allowed importer), closed-definitions (defines anything, but see helpers), hook-one-call, hook-args-verbatim, hook-result-unforwarded, result-not-read (assertions read results), build-calls-only, args-underived, no-default-deps (tests use defaults), wiring-calls-only. Open decision: no-ambient-access in tests; the determinism why (1193-1194) holds, but canon is silent and a clock or env read in a spec is the likeliest flaky test. Nothing imports a test, so any atom whose why concerns a consumer (ports contract, type-import scope, chain purity) is vacuous for it; keep only atoms whose why is the test's own isolation.
helpers:
Open question. Answer: yes, the straight-line constraint must reach local helpers, and by call-graph reachability, not by syntax. A 'no' makes the helper a laundering venue; drivers escape this only because closed-definitions leaves no room for a local helper, while the test's 'defines anything' grants exactly that room. Structure that avoids it: (1) every function a spec defines is classified, not free: a hook (runner callback), an assembly function (build-only, factory arms), a wiring function (registration), or nothing else; (2) a helper called from a hook is a hook body by reachability, so test-body-straight applies inside it, iteration methods (forEach, map, test.each) counted as loops; (3) a helper that needs real logic (branching, loops, a run() that spawns the CLI and parses output) cannot stay in the spec: it is placed by what it is, in a file of its own kind (adapter for a CLI runner or fake, model for a data builder, assembly function for a test factory), where that kind's rules judge it. This extends canon's 'shared test code is placed by what it is' (265-266) from shared to local helpers. A plain run() that only builds and calls stays in the spec. Known hole: a function passed as parameter or stored in data is unresolvable statically.

Method and structural findings. Criterion used for atoms: split when whys differ, or when sharing/exemption needs it (config lifts only root-immutable-bindings; boot exempts only the one call; tests exempt only registrations). Edge atoms split into target-side gates (who may import me: blob-import-gated, unit-import-gated, outside-import-gated, private-sealed) and importer-side limits (inward-deps, no-concrete-import); the canon's matrix row bundles both, so the test row 'imports anything / imported by nothing' is the two sides, not an exception. Canon also divides into import atoms (inside ruled by what it may depend on) and verb atoms (outside ruled by what it may do), per 234-236. Three atoms are declarations, not code shape: lib-purity-declared, load-declared, tech-claimed; they share the 'declared, not inferred' pattern but have three different whys. Convention: each atom's check starts with LAUNCH yes, partial or no; LANDING is the landing field. Weak launches: no-adapter-branch, no-default-deps, root-no-capture, assembly-returns-services, listen-driver-only, test-isolated-state, test-via-contract, no-prod-config. Judgment words kept as remainder, never atoms: 'thin', 'orchestrates, does not compute', 'meaningful port', 'documented behavior', 'implementation details', 'boring', 'taste', kernel litmus and utils judgments (1304-1311, 1400-1407), 'closed input set' (1172). Not in canon but silent: wiring branches in drivers, test ambient access, blob and the root atoms.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service, adapters < assembly < drivers < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must be developable, testable and reasonable without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import edge, importer kind vs importee kind, against the layer order.
atoms.landing: The map's arrows all point one way; an outward import is visible by path alone.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (and, unstated, by test); type-only imports and private/ of the same service are exempt.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place where dependencies are resolved, so a unit imported elsewhere scatters assembly logic and defeats code splitting.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind in {service, adapter}, not under private/, runtime import, importer kind not assembly.
atoms.landing: A reader sees that nothing but assembly knows a concrete implementation exists.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import blob, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantees, so any other layer importing it contaminates guarantees it had.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee has no layer suffix, importer kind not in {assembly, test, blob}.
atoms.landing: Unplaced code is visible as debt and has exactly one door into the graph.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies (and tests as callers), type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so consumers must type against service APIs, not against the wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind assembly, importer kind not in {driver, assembly, test}, every import kind.
atoms.landing: The chunk graph and the map show assembly as a root, never as a dependency.

atoms.name: driver-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: The runtime or the boot starts a driver; nothing else may reach it, or a hook could be chained through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind driver, importer kind not in {boot, driver}.
atoms.landing: The entry chain boot -> driver -> assembly is the only way in.

atoms.name: entry-unimported
atoms.statement: A boot file and a test file are imported by nothing.
atoms.why: The runtime starts these files (node runs the boot, the runner runs the spec); importing one would run or couple what only the runtime may start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero inbound import edges to files of kind boot or test.
atoms.landing: Entry points are leaves, so a human can list the program's starts by listing the leaves.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is hidden must stay changeable without touching outsiders.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import path contains private/ and importer is outside the owning service folder.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import path is an instant visible violation.

atoms.name: service-dag
atoms.statement: Dependencies between service packages, every import kind counted, form a DAG; a parent is import-blind to its public nested children.
atoms.why: A service cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: contract imports to service-package edges, cycle detection; the direction law is the same edge check.
atoms.landing: The service graph reads as layers of independent packages.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules form no cycle, even within one service; type-only cycles are out.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import graph cycle detection (madge-like).
atoms.landing: Every file has a load order a human can state.

atoms.name: concrete-import-gate
atoms.statement: A file imports concrete platform/IO code (node:fs, HTTP client, database driver, container library) only in a kind allowed to touch the world: adapter, a driver for its own claimed tech, test, blob; assembly only for a declared container library.
atoms.why: Contact with the world must sit where a contract (port) or a boundary (driver) covers it, or the inside bypasses its ports and becomes untestable.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: external package import classified concrete by declaration or reader claim, importer kind not in allowed set.
atoms.landing: A node: import in a service is red on sight; all IO is in adapters.

atoms.name: pure-lib-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party library counts as model only if its purity is declared in config, not presumed.
atoms.why: An undeclared library may hold I/O or ambient state, which would smuggle concrete code into the inside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: third-party import from a model/service/port file must match a declared-pure list, else read as concrete.
atoms.landing: The list of trusted pure libraries is one reviewable declaration.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: Every import path names the layer it reaches; no index file or barrel re-exports across layers.
atoms.why: The dependency matrix is enforceable by tooling and review only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no files named index re-exporting, imports resolve straight to a layer file.
atoms.landing: Reading an import line tells you the layer with no file to open.

atoms.name: port-runtime-free
atoms.statement: A .port.ts file contains no runtime code, only types.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it means an adapter or wiring has not been extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: port file emits no value declaration, call or statement beyond type exports/imports.
atoms.landing: Opening a port file shows nothing but shapes.

atoms.name: port-import-typed
atoms.statement: No runtime import edge touches a port file in either direction; ports are reached through import type.
atoms.why: Ports are erased at runtime, so a runtime edge to or from one is a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import of a port file lacking the type modifier, or a runtime import inside a port file.
atoms.landing: Ports never appear in the runtime graph.

atoms.name: root-immutable
atoms.statement: A module root holds no binding whose immutability the syntax does not prove (primitive type, as const, readonly types, Object.freeze), exported or not; instances are never exported.
atoms.why: A file must be testable in its own right: a test importing it gets the module every other test got, and nothing it runs changes what the next test sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root bindings (let, unfrozen collections, call results) against a proof-of-immutability check on declared types.
atoms.landing: State is visible only inside factories; a root holds only constants.

atoms.name: root-no-machine
atoms.statement: A root binding never stores a value read from the machine (environment, clock, randomness, tech); import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed fixed.
atoms.why: Such a value captures load-time machine state, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root initializers reading claimed tech/global names, property reads included, call results aside.
atoms.landing: A root constant is the same on every run.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Module evaluation performs no side effect: no call reaching tech or unclaimed code, no use case, no call into a local function of an effect-allowed file, no assignment or delete statement; exemptions are a closed list (the boot's one call, a spec's registration calls).
atoms.why: Whatever sits at the root runs on import, so loading must neither act nor leave anything that could change.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: calls and statements at root checked by callee kind and reader claims; effect-freedom of a tech call needs a reader declaration.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing a human has to know about.

atoms.name: outside-defines-nothing
atoms.statement: Assembly defines only assembly functions, a driver only its hooks and at most one wiring function, a boot nothing; any other function, class or variable is residue.
atoms.why: The widest import rights must carry the narrowest verbs, or the outside becomes the place where logic hides without contract, port or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations in a file of kind assembly/driver/boot against the kind's closed definition list.
atoms.landing: Outside files read as lists of calls; any other shape is an alarm.

atoms.name: ambient-reads-gated
atoms.statement: Model, service, assembly and boot never read the environment, time, randomness, console, timers or host globals; they receive them as arguments or through a port; adapters, drivers, tests and blob may.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting that machine up; assembly and boot hold no tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: global identifier and property reads (Date, Math.random, process, console, setTimeout, globalThis, document) in a gated kind, at root or in function.
atoms.landing: Everything that touches the machine is in files declared for it.

atoms.name: listen-only-driver
atoms.statement: Only a driver registers callbacks on the program's inbound tech (parser, server, runner, mounted component); an adapter calls tech only outbound.
atoms.why: The driver is the one place that receives events, so every event path is findable.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: a callback handed to a claimed tech outside a driver; indistinguishable from an outbound callback API (fs.readFile(cb)) without a reader cut.
atoms.landing: All entry paths of the program are in driver files.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A service or adapter factory declares its dependencies as parameters with no default values.
atoms.why: A default creates an import from service to adapter or config source and scatters assembly logic across modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializer on a factory parameter; deciding which parameters are dependencies needs the port/service types.
atoms.landing: Every dependency of a unit appears in its signature and is supplied from one place.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-factories
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory of a composition unit, another assembly, a blob file, or a model factory; no model function that computes, no use-case call.
atoms.why: Assembly decides nothing but which factory to call, so no pipeline or computation hides in the wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus the flavor's create* word to tell a model factory from a function.
atoms.landing: The assembly graph is the map of what builds what, with no hidden behavior.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: The only use cases an assembly may call are loads the project names in config.
atoms.why: Nothing in the shape of a call tells a load from a use case run for effect, so permission must be declared.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: awaited use-case call in an assembly must match the declared list.
atoms.landing: The few places where the graph depends on data are listed in one declaration.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: A call's result in assembly is only passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed (a declared load's result is a tech value, readable); a hook returns or drops its call's value and never reads, writes, hands on or logs it.
atoms.why: Touching what was built or fired is a decision or translation that belongs to a service, not to the outside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: data flow of the call-result binding: allowed sinks are return and factory argument (assembly) or return and nothing (hook).
atoms.landing: What the outside moves it never opens.

atoms.name: args-not-computed
atoms.statement: Arguments of a call in an assembly, a wiring function or a hook are literals, tech values as received, or instances; never derived, defaulted or transformed.
atoms.why: A derived argument is the outside doing logic itself instead of the service or adapter that needs the value.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expressions limited to identifiers, literals, and (assembly/wiring only) field reads.
atoms.landing: Arguments read as plain handoffs.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
