atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance or on a computed value is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operands trace to parameters or declared-load results, arms contain only factory calls.
atoms.landing: The graph's variants are readable as config switches.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and returns adapters only if every caller is a test.
atoms.why: Consumers type against service APIs, and a test factory hands back fakes because a spec asserts on what they recorded.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: returned values classified by the callee kind that built them; adapters returned requires all importers to be tests.
atoms.landing: Production assemblies expose services only.

atoms.name: driver-reader
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file has a reader bound to it by glob, or is bound on purpose to a reader that counts it as blob.
atoms.why: No other driver rule can be judged without the reading that says what is tech and what is a hook.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file of kind driver/test with no bound reader in config.
atoms.landing: Each outside file declares which technology it speaks.

atoms.name: driver-wiring-only
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver only wires: assembly calls, tech setup, sub-driver registration, with tech values, instances or literals as arguments.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place and a hook never wires.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statements in a driver outside hook bodies against the closed wiring list.
atoms.landing: A driver's top level reads as setup, its hooks as one-liners.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: Each hook makes exactly one use-case call; zero and two or more are violations.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence that is a use case nobody owns, zero hides logic with no home; one call is all there is to know about the link.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count call expressions in a hook body cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: The map draws a driver's link to a service as one arrow.

atoms.name: hook-reads-nothing
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event on as received: host values whole, nothing read off them, no default, no transform.
atoms.why: Any translation between event and call is a use case, and translation belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expressions of the hook's call are bare parameters, host globals or literals, no member access.
atoms.landing: Hooks contain no knowledge of the event's shape.

atoms.name: body-flat
atoms.statement: A hook body, and everything reachable from it in the file, contains no branch and no loop.
atoms.why: A path fork inside a body is behavior the reader must reconstruct, in a driver it is translation and in a test it is a scenario hidden from review.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: no if/switch/ternary/loop/&&/?? in reachable local functions; iterator methods, recursion and table-driven runners need an explicit loop list.
atoms.landing: One straight reading of a body shows everything it does.

atoms.name: driver-callees
atoms.statement: A driver calls only use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring functions and tech its bound readers claim; never an adapter, never a model, never an unclaimed name or pure library.
atoms.why: Anything a driver triggers must pass through a service contract, or it is an effect or a computation no contract and no test covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind or package against reader claims; matrix also bars runtime import of model/unit/blob in a driver.
atoms.landing: A driver's calls all land on services or the tech.

atoms.name: subdriver-call-site
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, outside any hook, passing tech and instances.
atoms.why: A hook calling a sub-driver or passing it a use-case result would chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: imported driver binding is used only as callee at wiring level with tech/instance arguments.
atoms.landing: One entry point can split into files without hiding a chain.

atoms.name: subdriver-export-one
atoms.statement: A sub-driver exports exactly one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: The only thing the root can do with the import is let it attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver imported by another driver.
atoms.landing: A sub-driver's surface is a single registration entry.

atoms.name: boot-one-import
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start; any other import gives it something to do or hold.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list of a boot file, tech and types included.
atoms.landing: The program's start is one import line.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's only root statement is one call to the driver's wiring function with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and the call is the whole start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements of a boot file count and argument list.
atoms.landing: The program has one visible start per entry point.

atoms.name: test-support-placed
atoms.statement: A file imported only by test files declares a non-test, non-blob kind: fake or in-memory implementation is an adapter, test factory an assembly, data builder a model, shared matcher or hook a driver.
atoms.why: Shared test code placed by what it is falls under that kind's rules instead of inheriting the test kind's exemptions.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer set of a file is all tests while its kind is blob or test.
atoms.landing: No file hides under a test label; support code is as legible as production code.

atoms.name: unit-exports-factory
atoms.statement: A .service.ts or .adapter.ts exports a factory function and no instance.
atoms.why: A composition unit is something built by assembly, and an instance exported from a module breaks the stable root.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: exports of a service/adapter file are functions, not values.
atoms.landing: Every unit is something you build, never something you import ready.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file implements a port it type-imports and holds only what that port needs.
atoms.why: An adapter exists to translate between a port's shape and an external technology.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: exported value assignable to a type-imported port type via the compiler; 'nothing of the hexagon's' is not structural.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the contract it fulfills.

rules.remainder: Says 'lateral (same layer) OK', which contradicts unit-assembly-only (service->service and adapter->adapter are forbidden); the matrix is a table of the intersection, not a rule.
'No index.ts indirection' is checkable; 'the layer is visible' is the landing, not a check.
Derived: the edge atoms composed transitively; its only own content is the third-party transitive purity, which only a declaration can settle. No atom of its own.
'Deterministic' for a third-party library cannot be proven; 'becomes untestable' is the why, not a check.
'Distinct from service-purity' is a placement note; adapters/drivers permitted is a scope clause.
'Build it and inject it behind a port' is assembly's atoms; 'unplaced code needs characterization tests' is a rationale.
Lists importers forbidden (model, ports, other service-layer code, adapters, drivers, blob) which is the same set the matrix states from the importer side.
Duplicate of service-assembly-only with a different suffix; same atom, same scope list.

Not an atom: a scope clause (type-only imports exempt) on unit-assembly-only, and its SomeService[method] shorthand note; it explicitly does not reach blob, private, service-dag, assembly or driver importers.
Not an atom: a scope clause (private/ of the same service exempt) on unit-assembly-only.
Two checks in one slug: file content and import edges.
Whole rule is a judgment: 'service branches on which adapter it got' and 'same result shape' have no structural check without type-level analysis; hole.
The direction law (parent import-blind to public children) is the same edge check stated again.
Judgment: 'documented behavior', 'no implementation details', 'refactor breaks no test'. Only mechanical shadow: layer-in-path and private-sealed on the test's imports. Hole.

'Assembly and driver in one' is a label that bundles nothing checkable; 'fixtures follow the same isolation rules' and 'production config has no place' have no structural check; '.e2e' is listed as a test kind but declared 'neither, outside the graph'. Exemptions it lists (hook count, services-only, defines anything, imports anything) are not carried atoms.

'No use-case call: a pipeline hiding in the wiring' and 'a decision the map cannot show' are whys; 'config wired as dependency by default' is guidance, not a check; the whole rule is a bundle of eight atoms, with 'adapters only when called by a test' being an in-rule exception.
'Lazy features are an assembly importing another' is guidance.

'Facade is missing' and 'logic with no home' are whys; the exit code and rendering being the service's job through ports is placement guidance, not checkable; the test tech exempts only the count by canon's words, leaving the rest unstated.
'Parsing and rendering are use cases' is the why; 'unclaimed' depends on reader claims, which is the mechanism.
'Never a hook, never hexagon data' restates hook-one-call and result-untouched.

'A shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' is an open clause, so a hole by definition; 'the reading declares a call effect-free' is a declaration mechanism; mutableModuleState lifts only the binding half.

kinds.note: The most constrained: imports model only, reads no machine, root is stable.
Types only, nothing else to carry.
As model plus the composition-unit atoms, as importee.
Does not carry concrete-import-gate or ambient-reads-gated: it is the kind allowed to touch the world. Whether stable-root reaches adapters and blob is ambiguous in canon (1110-1112 implies yes).
The only kind besides test allowed to import blob and units; root holds imports only, which is outside-defines-nothing plus root-no-effect.
No ambient or concrete gate: it holds the tech.
root-no-effect exempts its one call by kind.

Right to import units and blob and to read the machine comes from not carrying the gates (and unit-assembly-only/blob-import-gate name tests as allowed importers, which canon at 270 omits). Not carried: hook-single-call, hook-reads-nothing, result-untouched, args-not-computed, driver-callees, outside-defines-nothing, assembly-*, wiring-branch-only, driver-wiring-only, ambient/concrete gates, no-default-deps. Whether a spec importing a driver conflicts with driver-importers is unstated.
Graph atoms only; no layer guarantees by definition. Canon at 1110-1112 hints stable-root also reads blob, ambiguous.

sharedParts.problem: Stated three times with three definition lists (assembly functions; hooks plus one wiring function; nothing), also in L278-279 and L643-652, and the test kind is exempted by 'defines anything'; one atom with a per-kind allowed list removes the exemption.

Restated per layer: model bullet (L295), service 'module-level code stateless' (L341), assembly 'nothing at module root but imports' (L481), then stable-root; the layer wordings can drift from the single check.
A Date.now() or process.env stored at root of a model is red by both ambient-access ('same at module root') and stable-root; two slugs, one check, two reports.
Stated for model/service in ambient-access, as 'holds no tech' for assembly (L254, 490) and 'touches no tech' for boot (L712); same global-read check with a different scope list in each place.

Same flow check in two vocabularies (touched/computed/member-accessed vs read/written/handed on/logged); the allowances differ: assembly may hand results on, a hook may not, which is not visible as one atom.
Three wordings of one argument-shape check; assembly and wiring allow a field read of a tech value while hooks read nothing, hidden as three separate rules.
The same importer check duplicated for service and adapter slugs; the 'lateral OK' in inward-deps contradicts it, and the allowed importer set omits test although tests import units.
Assembly's right to blob is stated in blob-quarantine and again in assembly-builds-only (L453-455, 489-490), and the driver ban a third time (L650-652, 957-959).
The dependency matrix restates each import atom from the importer side while the composition slugs state it from the importee side; a driver->service import is forbidden four times.

'Nothing imports a boot', 'nothing imports a test' and 'only a boot or driver imports a driver' share one why (the runtime starts these files, L541-543, said only for drivers) but are stated three times.
The direction law (L817-826, parent import-blind to its public children) restates the cycle check as a second rule.
A spec calls a shared driver's wiring function (registerMatchers) while test-is-outside says 'imports anything'; whether a test is a driver for importer purposes is unstated.
'A hook does not wire' and 'never from a hook' repeat the count/placement check in three places; the test tech exempts only the count (L1057), leaving other hook atoms undefined for a test.
Canon exempts the test kind from about ten rules by text instead of carrying a selection; '.e2e' is both a test kind (L263) and 'neither assembly nor driver' (L1022).

testKind: A test builds units, calls them and asserts, and nothing imports it. CARRY: entry-unimported (a leaf, run by the runner), driver-reader (the test reader says what a hook is), root-immutable, root-no-machine and root-no-effect (registration calls by the runner are the closed exemption; this also forces each test to assemble its own instance, because a root-level instance is a non-provable binding), body-flat (the reviewer must read a scenario straight, and canon already names data-driven indirection as the way a suite defeats review), subdriver-call-site when it imports a shared driver, test-support-placed, and the universal graph atoms (layer-in-path, private-sealed, service-dag, module-acyclic, port-import-typed). DO NOT CARRY: hook-single-call (it calls the unit several times), hook-reads-nothing, result-untouched and args-not-computed (it reads results to assert and builds its inputs), driver-callees (it calls adapters/models directly, a plain function is tested directly), outside-defines-nothing (it defines fixtures), assembly-calls-factories, wiring-branch-only and assembly-returns-services (setup calls use cases and keeps fakes), ambient-reads-gated, concrete-import-gate and blob-import-gate (it is allowed tech, concrete and blob), no-default-deps (defaults are right in tests). So the ten exceptions become atoms the kind simply does not hold, and what it holds (leaf, stable root, flat bodies) is what makes a suite reviewable. Verified from canon text: the carried list and the exemptions in 1022-1023 and 1057. Inferred: body-flat for tests, since canon exempts only the count.
helpers: Yes, body-flat must reach inside local helpers; a 'no' is a laundering venue. Structure that avoids it: (1) scope the atom by reach, not by lexical body: it applies to the hook body and to every function reachable from it in the file (the same principle as chain-purity, constraint as a chain property); a loop or branch in a local run() is then red exactly as in the test body. (2) Make the way out a promotion, never an exemption: a helper that genuinely needs control flow leaves the file and is placed by what it is (test-support-placed): a run() that spawns the CLI and collects output is an adapter fixture behind a port, a looping setup is an assembly function, which allows a branch or loop only on parameters with factory arms (wiring-branch-only). Each such helper then carries its own kind's atoms, so nothing hides under the test label and the spec keeps straight lines like await run(args). (3) Treat other loop spellings as loops by explicit list: .map/.forEach/.reduce, recursion, and test.each tables; the checker cannot see a loop in a function value passed in from elsewhere, so a callee that is not a local function and not a declared pure model function stays a hole, limited by test-support-placed forcing imported helpers to have a kind. Residual hole: judgment of what counts as 'DRY-ed setup that hides the scenario', which no check sees.

atoms.name: import-inward
atoms.statement: A runtime import goes to the same layer or an inner one along model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot (test outermost).
atoms.why: The inside must be buildable, testable and reasonable about without knowing anything outside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer and importee kinds come from the flavor, compare ranks per runtime edge. Type-edge scope is unstated by canon (see hole in rules).
atoms.landing: A reader sees from any import list that nothing inner knows what is outer.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: Every import specifier resolves to the file of a declared layer; no index/barrel re-export hides which layer is imported.
atoms.why: The dependency matrix is enforceable (by tool or reviewer) only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolved target is not an index file or barrel re-export, and its kind is readable from its name.
atoms.landing: The layer of every dependency is readable from the import path alone, no file to open.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: Model, ports, service and assembly runtime-import no platform/IO code (node:fs, HTTP client, DB driver); a third-party package counts as concrete unless declared pure (or, for assembly, as a declared container library).
atoms.why: Concrete code bypasses the ports and makes the inside untestable.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes, given a config classification of packages and builtins (pure-declared / container / concrete); undeclared defaults to concrete.
atoms.landing: The import list proves that no effect enters the inside or the assembly.

atoms.name: assembly-only-import
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file is runtime-imported only by assembly files.
atoms.why: Assembly is the only place dependencies are resolved; a static import from a service to its adapters defeats IoC and code splitting and scatters assembly logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind service/adapter and public (not under private/), importer kind must be assembly; runtime edges only.
atoms.landing: Who builds what is answered by one place; services never visibly know the graph.

atoms.name: no-blob-import
atoms.statement: No file but assembly or a test imports a blob file, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so anything importing it contaminates a layer that had guarantees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee has no declared layer; importer kind not in {assembly, test}; both edge kinds count.
atoms.landing: Debt stays visible: unplaced code is reachable only from the two places that can quarantine it.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: No file outside a service imports from that service's private/ directory, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: private/ is the only visibility boundary.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path contains private/ and importer is outside the owning service directory; both edge kinds.
atoms.landing: A private/ import in a review is an instant violation; the public surface is the listing minus private/.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Service-package import edges form a DAG, every import kind counted.
atoms.why: A cycle means no service in it can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files to service packages, detect cycles on all edge kinds.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG; the direction of every parent/child pair is fixed.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules form no cycle, even within one service; type-only cycles are not covered.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently with undefined in minified production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: cycle detection on runtime edges only.
atoms.landing: Load order is never a question when reading a module.

atoms.name: ports-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds only types, and no runtime import touches a port in either direction.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code in it means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no runtime-emitting statements in a port file; any non-type import of or from one is red. The edge half is mostly derived from the content half; only the missing-type-keyword case is its own check.
atoms.landing: Opening a port file shows a contract and nothing executable.

atoms.name: no-contract-importers
atoms.statement: A kind that exports no contract is imported, type imports included, only by the kinds the matrix names: assembly by drivers and assemblies, driver by boots and drivers, boot by nothing, test by nothing.
atoms.why: These kinds have no contract to type against, so any import of them depends on an implementation; the runtime starts them, not other files.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind and importer-kind list per kind; all edge kinds.
atoms.landing: The chain boot -> driver -> assembly is the only way in; a test or boot is a leaf.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports no model file (type imports free).
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service, not driver code.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee kind model from a driver file, runtime edge only.
atoms.landing: The driver's import list is only assemblies, drivers and its tech.

atoms.name: boot-one-import
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: A boot's one thing is to start the program through its one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import count is 1 and its kind is driver.
atoms.landing: The entry is one line pointing at one driver.

atoms.name: ambient-access
atoms.statement: A file never reads or calls ambient environment (env, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) from a global; the caller or a port hands it over.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for a listed set of global names (the list itself is not in canon); same at root, in a condition, a value or a call.
atoms.landing: The signature lists everything the code depends on.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly, frozen literal, each to its depth).
atoms.why: A module must be the same on every load so a test importing it gets what every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: syntactic proof; config opt-out mutableModuleState lifts only this atom. Unresolvable named types prove nothing.
atoms.landing: Module-level state is visibly absent; a module exports factories, not instances.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-read
atoms.statement: A root binding stores nothing read from the machine (tech property, clock, randomness); import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed identity, not machine.
atoms.why: A stored machine value fixes the load-time environment, so the file cannot be tested under another without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: initializer expressions at root contain no tech or ambient read; the presumption list is closed.
atoms.landing: Root holds only values independent of where and when it ran.

atoms.name: no-root-calls
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation makes no call that reaches tech or something no reading claims, runs a use case, or enters a local function of a side-effect layer (adapter, blob).
atoms.why: Loading must not act or leave anything behind, so every load is the same.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: classify root call callees; property reads are presumed free, calls are not, until a reading declares a call effect-free. Not lifted by mutableModuleState.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing.

atoms.name: no-root-statements
atoms.statement: Module root holds no statement that only makes sense at run time (assignment, delete and the like); throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a run-time statement is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement-kind scan of root.
atoms.landing: Root is declarations and imports.

atoms.name: build-calls-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly builds: a factory of a composition unit, another assembly, a blob file (injected behind a port) or a model factory; a model function that computes is not a build.
atoms.why: The file with the widest import right must do almost nothing or it becomes the place logic hides.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus the flavor's factory name (stock create*) for model callees. Awaiting a call is the call.
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as the graph being built, and the map can draw it.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: What a call returns is never read, branched on, computed with, written, logged or member-accessed; it is only passed on to a permitted call or returned (or dropped).
atoms.why: Outside code that touches what it built or received is logic with no contract, port or test, and a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: result-flow analysis from each call to its uses. The declared-load result is reclassified as a tech value by load-declared, not excepted here.
atoms.landing: Instances flow through the outside unopened, so the outside is boring.

atoms.name: load-declared
atoms.statement: A use-case call in an assembly is legal only if the project declares it a load; its result counts as tech values from then on.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load the graph depends on from a use case run for effect, so the project must say.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee in the config declaration list; undeclared call is red and its resolution is the declaration.
atoms.landing: Every use case an assembly may await is a short named list.

atoms.name: args-given-only
atoms.statement: Every argument to a call in an assembly or a driver's wiring is a literal, a tech value (a field or destructured part may be read), or an instance built or received; nothing is computed in place.
atoms.why: A computed argument means the outside derives a value itself instead of the service or adapter that needs it, under its own rules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression classes (literal, parameter or field of one, instance binding); calls and operators in arguments are red.
atoms.landing: Each call's inputs are traceable to parameters or earlier builds.

atoms.name: branch-on-input
atoms.statement: In an assembly a branch or loop tests only a parameter or a loaded value, compared to a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A decision on an instance or computed value is one the map cannot show; it belongs to the service or adapter that owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand classes and arm contents.
atoms.landing: Variation in the graph depends only on configuration, visibly.

atoms.name: returns-services-only
atoms.statement: An assembly function returns services (one, or a record of services and shared model instances) and no adapter; a test factory is the one caller-conditional case.
atoms.why: Inferred: handing adapters outward gives a caller an effect no contract covers; the contract surface is service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for return types by flavor; the 'unless a test is the caller' clause needs a caller-kind check (see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: An assembly's return type is a service API.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file has a reader bound to its tech by glob; none is red (a reader that counts the file as blob is the declared way out).
atoms.why: Every other driver rule is judged through the reading, so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config glob binding; a reader's kind must agree with the flavor or be a config error.
atoms.landing: Each outside file states which tech it listens to.

atoms.name: claimed-tech-only
atoms.statement: A driver (and a test file) touches only imports and names that a bound reader claims as tech; an unclaimed import or name is red, and a pure library is model and red regardless.
atoms.why: Tech is exactly what a reading claims; anything unclaimed is undefined for judging hooks and wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import and global-name resolution against the reader's claims.
atoms.landing: A driver's whole outside surface is a small declared tech list.

atoms.name: one-call-per-hook
atoms.statement: Each hook, as the reader cuts hooks, contains exactly one use-case call, awaiting counted as the call.
atoms.why: Two calls mean the sequence between them is a use case nobody owns (it needs a facade with contract and test); zero means logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes, given the reader's hook cut and callee kind = service use case.
atoms.landing: The driver-to-service link is one arrow with nothing between.

atoms.name: no-branch-loop
atoms.statement: A function body contains no branch (if, switch, ternary, default or short-circuit fallback) and no loop (including iteration callbacks like forEach/map/reduce).
atoms.why: For hooks: translation around the call is the facade's use case. For tests (implied): the scenario must be readable as straight-line given/when/expect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow node scan; iteration-callback names must be listed or loops hide in them.
atoms.landing: The body is one flat sequence, readable as a statement.

atoms.name: args-as-received
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are what the event handed it, whole, plus instances and literals; nothing is read off them and host values go whole (process, never process.cwd()).
atoms.why: Choosing a field or defaulting a value is translation, which belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument is a hook parameter identifier, instance or literal; no member access or call.
atoms.landing: The hook is visibly a passthrough.

atoms.name: driver-callee-kinds
atoms.statement: A driver's calls never go to an adapter or a model.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers, and parsing/rendering are use cases of a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, including methods of instances from assembly.
atoms.landing: A driver's outgoing arrows land only on services, assembly and tech.

atoms.name: wiring-only-outside
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver only wires (assembly calls, tech setup, sub-driver registration), and a hook never wires.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place so no hook builds anything; the hook receives the hexagon already built.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: classify statements outside hooks and calls inside hooks by callee kind and region.
atoms.landing: A driver reads as setup followed by hooks, never mixed.

atoms.name: no-stray-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines nothing that exists at run time other than the functions its kind names (assembly: assembly functions; driver: hooks and one wiring function; boot: nothing).
atoms.why: A stray definition is residue: a model without a test, a service without a contract, blob hiding under a label.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declaration list versus the kind's role set; types are not definitions.
atoms.landing: Opening an outside file shows only its one role.

atoms.name: wiring-fn-shape
atoms.statement: A driver has at most one wiring function: a root driver's main() takes nothing and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's registerX takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: The signature bounds what can flow through wiring, so the only thing a parent can do with a sub-driver is attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count and parameter list of the wiring function.
atoms.landing: Wiring has one entry shape per driver.

atoms.name: driver-import-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, during its own wiring, never from a hook.
atoms.why: A hook calling a sub-driver or handing it a use-case result would chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: uses of a driver-kind import are call sites of its wiring function located outside hooks.
atoms.landing: Splitting hooks across files adds files, never behavior.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Exporting only the wiring function means a root can do nothing with the import except let it attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's export surface is one function.

atoms.name: boot-one-call
atoms.statement: A boot calls its driver's wiring function once, at module root, with no arguments, and evaluates nothing else (no tech, no binding).
atoms.why: The boot's one thing is to start; as the one module whose evaluation performs a call, its shape must be minimal and enumerable.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: exactly one root call to the imported function, zero arguments, no other identifiers evaluated; boot has no reader, so 'touches no tech' reduces to this structural check.
atoms.landing: The entry is the shebang, one import, one call.

atoms.name: explicit-deps
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory takes every dependency through its arguments, with no default values for dependencies.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import from the service to its adapters or config and scatters assembly logic across service modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers on factory parameters whose value is not a literal are checkable; whether a parameter is a dependency needs its type (port/service). Mostly covered by assembly-only-import.
atoms.landing: Every dependency of a unit is visible in its signature.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file type-imports the port it implements.
atoms.why: The suffix declares a port implementation, and an adapter reaches the hexagon only through that port.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: at least one type import from a port file in an adapter file. Canon implies it without a slug.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the contract it serves.

atoms.name: root-registers-only
atoms.statement: At a test file's module root the only calls are registrations the test tech owns.
atoms.why: The test runner loads the file and expects registration at load; nothing else may act at load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root call callees against the test reader's registration list.
atoms.landing: A spec's root is a table of contents of registrations.

atoms.name: e2e-black-box
atoms.statement: An .e2e file imports no program file and starts shipped entry points as a user would.
atoms.why: End-to-end tests are users of the shipped drivers, outside the graph.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no runtime or type import resolves into the program's files. Canon states the outside-the-graph status but no slug.
atoms.landing: An e2e names the shipped surface it exercises, and nothing inside.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is a permission, not a constraint. Hole: canon says the matrix governs runtime imports, so whether inward direction applies to type imports (model type-importing a service) is unstated.
'Violations visible by shape' is the landing goal, not a constraint.

Derived, not an atom: it is the per-edge atoms applied to every file. 'Partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a consequence. Transitive purity through third-party packages is an act of faith (declared pure), not checkable.
'Pure, deterministic libraries are model; purity declared, not presumed' is a config declaration, not checkable by structure (deterministic and side-effect-free are claims).

The list of ambient global names is not in canon (hole). 'At module root' duplicates root atoms: see sharedParts. 'Adapters and drivers reach the environment' is a scope statement (those kinds do not carry the atom).

'Assembly may take it because its rule bounds what it can do' is a justification that depends on build-calls-only and result-untouched: a cross-rule dependency, not a constraint. 'A test may take it for characterization tests' is a kind-scope statement.
None beyond the scope clause 'not by model, ports, other service code, adapters, drivers or blob' (all instances of the one atom).
Same atom as service-assembly-only with a different importee kind; the slug split is redundant.
Not an atom: an edge-kind modifier on assembly-only-import (type-only edges exempt). Each other import atom restates its own edge-kind scope (see sharedParts).

Not an atom: a scope modifier (private/ files exempt) of assembly-only-import. Hole: nothing constrains the factory of an adapter that doubles as composition root for its own private/ sub-adapters (159-167).
'Sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is the why. 'One port shaped to the inside's needs' (118-123) is judgment.
Hole: 'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' is only partly mechanical (instanceof or discriminant read on an injected dependency); no atom was made of it.
None.
The direction law (817-826) is a consequence of this atom plus adapter-implements-port, not a separate constraint. 'Enforced by tooling in CI' is process.
None.

Only the private-sealed part is mechanical. Hole: 'assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details', the (a)/(b) exceptions for internal unit tests, and 'unit under test identifiable at a glance' are judgments.

A bundle of exemptions rather than constraints: 'imports anything', 'defines anything', 'hook count and services-only do not apply' are absences of atoms; 'setup builds units with fixtures' and 'test bodies are hooks' are the region cut. Shared-test-code placement (adapter/assembly/model/driver by what it is) is derived from no-contract-importers and the other kinds' atoms. 'By the shape of the test tech' is judgment.

Molecule of eight or nine. 'Every call is there to build' and 'decides nothing but which factory to call' state intent; the checker sees callee kind. 'A pipeline hiding in the wiring' is a consequence. The model-factory/function split depends on the flavor naming convention (create*). Ambient-access in assembly is implied by 'holds no tech' (253-255, 491), not stated as a rule.
'An assembly has no contract to depend on' is the why.
Binding a reader that counts the file as blob is a declared escape hatch, a config fact.
'A lazily loaded feature is an assembly importing another' is illustration.

'The call is a use case' needs callee-kind resolution against service APIs. 'A second call means a facade is missing' is advice. Hooks are cut by the reader and 'a reader with its own cut says where the line sits' is reader-dependent and unspecified for the view-model case.

The whitelist 'use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring, own tech' is the union of hook-one-call's and wiring-outside-hooks' lists, so only 'never an adapter, never a model' is new (see sharedParts).
'Residue' and 'a model without a test' are the why, not checks. Hole: wiring functions branching or looping (a main() with an if) is not addressed.

'Never data from the hexagon' is covered by args-given-only plus result-untouched. 'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a scope note. Calling a sub-driver from a hook is also barred by one-call-per-hook and wiring-only-outside (redundant).
None.

'Holds nothing' is undefined (bindings? covered by root atoms). 'A program has one per entry point' is a count with no stated check. The root call exemption it needs from stable-root is made positive by this slug's own atom.

Molecule: four checks under one why, only one of which the mutableModuleState switch can lift (proof that they are distinct atoms). Holes: 'a shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule, not waved through' (1088-1090) is an open judgment clause; the presumption that import.meta.url is not a machine read; the closed exemption list (boot call, spec registration) is two kind-specific exceptions, dissolved here by giving boot and test their own positive root atoms.

kinds.note: Edge atoms about importers (assembly-only-import, no-blob-import, no-contract-importers) are carried by the importee's kind; model carries none of those as importee. A factory counts as model only when it depends on nothing (follows from import-inward).
Type-only content makes the root atoms trivially true.
Model logic inside a service file inherits the service's constraints; the reverse never holds.
Does not carry no-concrete-import or ambient-access: concrete systems and the environment are its business. 'Holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' (276-278) is a hole, not an atom.
Does not carry no-blob-import (assembly may import blob: the atoms above bound what it does with it). Open: the test factory returning adapters needs a home (see sharedParts).

Atoms are region-scoped: hook, wiring, root. Does not carry ambient-access (the tech's business) or no-concrete-import (replaced by claimed-tech-only). A reader's exemption is the only relaxation canon allows, each stated with its reason.
Does not carry the root atoms: boot-one-call replaces them positively (one call at root, nothing else). No reader is bound, so structure alone must show it touches no tech.
Carries no layer guarantee; its quarantine is entirely on the importer side.

Union semantics, region by region: its import rights are the union of assembly's and driver's (so none of no-blob-import, driver-no-model, no-concrete-import apply as such; claimed-tech-only gates concrete tech). See testKind.

sharedParts.problem: One constraint (importers of a contract-less kind) stated five times with its own scope and 'type imports included' repeated; tests and web components appear as silent exceptions of whichever list is read.
One atom is split across two slugs by importee kind and restated in prose, with the type-only exemption (runtime-import) and private/ exemption (public-unit) attached as separate slugs.

Stated for model, service, ports and assembly with a config-declared exception only in assembly (container library); the driver variant is the inverse (claimed tech) under a different name, so test inherits neither cleanly.
A machine read stored at module root is red under both; ambient-access exempts adapters and drivers while stable-root does not, so the same fact is judged by two rules with different scopes.

inRules: assembly-builds-only ('nothing at module root but imports', 480-481)
sharedParts.problem: Stable-root is restated per kind with different strictness: assembly's 'imports only' is stricter than the rule it cites, and boot and test get kind-specific exemptions inside the rule instead of their own atoms.
Assembly may pass a result on and read a declared load's result; a hook may do neither; the same 'never read, computed with or accessed' is written twice, the load exception sitting inside it.
The literal/tech value/instance triple is stated in four places, with the hook version stricter (no field reads) and the assembly version permissive.
Three scopes of control-flow policy (none around a hook call, input-only in assembly, none in a test body); only the first two are written, the test one is a hole.
Four closed lists of 'what this kind may define' written as separate rules, while the test kind has the open list 'defines anything', which is the laundering venue for helpers.

driver-calls-services' whitelist is the union of the hook list (use case only) and the wiring list (assembly, tech setup, sub-driver); only 'never adapter, never model' is its own content, so the slug is a molecule of two existing atoms plus one.

Whether a type-only import counts is a property of each import atom, restated in prose per slug (exempt for composition, counted for blob, private, assembly, driver, service cycles); nothing keeps the statements consistent, and inward-deps is silent.

A shared test factory is an assembly function in an assembly file that returns adapters 'unless a test is the caller', so the assembly atom carries a caller-conditional exception: the test factory has no kind of its own.
The only mechanical part of test-through-contract is already private-sealed; the rest of the rule is judgment, so the rule hides how little of it is checkable.

Defaults are forbidden for production factories and 'right here' for tests; once explicit-deps is carried by composition units only and defaults live in assembly or test factories, the exception disappears.
Canon lists .e2e as a test file kind (assembly+driver in one) and also says e2e tests are 'neither', outside the graph: two contradictory scopes for the same suffix.

testKind: CARRY (recommendation; the first group is inferred from canon, the rest is stated): import-inward at outermost rank, layer-in-path, private-sealed, no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle, no-contract-importers (nothing imports a spec), reader-bound, claimed-tech-only (the runner and matchers are claimed tech; an unclaimed node:fs is red, so fixtures must be adapters), driver-import-wiring-only (shared registerMatchers), root-bindings-immutable, no-root-machine-read, no-root-statements, root-registers-only (the closed 'registration' exemption turned positive), ambient-access (inferred from 'isolation and determinism' 1193-1201, confirm), and no-branch-loop (implied by 1150-1161). DO NOT CARRY: one-call-per-hook, args-as-received, result-untouched, driver-callee-kinds, wiring-only-outside (a body builds, calls and asserts, so it must read results and make several calls), build-calls-only, load-declared, returns-services-only, branch-on-input (replaced by the stricter no-branch-loop), no-blob-import (characterization tests need blob), driver-no-model (setup needs data builders), no-concrete-import (claimed-tech-only gates it), explicit-deps (defaults are legal in assembly and test factories). Why: a test is assembly and driver by region, so its import rights are the union of both (that is all 'imports anything' means) and it keeps only verb atoms that do not contradict building units, calling them and asserting; nothing imports it, so only importer-side and root atoms apply. The ten-ish exemptions are then not exceptions but absences of atoms. OPEN QUESTION (helpers): yes, the no-branch-loop constraint must reach helpers, and by construction, not by extension. Scope it to the file (every function body the file defines, plus module root, not just 'test body'), because a local helper with no atoms is blob inside a test file, which is the exact laundering venue canon rules out elsewhere ('a decision written in either is blob hiding under a label'). Structure that closes it: (1) the atom is scoped by file kind, so any helper a spec defines is straight-line; (2) iteration callbacks (forEach, map, reduce, .each tables) and recursion count as loops; (3) flow that a scenario really needs is, by definition, not test-local and gets placed by what it is (data builder to model, fake with logic to adapter, wiring to assembly function), where it faces that kind's atoms; (4) no-contract-importers on the test keeps a spec from growing into a shared helper library; (5) imported helpers face their own file's atoms. Residual holes, not atoms: a model builder with loops that computes expected values (legal in model, but defeats 'visible in the test, not reconstructed from helpers'), assertions hidden in a straight-line helper, and data-driven registration through test.each. The helper run() that starts the shipped CLI belongs to .e2e (outside the graph, e2e-black-box); in a .spec it is a straight-line local function over the CLI service. Note the unresolved .e2e double status.
helpers: WHY-FIRST REASONS, grouped (canon line of the reason): R1 inside knowable and testable without the outside (112-114, 133-134, 942) -> import-inward, no-concrete-import, ports-types-only. R2 nothing unguaranteed under guarantees (937-939, 953-955) -> no-blob-import (chain-purity derived). R3 layer visible at the import site so the matrix is enforceable (759-766) -> layer-in-path. R4 machine-dependent code needs the machine to test (947-949) -> ambient-access. R5 same module on every load, no leaks between tests (1081-1085) -> four root atoms. R6 assembly is the only place dependencies are resolved; defaults scatter assembly logic and defeat splitting (376-381) -> assembly-only-import, explicit-deps. R7 port is a contract, runtime code means unextracted adapter (986) -> ports-types-only. R8 visibility is ownership (995-996) -> private-sealed. R9 extraction independence (902-906) -> no-service-cycle. R10 ESM cycles fail silently in production (915-917) -> no-runtime-cycle. R11 a file with the widest import right must do almost nothing or logic hides (396-398, 435-437, 643-648, 416-419) -> build-calls-only, result-untouched, load-declared, args-given-only, branch-on-input, returns-services-only, no-stray-definitions, wiring-only-outside, boot atoms. R12 translation or a call sequence is a use case that needs a facade with contract and test; zero calls is logic with no home (596-600, 612-613) -> one-call-per-hook, no-branch-loop, args-as-received. R13 an adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers; parse and render are services (617-620) -> driver-callee-kinds, driver-no-model. R14 a decision on an instance is invisible to the map (477-479, 410-414) -> branch-on-input, result-untouched. R15 no driver rule can be judged without the reading; tech is what a reading claims (82-86, 585-587) -> reader-bound, claimed-tech-only. R16 a kind with no contract is started by the runtime, not imported (484-485, 541-543) -> no-contract-importers. R17 a sub-driver could chain two calls through indirection (637-639) -> driver-import-wiring-only, driver-exports-wiring. R18 tests prove the contract, are optimized for the reviewer, and stay isolated (1142-1148, 1152-1161, 1193-1201) -> mostly judgment; mechanical residue is private-sealed, root atoms and the implied no-branch-loop. Missing a stated why: returns-services-only (inferred), unified-port, chain-purity (consequence), test-factory home. CONVENTIONS I USED: (a) Import-side atoms are carried by the importer kind (import-inward, no-concrete-import, driver-no-model, boot-one-import, claimed-tech-only); importer-list atoms are carried by the importee kind (assembly-only-import, no-blob-import, no-contract-importers). A kind that lacks an atom simply does not carry it: that is how 'except' disappears. (b) Atoms are region-scoped: root, hook, wiring (outside hooks), setup. Driver = hook + wiring + root regions; test = the same regions plus setup; boot = root only. This is the structural key to the test kind: it is a region composition, not an exemption list. (c) Each import atom declares which edge kinds it counts: runtime only (assembly-only-import, no-runtime-cycle, import-inward per matrix), runtime and type (no-blob-import, private-sealed, no-contract-importers, no-service-cycle). Canon states this per slug; an atom-level field would remove the restatement. (d) Inputs a checker needs that canon leaves outside the atoms: flavor (suffix -> kind, create* factory names), reader (bound by glob: tech claims, hook cut, registration list, reader exemptions each stated with a reason), config (pure-declared packages, declared loads, declared container library, mutableModuleState, ambient name list: absent from canon). Reader exemptions are themselves a per-tech 'except' mechanism and deserve the same atom treatment. (e) Kind-scoped classification of a package: pure (model), concrete, claimed tech, unclaimed (red in driver). (f) Hole summary, none turned into atoms: 'thin', 'meaningful', unified-port branching, adapter 'holds only what its port needs', 'documented behavior', 'implementation details', stable-root's open clause 'judged by the rule', prod-config-in-tests (1200-1201), assembly 'nothing at root but imports' vs 'assembly functions defined' (literal contradiction at 477-481), fractal assembly inside a unit's private/ (159-167) governed by no atom.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or an inner one, by the rank model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: An inner layer must be understandable and testable without the layers outside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: kind of importer vs kind of target, from the flavor's names. Canon states it for runtime imports only (875); whether a type import of a port from model counts is unstated.
atoms.landing: The layer of every import path is visible, so a reader sees an outward edge without opening a file.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file imports no concrete platform/IO module (node:fs, an HTTP client, a database driver, a container library) unless the project has declared it pure or declared it as the tech.
atoms.why: A concrete import bypasses the ports, so the file cannot be tested without the world.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: import specifier resolved against a declared purity list and a declared container-library list; purity is declared, not inferred (943).
atoms.landing: A reader knows that a file with this atom touches no world; the world is only behind ports.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A file reads no ambient global (time, randomness, console, timers, environment, process, globalThis), at module root or in a function, in a call or a condition or a value.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on the machine it runs on and cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reference to an identifier in the ambient-name list that is not a received parameter.
atoms.landing: Every input of the file is in its signature; a reader finds no hidden input.

atoms.name: composition-import-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service or .adapter file is imported at runtime only by assembly (and by test files, which are assembly in part).
atoms.why: Composition units are built in one place, so no layer can know a concrete implementation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every runtime edge into a public (non-private/) service or adapter file; type-only edges are not counted (runtime-import).
atoms.landing: The assembly graph is the only place instances are made; a reader finds construction by looking at assembly files only.

atoms.name: assembly-import-gate
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies (test files included), type imports counted too.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own; its shape is the services it returns, so consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge, type edges included.
atoms.landing: A reader knows who can ask for the built graph: drivers, and nothing else.

atoms.name: driver-import-gate
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver (a test file counts as a driver here), type imports counted too.
atoms.why: A driver is what the runtime starts; nothing may depend on it except to attach its callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge into a driver file, type edges included.
atoms.landing: The start chain boot -> driver -> sub-driver is the only way in; a reader sees the entry tree.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: A blob (suffixless) file is imported only by assembly, test or other blob files, type imports counted too.
atoms.why: Unplaced code carries no guarantee, so it must not leak into a layer that has one.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge into a file the flavor leaves blob, type edges included.
atoms.landing: Every contamination path of the debt is one of two kinds of file; the debt is visible and bounded.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file or a test file, type imports counted too.
atoms.why: The runtime, not the program, loads an entry (node runs the boot, the runner runs the spec), so an import of it is a second, unowned way to load it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero inbound edges on files of kind boot or test.
atoms.landing: A reader knows a test or a boot is a leaf nobody depends on; shared test code cannot hide in a file with a test name.

atoms.name: private-seal
atoms.statement: A file under private/ is imported only from inside its own service directory (nested services and parent services excluded), type imports counted too.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what the service hides must not become another service's dependency.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path of the target vs path of the importer; needs service-boundary detection from the layout.
atoms.landing: An import path containing private/ from outside is wrong by shape.

atoms.name: service-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of imports between service packages, every import kind counted, has no cycle.
atoms.why: Two services in a cycle can be neither extracted, moved nor reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package-level graph from file edges, SCC detection.
atoms.landing: The service map is a DAG a reader can read bottom-up.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: The graph of runtime imports between files has no cycle.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-level runtime graph, SCC detection; type-only edges not counted.
atoms.landing: Load order is never in doubt.

atoms.name: no-barrel-file
atoms.statement: No file re-exports other layers' files to stand for them (no index.ts); consumers import the layer file itself.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the matrix cannot be enforced by shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: a file named index, or a file made only of re-exports, resolved as an import target. What counts as a barrel beyond the name is unstated.
atoms.landing: A reader reads the layer off the import path.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime-code
atoms.statement: A port file holds only types: no value, statement, class or function.
atoms.why: A contract is separate from any implementation; runtime code in a port means the adapter is not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any value-level declaration or statement in a file of kind port.
atoms.landing: A port file can be read as pure shape.

atoms.name: port-type-edges-only
atoms.statement: Every import of a port file, and every import a port file makes, is type-only.
atoms.why: A port has no runtime, so a runtime edge touching it is a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge flags on edges into and out of port files.
atoms.landing: The type keyword on an import marks 'contract only' for the reader.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file implements a port it imports as a type: what it returns conforms to that port's interface.
atoms.why: The inside must never know which adapter it talks to, so every adapter of a port presents the same interface.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: adapter file type-imports at least one port; conformance of the returned shape needs the TS engine.
atoms.landing: A reader sees which contract an adapter serves from its first lines.

atoms.name: no-default-dependency
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives its dependencies no default value.
atoms.why: A default creates a static import from the service to its adapters and spreads assembly logic across service modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializer on a service or adapter factory parameter; telling a dependency from a plain option is not structural.
atoms.landing: Assembly is the only place a dependency is resolved; a service signature lists what it needs, no more.

atoms.name: root-immutable-bindings
atoms.statement: Every binding at module root is provably immutable by its syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly types, Object.freeze over a literal), each proven to its depth.
atoms.why: A test that imports a module must get the module every other test got, and nothing it runs may change what the next test sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: syntactic proof per root binding; an unresolved named type proves nothing and is red; config key mutableModuleState lifts this atom and no other.
atoms.landing: State lives only inside factory closures; a module exports factories, never instances.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness), whatever its declared type; import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed free.
atoms.why: A stored machine value fixes the machine's state at load, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: initializer expression of a root binding reaches an ambient or tech name.
atoms.landing: A reader knows a root constant is a constant.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-call
atoms.statement: A call at module root reaches no tech, no use case and no local function of a side-effect layer (adapter, blob), unless the reading declares that call effect-free; a property read is presumed free.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act, or the module cannot be tested in its own right.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee classification at root; the test reader's registration calls are declared effect-free by the reader, the config setting does not lift it.
atoms.landing: Importing a file does nothing a reader has to guess.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-statement
atoms.statement: No module-root statement other than a declaration or an import acts when evaluated (assignment, delete, and their like); a throw is not one.
atoms.why: What sits at root runs on import, so a statement that only makes sense at run time is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds at root.
atoms.landing: Same as root-no-effect-call: load is inert.

atoms.name: factory-calls-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is to a factory: a service, adapter, assembly or blob file's export, or a model function the flavor names a factory, plus the use cases the project declared as loads.
atoms.why: Assembly has one right, to build; any other call is a decision or a use.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee file kind, flavor name for model factories, declared-load list; a blob callee is a factory by construction (514) with no guarantee behind it; await is the call.
atoms.landing: An assembly reads as a build list; the map draws it as arrows.

atoms.name: result-not-read
atoms.statement: The result of a call is never branched on, computed with or member-accessed (a declared load's result, a tech value, may be read as a tech value).
atoms.why: Touching what was built is logic in the wiring, and a decision on an instance cannot be shown on the map; reading a use-case result in a hook is translation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: dataflow from call result to expressions; needs the TS engine for member access on instances.
atoms.landing: Built instances and results travel untouched; a reader never looks for logic on them.

atoms.name: args-value-only
atoms.statement: Every argument of a call is a literal, a tech value (a field or destructured part may be read, no call on it), or an instance built or received.
atoms.why: A derived argument is the file opening the door itself instead of the unit that owns the value.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: syntactic form of each argument expression plus origin of identifiers (parameter, built instance, import).
atoms.landing: A reader sees what flows through the wiring without evaluating anything.

atoms.name: branch-on-tech-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value, compared to a literal or for truthiness.
atoms.why: A condition on anything built or computed is a decision the map cannot show, and it belongs to the unit that owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: condition expression form and origin.
atoms.landing: All variability of the graph is a visible switch on the received tech values.

atoms.name: returns-built-only
atoms.statement: An assembly function returns only what it built: services or shared model instances.
atoms.why: The assembly's shape toward its callers is the services it returns; a computed value there is a hidden computation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: return expressions traced to call results of factories; type of the instance.
atoms.landing: A reader knows what an assembly hands over.

atoms.name: adapter-return-test-only
atoms.statement: An assembly that returns an adapter instance is imported only by test files.
atoms.why: Handing back an adapter exists for a spec to assert on what its fake recorded; any other caller would reach into the outside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: the returned instance's kind plus importer kinds of that assembly file.
atoms.landing: The test factory is recognisable by its callers, with no exception in the assembly rule.

atoms.name: defines-role-only
atoms.statement: A file defines at module level only what its kind's role names: an assembly its assembly functions, a driver its hooks and its wiring function, a boot nothing.
atoms.why: A definition is where logic hides in a file allowed to import anything.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root declarations of function, class and variable against the kind's list; whether a local binding inside a function counts as a definition is unstated (the CLI example needs them).
atoms.landing: Everything a reader finds in these files is the layer's one thing.

atoms.name: one-wiring-function
atoms.statement: A driver defines at most one wiring function.
atoms.why: A second one is a second entry into the driver's wiring that nobody calls by contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count of wiring functions (the one the boot or a parent driver calls).
atoms.landing: The entry of a driver is one name.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file has a reader bound to it by glob.
atoms.why: Which names are tech, how hooks are cut and which rules the tech exempts come only from the reading; no driver rule can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config coverage; unbound is red, the way out is binding a reader (one that counts the file as blob, on purpose, is a binding).
atoms.landing: A reader knows the tech of each driver is declared, not guessed.

atoms.name: binding-agrees-flavor
atoms.statement: A reader binding gives a kind only to a file the flavor leaves blob, or agrees with the flavor's kind; any other binding is a config error.
atoms.why: A file has one kind; two answers would make every rule judged on it ambiguous.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: config vs flavor, no code needed.
atoms.landing: The kind of a file has one source of truth.

atoms.name: tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every import or name a driver uses beyond assemblies and drivers is claimed by a reader bound to it; an unclaimed one, or a pure library (model), is red.
atoms.why: Tech is what a reading claims and nothing else; an unclaimed name cannot be told from logic.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: lookup of imports and free names in the reader's claim list.
atoms.landing: Every outside dependency of a driver is on the reader's list.

atoms.name: wiring-calls-only
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver calls only assembly factories, its claimed tech (parser, server, mount) and sub-driver wiring functions.
atoms.why: Wiring is the driver's way to put the hexagon in the tech's hands; any other call there is logic outside a hook.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee classification for calls outside hook bodies.
atoms.landing: A driver's top level reads as set-up of the tech.

atoms.name: hook-max-one-call
atoms.statement: A hook contains no call but its one use-case call.
atoms.why: Two calls mean the sequence between them is a use case nobody owns; it needs a facade service with a contract and a test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call count in the hook body (await is the call); hooks cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: A hook is one arrow on the map.

atoms.name: hook-min-one-call
atoms.statement: A hook contains at least one use-case call.
atoms.why: A hook with no use case is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call count of the hook body is not zero.
atoms.landing: Every event visibly ends in a service.

atoms.name: hook-call-is-use-case
atoms.statement: The call in a hook goes to a use case of a service, never to an adapter, a model or an unclaimed tech.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers, and a model call there is parsing or rendering that no service owns.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee file kind through the instance's type.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is all there is to know about it.

atoms.name: body-no-control-flow
atoms.statement: A body contains no branch and no loop; the call it makes is unconditional.
atoms.why: A body that branches or loops says several things at once, so it is neither one handed-on event nor one readable statement of behavior.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: if, ternary, switch, loops, logical and nullish operators in the body (a default is a branch, 606-607).
atoms.landing: A body reads straight down.

atoms.name: args-no-read
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, the host's values whole, instances and literals; nothing is read off them (opts, never opts.files).
atoms.why: Reading the event is translation, and translation belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: arguments are bare identifiers or literals.
atoms.landing: What the tech hands in is what the use case receives.

atoms.name: result-not-handed-on
atoms.statement: A hook's call value is returned or dropped, never written, passed on or logged.
atoms.why: Using the result (printing, exit codes, transforms) is translation, and the facade service owns it through its ports.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: uses of the call result in the hook; needs dataflow.
atoms.landing: A hook ends with the call; nothing follows it.

atoms.name: driver-no-model-import
atoms.statement: A driver imports no model at runtime (a pure library counts as model).
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service; a driver holding model code is a model without a test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime edge from a driver to a model file or a declared pure package; type edges are free (880-883).
atoms.landing: A driver contains no domain knowledge a reader would have to read.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A driver file exports its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: If a hook were exported another driver could chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of the driver file.
atoms.landing: The only thing a parent can do with the import is let it attach callbacks.

atoms.name: driver-import-call-only
atoms.statement: A driver uses an imported driver only to call its wiring function, from its own wiring, passing tech and instances, never from a hook nor with hexagon data.
atoms.why: Any other use lets one hook reach two calls through another file.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every reference to a binding imported from a driver is the callee of a call outside hooks.
atoms.landing: Sub-drivers are visibly just registration.

atoms.name: bare-boot-call
atoms.statement: The wiring function a boot calls takes no parameters, and the boot passes no argument.
atoms.why: A boot touches no tech, so the driver reads process, document or argv itself.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter list of the wiring function called from a boot and argument list of the call, which is one fact seen from two files.
atoms.landing: The start line has nothing in its parentheses.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one file, a driver.
atoms.why: The boot starts the program; everything else is the driver's.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list of a boot file.
atoms.landing: The entry of the program is one import.

atoms.name: boot-calls-wiring-once
atoms.statement: A boot makes exactly one call at module root, to that driver's wiring function, and holds nothing else.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and that call is the start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements of a boot file.
atoms.landing: The start is one line.

rules.remainder: Lateral is fine, so service and adapters edges pass here and are closed only by the composition gates; whether type-only edges count for the ranks is unstated for model and ports.
What counts as a barrel beyond a file named index is not written.

No atom of its own: it is the per-edge atoms (inward-imports, no-concrete-import, blob-import-gate) applied to every file, so a chain holds when each link is checked. Left over: purity through a third-party package's own imports, which is declared, not seen.
'Pure, deterministic third-party library' is a judgment turned into a declaration list; it is only as good as the list.
The set of ambient names is a list; 'adapters and drivers reach the environment' is a scope (kinds not carrying the atom), not a constraint.
Why assembly may take blob ('build it and inject it behind a port') and why a test may ('characterization tests') are wishes; nothing checks the blob is injected behind a port.
None; same atom as adapter-assembly-only, differing only in target kind.
None; the same atom as service-assembly-only.
A scope clause on the gate (runtime edges only), not a constraint; the SomeService["method"] shorthand is a type-only use that needs no constraint.
A scope clause: the gate looks at public targets, private/ targets are ruled by the seal; adds no constraint.
'Sign the adapter is not extracted yet' is a diagnosis, not structure.
'The service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no structural handle (an adapter's identity is not visible to a checker); 'same result shape' needs the TS engine.
None beyond service-boundary detection.
The direction law (817-826) says which way a pair should point by role, a judgment; the sharing progression (1263-1329) is judgment with a litmus ('delete one consumer').
None.

Atom applies to the test as importer by implication only (test is 'outside' yet 'imports anything', see sharedParts). 'Assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details', and the exceptions (a) closed input set / (b) absurd fixture / 'meaningfully better diagnostics' are judgments.

'Assembly and driver in one' is a claim about the kind, not a constraint: the kind's atoms are the selection in kinds.test. 'Imports anything' and 'defines anything' are absences of atoms. 'Same isolation rules' for fixtures is unspecified. 'Registered by calls the test tech owns' is reader data. End-to-end tests are said to be 'neither, outside the graph' (1022-1023) while .e2e is in the kind (265).

'Config is wired as a dependency by default' is a default, not a check; 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' has no mechanical 'sibling'; a blob callee is called a factory by construction with no guarantee; 'nothing at module root but imports' is worded stricter than the atoms (assembly functions sit at root) and cites stable-root as its why.
None.
'Web drivers are open, research in progress': the recognition rule for components is the assembly gate applied to bound components; the rest is unwritten.
'Tech setup' is whatever the reader claims; 'a hook does not wire' follows from hook-max-one-call and hook-call-is-use-case; 'a lazy feature is an assembly importing another' is narrative.

'A second call means a facade is missing, zero means logic with no home' are diagnoses; the cut of hooks belongs to the reader; 'ruled for the stock cut' admits a reader with another cut without saying which atoms move.
None; it is a union of the callee sets of the other two driver rules.
'Residue' is a label; 'main reads its tech itself' is the effect of bare-boot-call; the scope of 'definition' (root only, or local variables too) is unstated.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is reader-specific.
None.
'One boot per entry point' has no structural definition of entry point; 'touches no tech' follows from the atoms; the boot is also what stable-root's exemption is made for.

'The shapes below are the known ones, a shape nobody has written is judged by the rule' is open judgment that no checker can run; 'what decides it is judged where it sits' hands off to other atoms; the exemption by kind for boot and spec registration is, in atoms, selection (boot carries boot-calls-wiring-once instead of root-no-effect-call) and reader data.
Stated in prose (374-381) with no slug in the Summary: 'assembly is the only place where dependencies are resolved' is the general claim; 'dependency' versus plain option has no structural handle.

Judgment words with no atom: model 'abstract' and 'domain of ideas'; service 'orchestrates, does not compute', 'use cases nameable'; adapter 'holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' (277-278, which sits against 153 'potentially its own model functions'); ports 'shaped to the inside's needs', 'belong to the hexagon that defines them'; 'only a driver listens to the tech' (no handle for files no reader reads).

kinds.note: The global atoms. Blob carrying them is implied (stable-root's exemptions are a closed list of boot and spec registration, 1127-1129; cycles say 'any file').
+ every-file set. Canon restates root-immutable-bindings in its own bullet (295-299) and ambient-access in another (292-294): the same atoms, said in the kind.
+ every-file set. No ambient atom is needed: with no runtime code it is vacuous.
+ every-file set. 'Module-level code must be stateless' (341) is root-immutable-bindings again. Orchestrates-not-computes is a remainder.

+ every-file set. Not carried on purpose: no-concrete-import and no-ambient-access (the adapter is where the world is touched). Other adapters are closed by the composition gate, assembly and drivers by their own gates. Internally an adapter is a hexagon with its own kinds; 'external dependencies injected from outside' (166-167) sits against 'adapters may import concrete' (869): unresolved.

carries: no-concrete-import (a declared container library by declaration)
kinds.note: + every-file set; its 'nothing at root but imports' is defines-role-only + the root atoms. Read with no reader bound.
+ every-file set. Hook atoms apply to the hook bodies the reader cuts; wiring atoms to the rest. Reads tech: no-ambient-access and no-concrete-import are not carried; tech-claimed takes their place.
+ every-file set except root-no-effect-call, which its own one call replaces. Read with no reader bound.

carries: root-no-effect-call (the test reader declares runner registration effect-free)
factory-calls-only and branch-on-tech-only on setup functions (recommended)
kinds.note: Selection, not exemption: see testKind. As target the test kind is named as permitted importer by blob-import-gate, and counts as assembly and as driver for the other gates.
