Declares nothing, so carries no layer atom. It is a permitted target of assembly and test only. Two wrinkles: assembly's factory-calls-only treats a blob callee as a factory by construction (514), and a blob helper imported by a test is a venue the test atoms cannot see into.

inRules: assembly-builds-only (nothing at module root but imports)
sharedParts.problem: One atom stated in four places, each scoped to its own kind; editing one leaves the others behind, and assembly's last clause (481, 1036) cites stable-root as its why while being stricter than it (root constants forbidden, assembly functions still at root).

Same why (the file depends on the machine) judged twice for model and service, once anywhere (ambient-access) and once at root load time (root-no-machine-read); adapters and drivers carry only the root half, so the pair cannot be one rule; each blocks 'same fact, one verdict'.

One atom behind two slugs differing only by target kind, plus two scope clauses (type edges exempt, private/ targets exempt) that are not constraints; repeated in the matrix. Each kind needing 'adapter but not service' gets an exception instead of a selection.

The same edge (X may not import blob; blob may not import composition units; driver may not import blob) is stated from the importer side in the matrix and from the target side in three rules: double counting in the box.

The matrix's importer-side cells (assembly cannot import drivers; driver cannot import boot or composition units) repeat the target-side gates; only driver->model and unclaimed imports are new in the matrix.

'Nothing imports it' stated separately for boot (711-712, 1074) and test (265, 1017), and as 'only boot or driver' for driver; the matrix's test row ('Anything', '-') contradicts it for a boot: a test importing a boot is allowed by 873 and forbidden by 1074.

Whether a test is 'outside' the service it tests is unstated; test-through-contract needs the seal to bind it, test-is-outside says imports anything, and 1172-1175 allows internal unit tests in two judgment cases.

One argument shape (literals, tech values, instances) stated in three rules; assembly and wiring may read a tech value (441-443), a hook reads nothing; the narrower hook scope is a second atom (args-no-read) that the rule words as an alternative to the first.

'The result is never branched on or computed with' is said for assembly (511-520) and for a hook (603-607) in different words; hook adds 'not handed on', assembly requires handing on: a loose and a strict version bundled under one wording.

What a driver may call is one fact at two scopes (in hooks: a use case; outside: assembly, tech setup, sub-driver wiring) stated three times, with the union in driver-calls-services; a rule that needs only one scope (the test tech, 'services-only does not apply') must exempt the union.
'Exactly one' bundles two atoms with two whys (two calls: an unowned sequence; zero calls: logic with no home) and the test kind exempts both under the word 'count'.

Five restatements of 'only the role's definitions' with five lists (assembly functions; hooks + one wiring function; nothing; anything), a definition of 'definition' that excludes the things it names (443-446) and an unstated depth (module root vs any local variable).
One fact seen from two files: the boot passes no arguments (711) and the root driver's main takes nothing (625); whoever edits one has to remember the other.

The spec registration is exempted twice by two mechanisms: 'the reading declares that call effect-free' (1115-1117) and 'exempt by kind, a closed list' (1127-1128); the boot is exempted by kind and also described as its own rule.

Forbidden for production factories (374-381) and 'right' in tests (1221-1223), stated as an exception; the structural resolution (the atom binds composition units, a test factory is an assembly function) appears nowhere. Also this rule has no slug.
'One port, one interface' is said as a constraint on adapters (131) and as a symptom in services (988), the second not checkable.

'Tech' and 'tech value' are defined three times with different content (80-88 terminology, 438-446 rules, 1096-1098 stable-root) and 'call' with await restated for assembly, driver and stable-root: a vocabulary shared across the atoms, defined per rule.
Whether a type-only import counts is restated per rule (exempt in one, included in six) instead of being an attribute of each atom; inward-imports and no-concrete-import do not say.

The test kind is 'assembly and driver in one' in the kind list and rule, 'imports anything' in the matrix, named explicitly in blob-quarantine and absent from the other gates; .e2e is in the kind list but 'neither, outside the graph' in the rule.

testKind: A test builds units, calls them, asserts, and is imported by nothing. Carry (selection from the atoms): reader-bound and binding-agrees-flavor (its hooks and tech come only from the test reader); entry-not-imported (this one atom is what keeps shared test code from living in a file with a test name: it must become adapter, assembly, model or driver); private-seal (test-through-contract, by implication); the three root atoms root-immutable-bindings, root-no-machine-read, root-no-effect-statement and root-no-effect-call, with runner registration (describe, it) declared effect-free by the test reader, so no per-kind exemption is needed (isolation: no shared mutable state between tests, no clock read at load); the two acyclic atoms and no-barrel-file; body-no-control-flow on every hook body, because a test that branches or loops says several things at once and can pass without asserting (this is my recommendation; canon only exempts hook count and services-only, and 'data-driven indirection' is judged defeating the review at 1155-1157); driver-import-call-only for shared registrations (registerMatchers). Setup functions in the file, if the spec defines test factories, should carry factory-calls-only and branch-on-tech-only (they are assembly functions); canon's 'defaults are right in tests' then needs no exception: no-default-dependency binds service and adapter factories, not assembly functions. Do not carry: inward-imports and no-concrete-import (the test is the sink of the graph and builds fixtures that touch the world; a ceiling on imports is incompatible with its role), no-ambient-access (what is tech is what the test reader claims), hook-max-one-call, hook-min-one-call and hook-call-is-use-case (a body builds, calls several units and asserts: canon exempts these as 'count' and 'services-only'), args-no-read, result-not-read and result-not-handed-on (an assertion reads the result), defines-role-only (it defines scenarios and fixtures), driver-exports-wiring-only (nothing imports it). It appears as permitted importer in blob-import-gate and counts as assembly and driver in the other gates. Open for the authors: .e2e is both in the kind and 'neither' (1022-1023); whether a spec may import a boot (matrix yes, 1074 no); 'same isolation rules' for local fakes; production config 'has no place' (1200) against production adapters 'fair game' (1193) is a judgment.
helpers: Yes, the constraint must reach local helpers; the 'no' opens a laundering venue, as the authors say. The fix is structural, not a rule about 'inside a helper': define a body as a hook plus the transitive closure of the local functions it calls in the file, and give every local function in a test file exactly one of two roles by how it is reached. (1) Reached from a hook: it is part of the body, carries body-no-control-flow (no branch, no loop) and nothing else is allowed in it that a body may not do. (2) Reached only from the setup (the file's root, or another setup function): it is a test factory, an assembly function in kind, carries factory-calls-only and branch-on-tech-only (a branch only on a parameter, arms that are factory calls), so a loop over data or a condition on an instance is refused there too. A local function with no role (unreachable, or reached from both without fitting either) is not allowed to exist: 'defines anything' shrinks to 'defines functions of these two roles'. What needs a loop (a data builder, a spawn-and-collect run() that waits for output) must leave the file and become what it is: a model builder (loops and computation are model's right, and visible as such), an adapter or driver fixture, with its own atoms and tests; so a helper's loop is never invisible, only moved to a file kind that rules it. Two honest limits remain, both holes not atoms: an imported helper is not under body-no-control-flow (the test may import blob, debt owned and quarantined to assembly and test, so a loop can sit in a blob helper until extraction); and a model data builder with loops is lawful yet can hide the scenario from the reviewer, which is the 'legible to the reviewer' judgment (1150-1161) no check holds. For an e2e run() that starts the CLI: the spawn is tech use, so it belongs in a driver or adapter-like fixture file, not in the test body's closure.

atoms.name: inward-only
atoms.statement: An import (runtime or type) goes only from a file to a file of an equal or inner layer: model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: Dependencies point toward the more stable knowledge, so the inside never depends on the outside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import edge, rank(kind(from)) >= rank(kind(to)); kind from the flavor's suffix. Lateral edges are further narrowed by unit-assembly-only.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a reader sees from an import path that nothing inner reaches outward; model's import list is only model.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A model, service or assembly file imports no concrete (platform/IO) package; what the machine provides arrives as an injected value.
atoms.why: Reaching IO directly bypasses the ports, so the unit cannot be exercised without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package class of each runtime import (default concrete unless declared pure, claimed as tech by a bound reader, or a declared container library); flag concrete for these kinds.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the import list of an inside file shows no node:/http/db names; every IO touch is behind a port.

atoms.name: declared-pure-lib
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as model only if the project declares it pure.
atoms.why: Purity of code outside the repo cannot be inferred, so it is declared, not presumed.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package name against the config's pure list; anything not listed is concrete or unclaimed.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the pure/concrete border is a visible list, so trusting a model import is a reading of config, not of node_modules.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A runtime import of a public .service.ts or .adapter.ts file comes only from an assembly (a test acts as one).
atoms.why: Only assembly knows the concrete graph, so units stay instantiable and swappable.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import edge whose target is a unit file not under private/ and whose importer kind is not assembly or test; type-only edges not judged here.
atoms.landing: LANDING: seeing `from '../icons/service'` anywhere but assembly is a red flag with no file to open.

atoms.name: blob-importers
atoms.statement: A file imports blob (type imports included) only if it is an assembly, a test or blob itself.
atoms.why: Blob carries no guarantee, so any layered file importing it contaminates a layer that had guarantees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge to a suffixless file, importer kind not in {assembly, test, blob}.
atoms.landing: LANDING: blob debt is quarantined and countable: the only places that touch it are the graph builder and characterization tests.

atoms.name: outside-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly is imported only by drivers and assemblies, a driver only by boots and drivers, nothing imports a boot or a test, type imports included (a test is the extra importer of an assembly or driver it calls).
atoms.why: The outside runs one way, boot to driver to assembly, so each outside layer stays known to nothing but its caller and stays boring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind per target kind in {assembly, driver, boot, test}; non-.ts components get their kind from a bound reader (the web recognition rule).
atoms.landing: LANDING: the call chain boot -> driver -> assembly is the only chain, one arrow on the map.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: No file outside a service imports a file under that service's private/ directory, type imports included; a nested service has no access to its parent's private/.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is hidden stays free to change.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge target path contains private/, importer outside the owning service directory; layer directories are not services (path-pattern helper).
atoms.landing: LANDING: `/private/` in an import path outside its service is an instant violation.

atoms.name: service-acyclic
atoms.statement: Imports between service packages, every kind included, form a DAG.
atoms.why: A service in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files to service directory, detect cycle over all edges (type-only and test edges included).
atoms.landing: LANDING: the service map is a DAG a human can read bottom-up; extraction order is visible.

atoms.name: module-acyclic
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules form no cycle, within one service too.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: cycle detection over runtime edges only.
atoms.landing: LANDING: module load order is unambiguous, so an undefined at runtime is never an import-order accident.

atoms.name: port-type-edge
atoms.statement: Every import edge to or from a .port.ts file is type-only.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; a runtime edge means an implementation is hiding in it or being loaded around it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import without the type modifier whose target or importer is a port file (runtime re-export, side-effect import, missing `type`).
atoms.landing: LANDING: a port never appears in a runtime import list.

atoms.name: layer-visible-path
atoms.statement: Every import path resolves to a file whose own name declares its layer (or is blob); no index barrel re-exports mixed layers.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site, or the edge rules cannot be enforced by shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolved target basename/suffix is a layer or suffixless blob; flag index.* barrels and re-exports crossing layers.
atoms.landing: LANDING: reading an import line tells the layer of what is imported without opening a file.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports no model file and no pure library.
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service; model logic in a driver has no contract and no test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime edge from a driver to a model-kind file or a declared-pure package.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a driver's import list is assembly, drivers and tech only; no domain vocabulary.

atoms.name: tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every package or global name a driver treats as tech is claimed by a reader bound to that driver; an unclaimed one is red.
atoms.why: Without a claim the checker cannot tell tech from logic, so no driver rule can be judged on it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a reader: imports and global names used in the driver against the bound readers' claims.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the tech a driver touches is an enumerated list in the reader, not an inference.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one
atoms.statement: A boot has exactly one import, and it is a driver.
atoms.why: Starting the program is one call to one driver, with nothing else for the boot to know.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import count and target kind in a .boot file.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the entry file is readable in one glance: one import, one call.

atoms.name: types-only-file
atoms.statement: A port file declares only types and interfaces; it holds no runtime statement.
atoms.why: Runtime code in a contract means an adapter has not been extracted yet.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any non-type declaration or statement in a .port file.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a port reads as a pure contract, never as code to run.

atoms.name: no-ambient-reach
atoms.statement: A model, service, assembly or boot file reads or calls no host global (time, randomness, console, timers, process, document, globalThis), at module root or in a function, in a condition, a value or a call.
atoms.why: What the machine provides must arrive as an argument, so the file's behavior is a function of its inputs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: name resolves to a global in a host list; the list is open-ended ('shapes nobody has written down'), so the checker holds a list plus reader claims.
atoms.landing: LANDING: every environment dependency of these files is a parameter you can see in the signature.

atoms.name: root-binding-immutable
atoms.statement: A module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly array/record/map/set, Object.freeze over a literal, each to its depth); no top-level let, no unfrozen collection.
atoms.why: A module that holds mutable state at load is not the same module for every test that imports it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: type/syntax proof per root binding; unresolvable named types prove nothing; mutableModuleState config lifts exactly this atom.
atoms.landing: LANDING: state lives only in factory closures, so an instance exists only where it was called and is reached by argument.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-capture
atoms.statement: A module-root binding's value is read from nothing the machine decides at load: no tech, clock, randomness, import.meta.env, even under a primitive type; import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed identity.
atoms.why: A value captured from the machine at load cannot be varied by a test without reloading the file.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: initializer flow to a root binding from a host/tech name or declared-effectful call; what counts as machine is the open list again.
atoms.landing: LANDING: constants at the top of a file are constants on every run.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-call
atoms.statement: No call at module root reaches tech or an unclaimed name, runs a use case, or enters a local function of a file whose layer allows side effects (adapter, blob); a property read is free.
atoms.why: Module root runs on import, so a call there acts at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee classification at root; effect-free declarations by a reader are the escape; mutableModuleState does not lift it.
atoms.landing: LANDING: importing a file never does anything.

atoms.name: root-no-effect-statement
atoms.statement: No module-root statement other than declarations and imports acts at load: assignment, delete and their like are red; throw is not.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a statement that only makes sense at run time is a load-time side effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statement kinds (ExpressionStatement with assignment/delete/update).
atoms.landing: LANDING: root reads as declarations only.

atoms.name: root-one-wiring-call
atoms.statement: The root of a boot holds exactly one call: the wiring function of its one driver.
atoms.why: Something has to execute when the runtime loads the program, and exactly one thing may.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: boot root has one ExpressionStatement, a call of the imported driver's function; replaces root-no-effect-call for the boot kind.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the single place where the program starts is the only root call in the tree.

atoms.name: root-registration-calls
atoms.statement: The only calls at a test file's root are registrations with the test tech (describe, test, hooks) whose callbacks are the test bodies.
atoms.why: The test tech owns loading and running; registering a body is how a test is made, and nothing else may run at load.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a test reader: root calls whose callee is a claimed registration; replaces root-no-effect-call for the test kind.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a spec's root is a list of registrations; nothing executes outside a test body.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: The definitions in a file (function, class, variable) are within the kind's list: assembly, only assembly functions; driver, only hooks and at most one wiring function; boot, none.
atoms.why: A definition is where logic hides, and residue in an outside layer is a model without a test or a service without a contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: enumerate declarations per file, compare to the kind's allowed list (the wording 'variable' needs a ruling for a local binding of a built instance).
atoms.landing: LANDING: an outside file defines nothing a reader must understand; its function names are the whole inventory.

atoms.name: wiring-no-params
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes no parameters, and the boot calls it with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot hands nothing over, so the driver reads its own tech and the boot stays free of tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: arity of the wiring function and of the boot's call; root vs sub-driver is told by a boot importing it.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the contract between boot and driver is the empty one: call main().

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory of a service, adapter, assembly or blob file, a model factory (flavor name, stock `create*`), or a declared load; nothing else is called.
atoms.why: An assembly decides nothing but which factory to call; any other call is a decision hidden in the wiring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus flavor name for model callees, plus the config's declared loads (a declared load's result counts as tech value from then on).
atoms.landing: LANDING: reading an assembly is reading the graph, one factory call per node.

atoms.name: args-as-given
atoms.statement: An argument of a build or wiring call is a literal, a tech value (a field or destructured part may be read in assembly and wiring), or an instance built or received; never a derived value.
atoms.why: A derived argument is a decision made in the outside, invisible on the map.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression shape (call, operator, template are derived); parameters of the wiring function are the tech values.
atoms.landing: LANDING: every argument is something you can point to: a constant, a parameter or a node of the graph.

atoms.name: result-pass-through
atoms.statement: What a call in an assembly or a hook returns is only returned or passed on to a build call (a hook: only returned or dropped), never branched on, computed with, member-accessed, written, handed on or logged; a declared load's result is the exception, read as a tech value.
atoms.why: The outside never looks into or touches what flows through it, so the map's arrow is the whole story.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow of a call's result binding to its uses; in a hook one-call already forecloses handing on.
atoms.landing: LANDING: an outside layer's values are opaque tokens, so you reason about the outside without opening its code.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A branch on graph shape is wiring; a condition on an instance's output is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operands traced to parameters or declared-load results, arms checked as build calls.
atoms.landing: LANDING: the variations of the graph are explicit and driven by input, visible on the map.

atoms.name: adapter-return-test-only
atoms.statement: An assembly function returns no adapter instance unless every importer of its file is a test.
atoms.why: Only a test needs its fakes back to assert on; production consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: return expression origin kind plus importer kinds of the file.
atoms.landing: LANDING: an assembly returning adapters is visibly a test factory; adapters never leak to a driver.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and every test file is read by a reader bound to its tech by glob.
atoms.why: Every driver rule is judged through a reading (hook cut, tech claims), so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file kind driver/test with no matching reader binding is red; a reader that counts the file as blob is the declared way out.
atoms.landing: LANDING: how each driver's hooks are cut is a named reader, not a guess; unread drivers cannot hide as green.

atoms.name: outside-calls-wiring
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks a driver calls only assembly factories, tech setup and sub-driver wiring functions; a hook never wires.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place only, so hooks stay the pure link from event to use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee classification via the reader's claims (what is tech setup); hook regions cut by the reader.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a driver reads as setup followed by hooks, the wiring never mixed with the firing.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call; zero and two or more are both red.
atoms.why: A sequence between two calls is a use case nobody owns; zero is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given the reader's cut: count of service calls in a hook body; test tech exempts the count by reader, not by rule.
atoms.landing: LANDING: each event is one arrow to one use case; the driver's link to a service is the whole of what there is to know.

atoms.name: hook-unconditional
atoms.statement: A hook's one call is not guarded by a branch, loop or try and no other statement sits in the hook.
atoms.why: Anything around the call is a decision or error mapping with no contract; it belongs to the facade service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: hook body is `[return] call`, no control flow.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a hook fits on one line and reads the same in every driver.

atoms.name: event-handed-whole
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, host values handed whole (`process`, never `process.cwd()`), instances and literals, nothing read off them.
atoms.why: Reading or defaulting an argument translates the event, and translation is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument is a hook parameter, a whole host name, an instance or a literal; no member access on the event (stricter than args-as-given, which lets assembly read fields).
atoms.landing: LANDING: the contract between event and use case is `opts` in, unchanged.

atoms.name: hook-calls-service
atoms.statement: The call in a hook is a use case of a service instance, never an adapter and never a model function.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers; parsing and rendering are use cases of a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee resolves to a service-typed instance's method; an adapter instance is unobtainable anyway under adapter-return-test-only.
atoms.landing: LANDING: every hook is traceable to one service API method on the map.

atoms.name: sub-driver-call-only
atoms.statement: An import of a driver is used only to call its wiring function, in the importer's own wiring (never in a hook), passing tech and instances, never a use-case result.
atoms.why: Otherwise a hook could chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: binding use sites of an imported driver are all call expressions of its wiring export outside hook regions.
atoms.landing: LANDING: splitting a driver across files is visibly just registration.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A sub-driver exports exactly its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: Then the only thing a parent can do with the import is let it attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver imported by another driver.
atoms.landing: LANDING: a driver file's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: only-driver-listens
atoms.statement: Only a driver (or test) hands callbacks to a claimed tech; other kinds may call into the same tech outbound without registering hooks.
atoms.why: The driving side must be one place, or events reach use cases by routes the map does not draw.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callback passed to a claimed-tech call outside driver/test; the border between outbound call-with-callback and listening is the reader's cut, and canon never draws it.
atoms.landing: LANDING: to find what fires the program you open drivers only.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file references the port it implements by type import.
atoms.why: A suffix is a declaration; an adapter that implements no visible port is an unplaced implementation.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: type import of a .port file present (structural assignability would need the tsc engine); canon states this as declaration, never as a rule.
atoms.landing: LANDING: an adapter's port is one import line away.

atoms.name: no-branch-loop
atoms.statement: No function body, closure or root statement in a test file contains a branch or a loop.
atoms.why: The suite is read as the behavioral spec, so each scenario (given X, when Y, expect A) must be visible in the test, not reconstructed from helpers or data-driven indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for syntax (if, switch, ternary, for, while, do); partial for iteration by callback (forEach, map, each) unless declared as loops; file-wide scope, so no reader or hook cut is needed.
atoms.landing: LANDING: every test reads straight down as one scenario.

rules.remainder: None of its own: 'lateral (same layer) OK' is narrowed to nothing-lateral-for-units by unit-assembly-only; the sentence reads as permission while other atoms forbid.
'Layer visible in the import path' for layer directories (icons/model/) vs suffixes needs the flavor to say which names count.

No atom of its own: 'a file is only as pure as its least-pure import' is the induction of the import atoms over every file; the transitive claim through third-party code rests on declared-pure-lib being believed. 'Partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a consequence, not a constraint.
'Becomes untestable' is the why. 'Concrete' is classified by package, so the classification table is hidden machinery (see helpers).

The host-name list is open-ended; canon says adapters and drivers reach the environment but is silent on assembly, which no-ambient-reach is extended to via 'holds no tech' (inferred, not a stated scope).
'Assembly may take it because its rule bounds what it can do' and 'a test may take it for characterization' are justifications, not constraints.

Its 'not by model, ports, adapters, drivers, or blob' list restates edges already forbidden by inward-only, blob-importers and the matrix; only 'not by other .service.ts' is its own. Omits test as an importer.
Same as service-assembly-only; 'not other adapters' is the lateral ban.

Not an atom: the scope clause of unit-assembly-only (runtime edges only). Its job is as much to say what the exemption does NOT reach: private-sealed, blob-importers, outside-importers, service-acyclic all count type imports.
Scope clause of unit-assembly-only (private/ files exempt); no atom.

'A sign the adapter hasn't been extracted yet' is a why. Parenthetical claims the edge atom follows from the file atom; the check differs (importer's modifier vs file's content) so it is kept separate.

Whole rule is a hole: 'service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no structural shape (the service cannot name an adapter, a discriminant field is judgment); 'produce the same result shape' is a wish.
Which directories are services (layer directories are not) needs a path convention.

The direction law (817-826) and 'wiring that would close a cycle is misplaced' are consequences of this atom plus unit-assembly-only; the 'component with no upward edges may be imported freely' is a judgment of role.
None.

Entirely judgment: 'documented behavior', 'no implementation details'. Only a fragment is structural (a test imports a unit's public layer file rather than private/), and canon allows internal unit tests as an exception (1170-1175), so even that is not a rule. A hole.

'Assembly and driver in one' is the bundle under suspicion, not a constraint. 'Imports anything' is overstated (private-sealed, service-acyclic still apply). 'Defines anything', 'hook count does not apply' are exemptions that disappear once atoms are assigned by kind. 'Same isolation rules' for fixtures, 'a fake is an adapter, a data builder is model' are placement judgments, not checkable from a test file. 'End-to-end tests are neither' leaves .e2e in the list while excluding it from the graph: unresolved. no-branch-loop is implied, not stated.

'It returns services (one or a record) and shared model instances' (return shape) has no atom beyond adapter-return-test-only. 'A pipeline hiding in the wiring' is the why. 'Shared instances flow down, never sideways' is not mechanical as stated. 'Nothing sits at module root but imports' collides with 'assembly functions are defined' and is read as closed-definitions plus the stable-root atoms. A model function vs factory is told by the flavor's `create*` name.
Says 'only drivers and other assemblies' while tests import assemblies (test factories, 505-508, 1214): test must be added (or the test counts as a driver); canon is inconsistent.
The reader binding vs flavor kind agreement ('binding that names a file differently from the flavor is a config error') is a config check, not code structure.
'Tech setup' is only classifiable through the reader. Branches or loops in a driver's wiring are neither allowed nor forbidden by the text (assembly allows wiring-branch-only); a hole.

What is a 'use-case call' (vs tech call) needs the reader. 'Wiring is the wiring function's; a second call means a facade is missing' are whys. 'Ruled for the stock cut; a reader with a cut of its own says where the line sits' hands a free parameter to readers. The test exemption of the count lives in a reader, not here.

No atom of its own: it re-says hook-one-call, wiring-outside-hooks and driver-no-model as one callee list. 'Never an adapter' is already unobtainable through the imports and assembly returns. A duplicate rule.
'Anything else is residue' is the why. A sub-driver's wiring `registerX(cli, services)` taking tech and instances has no parameter-shape atom (only counted and typed by the reader).
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a reader scope note.
None.
'Holds nothing' and 'touches no tech' reduce to closed-definitions and no-ambient-reach; one-per-entry-point ('a program has one per entry point') is a count over the tree, not a file property.

A molecule of at least four atoms plus two kind-swaps: the rule closes its own exemption list (boot, test) to two kinds, which the atoms replace by giving boot and test their own root atom. 'A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' is an open clause, judgment. mutableModuleState lifts only root-binding-immutable. 'The reading that claims it declares that call effect-free' hands a parameter to readers.

kinds.note: Edge atoms are properties of the graph, carried by every kind as importer or target; root atoms are carried by every kind except that boot swaps root-no-effect-call for root-one-wiring-call and test swaps it for root-registration-calls.
inward-only makes model import only model; the three content atoms are all that is left. Factory-takes-a-port is a classification by imports, no atom.
Imports model and ports only via inward-only, type-only via port-type-edge; port ownership by the defining hexagon is not mechanical.

Gets the same two atoms as model; difference is only the edges it may import (ports) and being a unit (unit-assembly-only as target). Use-case naming, 'orchestrates not computes', export of a factory: remainder.

Carries almost nothing of its own: it may reach concrete and the environment; edges carry everything else (unit-assembly-only as target, no lateral adapter import). 'Holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' is judgment; the direction law reduces to service-acyclic.
Widest import right with the narrowest call list; declared load, declared container library and declared blob use are config declarations, not atoms.
Hook atoms need the reader's cut; every driver atom except edges is judged through the reader. Reads the environment freely (so no-ambient-reach is not carried).
Read by flavor kind with no reader; swaps root-no-effect-call for root-one-wiring-call.
Plus the all-kind edge and root atoms (outside-importers makes nothing import a test); see testKind.

No content atom (no declaration, no guarantee). Constrained only by edges: cannot import units (unit-assembly-only), assembly, driver, boot (outside-importers), is importable only by assembly/test/blob (blob-importers), private-sealed, cycles. Hole: canon says stable-root holds everywhere (a local function of a blob counts as effectful), yet a legacy blob entry calling main() at root is called 'green' (654-658): contradiction; a root-no-effect-call for blob needs a ruling.

sharedParts.problem: One fact stated as two rules scoped to two kinds, plus two scope clauses; each rule's 'not by ...' list restates other edges.

inRules: assembly-builds-only (blob, the only layer that may)
hook text 'blob call there is already a violation'
sharedParts.problem: The same edge ban is restated in at least five rules from the target side and the source side, with different type-import exemptions in prose.

Four importer-set rules for four outside kinds are one atom; assembly-driver-only omits tests although tests import test factories, and the canon's own 'test = driver in one' implies a silent amendment.

inRules: model bullet 'depends on nothing outside model'
hexagon prose 'inside doesn't know the outside'
sharedParts.problem: The matrix is a derived view (importer side of every edge atom), yet it is presented as a rule table beside the atoms it is computed from; 'combined result of every rule' is consistent only if each cell has one owner atom.

inRules: assembly-builds-only ('holds no tech', tech values as parameters)
sharedParts.problem: One check (host global referenced) with two whys in prose (testability inside, one-thing outside); canon names the scope only for model and service, silent on assembly and boot except through other wording. May need splitting into inside/outside whys.
`const T = Date.now()` in a model is red twice; stable-root defers 'what decides it' to the layer yet also judges storage, so the same line has two owners.

inRules: service bullet ('module-level code must be stateless', 341)
assembly-builds-only ('nothing at module root but imports')
test-is-outside ('exempts the registration, not mutable state')
sharedParts.problem: Restated as model rule, service rule, assembly rule and test caveat; stable-root itself is a molecule (4 atoms) with a closed exemption list (boot, test) that is an 'except' in the rule.
The same triple (tech values, instances, literals) is stated three times, differing silently on whether a tech value may be read (assembly and wiring: yes; hook: no, hence event-handed-whole).
Same constraint ('never computed with, read, written, logged') worded twice with different allowed sinks (assembly: pass on to a factory; hook: return or drop).

inRules: 'Assembly and driver are not blob' paragraph 643-652
sharedParts.problem: One atom with a per-kind allowed list, written as three separate rules plus an exemption for test; the word 'variable' in the definition term contradicts binding a built instance.
Both sides of the same call; one fact in two rules.
The callee set is stated in three rules plus the matrix; driver-calls-services has no content of its own.
Return-side and caller-side halves of one constraint live in different sections; the 'assembly may do X when a test is the caller' is an exception written into the rule.
Test exemptions are carried by the reader, so the rules still say 'exempt'; moves the except sideways instead of removing it.
One package classification (pure, concrete, claimed tech, container) governs four rules; the classification table has no home in canon and exceptions (container library, declared pure) hang off it.

inRules: 'Wiring that would close a service cycle is misplaced' (909-912)
sharedParts.problem: Direction law and wiring advice are consequences of the same atom, stated as guidance that looks like rules.
Branch/loop is allowed in assembly wiring, forbidden in a hook, and for a test only implied by a why paragraph; same syntax judged per role with no stated rule for tests.

testKind: Carry: reader-bound (a spec no reader reads is red); outside-importers (nothing imports a test, so importer-side atoms cannot contaminate anyone); root-registration-calls in place of root-no-effect-call; root-binding-immutable, root-no-machine-capture and root-no-effect-statement (so a root `const svc = createX()` is red, which structurally forces 'each test assembles its own instance' and no shared mutable state); sub-driver-call-only (a spec calls a shared driver such as registerMatchers only to wire it); no-branch-loop (implied by 1150-1161, file-wide); the universal edge atoms layer-visible-path, private-sealed, service-acyclic (canon 909-912 counts test edges), module-acyclic. Do not carry: inward-only, no-concrete-import, unit-assembly-only, blob-importers (a test is an allowed importer of everything: builds units, drives adapters and the host, characterizes blob; 'imports anything' is slightly overstated since private-sealed and service-acyclic still bind); no-ambient-reach (tests fake time and drive the host; determinism is a judgment, canon 1194); driver-no-model, tech-claimed, hook-calls-service (a test calls models and adapters directly); assembly-calls-build, args-as-given, wiring-branch-only, closed-definitions, outside-calls-wiring, wiring-no-params; hook-single-call, hook-unconditional, event-handed-whole, result-pass-through (a test must read results to assert, which is the opposite of an outside hook). Why: the 'assembly and driver in one' bundle is the union of two atom sets that contradict each other inside one file: the assembly set forbids calling use cases and reading results, the driver set forbids assembly calls inside hooks and demands exactly one call; the union cannot hold, so canon exempts about ten rules. A test builds (so no build-only), calls (so no one-call), asserts (so reads results), and is imported by nothing (so importer-side atoms are moot). What survives is atoms about what the test is: its tech reading, its stable load, its isolation (no shared mutable root) and its legibility (straight-line). Judgment remainder, not atoms: test-through-contract, determinism of fixtures, 'production config has no place in tests', placement of shared test code. Also: .e2e files sit in the kind list yet canon calls them 'outside the graph' (1022): unresolved.
helpers: Open question (local helpers such as run() that starts the CLI). Answer: the constraint must reach inside, and the way to avoid the laundering venue is to scope no-branch-loop by FILE, not by ROLE. Applied to every function body, closure and root statement of a test file (hooks, local helpers, nested callbacks alike), the checker needs no reader to find 'the hooks', and there is no place left inside the file to hide a loop. A 'no' (hook bodies only) leaves the helper definition as the venue, because test files 'define anything'; a role-scoped rule always leaves the unscoped role as a window. Cost of 'yes': a local helper that needs a branch or a loop cannot stay in the spec file. It goes where its kind says (canon 1217-1219 already says shared test code is placed by what it is): pure data or logic to a model file (ruled by model atoms, with its own tests), a fake or a process-spawning runner with logic to an adapter, a build with variations to an assembly (wiring-branch-only bounds it to branching on parameters), a matcher or shared hook to a driver. A straight-line helper (`const run = (args) => spawnCli(args)`) stays local. So the atom's scope is the kind 'test', the same way every other atom's is. Residual holes to confess: (1) iteration without syntax (forEach, map, runner .each, recursion): declare iteration-by-callback calls as loops in the atom or accept it as a known limit; (2) a suffixless shared helper imported by tests is blob, and blob is an allowed import of tests, so blob is itself a laundering venue for test helpers (canon says 'no shared test code is blob' but nothing mechanical separates it from legitimate characterization blob); (3) a helper moved into a model file may still be data-driven indirection, which is judgment (test-through-contract). Shared machinery the atoms depend on (not atoms, but each hides decisions): package classes (pure, concrete, claimed tech, container), the flavor (suffix to kind, `create*` factory names), the reader (hook cut, tech claims, effect-free declarations, kind binding), and config declarations (pure libs, loads, container library, mutableModuleState). Every canon 'except' maps to one of these four parameter sources, which is where an exception can still leak back.

atoms.name: imports-inward
atoms.statement: A file's runtime imports reach only kinds at or below its own layer in model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot.
atoms.why: Dependencies point inward so each inside can be understood and tested without knowing the outside.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import graph resolved to kinds by flavor, compared to the layer order; type imports free except where another atom counts them (see helpers).
atoms.landing: The import path alone tells the layer relation; every map arrow runs one way.

atoms.name: composition-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is imported at runtime only by assembly (so never by service, adapter, model, port, driver or blob).
atoms.why: The graph is built in exactly one place, so services never know where their instances come from and chunking follows assembly.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every runtime import of a non-private service/adapter file; type-only imports and private/ files exempt.
atoms.landing: One glance at an importer list shows who builds what; no service reaches for another service.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private can move without notice.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path match private/ against importer's service root.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import path is an instant red flag in review.

atoms.name: blob-quarantine
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files (and blob) import blob, type imports included.
atoms.why: Code with no layer declaration carries no guarantee, so letting a layered file import it contaminates the layer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every import of a suffixless file.
atoms.landing: Blob is visible as debt and enters the graph at one known place.

atoms.name: concrete-adapters-only
atoms.statement: A package that is concrete (platform, I/O, state) or not declared pure is imported only by adapters, drivers (as claimed tech) and tests, never by model, service, assembly or boot.
atoms.why: A file that depends on concrete code bypasses its ports and cannot be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: yes against a declared pure/concrete package list; the purity of a package is a declaration the checker cannot infer.
atoms.landing: Reading a model or service import list tells that it touches no machine.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A port file contains no runtime statement, only types.
atoms.why: A contract carries shape and no behavior; behavior lives in adapters.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any non-type statement in a .port file.
atoms.landing: A port file reads as pure contract; the boundary is legible without code.

atoms.name: port-edges-typed
atoms.statement: Every import from or of a port file is a type-only import.
atoms.why: A runtime edge to a type-only file is always a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword, so it is a mistake.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import edges touching .port files without the type keyword.
atoms.landing: Ports show on the import graph as type edges only.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Dependencies between service packages, every import kind counted, form no cycle.
atoms.why: A cycle makes neither service extractable, movable or reasonable alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package-level graph with service boundaries, cycle detection.
atoms.landing: The service DAG on the map; extraction order is readable.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules form no cycle, even within a service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in production bundles.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: module graph of runtime imports, cycle detection.
atoms.landing: Import order is a plain tree; no hidden load-order dependency.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: A consumer imports from the layer file itself, never through an index re-export.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the other import atoms cannot be enforced by shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: no barrel/index module re-exporting layers; import specifiers resolve to a layer file.
atoms.landing: The kind of what is imported is read off the path.

atoms.name: assembly-by-drivers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so nothing may type against it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every import of an .assembly file.
atoms.landing: Assembly appears on the map only below drivers and assemblies.

atoms.name: driver-by-boot
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: Drivers are entered by the runtime or by their parent driver, never used as a library.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every import of a driver-kind file.
atoms.landing: The driver tree under one boot per entry point.

atoms.name: boot-unimported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file.
atoms.why: The boot is what the runtime starts; an importer would make it a module with consumers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero importers of boot-kind files.
atoms.landing: Boots are the graph's roots.

atoms.name: test-unimported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a test file.
atoms.why: A test file is run by the test runner, so any file others import is by definition not test kind.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero importers of .spec/.test/.e2e files.
atoms.landing: Shared test code visibly sits in other kinds.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver does not import model at runtime (types free).
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service; model in a driver is logic with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime import of a model-kind file from a driver.
atoms.landing: A driver's import list is assemblies, drivers and its tech only.

atoms.name: boot-imports-driver
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: The start is one arrow to one driver.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import set of a boot file equals one driver.
atoms.landing: Entry point to its driver is the whole boot.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: Model and service code read no environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis, at module root or in a function; they receive them.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine from a global depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: yes against a declared list of ambient globals/members; the list overlaps the reader's tech names (see helpers).
atoms.landing: No hidden input in model or service: everything the code depends on is in its arguments.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable from syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly shapes, frozen literal), to its depth.
atoms.why: A test that imports the module must get the module every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: syntactic proof table; a type the reader cannot resolve proves nothing; config opt-out mutableModuleState lifts only this atom.
atoms.landing: Module state is visibly nowhere; an instance exists only where a factory was called.

atoms.name: root-reads-nothing
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness).
atoms.why: The file could not be tested under another environment or at another moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: ambient/tech names in a root initializer; import.meta.url and __dirname exempt.
atoms.landing: Root constants are the same on every load.

atoms.name: root-calls-inert
atoms.statement: A call at module root does not reach the tech, an unclaimed name, a use case, or a local function of a file whose layer allows side effects.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee classification at root; property reads presumed free, calls judged until a reading declares them effect-free.
atoms.landing: Importing a file is safe; nothing happens on import.

atoms.name: root-statements-inert
atoms.statement: No module-root statement performs an assignment, delete or the like.
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a statement that only makes sense at run time is a side effect at load time.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds at root (a throw is exempt).
atoms.landing: Root holds declarations, never actions.

atoms.name: no-dependency-defaults
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives no default value to a dependency parameter.
atoms.why: A default resolves a dependency inside the service, scattering assembly logic and defeating code splitting.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers on factory parameters in .service/.adapter files; which parameters are dependencies needs the flavor.
atoms.landing: Every dependency of a unit is visibly handed by assembly.

atoms.name: unit-exports-factory
atoms.statement: A .service or .adapter file exports a factory that returns the unit's API.
atoms.why: Assembly treats a callee from such a file as a factory by construction, so the file must be one.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: exported function shape per file; canon never states it as a rule.
atoms.landing: The unit's contract is its factory's return.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter holds what its port needs and implements a port.
atoms.why: An adapter exists to translate between a port's shape and an external tech's shape.
atoms.check: LAUNCH weak: a type-import of a port is checkable; that the factory conforms needs the type checker; 'nothing of the hexagon's' is judgment.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the contract it fulfils.

atoms.name: calls-build-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory call (a composition unit's, another assembly's, a blob's, a model factory's) or a declared load, awaited or not.
atoms.why: Assembly decides only which factory to call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, plus the flavor's create* word to tell a model factory from a model function (never called).
atoms.landing: The assembly reads as a list of builds, drawn as the graph.

atoms.name: args-given-values
atoms.statement: Arguments to a build or wiring call are literals, tech values, or instances built or received, never a value derived by computation.
atoms.why: A derived argument is logic in a place with no contract; the unit that needs the value derives it under its own rules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression forms; scope differs on whether a tech value may be read (assembly) or only passed whole (hook).
atoms.landing: What flows into a factory is nameable at a glance.

atoms.name: result-opaque
atoms.statement: The result of a call is passed on or returned, never read, computed with, branched on or member-accessed, except a declared load's.
atoms.why: Touching what was built or returned is a decision the map cannot show and no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: uses of a call's bound result; scope: assembly may hand it to another factory, a hook may only return or drop it.
atoms.landing: Instances move through the outside as sealed values.

atoms.name: loads-declared
atoms.statement: The only use-case calls an assembly makes are the ones the project declares by name as loads, and a load's result counts as tech values.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for its effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declared list in config; undeclared use-case call in an assembly is a violation.
atoms.landing: The graph's data dependencies are an explicit short list.

atoms.name: flow-wiring-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value, against a literal or truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show; it belongs to the service or adapter that owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand origins and arm call kinds.
atoms.landing: Conditional wiring is visible on the map as variants of the graph.

atoms.name: returns-hexagon-only
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and returns an adapter only when every caller is a test.
atoms.why: The driver receives the hexagon; adapters are outside it and a spec asserts on what its fakes recorded.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: return value kinds plus caller kinds across files.
atoms.landing: What a driver can reach from an assembly is only use cases.

atoms.name: tech-only-in-driver
atoms.statement: Assembly and boot hold or touch no tech: tech values arrive as parameters, and no concrete or tech import or name appears there.
atoms.why: Only a driver listens to the tech; the other outside files stay boring.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reader-claimed names and concrete imports in these kinds; a declared container library is a configured exemption.
atoms.landing: Tech appears on the map only at driver and adapter.

atoms.name: defines-only-allowed
atoms.statement: A file defines nothing (function, class, variable) except what its kind names: assembly functions, or hooks plus at most one wiring function, or nothing for boot.
atoms.why: A definition is where logic hides, and interesting code outside has no contract, port or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations at root and nested, against a kind's allow-list; hooks from the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: The outside is the most boring part; a definition there is a signal.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: A driver or test file is read by a reader bound to its tech.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading that says what is a hook, a call and tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding lookup per driver/test file; red when none.
atoms.landing: Each driver names the tech it speaks to.

atoms.name: outside-hooks-wiring
atoms.statement: Outside its hooks, a driver only wires: assembly calls, tech setup and sub-driver registration.
atoms.why: Everything the driver does that is not a hook is the one-time build of the connection, nothing else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call classification outside hooks; what is tech setup comes from the reader.
atoms.landing: The driver's body reads as setup, then hooks.

atoms.name: one-call-per-hook
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call and no other call, awaited or not.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence nobody owns, zero hides logic with no home, so the link from event to service is one arrow.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: hook bodies from the reader's cut, call count and class; the test tech exempts the count.
atoms.landing: A driver's link to a service is one arrow, so the outside is reasoned about without opening it.

atoms.name: hook-call-unconditional
atoms.statement: A hook's use-case call sits under no branch or loop.
atoms.why: A condition around the call is a decision with no home; the facade service owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow ancestors of the call node.
atoms.landing: The one arrow is always drawn, never sometimes.

atoms.name: hook-args-whole
atoms.statement: A hook passes the event as received, host values whole, instances and literals, nothing read off them and no default on the way in.
atoms.why: Translating the event is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument forms (no member access, no call, no ??).
atoms.landing: What the tech hands in is what the service gets.

atoms.name: tech-is-claimed
atoms.statement: What a driver imports or names as tech is what a bound reader claims; an import or name no reader claims is unclaimed and red, and a pure library is model and red.
atoms.why: The tech is only what a reading claims, so anything else has no ruled meaning.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reader claims table against driver imports and global names.
atoms.landing: A driver's tech vocabulary is a stated list.

atoms.name: main-takes-nothing
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes no parameters and reads its tech itself, and a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: The boot calls with no arguments and touches no tech, so the driver reads its own tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: parameter list of the wiring function against its role.
atoms.landing: The boot-driver call is argument-free.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports exactly one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: The only thing another driver can do with it is let it attach its callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export surface of driver-kind files.
atoms.landing: A driver's whole public face is one function.

atoms.name: driver-imports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, during its own wiring (outside hooks), with tech and instances as arguments.
atoms.why: A sub-driver called from a hook, or fed a use-case result, lets one hook chain two calls through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import usage sites of driver imports.
atoms.landing: Split drivers still read as one wiring tree.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot's only statement is one call, at module root, to the driver's wiring function with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and it only starts.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statements of a boot file; checked with no reader bound.
atoms.landing: Start is one visible call.

atoms.name: scenario-straight-line
atoms.statement: A test body contains no branch or loop, and its given, when and then are visible in the body rather than rebuilt in helpers.
atoms.why: The reviewer reads the suite as behavior statements and a scenario with control flow cannot be read as one.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: branch/loop syntax in test bodies is mechanical; 'visible, not reconstructed' is judgment; canon states the intent only as prose.
atoms.landing: Each test reads as given X, when Y, expect A.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is false for service/service and adapter/adapter, contradicted by composition-assembly-only; the matrix omits services from the adapter row's forbidden list.
Corollary: enforcing every import atom on every file already makes purity transitive. Only residue: purity of third-party package internals, which is a declaration.
'Pure, deterministic' and 'purity should be declared, not presumed' are a declaration list, not structure; where an undeclared package sits (concrete or unclaimed) is not said.
'Environment' and 'machine' lack a closed name list.
Why assembly and tests may import blob (build and inject; characterization tests) is rationale, not a second constraint.
Scope clause, not a constraint: types exempt from composition-assembly-only; it must not reach assembly/driver/boot rules or private-sealed or blob-quarantine.
Scope clause: composition-assembly-only applies to public units only; private/ is exempt.
Hole: 'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no mechanical form once services cannot import adapters; it is a design wish.
Holes: 'assertions on documented behavior', 'no implementation details' and 'documented' are judgment; the only structural piece is not importing what is private.

Mostly a kind declaration and a list of exemptions (imports anything, defines anything, count and services-only, registration at root). 'Shared test code is placed by what it is' is a corollary of test-unimported. 'Fixtures are test-purpose adapters, same isolation rules' is a wish for inline fakes.
'Nothing at module root but imports' is defines-only-allowed plus the root atoms, restated; the container-library clause is a configured exemption of tech-only-in-driver.
Config consistency (a binding may not rename a flavor's kind) is a config check; 'a reader that counts the file as blob on purpose' leaves a driver treated as blob that only a driver may import.
'Tech setup' is defined per reader; 'a hook does not wire' is carried by one-call-per-hook's 'nothing else'; whether a branch outside hooks is wiring is unsaid.
'A second call means a facade is missing' is advice; 'ruled for the stock cut' defers the line to the reader.
No atom of its own: the allowed call set is the union of the two call atoms above, and 'never an adapter, never a model' is their complement plus the import atoms.
'Residue' is a name for the failure, not a check.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a reader exemption.
'One per entry point' needs the entry list; 'holds nothing' is not defined beyond defines-only-allowed.

Closed exemption list of two (boot's call, spec registration calls) is the canon's explicit except; 'a shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule' is a judgment clause; the reader declares which calls are effect-free.
Holes: 'orchestrates, does not compute', 'use cases nameable', 'a utility bag' are judgment words.
Hole: 'holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's', 'absorbs specificity'.
Hole: 'shaped to the inside's needs', 'port interfaces belong to the hexagon that defines them'.
'Each test assembles its own instance' follows from root-bindings-immutable; 'no production config in tests' and 'production adapters fair game when controlled' are judgment.
Hole: 'clever helpers', 'DRY-ed setup that hides the scenario', 'legible as a behavior statement'.
Corollary: a nested adapter's upward-only edges follow from these three; no atom of its own.

kinds.note: Inside kind: ruled by what it may depend on, no verb atoms; may define anything. A model factory that takes a port or service is reclassified as service, which needs model to type-import ports: an open type-import question.
Types only, so root atoms and verb atoms are vacuous; the unified-port wish has no atom.
Inside kind; may define anything including model code. Facade services get full service rights, no rule looks at size.
Does not carry no-ambient-access or concrete-adapters-only: reaching the machine is its business. root-calls-inert names adapters as a layer allowed side effects.

carries: concrete-adapters-only (importer side, container library by config)
kinds.note: Widest import right, narrowest verb list. A test factory is an assembly function in an assembly file and may return adapters because a test is its caller.
Needs no stable-root exemption: it builds inside its function. Reaches the machine through its claimed tech; that is permission, so no-ambient-access is not carried.
No reader bound. Holds the stable-root exemption (one call at root). One boot per entry point needs the entry list.

Canon reads it as assembly and driver in one but exempts only the hook count and services-only; the rest of the driver and assembly verb atoms cannot hold for a body that asserts on results. Detail in testKind.

carries: composition-assembly-only (importer ban: cannot import service or adapter)
kinds.note: Outside the matrix, no guarantees, owned as debt. Whether stable-root applies is unsaid: canon calls a blob entry green with root calls and says stable-root holds everywhere but the boot.

inRules: Dependency matrix service and adapter rows
sharedParts.problem: One atom stated as two slugs and prose, plus the matrix rows, while inward-deps says lateral is OK; runtime-import and public-unit are its scope clauses spread over two more slugs.

The literal/tech value/instance vocabulary is restated in four rules with different permission on reading a tech value (assembly may read a field, a hook may not), so any kind needing only the vocabulary gets all four.

A call's result is only passed or returned: stated once for assembly, once for hooks (stricter on handing on), once as 'never hexagon data'. A test body must read results, so it cannot take the hook rule's copy whole and gets an exemption instead.
Same atom with three different allow-lists, stated in prose per kind; the test's 'defines anything' is the same atom with an open allow-list, which is the venue for local helpers.

Branch/loop scoping is written three ways (assembly: on params with factory arms; hook: none, call unconditional; test: none, implied), with three different whys, bundled with unrelated clauses in each.

One list of host names (process, document, Date, console, timers) is judged forbidden in model/service, forbidden in assembly/boot, claimed in drivers, and checked at module root, from four rules, with the reader's claims as a fifth copy.
Packages are classified pure/concrete (service-purity) and claimed/unclaimed tech (reader) by two vocabularies for overlapping sets; where an undeclared package sits is unsaid.
driver-calls-services duplicates the call classes of the other two plus the import atoms; it adds no check, only a second place to edit.
The boot's 'no arguments' and the driver's 'main() takes nothing' are one constraint seen from caller and callee, ruled in two places.

stable-root is four atoms plus a closed exemption list naming two kinds; assembly restates it as 'nothing at root but imports', boot and test are exempted by name. Each kind that needs only some of the four gets an exception.

One pattern, importer-restricted(kind, allowed importers, types counted), appears eight times with no stated principle for when types count: they are exempt only for kinds that have a contract (service, adapter), counted otherwise (inferred, not stated).
'Each test assembles its own instance', 'module-level code must be stateless' and 'state lives in the closure' restate the same root atom in prose.

The reader both gates the driver rules and carries exemptions (test count, registration, markup children); an exemption stated with a reason is the canon's except, and the escape 'reader that counts it as blob' lets a driver be blob.
Test 'imports anything' contradicts private-sealed and no-service-cycle, which count every import kind unconditionally; canon does not say which wins.

testKind: TEST CARRIES (a test builds units, calls them, asserts; nothing imports it): reader-bound and test-unimported (stated); root-bindings-immutable, root-reads-nothing, root-statements-inert (stable-root exempts only registration calls, so a module-level instance or mutable binding is exactly the shared-state-between-tests failure; stated 1017-1018); scenario-straight-line (implied by 1150-1161); no-runtime-cycle (nothing can import it so it cannot be in a cycle, vacuous); calls-build-only, args-given-values only on the setup statements where fakes are built, which canon cannot cut mechanically (the setup half has no boundary, since describe callbacks are themselves hooks under the stock cut). TEST DOES NOT CARRY: imports-inward, composition-assembly-only, blob-quarantine (it imports anything, blob included, which is the whole point of characterization tests), concrete-adapters-only and no-ambient-access (it reaches the machine for fixtures), driver-no-model and tech-is-claimed (it exercises model, services and adapters directly), defines-only-allowed (it defines anything), one-call-per-hook (count exempted), hook-args-whole and result-opaque (it must read results to assert and build arguments to call), flow-wiring-only, tech-only-in-driver. WHY: a test is not a driver plus an assembly; it is a third kind with a different one thing (build a scenario, call, assert) whose verbs overlap those two kinds only partially. Canon exempts exactly two clauses (count, services-only) and leaves hook-one-call's other clauses and assembly-builds-only unreconciled with a body that asserts; that is the molecule problem, since result-opaque, args-given-values and defines-only-allowed live inside bundles the test can only take whole or by exception. Also unsaid: private-sealed and no-service-cycle against 'imports anything'. OPEN QUESTION (helpers): yes, the straight-line atom must reach the local helpers, and it can without a 'no'. Structure (my proposal, not tested against rixo's unfinished statement of the problem): (1) scope the atom to the body plus every function defined in the same file and reachable from a body, transitively, including callbacks passed to iteration builtins (.map/.forEach/it.each are loops in disguise) and recursion; (2) a helper that cannot satisfy it does not stay local: it moves to a file whose kind says what it is (a process starter with a polling loop is an adapter under a port, a data builder with a loop is model, a factory is an assembly function), which is canon's own rule that sharing a folder or file grants nothing and 'it splits into units instead' (232-234, 1217-1219); (3) at the file boundary the test calls an imported function and that function is judged under its own kind's atoms, so a loop lives only where loops are legal and labelled with a contract. So no helper can launder a loop, and the venue where a loop is allowed is a ruled kind, not an unruled definition inside a spec. Residual holes: what counts as a loop in disguise, and whether 'visible in the body, not reconstructed from helpers' can be mechanical at all.
helpers: CLASSIFIERS shared by many atoms (these are machinery, not constraints): (a) kind of a file from flavor and reader binding, with a bound reader giving a kind only to flavor-blob or flavor-agreeing files; (b) callee class: use-case call (method on a returned service API), factory (service/adapter/assembly/blob file, or model create*), model function, adapter call, tech call (reader-claimed), wiring call (sub-driver), load (declared), judged by assembly, driver, hook and root-call atoms with different verdict tables; await is the call; (c) package class: pure-declared, concrete, claimed tech, unclaimed; (d) hook cut: every callback handed to claimed tech under the stock cut, reader-overridable; (e) type-import table: counted by private-sealed, blob-quarantine, no-service-cycle, assembly-by-drivers, driver-by-boot, boot-unimported; exempt for composition-assembly-only, imports-inward, driver-no-model. ATOM FAMILIES: EDGE (import graph: imports-inward, composition-assembly-only, private-sealed, blob-quarantine, concrete-adapters-only, port-edges-typed, the importer-restricted five, cycles, layer-in-path, driver-no-model, boot-imports-driver), ROOT (four stable-root atoms), DEFINE (defines-only-allowed, port-no-runtime, driver-exports-wiring, main-takes-nothing, no-dependency-defaults), VERB (calls-build-only, args-given-values, result-opaque, loads-declared, flow-wiring-only, one-call-per-hook, hook-call-unconditional, hook-args-whole, outside-hooks-wiring, driver-imports-wiring, boot-calls-once, tech-only-in-driver, no-ambient-access, returns-hexagon-only). Canon's own axis: inside kinds are ruled by EDGE and ROOT, outside kinds by VERB and DEFINE (225-236). CONFIG DECLARATIONS as exception surfaces to review: declared loads, container library, mutableModuleState, pure-package list, reader exemptions with reasons, reader-as-blob escape; each is a project-level declaration, not a rule exception, but the reader exemptions and the registration/boot exemptions in stable-root are canon-level excepts. OPEN POINTS found: inward-deps 'lateral OK' vs composition-assembly-only; model-factory-takes-a-port reclassification needs model to type-import ports; whether a branch outside hooks is wiring; whether stable-root reaches blob; test versus private-sealed and no-service-cycle; chain-purity adds no check. UNSTATED atoms listed as implied: unit-exports-factory, adapter-implements-port, scenario-straight-line. Purely judgment, not atomized: orchestrate-not-compute, nameable use cases, unified-port, port shaped to inside, documented behavior, implementation details, no production config in tests, taste after extraction.

atoms.name: inward-only-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only kinds at its own layer rank or inward (model < ports < service,adapters < assembly < drivers < boot), lateral allowed.
atoms.why: The inside must not know the outside, so it can be developed and tested without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind vs target kind rank over runtime and type edges. Blob is unranked.
atoms.landing: Reader sees at the import line that the dependency points inward.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file whose job is not world contact imports no platform/IO package (node:fs, HTTP client, DB driver) unless the project declares the package.
atoms.why: World contact bypasses ports, so the file cannot be tested without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes, given a declared pure/concrete/container package list: classify each package import. Transitive mode gives chain-purity.
atoms.landing: Reader knows without opening the file that it touches no outside system.

atoms.name: package-classified
atoms.statement: Every package or global name a file reaches is classified: pure (model), concrete, or tech claimed by a bound reader; unclassified is red.
atoms.why: A rule cannot be judged on an import the checker cannot classify, and presuming purity gives false guarantees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: lookup in declared lists and reader claims; miss = red.
atoms.landing: Reader knows every external name was ruled once, by declaration.

atoms.name: no-ambient-reads
atoms.statement: A file reads or calls no ambient environment global (env, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis), at root or in a function, in a value or a call.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: identifier lookup against the global list, wherever it sits; imports are not involved. Names a bound reader claims (process) are tech, not ambient, for drivers.
atoms.landing: Reader knows time, env, randomness arrive as arguments.

atoms.name: unit-built-by-assembly
atoms.statement: A public .service/.adapter file is runtime-imported only by assembly (and test); private/ and type-only imports are out of scope.
atoms.why: Only assembly may know the concrete graph; everyone else sees contracts.
