atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge into a public composition unit, importer kind, edge kind, private/ path.
atoms.landing: Reader knows a service import in a non-assembly file is always a type.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: Blob is imported (type edges included) only by assembly, test and other blob.
atoms.why: A layer that imports unplaced code loses the guarantees its suffix declared.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target has no layer suffix and no reader gives it a kind; importer kind.
atoms.landing: Reader sees where the debt enters the graph: assembly or test only.

atoms.name: assembly-import-gate
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported (type edges included) only by drivers and assemblies (canon wording), and by test and bound components (see helpers).
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract; consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reverse edges into assembly files by importer kind.
atoms.landing: Reader knows an assembly's only callers are the outside.

atoms.name: driver-import-gate
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported (type edges included) only by a boot or another driver, and by a test calling its wiring function.
atoms.why: Only the starter reaches a driver; any other importer could chain hooks through indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reverse edges into driver files by importer kind.
atoms.landing: Reader knows a driver is reached from the start, never from the program's logic.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: Nothing imports a boot file or a test file.
atoms.why: The runtime (node, the test runner) is their only caller.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero in-edges to files of kind boot or test.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the entry is a root of the graph.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type edges included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, not implementation coupling.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path of target vs importer's service.
atoms.landing: Reader sees a private/ path in a foreign import as an instant violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: The service-package graph is acyclic, every import kind counting, type-only included.
atoms.why: A service in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: service-level edge graph with service boundaries known.
atoms.landing: Reader knows services form a DAG.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Module-level runtime imports are acyclic; type-only cycles are ignored.
atoms.why: Circular ESM works in dev and fails silently in minified production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: file-level runtime edge graph.
atoms.landing: Reader knows load order cannot hide an undefined.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: The layer is visible in the import path: no index file re-exports across layers.
atoms.why: A rule keyed on layers is only enforceable if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: index/barrel re-export detection; layer from suffix.
atoms.landing: Reader reads the layer off the import line.

atoms.name: ports-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file contains no runtime code.
atoms.why: A port is a contract; runtime code means an adapter was not extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any value-level statement in a .port file.
atoms.landing: Reader knows a port is shape only.

atoms.name: port-edges-type-only
atoms.statement: Every import edge into or out of a port file is a type-only import.
atoms.why: A runtime edge on a type-only file is a re-export, a side-effect import, or a forgotten type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edge kind on edges touching a .port file.
atoms.landing: Reader knows a port import is erased.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file declares the port it implements and conforms to that port's interface and result shape.
atoms.why: Replaceability: the inside never learns which adapter it got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: adapter references a port type, tsc checks conformance; 'which adapter it got' is not structural.
atoms.landing: Reader knows what contract an adapter serves.

atoms.name: no-default-dependency
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory has no default value for a dependency parameter.
atoms.why: A default scatters assembly decisions into service modules and creates hidden static edges.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializer on a parameter typed by a port/service; 'dependency' needs a type test.
atoms.landing: Reader knows assembly is the only resolver.

atoms.name: no-mutable-root
atoms.statement: No module-root binding whose immutability the syntax does not prove (primitive, as const, readonly types, Object.freeze), exported or not.
atoms.why: A test importing the module must get the module every other test got.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root bindings vs immutability proof; config mutableModuleState lifts exactly this atom.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the root holds only constants; state lives in factories.

atoms.name: no-root-capture
atoms.statement: No root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness); import.meta.url and __dirname are exempt.
atoms.why: The file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: provenance of root initializers vs ambient/tech names.
atoms.landing: Reader knows no constant is a snapshot of the machine.

atoms.name: no-root-call
atoms.statement: Module root performs no call that reaches tech or unclaimed names, runs a use case, or enters a local function of a side-effect layer.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee classification at root; property reads presumed free; throw allowed.
atoms.landing: Reader knows importing a file does nothing.

atoms.name: no-root-statement
atoms.statement: Module root holds no statement that does something on evaluation (assignment, delete and the like).
atoms.why: Whatever sits at root runs on import, so a run-time-only statement is a load-time side effect.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement kinds at root.
atoms.landing: Reader knows root is declarations only.

atoms.name: no-stray-definition
atoms.statement: In assembly, driver and boot, every definition (function, class, variable) is one of the kind's named role functions; types are not definitions.
atoms.why: A file allowed to import anything or hold tech must hold no logic, or logic hides there with no contract or test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: declarations vs the kind's allowance (assembly functions / hooks plus at most one wiring function / none).
atoms.landing: Reader knows the outside has nothing to read but wiring.

atoms.name: build-calls-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a factory call (composition unit, assembly, blob, model factory) or a use case the project declares as a load.
atoms.why: Assembly decides nothing but which factory to call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee classified by file kind and flavor (create*); declared-load list in config.
atoms.landing: Reader knows an assembly only builds; the map shows it as one arrow.

atoms.name: args-underived
atoms.statement: A call's arguments are literals, tech values received, or instances; never a call, operator, condition or default computed there.
atoms.why: A derived argument is logic done in a file that must hold none.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression shapes. Assembly may read fields of tech values, a hook may not (hook-passes-whole).
atoms.landing: Reader sees arguments as plain handed-over things.

atoms.name: result-opaque
atoms.statement: A call's result is never read: no member access, branch, computation, write or log; it is passed on or returned (a declared load's result, a tech value, excepted).
atoms.why: The outside never looks into what it built or fired.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: flow of the call's value; loads from declared list.
atoms.landing: Reader knows results are handed along, not interpreted.

atoms.name: wiring-conditions-plain
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value, against a literal or for truthiness.
atoms.why: A condition on anything else is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: provenance and shape of condition operands.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the graph varies only by config or parameter.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances; it returns adapters only to a test caller.
atoms.why: Consumers hold contracts; only a test asserts on its fakes.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: returned types by kind plus the importer kinds of that assembly.
atoms.landing: Reader knows what an assembly hands out.

atoms.name: driver-has-reader
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file is read by a reader bound to its tech; unread is red.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding lookup; a reader counting the file as blob is a declared way out.
atoms.landing: Reader knows which tech reading governs this file.

atoms.name: tech-claimed-only
atoms.statement: A driver reaches only tech its bound readers claim, plus services and assembly; an unclaimed import or name is red.
atoms.why: Tech is what a reading claims and nothing else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: reader claim lists vs names and imports in the driver.
atoms.landing: Reader knows exactly which tech the driver listens to.

atoms.name: driver-no-model
atoms.statement: A driver imports and calls no model function; a pure library is model and red there.
atoms.why: Parsing and rendering are use cases of a service, not driver work.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import and callee kind.
atoms.landing: Reader knows no computation hides in the driver.

atoms.name: driver-wiring-closed
atoms.statement: Outside hooks a driver calls only assembly functions, tech setup and sub-driver wiring; a hook wires nothing.
atoms.why: Wiring is done in one place per layer, so the hook stays the link.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee class by position (in or out of a hook, per the reader's cut).
atoms.landing: Reader knows where the graph is wired and that hooks do not.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes at most one call.
atoms.why: A sequence of two calls is a use case nobody owns; it needs a facade service with contract and test.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call count in the hook body, per the reader's cut.
atoms.landing: Reader knows one hook is one arrow on the map.

atoms.name: hook-has-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes at least one call, and it is a use-case call.
atoms.why: A hook with no use case is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: one use-case call (instance from assembly) in the body.
atoms.landing: Reader knows every hook reaches a service.

atoms.name: hook-body-bare
atoms.statement: A hook body is the call and its return: no branch, loop, declaration, assignment or default around it.
atoms.why: Translation around the call is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement shapes in the hook body.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the hook translates nothing.

atoms.name: hook-passes-whole
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event and host values on as received; nothing is read off them (process, never process.cwd(); opts, never opts.files).
atoms.why: Reading the event is translation, and translation belongs to the facade.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: member access or destructuring on hook parameters and host names in arguments.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the use case gets the tech's value untouched.

atoms.name: sub-driver-call-only
atoms.statement: A driver import of another driver is used only as a call to its wiring function, during the importer's own wiring.
atoms.why: The sub-driver may only attach its callbacks; a hook-level call would chain two calls.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: usage of the imported binding.
atoms.landing: Reader knows how one entry point splits its hooks.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports its wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: The only thing an importer can do with it is let it attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list vs the wiring function.
atoms.landing: Reader knows a driver's surface is one function.

atoms.name: root-wiring-no-args
atoms.statement: The root driver's wiring function takes no parameter and the boot calls it with no argument.
atoms.why: The boot touches no tech, so the driver reads its tech itself.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: arity of the function and of the boot call.
atoms.landing: Reader knows tech enters at the driver, not the boot.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one-driver
atoms.statement: A boot's only import is a single driver.
atoms.why: The boot starts one thing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import list size and kind.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the entry names its one driver.

atoms.name: boot-calls-once
atoms.statement: A boot's root holds exactly one call, to its driver's wiring function.
atoms.why: The boot is the one module whose evaluation performs a call, and only to start.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root statements = imports + one call to the imported binding.
atoms.landing: Reader knows the program starts in one visible call.

atoms.name: root-registration-only
atoms.statement: Root calls in a test file are registrations into the test tech, with no condition or loop around them.
atoms.why: A spec's root only declares which hooks the runner owns.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: root callee claimed by the test reader as registration; control flow at root.
atoms.landing: Reader sees the list of scenarios as written, not generated.

atoms.name: test-body-straight
atoms.statement: A test body has no branch or loop, counting iteration callbacks and the file-local helpers it calls.
atoms.why: The reviewer reads the scenario as given, when, expect, not reconstructed.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow nodes in the body plus the file-local call closure; a table or test.each is a loop at root.
atoms.landing: Reader reads a test top to bottom as one scenario.

atoms.name: no-prod-config
atoms.statement: A test file imports no production config source.
atoms.why: Production config couples the test to an environment.
atoms.check: LAUNCH weak: needs a declared set of production config files; conflicts with 'production adapters are fair game' (1192-1194).
atoms.landing: Reader knows a test runs on test config.

rules.remainder: None. Lateral OK is an absence.

'Pure, deterministic' is judgment, mechanical only via declaration; 'becomes untestable' is a wish.
None. 'The same at module root' repeats stable-root (see sharedParts).
'Assembly takes it because its rule bounds what it can do' is rationale, carried by the assembly atoms; 'characterization tests' is a wish.

None. Same atom as service-assembly-only.
Scope clause (type edges exempt) of unit-built-by-assembly; no constraint of its own.
Scope clause (private/ exempt) of unit-built-by-assembly; no constraint of its own.
'Sign the adapter is not extracted yet' is a diagnostic hint.
'The service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no structural check; same result shape only via the type system. HOLE.

None.
None.
'Assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details' is judgment. HOLE; only the private/ reach is mechanical.

'Defines anything', 'imports anything', hook-count and services-only do not apply are absences, not atoms; 'setup builds units with fixtures' and 'placed by what it is' are placement, not structure; 'e2e tests are neither, outside the graph' is a boundary note; test-body-straight and root-registration-only are not stated here, only implied.

'Pipeline hiding in the wiring' and 'decision the map cannot show' are judgment words; 'a model function that computes a value is not a build' needs the flavor's create* naming; 'behind the port that awaits it' is typed, not structural.
None. 'No contract to depend on' is the why.
'Bound to a reader that counts it as blob on purpose' is a declared exemption mechanism.
'Tech setup' depends on what the reader claims.

'Hooks are cut by the tech's reading' and 'ruled for the stock cut' are reader-side; 'a second call means a facade is missing' is a diagnostic; the test tech's count exemption is an exemption, not an atom.
None: a pure bundle of atoms owned by other rules. 'Never an adapter' is already forced by unit-built-by-assembly plus assembly-returns-services.
'At most one wiring function' and a sub-driver's `(cli, services)` signature are counts the atom does not yet express; 'a model without a test' is a why.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' needs a reader to tell mounting from importing.
None.
'A program has one per entry point' is project-level and needs declared entries. HOLE.

'The shapes below are the known ones, not a closed list; a new shape is judged by the rule' is open judgment. HOLE. Exemptions (boot call, spec registration) are other atoms (boot-calls-once, root-registration-only), not exceptions.
'No exceptions' contradicts the test-factory defaults at 1221-1224, which fit only if test factories are not production factories.

kinds.note: GLOBAL = inward-only-imports, layer-in-path, private-sealed, no-service-cycle, no-runtime-cycle (blob drops inward-only-imports). Model imports model and declared-pure libs only; a model factory taking a port is red through inward-only-imports, not a separate rule.
Root atoms are vacuous on a type-only file.
Orchestrates-not-computes and 'name your use cases' are judgment, no atom.

Does NOT carry no-concrete-import, no-ambient-reads, package-classified: it is where world contact lives. Fractal assembly inside an adapter factory is unruled by any assembly atom (canon 159-167): a hole.

no-ambient-reads is stated for model/service only; for assembly it follows from 'holds no tech' (implied extension). A declared container library is an entry in the declared package list, not an exception.
Does NOT carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-reads: tech-claimed-only takes their place. blob-import-gate bars blob imports.
Carries boot-calls-once instead of no-root-call: that is how the stable-root exemption stops being an exception.

Allowed importer in unit-built-by-assembly, blob-import-gate, assembly-import-gate, driver-import-gate (canon omits test from the last two wordings). Carries no inward-only-imports (imports anything), no-concrete-import, no-ambient-reads, no-stray-definition, hook-single-call, hook-has-call, hook-body-bare, hook-passes-whole, result-opaque, args-underived, build-calls-only, assembly-returns-services, driver-no-model, driver-wiring-closed. Cycle atoms are vacuous because nothing imports it.
Unranked: carries no inward-only-imports. Canon says blob 'claims none' (953-961) but stable-root names blob's local functions (1109-1113). I assume it carries the root atoms; this is unruled.

sharedParts.problem: One atom stated as two rules with parallel wording, with its type-only and private/ scopes as two more slugs, and again inside driver-calls-services ('never an adapter') and the matrix rows. Two bundles hold the same part.

Root-call ban lives in stable-root; assembly restates 'nothing at root but imports'; boot and spec need an exemption. Resolved only if boot and test carry boot-calls-once and root-registration-only instead of no-root-call; today that is an exception list.

The same atom is named by its slug in assembly ('stable-root') and in test ('not mutable state'). Test's 'each test assembles its own instance' (1196-1198) is the same check: a root-bound instance is not provably immutable.
ambient-access says 'the same at module root'; stable-root forbids the same stored read. One fact in model or service is reported by both.
Stated by slug for model/service only; assembly says 'holds no tech' and boot 'touches no tech' for the same check. Scope is worded differently per kind.

Stated as service-purity, 'never concrete tech' in assembly, 'imports nothing else, tech included' in boot, 'a pure library is model and red' in driver, and in the matrix; the driver version is really tech-claimed-only plus driver-no-model.
Three wordings of 'arguments are literals, tech values, instances'. Assembly may read a tech value's field; hook may not. Without a strict hook-only atom the two scopes conflict.
Assembly says 'passed on or returned'; hook says 'returned or dropped'; sub-driver says 'never hexagon data'. One check on the result's flow, worded three ways.
Three closed definition lists plus the glossary 'definition' (443-447) and 'define nothing at all' (278-279). Test says 'defines anything', which is the laundering venue.
Boot calls with no arguments; the root driver's main takes nothing. Same arity fact checked at both ends.
'A hook does not wire' (wiring-outside-hooks) and 'wiring is the wiring function's' (hook-one-call) and 'calling a sub-driver inside a hook' (sub-driver-wiring) are the same fact.
Importer set stated twice in the Driver section (542, 640) and omits test, yet a spec calls a driver's registerMatchers (634-635, 1217). Canon contradicts itself on who imports a driver.
assembly-driver-only says drivers and assemblies only; a shared test factory is 'an assembly function in an assembly file' called by specs (505-508, 1214-1217). The importer set omits test.
Importer set (assembly, test) restated in the matrix, assembly imports, driver-reader's 'a driver with unplaced code stays suffixless', and service/adapter rules naming blob as a banned importer.
Boot and test each say 'nothing imports it'; one atom, two wordings.
test-is-outside says 'imports anything'; test-through-contract says no implementation details. Whether a spec may reach another service's private/ is unruled.
'Tech is what a reading claims' appears in terminology, driver-reader, driver-calls-services and stable-root's call clause; the red for unclaimed names lives in two rules.

The IoC prose says defaults 'create static imports from the service to its adapters', already forbidden by unit-built-by-assembly; test-factory prose then allows defaults. The residue (defaults that import nothing illegal) is an atom only if test factories are exempt by kind.
Whether type imports count is restated per rule: exempt in one, included in six. It is a parameter of each import atom, not a rule.

testKind:
CARRY: driver-has-reader, entry-not-imported, private-sealed, no-mutable-root, no-root-capture, no-root-statement, plus two implied atoms that canon never states: root-registration-only (replaces no-root-call, the way boot-calls-once does for boot) and test-body-straight; no-prod-config only if production config files are declared (it conflicts with 'production adapters are fair game'). Allowed importer in four gates (unit, blob, assembly, driver); canon wording omits test from the assembly and driver gates.

DO NOT CARRY: inward-only-imports, no-concrete-import, no-ambient-reads, package-classified (a test drives the test tech and controlled fakes, imports anything); hook-single-call, hook-has-call, hook-body-bare, hook-passes-whole, result-opaque, args-underived (a test builds, calls and asserts, so it reads results and makes many calls by nature); build-calls-only, assembly-returns-services, wiring-conditions-plain (the setup half is test-purpose and returns fakes); driver-no-model and driver-wiring-closed (test data builders are model). Reason: nothing imports a test, so it is the end of the graph and only the load-time and legibility atoms still say something about it. With this selection the exemption list in test-is-outside is empty: each 'does not apply' is an atom the kind does not carry.

OPEN QUESTION (helpers): the constraint must reach inside local helpers, otherwise a loop hides in them. Two structures avoid the venue (inferred, not verified). (1) Preferred: remove 'defines anything' (the real hole); a test file defines only its hooks (no-stray-definition with allowed = hooks and registrations), so a helper like run() lives in its own file and is ruled by its kind: an assembly function if it builds, an adapter if it spawns the CLI or touches the machine, a model data builder if pure. Canon already says this for shared test code (1217-1219); the loophole is only that local code escapes it. (2) Fallback if local helpers must stay: test-body-straight reaches the call closure of file-local functions from a body, and counts .forEach/.map callbacks and test.each/describe-level loops as loops. A hidden loop in a local helper is then red, which pushes loops to another kind, the same outcome as (1). Both would cost writing convenience, which the authors say is not the thing to optimize.
helpers:
Helpers the checker needs, shared by the atoms: (1) kind-of-file from the flavor name, or a reader binding for a file the flavor leaves blob (conflict = config error). (2) tech claims per reader, plus the declared lists: pure packages, concrete packages, container libraries, loads, and the reader's hook cut and exemptions. (3) callee classification: factory (callee from service/adapter/assembly/blob file; model create* per the flavor), use case (member call on an instance), tech, sub-driver wiring function, local function; await is transparent to every count. (4) result and argument flow analysis. (5) edge kind (runtime or type) and private/ scope as parameters of each import atom. (6) importer-set tables per target kind, with test listed explicitly. (7) transitive closure mode for chain-purity.

Findings worth keeping: (a) driver-calls-services is a pure bundle of atoms owned by other rules, with no remainder. (b) stable-root splits into four atoms with different checks; config mutableModuleState lifts exactly one, which proves it is a molecule. (c) Both of stable-root's closed exemptions dissolve if boot and test carry their own root-call atom instead of no-root-call. (d) Canon omits test from the assembly and driver importer sets while its own text needs it. (e) A reader's 'counts as blob on purpose' (587-588) and per-reader exemptions (547-549) are the same exception mechanism as the kind-level test list: one place should own it. (f) Fractal assembly inside an adapter factory (159-167) is unruled. (g) Whether blob carries stable-root is unruled. (h) Holes, never atoms: 'orchestrates, does not compute', 'name your use cases', port 'shaped to the inside's needs', 'documented behavior', 'one boot per entry', 'service branches on which adapter', stable-root's open 'shapes not written down'. (i) Web-driver recognition rule (572-574: a reader-bound component may import an assembly, others not) is a component-level variant of assembly-import-gate, not yet an atom.

atoms.name: inward-imports-only
atoms.statement: A file imports no layer outward of its own (model < ports < service, adapters < assembly < drivers < boot); same-layer imports are free.
atoms.why: So the inner layer is understood and tested without the outer one.
atoms.check: Import edge: importer kind vs target kind from the flavor's file names. LAUNCH yes. Whether type-only edges count is stated nowhere for this atom (see sharedParts, type-import scope).
atoms.landing: The import list alone shows which way dependencies run.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service or .adapter file is runtime-imported only by assembly (and by a test); type-only imports and the owning service's private/ are outside it.
atoms.why: Exactly one place in the program knows the concrete graph.
atoms.check: Target kind in {service, adapter}, target not under private/, import not `import type`, importer kind. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A composition-unit import outside an assembly stands out in any import list.

atoms.name: assembly-importers-only
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: Importer kind of every edge to an .assembly file, `import type` included. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The only way into the graph is through a driver or another assembly.

atoms.name: driver-importers-only
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: The outside has one starter and nothing may depend back on a driver (why inferred; canon states the rule, not the reason).
atoms.check: Importer kind of every edge to a driver file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A driver is a leaf below the boot: its consumers are known without opening anything.

atoms.name: no-importers
atoms.statement: Nothing imports the file, type imports included.
atoms.why: It is an entry the runtime or the test runner starts, not a module others use.
atoms.check: In-degree zero for files of the kind. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: An entry is recognizable as a graph root; nothing can depend on it.

atoms.name: blob-consumers-only
atoms.statement: A blob file is imported, runtime or type-only, only by assembly, test, or other blob.
atoms.why: Importing blob contaminates a layer that had guarantees.
atoms.check: Target has no layer suffix; importer kind. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Debt stays visible: unplaced code is reachable only through the build and the tests.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: The file imports no concrete module (I/O, platform, HTTP client, database driver); the driver's tech, claimed by its reader, is not counted concrete here.
atoms.why: Concrete code bypasses the ports and makes the file untestable without its machine.
atoms.check: Import specifier classified concrete vs pure through lib-class-declared. LAUNCH partial: needs the declaration list; a pure library is model only if declared.
atoms.landing: Seeing the imports proves the file touches no machine.

atoms.name: lib-class-declared
atoms.statement: A third-party package counts as pure (model) or as a container only by explicit declaration in config, never by its shape.
atoms.why: Presumed purity is a false guarantee and nothing in an import says what the package does.
atoms.check: Lookup of the package in the project's declared lists. LAUNCH yes (the declaration is the input).
atoms.landing: The list of trusted packages is in one place and is a visible act of faith.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: No file outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, not implementation coupling.
atoms.check: Import path contains a private/ segment of another service. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in a foreign import path is an instant violation.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Service packages form a DAG; every import kind counts, type-only included.
atoms.why: A service in a cycle cannot be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: Package-level graph over all edges, cycle detection. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Every service can be lifted out alone; the map has no loops between boxes.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: No cycle of runtime imports between modules, type-only references excluded.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports fail silently in production bundles.
atoms.check: File-level runtime import graph, cycle detection. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Module load order is unambiguous.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: Imports name the layer file directly; no index.ts or barrel re-export hides the layer.
atoms.why: Every layer rule is enforceable only if the layer is visible at the import site.
atoms.check: Specifier resolves to a layer-suffixed file; no index/barrel re-export between. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The path tells which layer is consumed without opening a file.

atoms.name: port-body-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds type declarations and imports only, no runtime statement.
atoms.why: A contract carries no implementation; runtime code means the adapter is not extracted yet.
atoms.check: AST statement kinds in a .port file. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A port is read as pure shape.

atoms.name: port-edge-type-only
atoms.statement: Every import of a port file, and every import a port file makes, is `import type`.
atoms.why: A runtime edge touching a port is always a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing `type`.
atoms.check: Import edges with a port on either end must be type-only. LAUNCH yes. Same why as port-body-types-only, different check, so split.
atoms.landing: A runtime port import is a visible mistake.

atoms.name: boot-imports-one
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one module, a driver.
atoms.why: Starting is one arrow; any other import is something to touch.
atoms.check: Import set of the file equals one driver. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: One line of imports tells what the program starts.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot's only statement besides its import is one module-root call to the imported driver's wiring function, with no arguments.
atoms.why: The boot starts the program with one call; tech values are the driver's to read.
atoms.check: Root statement list = [import, one call], argument list empty, callee is the imported name. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The entry is two lines.

atoms.name: sub-driver-call-only
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function from its own wiring, passing tech and instances, never inside a hook nor with a use-case result.
atoms.why: A call from a hook would chain two use-case calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: Uses of a driver-kind import: callee = its wiring export, call site outside hooks, arguments tech values or instances. LAUNCH yes, hook cut comes from the reader.
atoms.landing: A multi-file driver is still one tree of attach-callbacks.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: The file reads or calls no environment, time, randomness, console, timer or globalThis from a global; its caller hands them in.
atoms.why: Code reaching the machine cannot be tested without setting that machine up.
atoms.check: Global identifier use, anywhere (root, function, condition, value, call). LAUNCH yes. Carried by model and service by statement; assembly and boot by implication (they hold no tech).
atoms.landing: Everything the file depends on is in its arguments.

atoms.name: no-root-mutable-state
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable (primitive, as const, readonly shape, frozen literal); state lives in factory closures and the module exports factories, never instances.
atoms.why: A module is the same on every load, so no test changes what the next one sees.
atoms.check: Root binding declaration vs syntactic/type proof of immutability, to its depth. LAUNCH yes; opt-out config mutableModuleState.
atoms.landing: Importing the file twice is harmless; instances are born where they are called.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-read
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the tech, the clock or randomness (the module's own location is exempt).
atoms.why: The file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: Root initializer expression reaches a tech/ambient source. LAUNCH yes. Same fact as no-ambient-access, root-scoped, for every kind.
atoms.landing: Constants in the file are the same on every machine.

atoms.name: no-root-effect
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation performs no side effect: no call into tech or unclaimed code, no use-case call, no call into a local function of an effect-allowed file, no assignment or delete (a throw is allowed).
atoms.why: Loading a file must neither act nor leave anything that could change.
atoms.check: Root statement/call classification by callee kind and reader claims. LAUNCH yes; an open clause ('judged by the rule, not waved through') is a hole, see rules.
atoms.landing: Importing a file can never do anything.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: Every run-time definition (function, class, variable) in the file belongs to the roles its kind names: assembly functions (assembly), hooks plus one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot).
atoms.why: A decision written in an outside file is blob hiding under a label.
atoms.check: Declarations at any depth vs the kind's named role list. LAUNCH yes given the hook cut (reader) and the assembly-function notion (returns instances). Parameterized by kind, not exempted by kind.
atoms.landing: A driver or assembly file is a list of nothing but wiring and hooks.

atoms.name: calls-build-only
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly builds: a factory of a composition unit, another assembly or a blob file, a model factory, or a declared load.
atoms.why: The assembly decides nothing but which factory to call.
atoms.check: Callee file kind by import resolution; model factory vs function by the flavor's naming (create*); await counts as the call. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: An assembly reads as a dependency graph, no behavior.

atoms.name: no-model-compute
atoms.statement: An assembly, driver or boot calls no model function that is not a factory.
atoms.why: Computation belongs to a unit with a contract and a test, not to the wiring.
atoms.check: Callee file kind model and not a factory. LAUNCH yes. Stated twice (see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: No hidden derivation sits between a tech value and the unit that needs it.

atoms.name: driver-closed-calls
atoms.statement: A driver calls only use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring functions and its own claimed tech, never an adapter.
atoms.why: An adapter call from a hook is an effect no contract covers.
atoms.check: Callee classification (instance returned by assembly, assembly import, driver import, claimed name). LAUNCH yes given a reader.
atoms.landing: A driver's outgoing arrows are only to services and the tech.

atoms.name: tech-claimed-only
atoms.statement: A driver's tech is exactly what the readers bound to it claim; an import or name no bound reader claims is red, a pure library included.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading that says what is tech.
atoms.check: Imports/free names in a driver vs the reader's claim list. LAUNCH yes by construction (the reader is the input).
atoms.landing: Where a program meets its runtime is a short declared list.

atoms.name: driver-reader
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file is read by a bound reader (one that counts it as blob on purpose is allowed).
atoms.why: Every driver rule is judged through the reading, so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: Reader glob binding exists for the file, binding agrees with the flavor. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: An unread driver is red, never silently exempt.

atoms.name: driver-only-listens
atoms.statement: Callbacks handed to claimed tech to receive its events appear only in drivers (and test files).
atoms.why: Where the program receives the outside world must be one known place.
atoms.check: A callback argument passed to a claimed tech call in a file of another kind. LAUNCH partial: inbound vs outbound callbacks on the same tech are not told apart by shape (adapters call the same tech).
atoms.landing: All event entry points are drivers.

atoms.name: wiring-hook-split
atoms.statement: Wiring calls (assembly, tech setup, sub-driver registration) occur only outside hooks, use-case calls only inside hooks.
atoms.why: A hook that wires moves the build into the event path.
atoms.check: Call class vs region (hook body or not) from the reader's cut. LAUNCH yes given a reader.
atoms.landing: Reading a driver: build and registration at the top, one call per hook below.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call; zero and two are both red.
atoms.why: A second call hides a sequence nobody owns, a missing call is logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count of use-case calls (await = the call) per hook body. LAUNCH yes given the hook cut; the test tech exempts the count.
atoms.landing: Each event maps to one arrow on the map.

atoms.name: hook-only-call
atoms.statement: A hook body holds that call and its return and no other statement: no default, transform, logging, assignment or exit code.
atoms.why: Translation around the call is the facade service's use case, which gets a contract and a test.
atoms.check: Statement list of the hook body. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: A hook can be read at a glance and never needs a test.

atoms.name: hook-unconditional
atoms.statement: A body has no branch, loop or try around or beside its calls.
atoms.why: A decision in a body is a path the reader must trace instead of read.
atoms.check: AST: no if/switch/ternary/loop/try/&&/?? in the body. LAUNCH yes. Stated for hooks (599, 607-608); for a test body implied by 'tests are written for the reviewer'.
atoms.landing: The body is straight-line: given X, do Y, expect A.

atoms.name: hook-no-event-read
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event and host values on whole: nothing read off them, defaulted or transformed (`opts`, never `opts.files`; `process`, never `process.cwd()`).
atoms.why: Reading off the event is translation, and translation is the facade's.
atoms.check: Argument expressions in the hook's call: bare names/literals only. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The hook shows the event reaches the service unchanged.

atoms.name: tech-value-no-call
atoms.statement: No call is made on a tech value (a parameter, an event, a loaded result) in an assembly or a hook; reading a field is allowed in assembly only.
atoms.why: Computing on what the tech hands over is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: Call whose callee root is a tech-value binding. LAUNCH yes given tech-value provenance (parameters, declared load results).
atoms.landing: Tech values travel; nothing is derived from them in the wiring.

atoms.name: arg-no-compute
atoms.statement: Call arguments in assembly, driver wiring and hooks are names, literals, tech values or instances, with no call, operator or default evaluated in place.
atoms.why: A derived argument is the outside opening the door itself.
atoms.check: Argument expression shape. LAUNCH yes. Allowed members differ by region (see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: What is passed is what was received or built.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: The result of an inside call is never read, branched on, computed with, member-accessed, written or logged: it is passed on (assembly) or returned (assembly, hook), or dropped.
atoms.why: The outside never touches what the inside produced, so the map's single arrow is the whole story.
atoms.check: Dataflow of the call's result binding. LAUNCH yes; a declared load's result is the one that may be read.
atoms.landing: Instances move through the wiring like sealed parcels.

atoms.name: loads-declared
atoms.statement: A use-case call in an assembly is allowed only when the project declares it a load; its result counts as tech values from then on.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for its effect.
atoms.check: Callee id in a config list of declared loads. LAUNCH yes (declaration is the input).
atoms.landing: The list of use cases the graph depends on is explicit.

atoms.name: branch-on-params-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: Condition expression operand provenance and arm call kinds. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: Conditionality of the graph is visible as config-driven wiring.

atoms.name: returns-no-adapters
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and adapters only when every caller is a test.
atoms.why: Drivers and other consumers reach services, never the adapters outside the hexagon.
atoms.check: Return value kinds vs the importer kinds of the assembly. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: An assembly's return shape says who may call it.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A composition-unit factory's dependency parameters have no default value.
atoms.why: Defaults smuggle assembly into the service and scatter dependency resolution.
atoms.check: Default initializers on factory dependency parameters in service and adapter files. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The factory's signature is the complete list of what it needs.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file implements a port type.
atoms.why: An adapter exists to make a port real for a technology.
atoms.check: Exported factory's result typed against an imported port (type engine). LAUNCH partial: needs the TS engine. No slug states it.
atoms.landing: Every adapter points at the contract it fulfils.

atoms.name: wiring-fn-shape
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes nothing and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent and is its only export.
atoms.why: The boot calls with no arguments and a sub-driver only attaches callbacks.
atoms.check: Parameter list and export list of the wiring function. LAUNCH yes.
atoms.landing: The shape of the entry chain is fixed: boot, main(), registerX(cli, services).

atoms.name: root-registers-hooks
atoms.statement: Every module-root call in a test file hands a hook to the claimed test tech or calls a shared driver's wiring function with it.
atoms.why: The test tech owns registration at module root, nothing else may run there.
atoms.check: Root call classification by the test reader. LAUNCH yes given the reader. Sibling of no-root-effect and boot-single-call: the root-call permission each kind gets.
atoms.landing: A spec file's root is a table of contents of its tests.

rules.remainder: none; the matrix (864-873) is the intersection of this and the importer-allowlist atoms, not a rule of its own.
none.
The 'chain' is the transitive closure of per-edge atoms, so nothing new; whether the check follows impurity inside third-party packages is unstated. 'false guarantees' is a wish.
'becomes untestable' is a consequence; 'deterministic' for libraries is not checkable, only declared.
none for the atom; 'adapters and drivers reach the environment' is a kind selection, not a part.
'unplaced code needs characterization tests' is a why for the test exemption, not a constraint.
none; same atom as adapter-assembly-only with a different target kind.
none; same atom as service-assembly-only.

Not a constraint: a scope clause (type-only exempt). The atoms that count types (assembly-importers-only, driver-importers-only, no-importers, blob-consumers-only, private-sealed, no-service-cycle) each carry it separately; inward-imports-only and no-concrete-import say nothing.
Scope clause (private/ exempt), not a constraint.
'a sign the adapter hasn't been extracted' is a diagnosis.
Hole: 'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no mechanical form (what is 'which adapter'?). 'same result shape' is only partly a type check.

none.
Hole: 'assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details' is judgment; only the import half (no private/) is structure, and test-is-outside's 'imports anything' contradicts it.

Not atoms: the ten-odd exemptions (see testKind); 'setup builds units with fixtures, same isolation rules' (which rules, on which region?); 'end-to-end tests are neither' vs .e2e being a test kind (263, 567).

A molecule of about ten atoms. Remainders: 'a pipeline hiding in the wiring' is judgment; 'a decision the map cannot show' is the why of branch-on-params-only; 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' (497-503) has no check.

none.
'tech setup' is only identifiable through the reader's claims; 'a hook does not wire' restates hook-one-call.

'a second call means a facade service is missing' and 'zero means logic with no home' are diagnoses; what is a use call is mechanical only through assembly flow; 'a reader with a cut of its own says where the line sits' is an open clause.
none; 'a pure library is model and red regardless' is no-concrete-import crossing into driver.
'residue' is a label; 'a model without a test' is the why.
'a parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a scope note that needs the web reader.
