'holds nothing, touches no tech' is derived from the shape atoms (nothing left to touch with); 'a program has one per entry point' is a wish.

Hole: 'a shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule' is an open clause, which contradicts 'exemptions are a closed list' in spirit; 'until the reading declares the call effect-free' makes one half reader-dependent. The two exemptions are the per-kind root-call permissions.
No slug; 'Assembly is the only place where dependencies are resolved' is derivable from other atoms.
No slug; outbound adapter calls into the same tech are allowed (536-537), the line is not mechanical.
No slug; 'an adapter holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's' (277-278) is a hole: no mechanical form.
'each test assembles its own instance' is the closure property; 'production config has no place in tests' (1200) has no mechanical form.
Hole: 'clever helpers, data-driven indirection, DRY-ed setup that hides the scenario' is judgment beyond a branch/loop ban.
North-star sentence (387-419): every outside rule is one line of this; 'taste is the last mile' is the declared hole.

kinds.note: Universal atoms; stable-root's non-effect half is carried through no-root-effect, boot-single-call or root-registers-hooks depending on kind. Test and private-sealed conflict (see test).
Most constrained by what it may reach. A dependency-free factory with closure state is model by classification, not by a different atom set.
port-body-types-only subsumes every root atom, since a type-only file has no root.
As target it also carries unit-assembly-only's importer allowlist. Model logic inside a .service file is judged by the host's atoms, not a separate set.

Not carried: no-concrete-import, no-ambient-access (adapters reach the machine). Tension: canon says an adapter may import concrete (250, 869) and also that an HTTP client is injected from outside (165-167). The adapter's factory also acts as an assembly for its private/ sub-adapters (159-167) with no assembly atom constraining it.

Imports blob legitimately (blob-consumers-only names assembly as allowed importer). no-ambient-access is implied (it holds no tech). Same five slots as driver and boot: import set, definition set, call set, argument set, result set.

Carries unit-assembly-only and blob-consumers-only as a plain importer (no composition unit, no blob). Its tech imports are not no-concrete-import violations because tech-claimed-only replaces it: a swap of atoms, not an exception.
Gets boot-single-call in place of no-root-effect. 'touches no tech' needs no atom of its own: with one import and one argument-less call nothing is left to touch with. Read with no reader bound.

See testKind. private-sealed is the open collision: 'imports anything' (264, 873) vs private-sealed (993-997) vs internal unit tests (1172-1175). .e2e is listed as a test kind (263, 567) yet 'neither assembly nor driver' (1022-1023): unreconciled.

Blob 'claims no layer guarantees' (371, 957); as target it is the subject of blob-consumers-only. Canon says stable-root's call clause applies to calls into a blob's local functions (1110-1113); whether blob's own root is judged is unstated (hole).

sharedParts.problem: One fact worded twice with different scopes: `const PORT = process.env.PORT` in a model is red under both. For adapters and drivers only the root half applies, so ambient-access cannot be dropped and the pair needs a stated subsumption.

inRules: service bullet 'module-level code must be stateless' (341)
test-is-outside parenthesis 'stable-root exempts the registration, not mutable state' (1016-1017)
sharedParts.problem: Five statements of one atom, two of them carrying a half-exemption note; the assembly rule also cites stable-root for 'nothing at module root but imports', which is stricter and actually comes from closed-definitions.
Same why (computation belongs to a unit with a contract), stated at call level in assembly and in import-matrix terms for the driver, so a check built from either wording alone leaves a hole.

inRules: assembly-builds-only (454-457, 513-516, 'passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with, or member-accessed')
hook-one-call (603-605, 'returned or dropped, never read, written, handed on or logged')
sharedParts.problem: Two vocabularies for one dataflow constraint with different allowed destinations; 'handed on' is the build act in assembly and a banned second call in a hook.

Three allowlists for arguments (assembly: literals, tech params, instances; wiring: tech values, instances, literals; hook: event as received, host whole, instances, literals). The real difference is one fact, whether a field may be read off a tech value: allowed in assembly (442), forbidden in hooks (601-602). That delta is hook-no-event-read; the rest is the shared atom.
Three phrasings of one atom with different allowed lists, and the fourth kind gets an exception. Parameterize by role list per kind; test selects no atom.

inRules: driver prose (650-652, no legal use for blob)
sharedParts.problem: One allowlist stated in five places, two of them from the allowed side; the type-import clause (959-961) is repeated and must stay in sync.

stable-root exempts boot's call and a spec's registration calls (1125-1128): the two exceptions are really three sibling atoms, one per root-call permission (none, one start call, hook registrations). Stated as an exemption it reads as an exception in the rule.

Eight rules are one statement shape (target T importable only by kinds S, type imports count yes or no) with different whys; the 'type imports count' attribute is stated per rule (974-977 no, 880-881 yes, 959-961 yes, 995-997 yes) and for inward-imports-only and no-concrete-import not at all.

Four declaration mechanisms with one shape: nothing in an import or call tells its class, so the class is looked up in a declared list; each is a rule with its own exception clause for the layer that needs the class.
Same atom carried by five kinds and 'excepted' for the driver (claimed tech) and adapter; tech-claimed-only is the swap atom for the driver, nothing yet for adapters except absence.
Same part at assembly (field read allowed, call not) and hook (neither allowed); the hook version strictly contains the assembly version.

inRules: test-is-outside (hook count and services-only exempt, nothing said of branches)
sharedParts.problem: Inside hook-one-call, 'unconditional' is bundled with the count and the translation ban, so the test tech exempts the whole rule or none; decomposed, a test carries this atom and not hook-single-call.
One region constraint stated in three rules.
An adapter's factory composes its private/ sub-adapters, so assembly work lives in an adapter file where no assembly atom applies; same laundering shape as test files.

testKind: Method: built from what a test does (builds units, fires them, asserts, imported by nothing). Verified from canon: test is 'assembly and driver in one' and is exempted from about ten places: inward-imports-only (imports anything), unit-assembly-only, assembly-importers-only, blob-consumers-only, no-concrete-import, closed-definitions ('defines anything'), hook-single-call (count), stable-root (registration), driver-calls-services, hook-only-call and the services-only restriction. Inferred: each exemption exists because an atom was bundled with others; a test is allowed to do what an assembly and a driver each do, but not both within one lexical region, so the rules that bind an assembly function or a hook as a whole could not be carried by the file. CARRY: no-importers (nothing imports a test), driver-reader (test reader), root-registers-hooks (replaces no-root-effect), hook-unconditional (canon: tests are for the reviewer; given X, do Y, expect A, with no path to trace), no-root-mutable-state and no-root-machine-read (the only isolation canon calls structural, 1196-1198), layer-in-path, and the cycle atoms trivially. DO NOT CARRY: inward-imports-only (a test is outermost), unit-assembly-only, assembly-importers-only, blob-consumers-only (the test is an allowed importer of each), no-concrete-import and no-ambient-access (the test tech owns time/IO fakes, unreconciled), closed-definitions (builders, fakes, helpers), hook-single-call, hook-only-call, hook-no-event-read, result-untouched, arg-no-compute (a test reads results, that is assertion), wiring-hook-split (each test builds inside its hook). OPEN: private-sealed collides with 'imports anything' and with internal unit tests (1172-1175); production config import (1200) has no check; .e2e vs 'neither assembly nor driver' (1022). HYPOTHESIS (not canon): if the build region is a named function (the test factory, 1207-1219, only 'strongly encouraged'), it carries the assembly atoms (calls-build-only, result-untouched, branch-on-params-only; returns-no-adapters already allows a test caller) and the hook carries only hook-unconditional plus root-registers-hooks. That separation of roles is what would let the test file carry atoms per function with no exemption.
helpers: Answer: yes, the constraint reaches inside local helpers; 'no' makes closed-definitions test-exempt, which is a laundering venue (it also repeats the drive-by exemption that this decomposition is trying to remove). Verified: canon sets no rule on helpers; test-is-outside says the test 'defines anything', and hook-unconditional's rule text is stated only for hooks. Inferred structure: scope the atom by definition site, not by call path. Every function defined in a test file is either a hook (carries hook-unconditional) or an assembly-role function, i.e. a local test factory (carries the assembly atoms: calls-build-only, no model compute, result-untouched, branch-on-params-only on parameters; returns-no-adapters lets it hand the fakes back since a test is its caller). A third role does not exist: a helper that needs a loop or a branch is logic and leaves the file, placed by what it is (a model unit with its own test, or an adapter fake), the same rule as driver-hooks-only's 'a local parseFoo is a model without a test' (623-628). Reach is 'defined in this file', not 'called from a hook': a transitive reach into imported code would forbid legitimate model loops and would still miss a helper nobody calls from a hook. A helper like run() that builds fake io, starts the CLI and collects output mixes two roles in one function and must split: a factory that builds and returns the recorder, and a hook that fires and asserts. Other venues the same structure must close: (1) a loop or conditional at module root wrapping registrations (test.each, for-of over a table) - root-registers-hooks must say whether a looped registration counts, and canon (1158, 'data-driven indirection') leans no; (2) a loop hidden inside an imported 'data builder model' (1020) is legal and invisible to the mechanical check; what remains there is judgment (does the helper hide the scenario?), which stays a hole, not an atom. Status: the lexical-scope-by-role answer is inferred and needs a ruling, because it contradicts 'defines anything' (1018).

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service, adapter < assembly < driver < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must be built, tested and reasoned about without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: resolve each import to a file kind, compare with the layer order. Parameter: type-only imports counted or not (see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: The suffix alone tells a reader everything the file can depend on.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A model, port, service or assembly file imports no concrete (I/O, platform, ambient-state) package; pure deterministic libraries count as model, and an assembly may import a container library only if config declares it.
atoms.why: A concrete dependency bypasses the ports and makes the file untestable without the machine.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs a declared package classification (pure / concrete / container); canon says purity is declared, not presumed, but not what an undeclared package is.
atoms.landing: The import list shows the file touches no machine.

atoms.name: unit-import-gate
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly (type-only imports and files under private/ are exempt).
atoms.why: Only assembly resolves dependencies, so the concrete graph is known in one place.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every runtime edge into a public unit; exemptions are the type keyword and the private/ path.
atoms.landing: The concrete graph reads from assembly files alone; chunk graph equals assembly graph.

atoms.name: blob-import-gate
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import blob, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantee, so any other importer loses the guarantees it declared.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importee has no layer suffix; importer kind.
atoms.landing: Every blob dependency has a visible assembly or test importer, so the debt is on the map.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports a file under its private/, type-only imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private can move without notice.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path contains private/ and importer sits outside the owning service directory.
atoms.landing: A private/ segment in an import path is an instant visible violation.

atoms.name: no-barrel-index
atoms.statement: Imports resolve to the layer file itself, never through an index.ts re-export barrel.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site or the dependency matrix cannot be enforced.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: index/barrel files (all exports are re-exports) and edges resolving to them.
atoms.landing: The layer is legible in every import path.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and assemblies (and tests), type-only imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract of its own, so nothing may type against it; consumers type against service APIs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge into an assembly file.
atoms.landing: Fan-in on the map shows who builds what.

atoms.name: driver-importers
atoms.statement: A driver file is imported only by a boot or another driver (and a test calling a shared wiring function), type-only imports included.
atoms.why: The runtime starts drivers and drivers join only through wiring, never as a library.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind of every edge into a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver is reachable only from its boot or its parent driver.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: A boot file or a test file is imported by nothing.
atoms.why: They are entries the runtime runs (Node, the test runner); an importer would turn them into a library.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: zero inbound edges (type-only included).
atoms.landing: Entries are leaves; each program entry is findable.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Edges between service packages, every import kind counted, form a DAG.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: collapse files to service packages, find strongly connected components. Direction law (nested adapter points up, parent blind to its children) is derived from this plus the adapter import set.
atoms.landing: The service map is a readable DAG.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime import edges between modules form a DAG, even within one service; type-only cycles are not covered.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in minified production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: strongly connected components on runtime edges.
atoms.landing: Module load order is well-founded.

atoms.name: driver-import-set
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports only assemblies, other drivers and what its bound readers claim as tech; never model, composition units, blob or boot.
atoms.why: A driver's one thing is connecting an event to a use case, so it has no legal use for anything else.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for kinds; tech membership via reader claim. Overlaps unit-import-gate and blob-import-gate for two of the banned kinds.
atoms.landing: A driver's import list is short, so its map arrow is single.

atoms.name: boot-import-one
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else, tech included.
atoms.why: Starting is its one thing; any other import is logic or tech that has a home elsewhere.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: import count and kinds.
atoms.landing: The boot reads as one import and one call.

atoms.name: port-no-runtime
atoms.statement: A port file contains no runtime code, only types.
atoms.why: A port is a contract at the boundary; implementations live in adapters and wiring in assembly.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: any non-type statement or declaration in a .port file.
atoms.landing: A port file reads as a pure contract.

atoms.name: port-type-edges
atoms.statement: No runtime import edge enters or leaves a port file; every edge is import type.
atoms.why: A contract has no runtime presence for anyone to depend on, so a runtime edge is always a re-export, a side-effect import or a missing type keyword.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: edges whose importee or importer is a port file, minus type-only ones.
atoms.landing: Port edges can be erased without changing runtime behavior.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: A model or service file never reads or calls the environment, time, randomness, console, timers or globalThis from a global, at module root or in a function.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine cannot be tested without setting the machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: free global identifier references against a listed set. Adapters and drivers are exempt by scope.
atoms.landing: Every input the file depends on is visible in its signature.

atoms.name: immutable-root-bindings
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, Object.freeze over a literal, readonly types to their depth) and a module exports factories, never instances.
atoms.why: A file must be the same module for every importer: nothing one test runs changes what the next sees.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: syntactic proofs are checkable; an unresolvable named type (Readonly<Store>) proves nothing, so needs the TS engine or a red.
atoms.landing: State lives in a factory closure, so who owns state is visible at the call site.

atoms.name: root-reads-nothing
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the tech, clock or randomness; a module's own location (import.meta.url, __dirname) is exempt.
atoms.why: A stored machine read freezes load-time state, so the file cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs a notion of machine-read source (reader claims, ambient list); property reads presumed free, calls judged by root-no-effect.
atoms.landing: Configuration enters through arguments, never through load.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Evaluating module root performs no side effect: no call that reaches tech, an unclaimed name, a use case or a local function of an effect-allowed file, and no assignment or delete; a throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Loading a file must neither act nor leave anything behind that could change.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: call classification needs readers (effect-free declarations) and callee layer; kind-keyed closed exemption list: the boot's one call, a spec file's registration calls.
atoms.landing: Importing a file is inert; the one module that acts at load is the boot.

atoms.name: no-default-deps
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives its dependency parameters no default value.
atoms.why: Defaults create static imports and scatter assembly logic into services; assembly is the only place dependencies resolve.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: parameter initializers in exported factories; canon never says which parameters are dependencies. Prose only, no slug.
atoms.landing: A service signature lists every dependency, none hidden.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines only what its kind's list allows: assembly functions (assembly), hooks plus at most one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot); types are not definitions.
atoms.why: A file allowed to import anything must be allowed to define nothing else, or logic hides there.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: non-type declarations (function, class, variable) at any depth against the kind list; hook identification needs the reader. Test's list is currently 'anything'.
atoms.landing: Outside files read as pure wiring with no residue.

atoms.name: one-wiring-function
atoms.statement: A driver holds at most one wiring function.
atoms.why: The boot or parent attaches a driver through one call, keeping it one arrow on the map.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: count of exported/defined non-hook functions.
atoms.landing: One entry point per driver file.

atoms.name: wiring-signature
atoms.statement: A root driver's wiring function takes nothing and reads its tech itself; a sub-driver's takes tech and instances from its parent.
atoms.why: Only the driver receives the tech's events; a root has no parent to hand it any and a child gets only what the parent passes.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: parameter lists are checkable; 'reads its tech itself' needs the reader. Prose only, dropped from the summary rule.
atoms.landing: Who hands the tech to whom is visible in two signatures.

atoms.name: assembly-calls-build
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly is a build: a factory of a composition unit, of another assembly or of blob, or a model factory; never a model function, a use case or a tech call.
atoms.why: An assembly's one right is to build, and any other call is logic in the one file that may import everything.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes by callee file kind; model factory vs function depends on the flavor's create* word (naming-dependent).
atoms.landing: The map draws the graph from assembly files and nothing else.

atoms.name: declared-loads
atoms.statement: A use-case call in an assembly is allowed only if the project declares it as a load, and its result then counts as a tech value.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, so the exception must be written down.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee membership in a config list; an undeclared call is red with the declaration as its resolution.
atoms.landing: The one use case the graph depends on is named in config.

atoms.name: inert-arguments
atoms.statement: Arguments to a call are literals, tech values (received parameters, claimed tech) or instances built or received; nothing computed (assembly and wiring may read a field of a tech value, a hook may not, a boot passes none).
atoms.why: A computed argument is logic written inside the call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression classes; the field-read allowance differs by scope.
atoms.landing: A call line reads as a pure link.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: A call's result is only returned, dropped or (assembly) passed to another factory; never read, computed with, branched on, written, logged or member-accessed, except a declared load's result.
atoms.why: Looking into or acting on what was built or fired is logic the map cannot show and no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: dataflow from call result to sinks; allowed sinks differ (assembly may pass on, hook may not).
atoms.landing: Instances move through the outside as opaque handles.

atoms.name: wiring-branch-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or a loaded value, against a literal or for truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show; it belongs to the service that owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operands classified; arms are build calls.
atoms.landing: Graph variants are visible as conditions on inputs.

atoms.name: returns-services-only
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services (one, or a record) and shared model instances, and adapters only when every caller is a test.
atoms.why: Consumers reach the hexagon through contracts; a returned adapter is an effect no contract covers.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: return value kind plus caller kinds (a test caller exception keyed on the importer).
atoms.landing: What an assembly hands out is exactly the surface the driver fires.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: A driver or test file is bound to a reader of its tech; none is red.
atoms.why: Hooks, tech and calls are defined by the reading, so no driver rule can be judged without it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: glob binding in config; a deliberate blob-counting reader is the escape.
atoms.landing: The tech and hook cut of each driver is named in config.

atoms.name: tech-claimed-only
atoms.statement: What counts as tech in a driver is what a bound reader claims; an import or name no reader claims is unclaimed and red, and a pure library is model and red.
atoms.why: Tech is a claim of a reading, not a guess, so the tool must refuse what it cannot read.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: names and imports against reader claims.
atoms.landing: Every tech touchpoint in a driver was claimed on purpose.

atoms.name: driver-call-targets
atoms.statement: Outside hooks a driver calls only assembly factories, claimed tech and sub-driver wiring; inside a hook, one use case; never an adapter, a model or blob.
atoms.why: A driver's one thing is the link: an adapter call is an effect no contract covers and a model call is a use case nobody owns.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: callee classification; 'use case' = call on an instance an assembly returned, needs dataflow or types.
atoms.landing: A driver's links to services are all there is to know of it.

atoms.name: hook-single-call
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call.
atoms.why: Two calls hide a sequence nobody owns and zero hides logic with no home; the facade service is where either belongs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: call count per hook, hooks cut by the reader; the test tech exempts the count.
atoms.landing: Each event maps to one use case, one arrow.

atoms.name: hook-unconditional
atoms.statement: The hook's call is not under a branch, short-circuit or try.
atoms.why: A condition around the call is logic with no contract; the facade owns it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow ancestors of the call inside the hook.
atoms.landing: Every hook always fires its use case.

atoms.name: hook-args-received
atoms.statement: A hook's arguments are the event as received, instances and literals: nothing read off them, no default, no transform (process whole, never process.cwd(); opts, never opts.files).
atoms.why: Reading or defaulting is translation, and translation is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expressions are bare identifiers or literals.
atoms.landing: What the service receives is exactly what the tech sent.

atoms.name: hook-body-only-call
atoms.statement: A hook body holds the call and at most its return; no other statement (no log, exit, write).
atoms.why: Everything else is logic the driver may not hold; the service sets the exit code and renders through ports.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: statement list of the hook body.
atoms.landing: A hook is one line a reader trusts without opening.

atoms.name: sub-driver-call-only
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function, during its own wiring, never inside a hook and never with a use-case result.
atoms.why: Otherwise one hook could chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every use of the imported binding is a call in the wiring function; arguments by inert-arguments.
atoms.landing: Driver files split by taste with no hidden chains.

atoms.name: sub-driver-exports
atoms.statement: A sub-driver exports its one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: The only thing a root can do with the import is let it attach callbacks.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: export list of a driver file.
atoms.landing: A driver's public surface is one function.

atoms.name: boot-single-call
atoms.statement: A boot calls its driver's wiring function once, at module root, with no arguments.
atoms.why: Starting is the boot's one thing and it is the one module whose evaluation performs a call.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: exactly one root call statement, empty argument list.
atoms.landing: The program's start is one line.

atoms.name: boot-no-tech
atoms.statement: A boot references no tech or ambient global (process, document, the parser).
atoms.why: Reading the tech is the driver's one thing.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: free global identifier references in the file.
atoms.landing: Entries are inert wrappers.

atoms.name: only-driver-listens
atoms.statement: Only a driver (or test) file hands callbacks to a claimed tech's events; adapters call the same tech only outbound.
atoms.why: The driver is the one place the program receives the tech's events; a listener elsewhere is an unvetted entry.
atoms.check: LAUNCH weak: telling listening from outbound calling needs a reader bound on non-driver files, and canon says assembly and boot have none; whether an adapter registering a callback counts is unstated.
atoms.landing: Every way into the program is a driver hook on the map.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file implements a port it type-imports, and what it exposes conforms to that port's shape.
atoms.why: Adapters are replaceable only through the port, so the inside never knows which one it holds.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: factory return type assignable to an imported port type (needs the TS engine). Fixtures are adapters under the same atom.
atoms.landing: Each adapter names the one contract it serves.

atoms.name: straight-line-body
atoms.statement: A test body, and every function defined in its file that it reaches, contains no branch or loop, callback iteration (map, forEach, test.each) included.
atoms.why: The reviewer must read each test as given, when, expect without reconstructing the scenario from indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: control-flow nodes and iteration calls in hook bodies and in file-local functions reachable from them. Canon states only the judgment version ('clever helpers, data-driven indirection'); the ban is the authors' premise.
atoms.landing: The scenario is visible in the test, fixture and assertion close enough to compare by eye.

rules.remainder: 'Lateral (same layer) OK' is contradicted for service, adapter, driver, boot and test by unit-import-gate, driver-importers, entry-not-imported; 'service, adapters' share a rank yet may not import each other. 'See matrix for the combined result' defers to rules instead of stating an atom.
'Violations visible by shape, by review, by tooling' is a wish, not a check.

Not an atom: it is the transitive closure of the three atoms above. 'Partial extraction produces false guarantees' is a why, and 'valid only if the full chain honours the constraints' is a property of the checker, not a new constraint.
'Purity should be declared, not presumed' is a config precondition; what a package with no declaration counts as is unstated. 'Concrete' vs driver 'tech' vs 'unclaimed' are three vocabularies.

'Distinct from service-purity' is cross-reference prose. Scope (model, service only; adapters and drivers reach the environment) lives in the rule text, not in a kind list. Root-level environment reads are judged twice (here and root-reads-nothing).

'Blob importing blob is fine' is a scope clause; 'assembly may take it because its rule bounds what it can do' and 'test needs characterization tests' are whys; 'a driver's blob call is already a violation' restates driver-call-targets.
Duplicate half of one atom with adapter-assembly-only; the 'not by ... blob' clause makes blob an importer-side ban here and an importee-side ban in blob-quarantine.
Duplicate half of one atom with service-assembly-only.
Not an atom: a scope parameter (type-only exempt) of unit-import-gate. It also fixes the SomeService['method'] shorthand as legal; whether that exemption is stated per edge atom is the open part.
Not an atom: a scope parameter (private/ exempt) of unit-import-gate; 'internal composition is unrestricted' also leaves private units free of every other rule or says nothing about them.
'Sign the adapter hasn't been extracted yet' is a diagnosis, not a check.

Whole rule is a hole: 'the service layer branches on which adapter it got' has no structural definition (no named tag, instanceof or adapter identity). 'Adapters absorb source-specific details' is a wish. Judgment, never an atom.
Nesting prose (nested service cannot reach parent's private/, layer directories are not nested services) needs a definition of service boundary by directory, stated only in prose.
Sharing progression (kernel, merge, anti-corruption boundary) is guidance, not checks; direction law is derived.

Only 'input via public API' has structure (private-sealed plus factory closures). 'Assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details' is a judgment; the (a)/(b) exceptions for internal unit tests are judgment.

A bundle by exemption: 'imports anything' (drops inward-imports, no-concrete-import, unit-import-gate, blob-import-gate), 'defines anything' (opens closed-definitions), 'hook count and services-only do not apply' (drops hook-single-call, driver-call-targets), registration exempt from root-no-effect. Silent on hook-args-received, hook-body-only-call, result-untouched, inert-arguments, no-default-deps (prose says defaults are right), returns-services-only. 'Same isolation rules' for fixtures is undefined; 'shared test code is placed by what it is' is a placement judgment; '.e2e' is named as test kind but 'end-to-end tests are neither, outside the graph' contradicts it.

Largest molecule (8 atoms, 1 slug). 'Nothing at module root but imports' collides with 'nothing but assembly functions is defined' (functions sit at root). Model factory vs function rests on the flavor's create* word. 'A dependency not yet extracted is built here behind the port that awaits it', 'default wiring of config', 'shared instances flow down, never sideways' are judgment or guidance with no structural form. Container libraries: 'constructs and never calls a use case' repeats assembly-calls-build.
Importer set omits tests, which call assemblies (test factory pattern); the test exception lives elsewhere.
Escape: a reader that counts the file as blob on purpose is a config choice.

'A hook does not wire' is derived from hook-single-call (the one call is a use case). 'Tech setup (parser, server, mount)' is whatever the reader says. 'Lazily loaded feature is an assembly importing another' is guidance.

Second-largest molecule. 'Use-case call' vs other call needs classification; 'a facade service is missing' and 'zero means logic with no home' are diagnoses; 'ruled for the stock cut' defers to readers; 'the test tech exempts the count' is the sole test relaxation stated.
'A pure library is model and red regardless' crosses into no-concrete-import and driver-import-set; 'parsing and rendering are use cases of a service' is a why.
'Residue' and the two examples (a local parseFoo is a model without a test) are diagnosis.
'A parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule' is a reader-scope clause; 'never hexagon data' is inert-arguments plus result-untouched.
Importer set omits tests though shared registerMatchers is called by spec files.
'One boot per entry point (a bin, a server, an app)' is a program-level count with no per-file check; 'holds nothing' has no separate shape beyond closed-definitions.

Explicitly open-ended: 'a shape nobody has written down yet is judged by the rule, not waved through' is a judgment clause no checker can launch. 'Reading declares a call effect-free' extends it by reader. Exemptions (boot call, spec registration) are kind-keyed. Whether it applies to blob files is unstated ('everywhere else' vs blob 'no guarantees'). Duplicated by model bullet, service bullet, assembly rule, ambient-access ('same at module root').
No slug. 'No exceptions' contradicted by the test factory pattern, where defaults are right.
'Abstractness', 'knowledge', 'most valuable' are wishes; 'a factory that takes a port or service is a composition unit' is a classification derived from inward-imports (model cannot import ports).
'It orchestrates; it does not compute', 'decisions', 'if you cannot name the use cases you have a utility bag' are judgment words; 'returned API is the contract' is a wish.

'Holds what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's', 'absorbs specificity', 'translates' are judgment; adapters get no verb list at all in canon (outside kind, but nothing restricts what they do).

'Each test assembles its own instance' is immutable-root-bindings for a different why (test isolation, not importer identity). 'Production config has no place in tests', 'fixtures deterministic', 'shared fixtures follow sharing rules' are judgment.
Only the implied atom is structural; 'legible as a behavior statement', 'unit under test identifiable at a glance', 'fixture and assertion close' are judgment.
Stated as a bold sentence, no slug, not in the summary.

kinds.note: Cross-cutting edge atoms every kind carries (test: no-runtime-cycle is vacuous since nothing imports a test). Blob carries them too. Type-import treatment is a per-atom parameter.
Constrained by what it may depend on, not by what it may do; the only kind that carries both no-concrete-import and no-ambient-access with immutable root.
Root atoms are vacuous (no runtime code). unified-port stays a hole.
Also importee side of unit-import-gate. May type-import another service's API but never runtime-import it. Decisions, orchestration are judgment holes.

Does NOT carry no-concrete-import or no-ambient-access (reaching the machine is its business). Canon gives it no verb list: the one outside-ish kind with import rights narrow and doing-rights unrestricted, a hole by omission.

Imports blob legally (blob-import-gate allows it). no-ambient-access is implied by inert-arguments and assembly-calls-build, not carried separately. Not reader-bound. Holds eight atoms inside one slug.
Does not carry no-ambient-access (the tech is its business). Hook atoms are scoped to hooks by the reader's cut.
closed-definitions list is empty and inert-arguments takes zero arguments; root-no-effect is exempted for its one call. No reader bound.
closed-definitions needs its own list (hooks, straight-line local helpers, data literals) instead of 'anything'. Everything else canon exempts is simply not selected. See testKind.

Importee side of blob-import-gate; as importer it may import blob and presumably model and ports but never units. No content atoms by definition. Whether stable-root applies is unstated; canon names blob as an effect-allowed layer for root-no-effect callee judgment.

sharedParts.problem: One constraint is stated as two slugs, one per suffix, plus two slugs that are only scope modifiers (type-only, private/). Importer set says 'assembly only' while tests call assemblies and import units; the test exception sits in test-is-outside.

sharedParts.atom: (type-import scope, a parameter of every edge atom)
sharedParts.problem: Whether type-only imports count is declared six times with opposite answers, and the matrix prose ('a driver or assembly may type-import from any layer', lines 880-883) contradicts blob-quarantine, private-sealed, assembly-driver-only and driver-not-imported. It should be one attribute per edge atom (types: exempt | counted), not wording in each rule.

Stated in model (stable root), service (module-level stateless), assembly (nothing at root but imports), and test (exempts registration, not mutable state) at different strictness. For a test file the stable-root why (an importer sees the same module) does not hold since nothing imports it; the surviving why is test isolation. Inferred: same check, two whys, so the atom may need splitting by why.

An environment read at module root is judged by ambient-access in model and service and by stable-root everywhere else; stable-root delegates ('judged where it sits, by its layer') yet adds its own binding check, so one fact can be reported by two rules.

The same constraint (definition list closed per kind) is written three times with three vocabularies ('defined', 'residue', 'holds nothing'), with the glossary of 'definition' given once in assembly prose. Test says 'defines anything', the open set that makes every test-file helper a laundering venue.

Three wordings of one atom ('literals, tech values received as parameters, or instances'; 'tech values, instances, literals'; 'event as received, instances and literals'); the only real differences (field read allowed in assembly and wiring, forbidden in a hook, boot none) are buried in a single sentence at line 440-442.

Assembly may pass a result on, a hook may only return or drop it; both forbid reading. A test touches built instances and use-case results by nature, so one atom cannot serve 'assembly and driver in one'; scoping needs the distinction build result vs use-case result.

'A driver never calls an adapter, a model, or blob' is stated at call level (driver-calls-services, blob-quarantine) and import level (matrix row, driver-import-set); 'a hook does not wire' is stated twice (wiring-outside-hooks, hook-one-call).

'Nothing imports it' is separately stated for boot and test; driver-not-imported and assembly-driver-only are the same shape with wider importer sets. Test is a hidden member of every importer allowlist (assembly, driver) without being listed.

Tests are 'read by a test reader' in one rule and 'driver or a test file' in another; assembly and boot are said 'no reader bound' twice (lines 510-512, 720-721) as a separate statement rather than as the absence of this atom.

What counts as tech (claimed by a bound reader, else unclaimed) is defined in Terminology, in the driver prose, in driver-calls-services and in stable-root, and 'concrete', 'tech', 'effect-allowed layer', 'unclaimed' are four overlapping classifications of the same package.

One import ban is restated per kind with different exception words (pure library = model; declared container for assembly; reader-claimed tech for driver; adapter allowed). Pure-library-is-model-and-red appears in driver-calls-services without a home atom.
Blob appears as importee (blob-quarantine) and as importer (the 'not by ... blob' clauses of the composition rules), and assembly's right to import blob is restated in assembly prose.
Different whys and checks but one fact (a runtime cycle across two services) is reported by both; direction law and 'wiring that would close a cycle is misplaced' are derived, not atoms.

'An assembly that returns adapters can only be called by tests' makes an exception keyed on the caller's kind, yet assembly-driver-only says only drivers and assemblies import an assembly. The test caller is a hidden fourth importer kind.
'No exceptions' for defaults, then 'default argument values are right here' for test factories, with no kind-level statement of which kinds carry the atom.

testKind: The test kind is a glued bundle ('assembly and driver in one') that is then exempted from about twelve atoms; with atoms, nothing needs an except because the atoms are just not selected. Because nothing imports a test, every atom whose why concerns what depends on a file (importer sets, contamination) is vacuous, and the only edge atoms that bind it are entry-not-imported (it is a leaf), private-sealed (tests reach units through the public API, which is test-through-contract's one structural half), no-service-cycle (canon: fixtures are test-purpose adapters, not the real nested ones) and no-barrel-index. Because it builds units, calls them and asserts, the build atoms (assembly-calls-build, result-untouched, returns-services-only, inert-arguments) and the link atoms (hook-single-call, hook-args-received, hook-body-only-call, driver-call-targets) cannot apply: the point of a test is to touch what it built and read what it called, so those atoms are opposite in sign to its job. CARRY: reader-bound (the test reader says what a hook, a registration and an assertion are), entry-not-imported, immutable-root-bindings (for the isolation why: each test assembles its own instance), root-no-effect with the runner's registration calls as the reader-declared exemption, private-sealed, no-service-cycle, no-barrel-index, closed-definitions with its own list (hooks, straight-line local helpers, data literals) instead of 'anything', and the implied straight-line-body. DO NOT CARRY: inward-imports, no-concrete-import, unit-import-gate, blob-import-gate (a test must import anything, blob for characterization), no-ambient-access (tests control the machine), no-default-deps (defaults are right in a test factory), hook-single-call, hook-unconditional, hook-args-received, hook-body-only-call, driver-call-targets, assembly-calls-build, declared-loads, wiring-branch-only, returns-services-only, result-untouched, inert-arguments. Open: root-reads-nothing is probably carried but its stable-root why (importer identity) does not hold for a leaf file, so it needs its own isolation why; and canon is silent on whether a hook-body atom stays for test bodies. Separate from tests: shared test code is already placed by what it is (fake = adapter, factory = assembly function, data builder = model, matcher = driver), which is the right idea and means the leftover test kind is only the file-local part.
helpers: Yes: the constraint must reach the helpers, and the clean way is to stop framing it as a rule on the body. Two atoms are being conflated: straight-line-body (no branch or loop) and closed-definitions for the test kind. Canon's 'defines anything' for test is the laundering venue itself, so closing the test's definition set removes the question. Structure: (1) the straight-line check follows file-local call edges from each hook (transitive closure within the spec file), so any reachable local function containing a branch, a loop, recursion or callback iteration (map, forEach, test.each, reduce) is red as if inlined; (2) the test kind's closed-definitions list is hooks, straight-line local helpers and data literals, nothing else, the same shape as driver-hooks-only ('a local parseFoo is a model without a test'); (3) anything that needs control flow leaves the file and is placed by what it is, as canon already says for shared test code: a run() that starts the CLI is an adapter (or a driver-user outside the graph if it is end-to-end), a scenario builder is an assembly function, a data builder is model, a matcher a driver. There the loop is legitimate under that kind's rules, and the venue is no longer hidden: it is an import, with a kind, a contract and a test. A plain 'no' (helpers exempt) is unacceptable because it lets the straight-line atom be satisfied by relocating the loop one function down. Residual hole to flag, not decide: a shared kinded helper that takes a list of cases or a callback and loops over them re-opens data-driven indirection through a legitimate door; closing it needs either a limit on what a test body may pass to imported helpers (no arrays of cases, no callbacks) or a reviewer judgment; neither is stated in canon.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file imports only files of its own layer or an inner one in the order model < ports < service/adapter < assembly < driver < boot.
atoms.why: The inside must be developable and reasoned about without knowing the outside exists.
atoms.check: Resolve each import's target kind from the flavor and compare ranks.
atoms.landing: A reader sees dependency direction from the import path alone.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file of an inside, assembly or boot kind imports no platform/IO/ambient-state package (node:fs, HTTP client, DB driver) unless it is declared pure.
atoms.why: Code that touches the machine bypasses its ports and cannot be tested without that machine.
atoms.check: Match each import specifier against the declared-pure list and the reader-claimed tech list; anything else is concrete or unclaimed.
atoms.landing: Concrete dependencies are visible as adapters, never inside a unit.

atoms.name: unit-assembly-only
atoms.statement: A public .service.ts or .adapter.ts is runtime-imported only by assembly; private/ files and type-only imports are outside this atom.
atoms.why: Composition happens in one place, so the chunk graph is the assembly graph and services never know the concrete graph.
atoms.check: For each runtime import of a public service/adapter file, require the importer kind to be assembly.
atoms.landing: The map shows every wiring edge as an assembly edge.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: No file outside a service package imports from that package's private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership: what is private may move without notice.
atoms.check: Compare the importer's service directory with the target's enclosing private/ owner.
atoms.landing: `/private/` in an import path is an instant visible violation.

atoms.name: no-index-barrel
atoms.statement: No file re-exports other files' layers behind one path (no index.ts indirection).
atoms.why: The consumer must see which layer it imports at the import site.
atoms.check: Flag modules that are re-export-only or named as an index entry.
atoms.landing: The layer reads straight off every import line.

atoms.name: blob-quarantine
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import blob, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: A layer with guarantees imported blob would inherit its lack of guarantees.
atoms.check: For every import of a suffixless file, require the importer to be assembly, test or blob.
atoms.landing: Debt is visible and confined to the graph-building edge.

atoms.name: assembly-importers
atoms.statement: An assembly file is imported only by drivers and other assemblies, type imports included.
atoms.why: An assembly has no contract; its shape is the services it returns, so nothing may type against it.
atoms.check: For each import of an assembly file, require importer kind driver or assembly.
atoms.landing: The hexagon is built from exactly one direction on the map.

atoms.name: entry-not-imported
atoms.statement: A boot is imported by nothing, a test by nothing, a driver only by a boot or another driver, type imports included.
atoms.why: These files are started by the runtime (node, the test runner, the framework), so no code may reach them except the starting chain.
atoms.check: Importer kinds of each boot, test and driver file against the allowed set per kind.
atoms.landing: Every run-time entry point is a leaf the reader finds without searching.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Services form a DAG: no file pair in two services imports each other transitively, every import kind counted.
atoms.why: A cycle makes neither service extractable, movable or reasonable alone.
atoms.check: Fold the import graph by service directory and detect cycles.
atoms.landing: The service map is a readable acyclic diagram.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime (non-type) imports among modules form no cycle, even inside one service.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in minified production code.
atoms.check: Detect cycles in the runtime-only module graph.
atoms.landing: Little for a human; a safety guarantee.

atoms.name: types-only-file
atoms.statement: A port file declares only types: no value statement, no runtime export.
atoms.why: A contract has nothing to run; runtime code there is an adapter not yet extracted.
atoms.check: Scan the file's AST for any value declaration, expression statement or value export.
atoms.landing: Opening a port shows pure contract.

atoms.name: port-type-edges
atoms.statement: No runtime import goes to or from a port file; ports are reached by `import type` only.
atoms.why: A runtime edge on a type-only file is always a leaked re-export, a side-effect import or a missing `type` keyword.
atoms.check: Runtime import specifiers whose source or target is a port file.
atoms.landing: `import type` on a port is a reader-visible promise it is a contract.

atoms.name: no-ambient-access
atoms.statement: Code reads no ambient host value (environment, clock, randomness, console, timers, globalThis) from a global; callers or ports hand it in.
atoms.why: Code reaching the machine depends on it and cannot be tested without setting it up.
atoms.check: Resolve free global identifiers against the host-name list, in any position (root, condition, value, call).
atoms.landing: What a unit needs from the world is exactly its factory arguments.

atoms.name: no-root-state
atoms.statement: No module-root binding holds mutable state: no top-level let, no unfrozen collection, no binding whose immutability the syntax does not prove.
atoms.why: A test importing the module must get the module every other test got, unchanged by what ran.
atoms.check: Root binding kinds plus type/initializer proof (primitive, as const, readonly, Object.freeze) to its depth.
atoms.landing: State is visible only inside factories, so instances are reached by argument.

atoms.name: no-root-machine-read
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the machine (tech, clock, randomness); import.meta.url and __dirname are presumed not machine reads.
atoms.why: A file holding load-time machine state cannot be tested under another environment or moment without reloading.
atoms.check: Root initializer data flow from host names, claimed tech and clock/random sources.
atoms.landing: Root bindings are constants a reader can trust.

atoms.name: inert-root
atoms.statement: Module-root evaluation performs no effect: no call reaching tech, an unclaimed name, a use case or a local function of a side-effect layer, and no bare assignment or delete; a throw is allowed.
atoms.why: Loading a module must not act, or every importer and test triggers it.
atoms.check: Classify each root statement and each root call's callee against the reader's effect-free declarations.
atoms.landing: Importing is safe; the only execution at load is where the runtime starts it.

atoms.name: no-dependency-defaults
atoms.statement: A composition unit's factory gives its dependency parameters no default value.
atoms.why: Defaults smuggle assembly into service modules and create static imports from service to adapters or config.
atoms.check: Default initializers on the factory's destructured dependency parameters.
atoms.landing: Dependencies are exactly what the signature names; the only resolver is assembly.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: Each outside kind defines only what its list allows: assembly only assembly functions, driver only hooks and at most one wiring function, boot nothing; types are free.
atoms.why: Any other definition is residue where logic hides without a contract or test.
atoms.check: Enumerate run-time declarations (function, class, variable) in the file against the per-kind list.
atoms.landing: Opening an outside file shows nothing but its one thing.

atoms.name: callees-closed
atoms.statement: Every call in an outside file targets a callee kind allowed at that position: assembly builds factories; a driver's hook calls one use case; its wiring calls assembly, claimed tech, sub-driver wiring; a boot calls its driver's wiring function.
atoms.why: An outside layer does its one thing and its calls carry a contract and a test.
atoms.check: Resolve each callee's file kind (flavor) or tech claim and compare against the allow-list for the call's position.
atoms.landing: The map draws each outside file as one arrow kind.

atoms.name: call-count-exact
atoms.statement: A hook makes exactly one use-case call (zero or two is red) and a boot makes one call, at root.
atoms.why: A sequence between two calls is a use case nobody owns; zero is logic with no home.
atoms.check: Count call expressions in the hook body or boot root.
atoms.landing: One hook equals one arrow equals one use case.

atoms.name: args-plain
atoms.statement: Call arguments in outside files are only literals, tech values (a field read allowed in wiring) or instances built or received, never computed.
atoms.why: A derived argument is the outside opening the door itself; derivation belongs to a unit with a contract.
atoms.check: Classify each argument expression by data-flow origin (literal, parameter tech value, instance) and reject calls and arithmetic.
atoms.landing: Wiring and hooks read as pure plumbing.

atoms.name: hook-args-whole
atoms.statement: A hook hands the event to its call as received: nothing read off it, the host's values handed whole (process, not process.cwd()).
atoms.why: Any default, read or reshaping around the call is translation, which is the facade service's use case.
atoms.check: Hook-call arguments are identifiers bound to the hook's parameters or host globals, no member access or default.
atoms.landing: The driver is thin by shape.

atoms.name: hook-result-untouched
atoms.statement: A hook returns the call's value or drops it, never reads, writes, hands on or logs it.
atoms.why: A branch, transform, print or exit-code write on the result is translation that belongs in the facade.
atoms.check: Data-flow of the call result inside the hook: only return or discard.
atoms.landing: Exit codes and rendering are legible in the service contract.

atoms.name: branch-closed
atoms.statement: Branches and loops in an outside body are allowed only per kind: none in a hook or test body; in assembly only on a parameter or loaded value, compared to a literal or truthiness, with factory-call arms.
atoms.why: Decisions on anything else are invisible to the map and belong to the service that owns them.
atoms.check: Statement kinds if/switch/loop/ternary/&&/??, their condition origin and arm contents.
atoms.landing: No decision hides in wiring or in a hook.

atoms.name: built-result-opaque
atoms.statement: In an assembly, what a call built is passed on or returned, never branched on, computed with or member-accessed; await counts as the call.
atoms.why: Touching a built instance is the assembly deciding, which the map cannot show.
atoms.check: Result flow of each factory call: sinks limited to argument, return, binding.
atoms.landing: Assembly shows structure only, no behavior.

atoms.name: declared-load
atoms.statement: An assembly awaits a use case only if the project declares it as a load; the load's result then counts as a tech value.
atoms.why: Nothing in a call's shape tells a load from a use case run for effect, so the exception must be named.
atoms.check: Callee symbol membership in the declared-loads list.
atoms.landing: The one use-case dependency of the graph is a named exception.

atoms.name: returns-services-only
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services and shared model instances, and adapters only if every caller is a test.
atoms.why: Hooks must reach the hexagon only through its services; adapters returned would be reachable effects.
atoms.check: Layer of the types in the return value, and the importer kinds of that assembly.
atoms.landing: Drivers get services, nothing else.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver and test file has a bound reader, or a reader that counts it as blob on purpose.
atoms.why: Every driver atom is judged through the reading, so none can be judged without it.
atoms.check: Config reader glob matched against each driver/test file.
atoms.landing: Each driver announces the tech it listens to.

atoms.name: outside-imports-closed
atoms.statement: A boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else; a driver imports only assemblies, drivers and its claimed tech (type imports free).
atoms.why: The outside imports only what its one thing needs.
atoms.check: Runtime import targets by kind against the per-kind allow-list.
atoms.landing: The outside's reach is known without opening it.

atoms.name: driver-exports-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver exports at most one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.why: An importer able to call a hook could chain two calls through one level of indirection.
atoms.check: Export list of each driver file.
atoms.landing: A sub-driver's only offering is attaching callbacks.

atoms.name: entry-no-args
atoms.statement: A boot calls its driver's wiring function with no arguments, and a root driver's wiring function takes none.
atoms.why: The boot touches no tech and the root driver reads its tech itself, so there is nothing to pass.
atoms.check: Argument count at the boot call and parameter count of the root wiring function.
atoms.landing: The entry is a bare start.

atoms.name: tech-claimed
atoms.statement: Every import or global name a driver reaches is claimed by a bound reader; unclaimed names and pure libraries are red.
atoms.why: What counts as tech is only what a reading claims, or no driver rule can be judged.
atoms.check: Match driver imports and globals against bound readers' claims.
atoms.landing: A driver's tech is a declared list.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter exports a factory whose result implements a port type.
atoms.why: The suffix declares a port implementation; without one it is an unplaced unit.
atoms.check: Adapter has a type import of a port and its returned shape is annotated or satisfied against it.
atoms.landing: Every adapter is read against the contract it serves.

"Violations visible by shape" is a wish; the checker only sees barrels.
A theorem of three atoms over the transitive import closure, not a new constraint; purity of a third-party package's own dependencies is trusted by declaration.
"Purity should be declared, not presumed" is an oracle input (declared-pure list), not a constraint.
None; the host-name list is an oracle (see helpers).
None.
None; same atom as adapter-assembly-only with a different layer parameter.
None; duplicate of service-assembly-only by atom.
A scope switch (are type imports counted?) applied to each import atom, not a constraint; its per-atom outcome is scattered over seven rules.
A scope switch (private/ files are outside unit-assembly-only), not a constraint.
None.
"If the service layer branches on which adapter it got" is a judgment no structure shows; hole. Only the implied adapter-implements-port is checkable nearby.
None.
The direction law (817-826) is a consequence of this plus unit-assembly-only.
None.
"Assertions on documented behavior, no implementation details" is judgment; only the private/ import part is checkable, and a spec in the service's own folder may count as inside (unspecified).

Its content is mostly exemptions from other atoms; "setup builds units with fixtures, same isolation rules" and the placement of shared test code by what it is are rulings, not checks; e2e tests being outside the graph is a kind exclusion.
"A pipeline hiding in the wiring" and "decides nothing but which factory" are judgment words beyond the shape checks.
None.
None; the binding-vs-flavor conflict is a config error, not code structure.
"Tech setup" membership depends on the reader's claims.
"A facade service is missing" is advice; the cut of a hook is the reader's, and a non-stock cut is unspecified.
None; restates the callee set of wiring-outside-hooks and hook-one-call without positions.
"Residue" is a label; sub-driver wiring signature (cli, services) has no mechanical check beyond args-plain.
"Parent component rendering a child in markup is not this rule" is a tech-reading scope note.
None.
