"A shape nobody has written down is judged by the rule, not waved through" is an open-ended judgment clause; the closed exemption list (boot call, spec registration) is two except clauses.

kinds.note: Never a unit-assembly-only target; importable by anything inward of it; canon states root-state in its own bullet again.
No runtime content, so root atoms and no-runtime-cycle are vacuous; no ambient or concrete atom needed beyond types-only.
"Orchestrates, does not compute" and the use-case naming are judgment remainders; "model logic in a service file is fine" contradicts the first (hole).

Does not carry no-ambient-access or no-concrete-import (reaching the machine is its job); "holds only what its port needs and nothing of the hexagon's" is a judgment remainder; no-dependency-defaults is implied by 165-167.
A declared container library is an exception to no-concrete-import by configuration; no-ambient-access implied by "holds no tech"; assembly may import blob.
Does not carry no-ambient-access (reads the tech); hook atoms apply per the reader's cut; the reader, not the atom, supplies exemptions.
inert-root carries a one-call exemption by kind (an except clause); no reader bound; no-ambient-access implied by "touches no tech".

See testKind; closed-definitions, branch-closed and no-ambient-access carried are recommendations beyond canon's words ("defines anything" in canon); unit and blob importer lists include test as a member, not an exemption.

Only as importee (importers: assembly, test, blob); canon says "no guarantees" yet stable-root states no blob exemption while 654-655 describes a legacy blob entry calling at root, so inert-root on blob is unresolved; cycle atoms apply to graph, blob is "outside the matrix" (unspecified).

sharedParts.problem: Stated as global-reach everywhere for model/service (944-952) and again as machine-read at root for every kind (1093-1105, adapters included where reach is allowed); stable-root defers to ambient-access (1121-1123) while making root process.cwd() red in adapters, so scope (anywhere vs root) is unresolved.
One constraint worded in five places; test-is-outside says the spec "defines anything" while also saying stable-root exempts the registration "not mutable state", which contradicts.
Four per-kind definition lists in four rules, with test the one list that is open ("defines anything"), which is exactly where helpers launder logic.
driver-calls-services lists the callee set without position, wiring-outside-hooks and hook-one-call state the position-specific halves; same set stated three times at different scopes.
Same argument whitelist worded four ways; assembly/wiring allow a field read of a tech value, hook allows none (separated here as hook-args-whole).
"Exactly one call" stated for hook and boot separately; test exempts the count for hooks.
"Nothing imports it" stated for boot, test and driver in three rules; the test imports assembly, which assembly-driver-only forbids unless the test counts as a driver.
Boot passes no arguments and root main() takes none: two sides of one fact in two rules.

Root-call exemptions are a "closed list by kind" (boot call, spec registration, 1126-1128) while the driver section says the reader exempts "a test runner's registration" (562-564): two homes for one exemption.

Three classifications of one import: concrete (platform/IO, 884), tech (what a reader claims, 80-91), pure library (model, red regardless in a driver 1062-1063); how a package is sorted is spread over three places.

Two slugs for one atom plus two scope switches; private/ lets a composition unit's factory import and call private sub-adapters (assembly work inside an adapter), which is in tension with service-purity/chain-purity for a service.
The importer set {assembly, test} is restated in the matrix, in the test rule and in assembly prose, while service/adapter rules also list "blob" among forbidden importers: same fact, four wordings.
One per-atom parameter (do type imports count?) stated as rule runtime-import plus five scattered counter-clauses; not an atom, a modifier.
Test appears as an exception clause in at least seven places; the symptom of a kind built as a bundle instead of a selection of atoms.

testKind: Test files are read by a test reader and judged by a selection of atoms, with canon's exemptions turned into choices. Carry: reader-bound, entry-not-imported (nothing imports a test), no-root-state (per-test isolation, 1196-1198; canon's \"defines anything\" cannot override it), no-root-machine-read, inert-root with spec registration declared effect-free by the test reader instead of a special exemption, private-sealed, the two cycle atoms (test edges count), plus recommended and not stated in canon: no-ambient-access (determinism, 1193-1194) and branch-closed with the \"none\" setting over the whole file, because a test must read as given/when/expect for the reviewer (1152-1161). Importer sets for units and blob list test as a member. Do NOT carry: no-concrete-import and inward-imports (a test builds units with fixtures and real adapters), callees-closed, call-count-exact, args-plain, hook-args-whole, hook-result-untouched (a test calls many things and must read results to assert), built-result-opaque, declared-load, returns-services-only (a test is the allowed caller), driver-exports-wiring, entry-no-args, tech-claimed, outside-imports-closed, no-dependency-defaults (defaults are right in test factories, 1221-1223). Why: a test builds units, calls them and asserts; nothing imports it, so every importer-side or export-side atom is vacuous. Open question (reasoning inferred, not tested on a codebase): the answer is yes, the atoms reach inside local helpers, by lexical scope of the file, not by call-graph. A \"no\" is unacceptable because it lets a loop hide in run(). To keep that from being too strict, give a test file a closed definition list instead of \"defines anything\": hooks, call-through helpers shaped like a hook (a one-line run(args) that calls the CLI and returns), assembly-shaped functions (test factories: build calls only), and provably immutable data. Any helper needing a branch, loop, polling or process spawn must leave the file and be a file of its own kind, where that kind's atoms judge it: a fake or in-memory implementation is an adapter (loops and tech allowed there), a data builder is a model, a registered matcher or shared hook is a driver the spec calls, a shared test factory is an assembly. So nothing local can hold logic and every place logic may live is itself bounded; the laundering venue closes because there is no unruled place left, not because the rule chases calls.
helpers: Oracles the atoms need (each is a decision input, none an atom): (1) layer-of-file from the flavor's name (368-371, 567-571); (2) the reader: tech claims, hook cut, effect-free call declarations, test registration role (545-566); (3) import classification concrete / declared-pure / claimed-tech / unclaimed (884-886, 942-943, 80-91, 1062-1063); (4) host-global name list for no-ambient-access, which must agree with reader claims for process/document; (5) factory-vs-function by flavor word (create*) for model callees (516-518); (6) project-declared loads list (469-474) and declared container libraries (492-495); (7) data-flow for args-plain, built-result-opaque, hook-result-untouched. Confidence: decomposition is my reading of all 1474 lines; the two parameter tables (per-kind lists in closed-definitions, callees-closed, outside-imports-closed) are inferred from canon's prose, not stated as tables. Remainder holes worth naming: unified-port (judgment), orchestrates-not-computes (judgment), kernel litmus and anti-corruption signals (Sharing, 1304-1325, advice only), use-case level labels (map annotation, not a violation), one boot per entry point (needs outside data), stable-root's open-ended \"judged by the rule\" clause. Unresolved canon points: blob and stable-root (654-655 vs 1126-1128), test spec inside the service folder vs private-sealed, \"defines anything\" vs \"not mutable state\" for tests.

atoms.name: inward-imports
atoms.statement: A file runtime-imports only files of its own layer or an inner one (model < ports < service,adapter < assembly < driver < boot).
atoms.why: The inside must be understandable and testable without knowing anything outside it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: layer rank of importer vs target from the flavor's kind; type-only imports unspecified for model/port/service (see sharedParts).
atoms.landing: The layer visible in each import line tells a reader what the file can possibly know.

atoms.name: layer-in-path
atoms.statement: An import specifier names a file that declares its layer, never a barrel (index.ts) that re-exports several layers.
atoms.why: The layer must be visible at the import site, or no layer rule can be read by tool or reviewer.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: specifier resolves to an index/re-export file, or to a file with no layer suffix where one is required.
atoms.landing: Reading `from '../icons/service'` says which layer is consumed with no file to open.

atoms.name: no-concrete-import
atoms.statement: A file does not runtime-import concrete platform/IO code (node:fs, HTTP clients, DB drivers); only declared-pure libraries are importable.
atoms.why: Concrete contact bypasses ports and makes the file untestable without setting the machine up.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes given a declared pure-library list and a declared container-library exception for assembly; determinism of a lib is declared, never checked.
atoms.landing: The reader knows the file cannot do I/O, so its tests need no machine.

atoms.name: closed-imports
atoms.statement: A driver runtime-imports only assemblies, drivers and the tech its bound reader claims; a boot imports exactly one driver and nothing else.
atoms.why: The outside kinds get a whitelist, not a blacklist, so the widest reach carries the narrowest verbs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind vs target kind plus reader claims; type-only imports free for driver (not blob).
atoms.landing: The outside is reasoned about without opening its code: its imports are the whole story.

atoms.name: port-types-only
atoms.statement: A port file holds no runtime code and no runtime import edge touches a port file in either direction.
atoms.why: A contract is a shape; runtime code in it means the adapter has not been extracted.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: runtime statements in .port files; runtime import/re-export/side-effect import to or from a port.
atoms.landing: A reader trusts that a port file is the contract and nothing else.

atoms.name: composition-assembly-only
atoms.statement: Public .service and .adapter files are runtime-imported only by assembly (and test); type-only imports and private/ files are out of scope.
atoms.why: Dependencies are resolved in one place, so services never know their neighbors' implementations.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target kind service/adapter, not under private/, import not type-only, importer kind not assembly/test.
atoms.landing: All wiring sits in assembly files; the chunk graph equals the assembly graph.

atoms.name: blob-consumers-only
atoms.statement: Only assembly and test files import blob, type imports included; blob importing blob is free.
atoms.why: Blob claims no guarantees, so any other importer inherits none.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: target has no layer suffix, importer kind not assembly/test/blob.
atoms.landing: Debt stays visible and fenced: every blob edge is in an assembly or a test.

atoms.name: outside-not-imported
atoms.statement: An assembly is imported only by drivers, assemblies (and tests); a driver only by a boot or drivers; a boot and a test by nothing; type imports included.
atoms.why: The outside kinds are callers in a chain, so nothing may depend on code that builds, fires or starts the program.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: importer kind per target kind, all import kinds.
atoms.landing: The entry chain boot -> driver -> assembly -> services reads as one line on the map.

atoms.name: private-sealed
atoms.statement: Nothing outside a service imports from its private/ directory, type imports included.
atoms.why: Visibility is ownership, not implementation coupling.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: path contains /private/ and importer is not in the owning service package.
atoms.landing: An instant visible violation in review: `/private/` in a foreign import.

atoms.name: no-service-cycle
atoms.statement: Dependencies between service packages, every import kind counted, form a DAG.
atoms.why: A cycle means neither service can be extracted, moved or reasoned about alone.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: package-level edge graph, SCC detection.
atoms.landing: The service map is a readable DAG; direction of nested adapters is forced upward.

atoms.name: no-runtime-cycle
atoms.statement: Runtime imports between modules, even in one service, form no cycle; type-only edges are not counted.
atoms.why: Circular ESM imports work in dev and fail silently as undefined in production.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: module-level runtime import graph.
atoms.landing: Load order is never a question when reading a file.

atoms.name: sub-driver-wiring
atoms.statement: A driver imports another driver only to call its wiring function from its own wiring, never a hook, never hexagon data.
atoms.why: Calling a sub-driver from a hook or handing it a use-case result would chain two calls behind one indirection.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: every use of a driver-imported binding is the callee of a call outside hooks; the target exports one wiring function and no hook.
atoms.landing: A driver tree is a split of one entry point, nothing more.

atoms.name: touches-no-globals
atoms.statement: A file does not read or call the ambient machine (environment, time, randomness, console, timers, globalThis, host names such as process/document) from a global.
atoms.why: Code that reaches the machine cannot be tested without setting the machine up; for assembly and boot, the tech is the driver's, not theirs.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: closed name list from flavor/reader; partial on aliasing (`const g = globalThis`). Same check, two whys (inside vs outside kinds): see sharedParts.
atoms.landing: A reader knows the file's output depends only on its arguments.

atoms.name: root-bindings-immutable
atoms.statement: Every module-root binding is provably immutable by syntax (primitive type, as const, readonly, Object.freeze to its depth); no top-level let, no unfrozen collection.
atoms.why: A test importing the module must get the module every other test got, whatever ran before.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: syntactic proof per binding, unresolved named types prove nothing; lifted by `mutableModuleState: true`.
atoms.landing: State is only in factory closures; a module exports factories, never instances.

atoms.name: root-no-machine-read
atoms.statement: No module-root binding stores a value read from the tech, the clock or randomness (the module's own location excepted).
atoms.why: The file could not be tested under another environment or moment without reloading it.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: tech/ambient name reads bound at root; a property read is free, a call is not.
atoms.landing: Nothing in the file differs from one load to the next.

atoms.name: root-no-effect
atoms.statement: Module evaluation performs no side effect: no call reaching tech, unclaimed code, a use case, or a local function of a side-effect layer; no assignment or delete statement; a throw is allowed; closed exemptions are the boot's one call and a test runner's registration calls.
atoms.why: Loading a file must neither act nor leave anything behind.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: root call classification needs the reader's effect-free declarations and a local call graph; exemptions come from kind and reader.
atoms.landing: Importing a file is always safe.

atoms.name: closed-definitions
atoms.statement: A file defines at run time only what its kind names: assembly functions (assembly), hooks and at most one wiring function (driver), nothing (boot).
atoms.why: A closed verb list stops logic from hiding in the layer that may import anything.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: functions, classes, variables found by statement kind, minus hooks and wiring/assembly functions; table per kind.
atoms.landing: The outside holds no logic to read; any definition is visible residue.

atoms.name: closed-callees
atoms.statement: Every call in an assembly, driver or boot targets only what the kind lists: factories, assemblies, declared loads (assembly); use cases, assembly factories, sub-driver wiring, claimed tech (driver); one driver wiring call (boot).
atoms.why: The outside does one thing each, and a call outside the list is a decision with no contract.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: callee file kind, flavor word (create*), declaration lists, reader claims; await counts as the call.
atoms.landing: The map shows what each outside file connects, with no hidden decisions.

atoms.name: args-verbatim
atoms.statement: Call arguments in an assembly, a driver's wiring or a hook are literals, tech values as received, or instances; a hook reads nothing off the event, an assembly or wiring may read a field of a tech value; a boot passes none.
atoms.why: Deriving or defaulting an argument is translation, and translation belongs to a service.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: argument expression shapes; `opts.cwd ?? process.cwd()`, `join(cwd,'x')` and `opts.files` in a hook are red.
atoms.landing: What flows through the outside is exactly what arrived.

atoms.name: result-untouched
atoms.statement: The result of a call in an assembly or hook is only returned or passed on (assembly), or returned or dropped (hook): never read, computed with, member-accessed, branched on, written, logged or handed to another call by a hook.
atoms.why: Looking into a result is a decision, and the outside never decides.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: data-flow on the call result; a declared load's result counts as a tech value, so it may feed arguments and conditions.
atoms.landing: The outside carries values it never inspects, so it cannot hide logic.

atoms.name: wiring-conditions-only
atoms.statement: A branch or loop in an assembly tests only a parameter or loaded value against a literal or truthiness, and its arms are factory calls.
atoms.why: A condition on an instance is a decision the map cannot show.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: condition operand classification, arm call kinds.
atoms.landing: Every conditional in the graph is a visible wiring choice, not behavior.

atoms.name: straight-line-body
atoms.statement: A hook body contains no branch, loop, try or conditional expression.
atoms.why: One unconditional arrow from event to use case is the whole connection; anything else is logic with no home.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes for if/switch/loops/ternary/try; partial for `&&`/`??` and iteration methods (need a declared list).
atoms.landing: The body reads top to bottom with nothing to simulate.

atoms.name: hook-calls-once
atoms.statement: Each hook, by the reader's cut, makes exactly one use-case call and no other call.
atoms.why: Two calls hide an unowned sequence; zero is logic with no home; the link is one arrow.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: hook boundary from the reader, count callees resolving to service use cases and other calls; the test reader exempts the count.
atoms.landing: The map draws each hook as one arrow.

atoms.name: wiring-hooks-split
atoms.statement: Use-case calls occur only inside hooks; assembly calls, tech setup and sub-driver registration occur only outside hooks.
atoms.why: Who builds and who fires are kept apart even inside one driver file.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: location of each call vs hook boundary.
atoms.landing: A driver reads as a setup block plus a list of one-liners.

atoms.name: assembly-returns-services
atoms.statement: An assembly returns services or shared model instances, and adapters only when a test is its caller; an adapter-returning assembly has only test importers.
atoms.why: Consumers type against service APIs, and adapters are reachable only from tests.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: returned expression kinds and importer kinds of that file.
atoms.landing: What an assembly yields is the program's service surface.

atoms.name: reader-bound
atoms.statement: Every driver file and test file is read by a reader bound to its tech, or by one that counts it as blob on purpose; otherwise it is red.
atoms.why: No driver rule can be judged without the reading that cuts hooks and claims tech.
atoms.check: LAUNCH yes: coverage of glob bindings over files of kind driver/test; a binding naming a file against its flavor is a config error.
atoms.landing: The tech each driver listens to is named in config.

atoms.name: injected-deps
atoms.statement: A service or adapter factory takes its dependencies through its arguments with no default values; env, time, randomness, console and timers included.
atoms.why: Defaults create static imports and scatter assembly logic across service modules.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: default initializers on dependency parameters of composition-unit factories; which parameters are dependencies needs types; test factories are exempt (defaults are right there).
atoms.landing: Every dependency of a service shows in its factory signature.

atoms.name: adapter-implements-port
atoms.statement: An adapter file's exported factory conforms to a port interface, and every adapter of a port yields the same result shape.
atoms.why: The inside never needs to know which adapter it talks to.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: type assignability of the factory's return to a port type, if the adapter-to-port link is declared by annotation or satisfies.
atoms.landing: A reader sees which port each adapter fills.

atoms.name: only-driver-listens
atoms.statement: Only drivers (and tests) hand callbacks to a tech a reader claims; adapters call the tech outbound behind a port.
atoms.why: One place receives the tech's events, so that is the only place needing the reading.

atoms.landing: Event entry points are found in drivers only.

atoms.name: test-no-prod-config
atoms.statement: A test file imports no production config; it injects test config.
atoms.why: Production config couples the test to an environment.
atoms.check: LAUNCH partial: needs a declared set of production config files.
atoms.landing: A test's environment is exactly what it passes in.

testKind: Canon puts test = "assembly and driver in one" (263, 1011) but exempts it from about ten atoms; the exemptions are exactly the atoms that conflict. Facts a test has: it builds units (setup), calls them from hooks (many calls), and asserts (reads results), nothing imports it. CARRY: reader-bound (the runner's reading cuts hooks and exempts registration), outside-not-imported as target (nothing imports it), the three root atoms (root-bindings-immutable and root-no-machine-read in full, root-no-effect except runner registration), layer-in-path, private-sealed, no-service-cycle (canon itself counts test edges: 909-912), no-runtime-cycle, test-no-prod-config. 'Imports anything' (matrix 873) is therefore false: three import atoms still bind a test. CANDIDATE, not stated: straight-line-body on test bodies and on every local function reachable from them (why: the reviewer reads the scenario as given/when/expect, 1152-1161). DO NOT CARRY: inward-imports and no-concrete-import (a test must import anything to build units with fakes and characterize blob), closed-imports, closed-callees, closed-definitions (local fakes and builders), hook-calls-once, args-verbatim, result-untouched (a test calls many things and reads results; the only atoms exempt by nature), touches-no-globals (e2e and timers), injected-deps (test factories take defaults). Permitted importer, not carrier: composition-assembly-only, blob-consumers-only. With atoms the exemption list disappears: the test kind is a selection, and 'except' is never written. Contradiction to settle: .e2e is named as test kind (263) yet 1022-1023 says e2e tests are neither assembly nor driver, outside the graph.
helpers: Answer: yes, the no-branch/no-loop atom must reach local helpers, and it must reach them as a closure, not by naming. Canon is silent on test-body control flow (the hook-count exemption is the only related text), so this is the candidate atom straight-line-body applied to the test kind. Structure: the constrained unit is every function defined in the spec file that a hook reaches through local calls (reachability over the file's own call graph), not only the lexical hook body. A helper with a loop is then red in the spec file, and its way out is the placement canon already gives shared test code (1218-1219) with the shared/local distinction dropped: place by what it is. A run() that spawns the CLI touches the concrete world, so it is an adapter file (a test-purpose launcher, may loop, carries adapter atoms and is imported by the test: imports are unconstrained for tests); a data builder with a loop is a model; a setup that builds units is an assembly function (closed-callees, wiring-conditions-only apply, loops only as wiring on parameters); a shared matcher or registration is a driver. So the test file's own definitions shrink to hooks plus assembly-shaped functions, which matches 'assembly and driver in one' literally instead of 'defines anything'. This closes the laundering venue without a 'no': logic leaves the file for a kind that bounds it, as hook-one-call does with the facade service (675-685); across files the callee carries its own atoms. Residual venues, not solved here: (1) iteration methods (forEach/map/reduce) and recursion launder a loop unless the check lists them; (2) test.each is the runner's own loop, a reader exemption stated with its reason, though canon calls data-driven indirection harmful (1158); (3) fake adapters under public-unit/fractal assembly are unbounded; (4) whether assembly-shaped helpers may branch on test parameters needs a ruling (wiring-conditions-only allows it). Honest status: the structure above is the proposal; the whole problem statement is unsettled, the wrong answer is only 'no'.
